Reflow 2.0 — projected viewpoints

Every element below is projected from reflow2.json (2421 nodes, 9862 edges). Nothing is hand-drawn: the renderer may only emit what the graph states, and everything it needed but could not find is confessed at the end — per the doctrine that a fill-in during rendering is a defect in the model, not a job for the agent. The catalogue: docs/viewpoints.md.

Functional viewpoint

≈ OV-5: what must be true, and what the system does about it. Capability status from the graph.

flowchart LR
  req_a_cluster_can_be_declared_deliberately_separate["A cluster can be declared deliberately separate, so disconnected_community reports undeclared islands instead of one permanent warning (medium)"]
  req_a_comparison_discloses_build_skew["A comparison says when its two sides were written by different builds (medium)"]

ATOMICITY: one bad item rejects the whole batch and the good items BEFORE and AFTER it are both absent; an edge into a missing node rolls back the good edge beside it; one unknown artifact leaves every other baseline unmoved. EVERY FAILURE: two bad items in a batch of four come back as two failures with their indices, and a failure carries its POSITION so two entries sharing an id are still distinguishable. PER-ITEM JUDGEMENT: two accepts with two DIFFERENT dispositions produce two different change-event records and design_holds never borrows design_updated's event; two acknowledged gaps keep two different rationales. COVERAGE: one bulk edge form produces byte-identical properties to the typed helper it replaces, defaults included, so nothing is silently dropped. SURFACE: a rejected batch is an ERROR carrying every failure in its data rather than a payload that reads as success; two gaps whose prompts share an id are each replayed against ONLY their own answers; a half-answered ask batch is refused naming which half and writes nothing; an empty ask batch is refused rather than treated as a no-op. PROVEN ON THE REAL SURFACE: driven over stdio JSON-RPC against the built binary on a copy of reflow2's own 1205-node design — 138 tools served, 20 nodes and 20 edges each in one call, a rejected batch returning BOTH failures with the good item before them unwritten, and two accepts carrying two different change types. Certify that a restructuring preserved functioncomparepreserve.rsThe function-preservation check refuses what it cannot classify (crates/reflow2-core/tests/preserve.rs) — 15 cases. The suite defends the REFUSAL half, because a classifier that recognises ALLOCATED_TO and calls everything else benign hands out green certificates for changes it never looked at (BL-170's fourth quadrant). So: an unknown node type blocks certification, an unresolvable edge endpoint blocks it, a reworded capability blocks it (a rename and a scope change are the same bytes), and a known function change OUTRANKS an unknown, because more information cannot un-move a capability. `every_schema_node_type_has_a_class` walks the live schema — all 29 types — and fails the build when a new one lands with no class, so the omission is caught before a release rather than by a false green; it also asserts three known types are present, so it cannot pass by iterating an empty set. The load-bearing case is `depends_on_is_read_from_its_endpoints_not_its_type`: DEPENDS_ON is the functional DAG between Capabilities and packaging between Components, and classifying by edge type alone would file all 51 of this design's cross-system dependencies as function changes. MUTATION-CHECKED against four seeded regressions (unknown types falling back to structure, the verdict order inverted, one function endpoint sufficing for a function edge, a reworded function node waved through) — each was caught, none silently. Time-bound claims land in a TemporalFact, and age is visible where claims are readtemporaldates.rsA dated claim reads back with its age, and an undated one says nothing (crates/reflow2-core/tests/a_claim_carries_its_age.rs) — 15 cases, all passing 2026-08-16. WHY THE FILE EXISTS AT ALL: 112 of 205 TemporalFacts carried a `valid_from` the schema did not declare and NOTHING read, so declaring it without a reader would have changed the schema and left the corpus exactly as inert. These cases are the evidence that the property now does something. THE ARITHMETIC IS TESTED WHERE IT FAILS SILENTLY — the epoch and the day either side of it (a sign error's first victim), and the Gregorian century exceptions: 1900 was NOT a leap year and 2000 WAS, which a naive `% 4` gets wrong one way and a naive `% 100` the other. Ten malformed inputs are checked to DECLINE rather than guess, including `16-08-2026`, which is a real date in the other convention and must never be silently accepted. WHAT A HIT SAYS: a dated fact reports `as_of` and `age_days`; an UNDATED node serialises to `{}` so the ordinary hit is byte-identical to what it was before ages existed; and a date that will not parse still reports `as_of` but no `age_days` — the two fields are separate precisely so 'dated, but I cannot read the date' is sayable, and collapsing them would make it indistinguishable from undated. THREE COUNTERWEIGHTS DECIDE THE SHAPE, each guarding against a plausible wrong answer: a claim dated in the FUTURE reports a NEGATIVE age rather than clamping to zero, because clamping renders a forecast or a typo as 'current'; a claim expiring TODAY is NOT yet expired, since `valid_to` is the last day it holds and an off-by-one here retires a live fact a day early; and an UNREADABLE `valid_to` never expires anything, because guessing would silently mark real facts dead. MUTATION-CHECKED FOUR WAYS, each killing exactly the right case: dropping the century exception fails the leap and anchor cases; clamping a future date fails the negative-age case; expiring on the last valid day fails the boundary case; treating an unreadable end date as expired fails the counterweight. `today` IS A PARAMETER IN EVERY CASE — a test that read the clock would pass today and fail in a fortnight, which is the one failure mode a module about staleness must not have. VERIFIED END-TO-END on the real store through a restarted server: `age_days: 0` on a fact dated today, `age_days: 9` on one dated 2026-08-07, and no age fields at all on an undated fact, in one reply. NOT COVERED: `where-am-i` still does not mark age, so only half of `cap:claims-carry-their-age` part 3 is checked here. (passing)

THE CASES: assigned decisions are LISTED, not merely counted, carrying decision_id, name and approver_id (flo2's F4, hit independently here the same day where finding two meant jq-ing the export); scoping to one contributor returns only their assigned decisions and names them in `next`; scoping does NOT make an unassigned musing somebody's problem, so the deliberate quiet around thinking out loud survives; an unknown contributor_id is REFUSED rather than answered with an empty list, with a positive control proving the same call succeeds for a real id — because a typo would otherwise produce 'nothing is owed to you', the most reassuring possible reply and the one least likely to be questioned. CASE 2, owning_something_does_not_drag_a_person_into_a_blast_radius: propagate_from over an owned node at depth 5 must not reach the Contributor — the exclusion AUTHORED_BY and CLAIMS already carry, asserted rather than assumed for the third of the kind. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be found: nothing verifies that ownership is the RIGHT attribution for any given node, because that is a judgement; and no check exists for unowned ground, because none was built. PREFIX (BL-125): a bare hex digest matches its own `sha256:`-prefixed baseline and vice versa, the drift event id is identical whichever dialect was observed, and both counterweights hold — a genuinely different digest still reports `checksum_change` with its `realizes` edges intact, and a non-hex fingerprint is left verbatim. LENGTH (BL-160): a full 64-char digest matches a 16-char baseline and a truncated observation matches a full baseline, on the drift comparison AND on `set_artifact_checksum`'s would-move-the-baseline guard — the half that is not a gate problem at all but a BL-157 bulk sweep failing on every short-registered artifact for a change that never happened. When the two dialects agree the LONGER digest stays on the record, which also makes the accept idempotent ACROSS dialects: re-stating it coarsely mints one claim, not two. FIVE COUNTERWEIGHTS, and they are what keep the length rule from being a way to stop noticing: two FULL digests sharing their first sixteen characters are still drift (the case a truncate-both-to-N would pass); a truncated observation that disagrees WITHIN its own length is still drift; a genuinely different digest is still refused as a first baseline, still naming the disposition that would be honest; prefix tolerance does not escape the `sha256:` dialect, so `blake3:zz` and `blake3:zzzz` stay different; and an EMPTY digest agrees with nothing, because every string starts with the empty string. No minimum prefix length is imposed, deliberately — a short baseline is a weak baseline, but its strength is decided when it is REGISTERED, and a read side refusing to honour what the write side accepted is the same write/read disagreement this suite exists to close. WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX: the four bug cases failed and all five counterweights passed. MUTATION-CHECKED SEVEN WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it: make agreement always-true and all seven counterweights fail while every bug case passes (which is what proves the counterweights carry the weight); revert to `==` and exactly the four bug cases fail; drop the sha256-dialect restriction and only the two dialect-boundary cases fail; truncate both sides to 16 and only the two sharing-a-prefix cases fail; drop the both-non-empty guard and only the empty-digest case fails; fix drift.rs alone and only the two accept-path cases fail; drop the longer-digest-wins rule and only the idempotence case fails. THE TEST WAS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT: the first version of the still-refused counterweight used a SHORT baseline, and against a 16-char baseline `NEAR` is a legitimate extension rather than a different digest — a 16-char baseline only ever pinned 16 characters, which was established by writing it wrong rather than assumed. PROVEN ON THE REAL DESIGN, and it is the row's own scenario replayed: the built binary driven over stdio JSON-RPC against a throwaway copy of reflow2's own 1221-node design, sweeping all 109 registered artifacts off the actual working tree with the FULL 64-char digest — 51 truncated baselines, all 51 unchanged, and the only 4 `checksum_change` findings are the four files this change edited. `tools/reflow2_check.py`'s Python workaround is DELETED, and tools/test_reflow2_check.py pins the pair end to end: an untouched file registered short gates GREEN, and the same short baseline on a genuinely edited file still gates RED. FOUND BY DOGFOODING BEFORE IT SHIPPED: comparing dates as whole strings called 2026-07-28 stale against 2026-07-28T14:52:00-04:00, an ordering nobody recorded, asserted by the very report that exists to stop that — now same-day is Unknown, pinned by a test, with the counterweight that an earlier DAY is still stale. (passing)
Describe the vocabularyschema, vocabularyschema.rs, build.yaml, core.yaml, dimensions.yaml, environment.yaml, functional.yaml, inference.yaml, operate.yaml, readiness.yaml, structure.yaml, temporal.yaml, verify.yaml, vocabulary.rs'Which of my rules have no detector?' is askable, and asked: an enforced DesignRule with no PASSING verification is a 0.6 gap; an advisory one is not; a `planned` check does not silence it; a passing one closes it; `enforced` absent reads as the schema default TRUE and is still asked about. Plus the self-seeding half — a build with zero recorded conventions is asked once at 0.45, a design with no build yet is NOT (artifacts are the trigger, not components, because at genesis no convention has been chosen), and one recorded convention answers it. Eight cases in crates/reflow2-core/tests/enforced_rule_needs_a_detector.rs. VERIFIED AGAINST REALITY, not just fixtures: run over reflow2's own committed export it returns exactly four gaps, naming rule:bl-135, rule:bl-212, rule:bl-41 and rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party — reproducing the reported four-of-four. The placement was found BY a test, not by review: the first draft sat inside detect_unverified_capabilities, which early-returns when a project has zero verifications, so it silently never fired on a young design. (passing), write_side.rs (passing)
Say what to work on next, as a projection with its reasoning shownreportreport.rswhat_next answers in four bands, the exploration slot is not optional, and liveness is what makes the shaping band readable (crates/reflow2-core/tests/what_next.rs, 11 cases). THE ONE THAT MUST NEVER REGRESS is a_marked_decision_is_never_ranked_however_it_would_score: a `proposed` Decision carrying AUTHORED_BY role=approver is the user's own durable self-prioritisation — it already existed and was simply never named one — and no computed score may reorder it or demote it into the ranked band, so the test gives a marked decision every scoring signal available and asserts it still never appears there. MUTATION-CHECKED: removing the band-1 short-circuit fails exactly that test and no other. THE SECOND LOAD-BEARING CASE is a_decision_nothing_points_at_is_still_surfaced. Every ranking signal here is built on connectedness, so a decision nothing points at scores zero forever and would never be shown — dec:bl-155's unused-versus-unreachable trap arriving through a ranking instead of a usage count. A suite that only checked the ranking would stay green while the fifth slot was dropped as over-engineering, which is precisely what the two independent derivations of that slot (the Q-table framing, and Anthony's own 'top 4 and bottom 1') exist to prevent. THE SHAPING BAND'S CASES PIN A CAVEAT THIS DESIGN RECORDED BEFORE THE CODE EXISTED: cap:what-next warned that raw GOVERNED_BY in-degree is the wrong signal because its top hit was a pruning decision governing ten DROPPED requirements, and a_decision_governing_only_retired_work_does_not_shape_anything IS that fixture — a 9-dead-node decision must lose to a 3-live-node one. MUTATION-CHECKED: removing the liveness filter fails exactly the two liveness tests and no others. breadth_of_governed_types_is_reported_but_never_ranks pins the refinement that was TRIED AND REJECTED on measurement — weighting by distinct governed types demotes every exemplar the capability names as correct, because governing eight Components is shaping and single-typedness is not shallowness — so `shapes` is reported and kept out of the score. ALSO PINNED: retired governed nodes are COUNTED and reported rather than silently dropped; the shaping band holds only ACCEPTED decisions, never open ones, because it answers a different question for a different reader; `alignment: supporting` on a CONTRADICTS edge is corroboration and must not raise the score, which heal.rs paid for once already; `decision:ack:` review records are excluded both as decisions and as governed sources, because they dominate raw GOVERNED_BY counts (measured, excluding them took that edge type from 867 to 255) so leaving them in makes the answer confidently wrong rather than merely noisy; the unexplored pick is stable across two readings of an unchanged design and ADVANCES when a decision is settled, since the core takes no clock and no RNG and the rotation is derived from the count of accepted decisions; and `not_shown` accounts for every open decision the answer omitted. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be discovered: nothing here checks that the WEIGHTS are right. They are a deliberately coarse guide against a stated acceptance criterion of 'general ballpark', and the tests assert the ORDER the signals produce, never the absolute numbers. (passing)

As-released viewpoint

≈ SV-8: what actually shipped, hashes frozen at cut so history cannot rewrite itself, and the diff against what was built (BL-34).

function, Show where to extend or simplify a feature that already exists, A changelog is a derivable view of the graph's own delta, A claim names the session that made it, and a claim nobody is its two sides came from different builds, Hold and collapse a decision point (forkable alternatives), The server explains its own absence instead of vanishing, Delta reconcile: present what changed newcomer where a new piece of work belongs, Two people work one design at once through isolation, not through a lock, The practice of planning delivery in increments is served, so a consumer does not when a settled road may be worth re-opening, Neutralise hidden instructions in text arriving from outside, and say what was stripped, A team asks the detectors about its own part, and is told what it did not see, A seat is minted on request and carried by the caller, and a claim that cannot name one is refused, A session names the design it wants by graph_id, and the server maps id to path, A session that never opened a skill is visible, and says so before it ends, The moment tells the agent which skill it needs, Serve the skills AND the working instructions from the binary, so a project holds only a pointer, The agent asks about the thing, not about the schema — an interview step and a routing table, A seat reports which shared records have moved ahead of it, and names what arrived, deployed to: Developer machine (rolled_back)

Decision viewpoint

No clean DoDAF box — the record of why, which DoDAF leaves to AV-1 prose. Each decision, its rationale, and what it governs.

DecisionWhyStandingGoverns
A claimed region may be defined by a QUERY as well as by a seed and a depth — and never by a stored node list
DECIDED 2026-08-08, Anthony's word: a claim may be described by a QUERY in addition to seed+depth, and an explicit stored node LIST is refused. Seed+depth remains and is unchanged for the work it already fits. WHY THE LIST IS THE ONE OPTION REJECTED, and this is the whole of the reasoning: the original choice — 'the region is COMPUTED from seed+depth rather than stored as a node list, so it follows the design as it changes' — was made to stop a claim going stale the moment the design moves. A query PRESERVES that property, because it is still evaluated fresh every time anyone reads the board; a stored list is the single option that throws it away. So this widens how a region may be DESCRIBED without weakening the guarantee the original decision bought. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS: cross-cutting duties — an audit, a sweep over everything of one kind, cold-validating what another session recorded — which are a general category rather than one team's oddity, and which no radius can express. SUPERSEDES NOTHING: the seed+depth rule stands as the default; this is an addition, so the earlier choice is neither re-opened again nor un-accepted (dec:reopen-supersedes). STILL UNANSWERED and deliberately not decided here: what query language, and whether an unevaluable or empty query is refused at claim time or reported at read time. Both are build questions; the shape is settled, the surface is not.		Because the cost was measured rather than argued. dev_storyflow w-aa0607ff, 2026-08-08: their lane was 'cold-test the retrievability of nodes another session mined', spanning two unrelated slices — there is no seed whose depth-2 radius is that work. They claimed a representative node and put the truth in the `note`, so claim_report's PROSE was right while its STRUCTURED answer was wrong for them, which is the exact failure a structured board exists to remove. THE STRONGER EVIDENCE IS BEHAVIOURAL AND IT IS THREE FOR THREE: both prior workers on that lane skipped claim_region entirely and kept a text file of document paths, because a flat list described their region better than the graph could. A tool losing to a text file is the same shape as the finding that drove the read-half increment — 'today a document BEATS the graph for making a decision, and that is a fair fight the graph loses'. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT WAS PUT AND WEIGHED, not skipped: a claim is ADVISORY and never a lock, so a wrong region misleads a colleague rather than corrupting a write, which argues for keeping the mechanism simple. It was outweighed because an advisory board whose structured field is routinely wrong is how a signal gets trained into being ignored — the same objection that condemned permanently-`live` seat liveness in the same session, and the reason both were treated as real rather than cosmetic.acceptedA claim describes its region by a query, for work no radius can express, Claim a region of the design so two people do not collide in it
A failing check may state what it fell short of; where it does not, the report says the bar was never stated
Verification gains an OPTIONAL criterion — what the check was measured against. A `failing` carrying one is reported as a MEASUREMENT; a `failing` without one is reported as a bar never stated, and is never presented as though a threshold existed. Nothing is refused and no existing check breaks.		Anthony's call, 2026-08-01, from three options. THE PROBLEM, from the music_graph adopt pass (BL-143): that repo's central fact is that everything runs and almost nothing is correct. A smoke run was recorded `passing` (it truly does run) and an accuracy measurement `failing` — but nothing in the repo states an acceptance threshold, so `failing` was the reporter's judgement stored as if it were data. Their words, and the caveat went into a description where no detector reads it. WHY OPTIONAL RATHER THAN REQUIRED. Option (b), refusing `failing` without a criterion, is the strongest version and was rejected on two counts: it breaks every existing failing check until someone supplies a bar retroactively, and it blocks the honest case where something is plainly broken and no threshold was ever written down. More importantly it is OUT OF STEP WITH THE FAMILY. BL-106, BL-126 and BL-136 all REPORT the gap rather than refusing the work — an unscoped check is counted as unscoped, an undated one as unknown, a consumed one as consumed, and none of them is forbidden. This is the fourth axis and it should behave like the other three. WHY NOT A NEW STATUS. Option (c), adding `inconclusive`, is the cheapest and gives 'it runs but correctness is unknown' a home — but it treats the symptom. Someone can still write `failing` as a pure opinion and nothing notices, which is the exact defect. It is not foreclosed and could still be added later for its own reasons; it simply does not answer this question. THE SHAPE THIS COMPLETES. The evidence-quality family now has four faces, all asking whether a green or red tick means what a reader will take it to mean: BL-106 a check stale in TIME, BL-126 narrow in INPUT SPACE, BL-136 not INDEPENDENT of what it validates, and this one — no CRITERION, so there is nothing for the evidence to be evidence of. The first three ask how good the evidence is; this asks what it was evidence FOR. NOT YET BUILT. The shape is settled; the build is BL-143.acceptednothing
OPEN — a claim in the graph cannot be announced before the work, because the export it rides in may only be written once per PR
RECORDED AS A FINDING PLUS AN OPEN QUESTION, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Found 2026-08-04 IMMEDIATELY AFTER accepting `dec:coord-board-in-graph`, while updating AGENTS.md to match the move — by noticing that a sentence in it had silently become false. Nothing here is settled, and this does NOT reverse the move. THE COLLISION, BETWEEN TWO RULES THAT ARE EACH CORRECT ALONE. (1) `dec:export-once-per-pr` and AGENTS.md: 'a branch may hold as many commits as you like; only one of them may touch `docs/design/reflow2.json`, and it should be the LAST' — because PRs squash-merge, so only the final export's `prev_content_hash` survives and an intermediate export puts a hole in the lineage chain. (2) `dec:coord-board-in-graph`, accepted minutes earlier: a claim is graph state, recorded by `claim_region`, and it travels in the committed export. TOGETHER THEY SAY: A CLAIM MADE BEFORE THE WORK BECOMES VISIBLE TO ANYONE ELSE ONLY WHEN THE PR MERGES — which is after the work is finished. Claiming first is exactly what a claim is for. ⭐ THIS FALSIFIES A CLAIM MADE ON THE DECIDING NODE, AND THE CORRECTION BELONGS ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN BEING QUIETLY ABSORBED. `dec:coord-board-in-graph` argued, both while open and at acceptance: 'both travel in the committed export exactly as COORD.md travels in git — so VISIBILITY IS UNCHANGED.' That is wrong, and the asymmetry is precisely the one that matters. COORD.md could be committed and pushed AS ITS OWN COMMIT the moment work started — AGENTS.md even prescribed it ('put the COORD claim commit, which carries no export, FIRST'). The export cannot be, because writing it early is the thing that breaks the lineage chain. The old advice was not merely superseded; the property it depended on — that a claim costs no export — is the property the move removed. WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: NOTHING, AND THAT IS WHY THE MOVE STANDS. reflow2 has one writer. `dec:coord-board-in-graph` already records that the claims layer is 'UNPROVEN under contention' and that the single-writer proof is all that was obtained. This is a second, sharper instance of that same limit — and it is worse than the general statement, because it is not that contention is untested but that a KNOWN MECHANISM makes pre-announcement impossible. OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) ACCEPT IT AND SAY SO — with one writer a claim is a note to your future self, and the export at PR time is soon enough. Cheapest and honest; the counter is that it silently retires 'claim before you work', which is the discipline the board existed to enforce. (b) LET A CLAIM COMMIT EXPORT, AND EXEMPT IT FROM THE CHAIN — the export gate would need to distinguish a claims-only delta from a design delta. Counter: the gate exists because silent chain breaks happened repeatedly ((BL-107), six commits in a row; (BL-156)), and an exemption is a hole in exactly the check that catches them. (c) CLAIMS LEAVE THE EXPORT — a separate small committed file, written per claim, merged by union like COORD.md was. Counter: that is COORD.md with extra steps, and re-splits the fact into two places, which is the failure the move existed to end. (d) PUBLISH CLAIMS OUT OF BAND — a hosted surface or live tier, which `dec:central-host` and `dec:live-tier` both already ask about. Counter: both are open, both are much larger than this, and `dec:multi-writer-architecture` settled on the repo file with no hosted service. WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED: that COORD.md's `merge=union` in `.gitattributes` is what made the old claim commit cheap and conflict-free, and that `docs/design/reflow2.json` uses the `merge=reflow2` three-way driver instead — the two files were never merging the same way, and any option here inherits that difference. NOT CHECKED: whether `release_claim` has the same problem in reverse — a claim released mid-branch is also invisible until the PR merges, which would mean a finished lane still reads as held by exactly the mechanism that was supposed to fix stale claims. Liveness would cover the case where the session ended, but not the case where the same session released and kept working.		Filed the moment it was found rather than after, because it was found by the cheapest possible route — updating a document to match a decision, and noticing that one sentence in it had become false — and that route only exists while the change is being made. An hour later the sentence would have read as merely stale. Recorded as its own node rather than as an amendment to `dec:coord-board-in-graph` because that decision is ACCEPTED and this does not reopen it: the move was right, one of its supporting arguments was wrong, and those are different facts. Folding a falsification into an accepted node would either weaken a decision that should stand or hide the correction — `dec:reopen-supersedes` sets the rule that a settled choice is not un-accepted, and this is not a re-opening. The unchecked item about `release_claim` is named so its absence reads as a hole rather than as completed analysis — and it is the more alarming half, since it would undo the stale-claim fix that was the whole justification for the move.proposedClaim a region of the design so two people do not collide in it
When a detector's NAME is wrong, fix what it SAYS — the key is a contract and the sentence is not
`req:a-report-says-what-it-swept-and-whether-its-checks-ran` (b) offered exactly two ways out for `disconnected_community`: 'Either rename it to what it computes (\'tightly-coupled cluster\') or make it compute what it claims.' NEITHER WAS TAKEN. The message was rewritten to describe the walk it actually made, and the category key `disconnected_community` was left alone. WHY RENAMING LOST. The key is a consumer contract in three places at once: it is a documented HEAL category, it is what `detect_defects` callers match on, and `ility.rs` uses it as a named ility source (`detect_defects.disconnected_community`). Renaming it would break every consumer in order to fix a sentence — the cost lands on people who did nothing wrong, to repair prose they never read. dev_storyflow's fleet matches on these keys. WHY RECOMPUTING LOST, and this is the one worth reading. 'Make it compute what it claims' sounds like the honest option and is the wrong diagnosis: the detector's computation is not broken. It runs connected components over `design_network()`, correctly. THE REQUIREMENT'S OWN TEXT MISDESCRIBES IT AS COMPUTING MODULARITY, WHICH IT DOES NOT. What is narrow is the NETWORK, and the narrowing is deliberate and load-bearing — `NON_DESIGN_TYPES` and the exclusion of `CONTAINS` exist because provenance nodes and decomposition scaffolds distort the topology, each for a reason with its own record (BL-84, BL-124). Making it 'compute what it claims' would mean walking the whole graph, which would undo those and report every Fragment as an island. The fix was never in the algorithm. ⭐ SO THE GENERAL FORM, which is why this is a Decision and not a code comment: WHEN A CHECK'S NAME OVERSTATES ITS COMPUTATION, THE THIRD OPTION IS USUALLY RIGHT — leave the identifier, leave the algorithm, and make the OUTPUT state its own scope. A key is an interface; a message is addressed to a reader; only the second is free to change, and only the second was ever wrong. ── A LARGER ROAD NOT TAKEN, recorded because it will be re-proposed ── The requirement is titled 'A report says what it swept', and the fullest reading of that is to change `detect_defects` itself to return `{swept: {...}, defects: (...)}` instead of a bare array — which is what the SCOPED variant already does (`Scoped` carries `total`, `in_scope`, `region_size`, `note`), so the two halves of one tool are inconsistent today and that asymmetry is real. NOT DONE HERE, on scope rather than on merit. It breaks every consumer that indexes the array, it is a minor version bump, and the requirement's own owed items are enumerated (a), (b), (c) and are all satisfiable without it. The requirement also states its own boundary: 'NOT IN SCOPE: whether every reporting tool needs this treatment or only those whose zero is read as permission.' Doing the shape change under the cover of finishing (b) and (c) would have been the widening this project keeps warning about. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether the unscoped `detect_defects` should match the scoped one's envelope. That is a genuine open question about surface consistency, and it is Anthony's, not an implementer's.		The category key is an interface — matched by callers and used by name as an ility source — while the message is addressed to a reader. Only the message was ever wrong, so only the message changed. 'Make it compute what it claims' was rejected on a sharper ground than cost: the computation is correct, and the narrowness people mistake for a bug is the deliberate exclusion of provenance nodes and CONTAINS, each with its own record. Widening the walk would undo BL-84 and BL-124 and report every Fragment as an island.proposedA finding describes the walk that produced it, and an empty orientation read says which zero it is
DECIDED — a named edge-set projection gets the standard graph battery as MEASUREMENT; build ONE slice first (centrality over the reasoning projection) before the general surface
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD, WITH A SCOPE CONDITION: BUILD EXACTLY ONE SLICE FIRST — CENTRALITY OVER THE `reasoning` PROJECTION — AND DO NOT SHIP THE GENERAL SURFACE UNTIL THAT ONE HAS PROVED USEFUL.** The shape below is accepted. The sequencing is the ruling: the highest-value slice was already named inside this node, and `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` already records the missing capability in its own words — *'WHICH FEW DECISIONS SHAPE EVERYTHING ELSE... neither what-next nor where-am-i answers it today, and it is what a newcomer actually needs'* — and says it should be a COMPUTATION rather than another paragraph. **That computation is one call away and has never been made.** ⚠️ **THE TWO TRAPS TRAVEL WITH THE FIRST SLICE, NOT WITH THE GENERAL SURFACE**, so neither is deferred by narrowing scope: the exclusion list is part of the projection (the first hand run returned the ten most influential 'decisions' as all `decision:ack:` review records; excluding them took the edge set 867 → 255), and the result is a READING, never a defect. Emitting defects from a broad projection is BL-42's exact shape, where one detector became 20 of 31 defects and had to be cut back. ⚠️ STILL NOT SETTLED BY THIS, and deliberately left to the first slice to answer in practice: whether this is a new served tool, an extension of `graph_report`, or an argument on existing detectors; whether a projection is a node type or a static list in code; and whether centrality should be betweenness (already imported) or reachability (what was computed by hand) — `dec:idea-is-betweenness-the-right-centrality` asks that and this does not answer it. ═══════════════ THE ACCEPTED SHAPE, AS PROPOSED ═══════════════ Anthony's framing 2026-08-10, and it is correct: graph algorithms run on any set of nodes and edges, so the analyses should be available across the design rather than wired one-per-detector. Measured basis in `fact:graph-analysis-covers-a-third-of-the-edge-types` — 23 of 35 populated edge types and 31% of edges get no graph analysis at all, including the entire golden thread and the delivery plan. THE SHAPE: a PROJECTION is a named edge set plus its exclusions. Given one, run the standard battery — strongly-connected components and cycles, connected components, centrality, communities and modularity, articulation points, toposort depth — and REPORT IT AS MEASUREMENT, NEVER AS A VERDICT. `flow.rs` already uses exactly that language for its own cycles ('reported, never judged') and `dec:views-are-projections` already says every view is a projection, so this adds a surface rather than a concept. FIVE STANDARD PROJECTIONS, each already exercised by hand on 2026-08-10: golden thread (SATISFIES+REALIZES+VERIFIES+ALLOCATED_TO), reasoning (GOVERNED_BY+OBSOLETES+CAUSES+ANTICIPATES), the plan (PRECEDES+SCHEDULED_FOR), structure (the existing DEPENDS_ON + contract-derived set, unchanged), and risk (RISKS+BLOCKS+CONTRADICTS+VIOLATES+MASKS). THE EXCLUSION LIST IS PART OF THE PROJECTION, NOT A CAVEAT. `structure.rs` already excludes review records and `heal.rs` already names ARTIFACT_BOOKKEEPING (INCLUDES, CHANGED, YIELDED, AT_EPOCH). Those exclusions exist as private constants inside detectors; a projection surface has to lift them into the projection definition or every general run gives a confident wrong answer. MEASUREMENT AND JUDGEMENT STAY SEPARATE. A battery result is a reading. A finding becomes a DEFECT only where somebody has decided what that finding MEANS for that projection — a cycle in DEPENDS_ON is a defect, a cycle in CAUSES+OBSOLETES turned out to be an ordinary time sequence. WHAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT PROPOSED: running every algorithm over every edge type and raising what it finds. That is the naive reading of 'run it on all edges' and it fails twice over — once on exclusions, once on meaning.		Anthony asked for this to be captured after measuring the coverage gap himself in conversation — his assumption that the ops are edge-agnostic was right, and the measurement confirmed the wiring is what limits them. Recorded as `proposed` with him as approver rather than accepted, because the shape has three unsettled sub-questions and because the last time this project shipped a broadly-firing structural detector it cost a cut-back (BL-42). The counter-argument is therefore recorded INSIDE the decision rather than left for a reviewer to supply. The evidence deliberately includes the failed first run. A proposal for a general analysis surface that did not mention that its own first trial returned garbage would be arguing from the successful half of one experiment.acceptednothing
PROPOSED — when provenance ties, the merge survivor is the node whose deletion destroys less, and a genuine tie refuses instead of picking
PROPOSED RESOLUTION of the standing contradiction between `dec:merge-survivor-provenance` and the two facts that contradict it (`fact:apply-heal-would-have-destroyed-the-wrong-contributor`, `fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status`). AWAITING ANTHONY'S WORD — recorded at `proposed` with him as approver, so the loop reports it as owed rather than letting it read as settled. DO NOT RE-OPEN THE PROVENANCE RANKING. It is correct and it is not what fails. The failure is entirely in the TIEBREAK beneath it: provenance ranks authored > planned > imported > reconciled > inferred > healed, and in practice both sides of a real collision are hand-authored, so the rank TIES and `a <= b` on the node id decides. Twice observed, twice choosing the worse node — `req:backend_as_product` (medium, accepted) over `req:graph_is_the_content_bible` (critical, proposed) at dev_storyflow 2026-08-08, and `ctr:anthony` (8 edges, no description) over `who:ajs` (161 edges, full description) here on 2026-08-09. THE ARGUMENT THAT UNBLOCKS THIS, and it is the whole point of the node: DEGREE IS NOT A POLICY. The reason the rule was deliberately left alone is recorded in `fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status`: ranking priority above status, or the reverse, asserts a claim about what matters more in a design, and `dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement` says reflow2 must not default that — it is the user's. THAT REASONING IS SOUND AND IS NOT BEING OVERTURNED. But 'destroy fewer edges' is not a claim about what design content matters; it is a property of the MERGE OPERATION. And the thing it would replace — alphabetical id order — is arbitrary by construction. Substituting a non-arbitrary tiebreak for an arbitrary one asserts no policy at all, which is exactly why this can be done while the priority/status question stays the user's. FOUR PARTS, SMALLEST FIRST. (1) WHERE PROVENANCE TIES, BREAK BY DEGREE — keep the node whose deletion destroys less of the design. Degree is already computed and 161 against 8 is not close. (2) WHERE DEGREE ALSO TIES, REFUSE RATHER THAN PICK. A merge that genuinely cannot distinguish should ask. `dec:ask-not-repair` already holds this shape for the suspicion half; this extends it to the survivor half. A refusal that names both candidates is strictly more useful than a coin toss that names neither. (3) KEEP PRIORITY AND STATUS OUT OF THE RULE, PUT THEM IN THE DISCLOSURE. 'You are deleting a critical, still-unconfirmed node in favour of a medium, accepted one' is INFORMATION, not a policy, and the machinery to say it already exists — `chg:a-merge-proposal-discloses-what-it-would-destroy` built `would_destroy` and the alphabet-chose-the-victim line in August. This adds a sentence to an existing disclosure rather than a rule to an existing ranking. (4) THE SCORING HALF IS SEPARATE AND PROBABLY WORTH MORE. Similarity is prose-only, unweighted by shared referents, which is what let two requirements sharing no requirement, surface or actor score 81-85. Fixing the survivor rule makes a bad merge less destructive; fixing scoring stops the pair reaching a merge at all. Recorded here so the two halves are not confused, NOT claimed by this decision. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated because the defect count will not move and somebody will look for it: recording this does not clear `heal:0fc0362a90ff913b` or `heal:7456a4d260ca45ce`. The contradiction detector fires on every CONTRADICTS edge whose alignment is not `supporting` and NEVER LOOKS FOR A RESOLVING DECISION, despite its own doc comment and its `suggested_fix_type: generate_decision` saying otherwise. The honest closure path is that when the tiebreak actually changes, the two facts become historical observations about the OLD rule and their CONTRADICTS edges should be retired as part of that change — not silenced now. EVIDENCE GAP, stated rather than papered over: degree is KNOWN to decide the contributor case correctly (161 v 8). Whether it separates dev_storyflow's pair is UNVERIFIED — that is their graph and it was not read. If their two nodes have similar degree, part (1) helps less than this decision implies and part (4) carries more of the weight.		Written at Anthony's request on 2026-08-10 after he asked for the merge-survivor pair in plain English and then for the recommendation to be recorded. The recommendation is mine; the decision is his to make, which is why this is `proposed` with an approver edge rather than accepted. The load-bearing move is separating the tiebreak from the ranking. Reading `fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status` first is what made that possible — it states plainly that the rule was NOT re-opened on purpose, and names the principle. Without that, the obvious proposal is 'consult priority and status', which walks straight into the judgement reflow2 refuses to default and would have been rejected for a good reason. The finding that the blocked path and the open path are different paths came from reading why it was blocked. Deliberately does not claim the scoring half, and deliberately records the unverified half of its own evidence.acceptednothing
The kit may report its own adoption, because adoption never reaches the debt computation — and a test holds that line rather than a promise
The distinction req:skill-adherence-is-measured offered is REAL, and it is drawn here: dec:loop-status-state-not-history governs what the LOOP may reason from when it computes debt, and adoption data may never enter that computation. It does not forbid the KIT reporting a fact about itself. Three things make the line enforceable rather than promised: (1) adoption is counted in SESSION state — the hook's per-session tally file — and in transcripts read offline, never in the design graph, so it is not graph state and cannot be reasoned from as if it were; (2) no adoption field is read by loop_status, detect_gaps or detect_defects; (3) a check asserts that the loop's answer is UNCHANGED whether or not adoption data exists, which is what converts the separation from a convention into a property. The test to apply to any future addition: does this measurement ever change what the loop says is owed? If yes, it is forbidden regardless of what it is called.		WHY THE DISTINCTION IS NOT A RATIONALISATION, which is what the requirement asked to be settled. dec:loop-status-state-not-history exists to protect ONE thing: the answer to 'what does this design still need?' must not depend on who did what. If debt read run history, two identical designs would owe different things because their session logs differ, and the design would stop being the single source of truth. That is the harm, and it is specific. Adoption answers a different question, for a different reader, with a different consequence — 'is the TOOL being used as intended?', read by the maintainer, changing the TOOL. It never touches the protected answer. So the distinction is not 'a different name for the same thing'; it is a different question that happens to be answered from the same kind of evidence, and the decision constrains the QUESTION rather than the evidence. THE PRECEDENT ALREADY EXISTS AND WAS FOUND RATHER THAN INVENTED. tools/surface_usage.py has done exactly this since 2026-08-01: it reads session transcripts offline, counts get_skill calls among them, and states in its own module docstring that it 'writes nothing back into any design — 'looking is not writing' (dec:loop-status-state-not-history). Nothing here becomes graph state.' So the shape this decision blesses was already shipping and already reasoned; what was missing was the ruling that makes it deliberate rather than incidental, and a place for the near-real-time half. WHAT IS ACTUALLY BUILT UNDER IT, and why it is small. The measurement half largely existed. The hole named by chg:undefer-skill-adherence-measurement is different and narrower: cap:skill-triggers recognises SHAPES, every shape it knows is a shape in the graph-write stream, and 'no skill has been loaded' is not a graph write — so the one situation the user kept having to correct by hand was the one situation the mechanism structurally could not see. Counting get_skill per session closes that, and it is session state by nature. THE COST THIS ACCEPTS, stated because the file it lands in resists exactly this. A new arming branch is a NEW interruption, and ver:skill-triggers' own counterweight says a trigger that fires on correct work is the failure BL-23 and BL-42 both name. So the branch is placed LAST, after every other Stop branch has declined, and is conjoined tightly: the session must have TOUCHED reflow2 (a total bypass is already caught upstream), must have edited at least the bypass threshold of files (so a trivial or read-only session is silent), and must have loaded ZERO skills. It therefore fires only on the session that did everything else right and still never opened a skill — which is precisely the case a human had to catch, twice, by asking. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. This measures LOADING, not FOLLOWING. An agent can call get_skill and ignore every word of it, and nothing here would know. Adherence in the strong sense stays unmeasured, and the requirement's name should not be read as claiming otherwise. The honest claim is that not-loading is now visible where it was invisible. BOUNDARY CARRIED FORWARD from the requirement, unchanged: whatever is reported respects report-friction's redaction discipline — tool names and argument SHAPES, node TYPES not ids, counts not contents — because reflow2 installs into other people's projects and the thing being measured is the user, not their design. Approved by Anthony 2026-08-07 ('yes, build it') against the recommendation as stated, after he asked for the question in plain terms. The prior 'yes, build it' of 2026-08-06 un-deferred the requirement; this settles the precondition it carried.acceptedA session that never opened a skill is visible, and says so before it ends
Seats coordinate by announcement and provable order, never by exclusion
Take a claim when you need one and start — but publish it by pushing it, every time, not only when contested; a claim nobody can see is not a claim. When two claims cross, the winner is whichever landed first in git history, and both parties can verify that independently. Rejected: a coordination service or lock manager (contradicts dec:multi-writer-architecture, and single-writer exclusion is the observed failure), and asking before every claim (the fleet measured that timidity starves the pool).		The StoryFlow fleet runs 15+ concurrent seats on exactly this rule — grab-and-go, announce always, crossings settled 'first-on-disk, both provable'. reflow2 has better material for the provable half than a markdown timestamp: a content-hash chain and git order. The alternative people reach for by reflex is a lock, and a lock is exactly what took five of six sessions offline on 2026-07-25.acceptedA claim names the session that made it, and a claim nobody is working says so, Claim a region of the design so two people do not collide in it, Refuse to write a design over work the shared record already holds, A seat learns the shared design moved before it writes over it
The agent navigates content; the graph records where it landed — an opaque locator reflow2 never parses
DECIDED by Anthony 2026-07-31, closing the pointer-granularity question under `cap:content-store` before anything is built. reflow2 BUILDS NO RETRIEVAL LAYER. No span vocabulary, no chunk-addressing scheme, no offsets in the schema, no search into blobs. Reading a 1000-page document and finding the relevant passage is the AGENT's job, and an agent already does it well. WHY THIS IS DOCTRINE RATHER THAN A SHORTCUT. It is the division of labour reflow2 already has, applied to a new component. `dec:three-party-checks`: 'The LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides.' Navigating content is squarely the first of those. The precedent is consistent across the system — reflow2 performs NO FILE I/O, and `coverage_report` and `reconcile_artifacts` take what the agent observed rather than scanning; `dec:corpus-ingest-mechanism` makes extraction itself the agent's job through the SP-3b handshake. Adding a blob changes where bytes live, not who reads them. THE ONE PART THAT IS NOT THE AGENT'S JOB, and it is the whole reason this decision is not simply 'do nothing': NAVIGATING is the agent's, RECORDING WHERE IT LANDED is the graph's. If an agent reads a corpus, extracts a requirement, and the graph stores only 'this came from that document', then auditing that requirement later means RE-RUNNING A NON-DETERMINISTIC SEARCH — and a different agent may land elsewhere and reach a different conclusion. The design would hold a provenance link that does not reproduce, which is a link that cannot do the one job provenance has. THE MECHANISM IS A CONVENTION, NOT A FEATURE. `Fragment.content_ref` already exists and is already declared as 'pointer to the source content (path/hash)' — an opaque string. The agent writes whatever locator suits the medium alongside the content hash: a line range for markdown, a page for a PDF, a timestamp for a transcript, a cell for a spreadsheet. reflow2 STORES IT, RETURNS IT, AND NEVER INTERPRETS IT — no parsing, no validation of the locator's shape, no computation over it. The next agent knows what to do with it because it is the same kind of agent that wrote it. Zero new vocabulary, zero new code, and the audit trail reproduces. A CORRECTION ON THE RECORD, because the argument that nearly went the other way was wrong. It was argued that spans go stale when a document is edited, and that content-addressed chunks were therefore safer. That objection assumed MUTABLE FILES, which `dec:where-content-lives` had already ruled out: blobs are content-addressed and immutable, so an edited document is a DIFFERENT HASH rather than the same one with shifted lines. A locator into a content-addressed blob cannot rot. The staleness case was smuggling in an assumption the storage decision had already removed. PRIOR ART CHECKED, so nobody reviews it again. The official MCP memory server (`modelcontextprotocol/servers/src/memory`) was read on Anthony's prompt. Its model is entities / relations / observations in a JSONL file, eight tools, substring search. IT OFFERS NOTHING ON THIS QUESTION because it never meets it — no chunking, no external pointers, no spans, no large content; everything is short atomic strings held inline. What it DOES corroborate is the deeper answer: its stated rule is 'observations should be atomic — one fact per observation', i.e. decompose at WRITE time so there is never a large thing to search at READ time. That is the same conclusion `cap:session-memory` reached independently ('a pointer to a 3 MB transcript is a RECEIPT, not documentation'). EXPLICITLY NOT IMPORTED: `read_graph` returning the entire graph (at 1000+ nodes it would swamp a context window; `cap:bounded-reads` is better and exists for this reason); untyped free-string entity types (the typed schema is what makes detectors computable at all); and delete-without-history, which is what `req:intent-preserved` forbids and `retire-from-design` exists to prevent.		Anthony's framing, and it is sharper than 'do not reinvent the wheel': the capability already exists in the system, it just does not live in reflow2. An agent that can be told to review a thousand pages does not need reflow2 to teach it how. THE METHOD FINDING, which is the second instance today and therefore a pattern rather than a coincidence. Two design forks were recorded, both with genuine options and real trade-offs, and BOTH DISSOLVED WHEN SOMETHING OUTSIDE THE DESIGN WAS CHECKED rather than chosen between. `dec:where-content-lives` collapsed once `object_store` turned the storage backend into runtime configuration; this one collapsed once the agent's own capabilities were counted as part of the system. In both cases the recorded options were honest and the deliberation was not wasted — it is what made the dissolution recognisable. The habit worth keeping: before choosing between branches of a fork, ask what already exists that would make the fork unnecessary. Design inward only after looking outward. Left as a convention deliberately rather than a validated field, because validating a locator's shape would mean reflow2 deciding what media exist — and the moment someone stores something nobody anticipated, a validator becomes a refusal of correct work. An opaque string costs nothing and forecloses nothing.acceptedStore bytes beside the design and point at them by content hash
An aggregate gap is keyed on its rule; every other gap still keys on its subject
`gap_id` keys a gap on its RULE alone when the gap is an AGGREGATE — one per project, whose `affected_ids` are the whole population the rule ranges over rather than the nodes the finding is about. Every other gap keeps hashing its affected set. Today exactly one source qualifies: `unvalidated_capability`. The discriminator is an explicit `GapSource::is_aggregate()` written as an exhaustive match, not a wildcard, so a future aggregate detector has to come to this function and decide rather than silently inheriting per-node keying. NOT KEYED ON `GapScope::Project`, which is the obvious-looking answer and is wrong. `unsatisfied_requirement` and `status_contradiction` are project-SCOPED but carry a single requirement each, and `kpp_breached` is per-KPP. Keying on scope would collapse every unsatisfied requirement in the design into one gap sharing one judgement — accept one and the rest go silent. A test pins this specific trap (`a_project_scoped_but_per_node_gap_still_keys_on_its_subject`) and a mutation confirms it fails when the trap is taken. Also NOT chosen: (b) expiring only when a member is removed, which keeps the id unstable and merely narrows when it moves; (c) letting each acknowledgement declare its own expiry condition, which is more machinery than the problem needs and puts the judgement about mechanism into every reason string; (d) modelling rollups as a different KIND of gap, which is a schema change for something the id function can express.		Anthony's word, 2026-07-30: he was told the finding had a close sibling in the defect-side mechanism and said that was a good approach. WORTH RECORDING PRECISELY, because the reading that prompted this was half wrong. The sibling was described as 'defect acknowledgements expire by shape, and this is the gap side catching up'. Reading the code showed `heal.rs`'s `issue_id(category, affected)` hashes its affected set exactly as `gap_id` does — the defect side has no cleverer keying. What it actually has is the `retired` REPORTING that `reviewed_gaps` already implements too. So mirroring the sibling alone would not have fixed anything: the churn comes from the id derivation, and the fix had to be there. The sibling still earns its place, because `retired` reporting is what makes a stable id safe — when the rule stops firing the standing review is shown as retired rather than silently kept. THE TRADE-OFF IS REAL AND ACCEPTED. A stable id means a capability added later is covered by the earlier judgement without a fresh look. That is what a STANDING disposition means — 'validation is tracked in the trials programme' is a claim about the practice, not about any one capability — and it is what the twenty re-acknowledgements were each re-asserting unchanged. The growth stays visible without the churn: a review records the count it was made at in its own reason, and the live gap's title carries the count now, so a reader comparing them sees the set grew. THE MIGRATION IS DELIBERATE AND VISIBLE. The rollup's id moves once, from the member-hashed `gap:80f8bc457bfe9e16` to the stable `gap:0a77650b58242054`, so the twenty historical acknowledgements no longer match it and one fresh acknowledgement is needed — the last one this gap should ever need. Those twenty are left exactly as they are rather than withdrawn: withdrawal marks a Decision `superseded`, which would claim the judgement was revoked, and it was not. `reviewed_gaps` reports them as `retired` instead, which is the honest description — the judgement was real and the situation it named has moved on.acceptedA gap about the whole population is keyed on its rule, so a standing judgement carries, An acknowledgement of a set-scoped gap must not expire merely because the design grew
Alternatives are unranked forkable siblings; the human judges in hindsight, not a stored score
EPIGRAPH — 'Two roads diverged in a wood, and I— / I took the one less traveled by, / And that has made all the difference.' — Robert Frost, 'The Road Not Taken'. Aptly, the poem is itself a hindsight tale: the speaker concedes the two roads were worn 'really about the same' and foresees telling it 'with a sigh' ages hence — the difference is authored in retrospect, not known at the fork. That is this decision's whole bet: credit for a road taken is assigned in hindsight, by the human, never scored in advance. (Unofficially, 'the Robert Frost decision.') reflow2 holds every Decision's alternatives as UNRANKED, forkable siblings — not a scored trade-study runner-up. The design is modelled as a navigable decision-MDP: the graph is the world-model (propagate/detect/compare evaluate a fork's consequences before anything is built), branches are the replay, and the reward signal is two-channel — the structural detectors (in-model holes: SPOFs, cycles, gaps) plus field trials (out-of-model holes only a real episode reveals, e.g. BL-74's loop-on-virtue collapse). Alternatives are stored cheaply (the unchosen option + its rationale, at the decision's epoch) and their consequence design is COMPUTED on demand by forking that epoch and replaying — never eagerly maintained as N full parallel designs, which would combinatorially explode and rot as the main line moves on (a non-stationary design). Which fork to expand is chosen by where the surprise is — a fresh defect, a failed trial, or a rationale that already flags doubt points back to a decision (high 'TD error') — not by enumerating the whole tree. Crucially the human is the reward function and does the credit assignment and policy update; reflow2 supplies the replay buffer and the world-model but never auto-optimizes a design by replay-and-score.		User decided the ranked-vs-unranked scope 2026-07-22 after developing the idea across three framings — choose-your-own-adventure (the decision tree you can turn back to), Analysis of Alternatives (the runner-up kept live), and a reinforcement-learning gridworld (replay an episode until you cross without falling in a hole). Unranked over a scored AoA because reflow2 routes judgment to the human (dec:report-dont-judge, dec:three-party-checks): a stored ranking would be the system asserting a preference it cannot honestly hold, and design episodes are too few, too expensive and too subjective for a stationary reward anyway. Derived-over-stored (store the fork, compute the consequence) is reflow2's recurring lesson (dec:certainty-derived, dec:component-verified-computed) and the only defence against an eagerly-maintained alternative rotting under a moving main line. Model-based-planning-not-model-free-crashing is the whole point of a design brain: propagate_change computes the blast radius before you edit, so you simulate the hole instead of falling in it — but BL-74 proves some holes are out-of-model and only a field episode finds them. This unifies the branch (BL-70), merge (dec:merge-three-way / dec:merge-conflict-semantics — how a forked road comes home) and claims (BL-44) threads under one primitive: alternatives as first-class, forkable, comparable, mergeable. The hindsight pass that motivated it is the mechanism already working by hand — dec:merge-survivor-provenance carries a 'reconsider' note tracing a near-bad merge back to its own fork. Deferred to their own decisions: how an alternative attaches to a Decision in the schema, the fork/branch ref layer (BL-70), the 'when has an episode taught us enough to revise' trigger, and the tool surface.acceptedHold and re-fork a decision's unchosen alternatives
When unplanned work takes a version number, every planned increment slips up one rather than being re-scoped or squeezed in
ACCEPTED on Anthony's word, 2026-08-08: 'when we add in unplanned change to a version, we should just slip the other versions up one to accommodate (what was scheduled for v0.25.0 gets pushed to v0.26.0 and what was scheduled for v0.26.0 gets automatically pushed to v0.27.0 and so on).' The planned increment is NOT re-scoped to make room, and the unplanned work is NOT held back to protect the number: the number moves and the plan travels with it, intact. APPLIED IMMEDIATELY to the v0.25.0 cut, which shipped the storyflow HEAL disclosure fixes rather than the READ half epoch:v0250-planned was scoped for. WHAT THIS SETTLES that was otherwise decided ad hoc each time: an unplanned cut has three possible responses — rename the planned increment's contents into the new number (which silently redefines what was agreed), drop items to fit (which asserts a withdrawal nobody made), or slip. Slipping is the only one that changes no promise, and it means a plan's CONTENT is stable while its DATE is not — which is what req:plans-move-honestly already says about confidence decaying with horizon. WHAT IT COSTS, and it is worth stating: every slip renames four or more planned epochs, and the version number is currently baked into their IDs (epoch:v0250-planned), which cannot be renamed. So the routine act this decision makes routine is the one the current id scheme handles worst — see dec:idea-a-planned-increment-is-named-by-content-not-by-number.		Recorded because it was decided in conversation and would otherwise be re-derived at every cut, which is the failure this project exists to prevent. The immediate trigger: v0.25.0 shipped unplanned work, and I stopped mid-cut rather than assume what should happen to the planned increment — the answer was a policy, not a one-off. Anthony's phrasing makes it automatic ('and so on'), so it is a rule a session can apply without asking again.acceptedRETIRED 2026-08-08 — superseded by epoch:planned-read-half. Kept, not deleted, because it holds the plan's snapshot history — dec:arrival-delta reads plan movement from a target's FIRST snapshot, and deleting the node would delete the trail. The content lives on at epoch:planned-read-half under dec:idea-a-planned-increment-is-named-by-content-not-by-number., RETIRED 2026-08-08 — superseded by epoch:planned-status-accounting. OPEN — the Anchor node type is superseded by Snapshot but still advertised: retire it or implement it?
UNDECIDED, recorded 2026-07-28. schema/structure.yaml:108 declares an Anchor node type with design_intent, key_decisions, checksum and created_at. Nothing in the core creates it, nothing reads it, there is no node::ANCHOR constant, and reflow2's own design contains ZERO instances. It was superseded: temporal.rs:62 describes Snapshot as 'a checksummed baseline (generalizes the P2 to P3 Anchor)', and Snapshot has 14 live instances while DriftEvent has 37. THE PART THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN TIDYING: the schema still advertises the type, and does so from BOTH SIDES of a relationship that cannot exist. (1) describe_schema returns Anchor to any agent asking what the vocabulary contains, serving this hint with it — 'A checksummed baseline of the design taken when leaving P2 for a build round (P3). Not extracted from prose — created by the workflow at the structure to build transition. DriftEvents reference the Anchor they diverged from.' (2) AMENDED 2026-07-28, reviewing resync_protocol.json and phase_transitions.json: DriftEvent's OWN extraction_hint (schema/verify.yaml:63) makes the matching claim from the other end — 'A recorded divergence between the design (graph/Anchor) and reality (filesystem/build). Produced by drift detection, not extracted from prose. References the Anchor it diverged from via DEPENDS_ON.' No DriftEvent references an Anchor, because none exists; all 37 reference something else. So the vocabulary describes a DEPENDS_ON relationship between two types in both directions, and that relationship has zero instances and no code path that could create one. An agent reading either hint and following it creates a node nothing will ever read, and believes it has anchored a build round. Three options. (a) RETIRE the type from the schema, which is the honest reading if Snapshot fully covers it — but removing a node type strands any graph that already carries one, the same objection that kept `review` and `simulation` in Verification.method when the taxonomy grew. (b) IMPLEMENT it, if the P2-to-P3 anchoring semantics are meant to survive as something distinct from a general Snapshot. (c) REDIRECT — keep the name as an alias or documented synonym of Snapshot so old graphs still load, while the discovery surface stops advertising it as a separate thing to create. Whichever is chosen, TWO hints must move with it, not one — that is what the amendment adds. And the question underneath is the same one dec:one-retire-edge asks about edges: what should CONSULT the retirement, and does a retired vocabulary item stop being offered or get offered with a warning?		Found 2026-07-28 reviewing the original reflow's workflow_master.json, whose architecture_anchor is the mechanism this type was modelled on. Recorded rather than fixed because all three options are defensible and the choice is Anthony's — it is a vocabulary call, and those have been his every time. Note the shape it shares with the other findings from this review: a schema declaring something no computation reaches (req:functional-vocabulary-computes), a default asserting a choice nobody made (req:defaults-do-not-assert, req:edge-defaults-do-not-assert), and now a whole TYPE advertised on the discovery surface after being superseded. This is the same defect at node-type granularity, which is the level the earlier sweeps did not examine — they measured properties, not types.proposedDesign intent is read back into a long build, not only the debt the loop is owed
