(5) CLAIMS AGAINST REAL DATA — claim_report overlaps computed against open PRs' changed files rather than announcements, and dec:advisory-concurrency's 'first-on-disk, both provable' has an exact GitHub expression in which PR opened first. (6) RELEASE NOTES DERIVED from the graph — delivered requirements and the decisions in that epoch, cut and attached by github-mcp. THE OBJECTIONS, recorded beside the ideas. Context cost is real: reflow2 serves 106 tools and github-mcp is comparably large, so an agent holding both pays in tool-selection noise — both have an answer (find_tools, and GitHub's toolsets/dynamic discovery, noted in docs/github-mcp-nuggets.md) and neither answer is free. And the load-bearing one: reflow2's proposition is that it works with no service and no account. Any pairing must be ADDITIVE AND NEVER REQUIRED, or reflow2 excludes GitLab, self-hosted, air-gapped and classified environments — which is the population this tool was built for.		Raised as brainstorming while looking at how two people collaborate over plain git, so nothing here is scheduled and nothing is promoted. Kept as ONE decision rather than six because the pairings are a menu under a single question — whether reflow2 reaches for a second MCP surface at all — and answering that decides the shape of every item. Worth recording rather than leaving in conversation because two of the six touch decisions already on the record: (1) bears directly on dec:central-host, where the publishing case is named as the strongest argument for hosting a server, and GitHub-as-distribution would weaken that argument without any hosting at all; (2) bears on req:nudge-path-proven, which is accepted work about a notification path reflow2 cannot currently prove reaches anybody. The architectural observation is the part most likely to be forgotten and re-derived: MCP integration happens in the agent's context, not in either server's code, so the whole idea is skill-shaped and reversible — which is also why it can be tried cheaply on one pairing before deciding anything.proposednothing
Governance and management stay in reflow2 and get properly integrated — the weak connection is catch-up debt from a late addition, not a boundary asking to be drawn
DECIDED — Anthony, 2026-08-09, answering dec:idea-governance-management-split: 'my decision is not to split governance/management out from reflow2, but integrate it properly into reflow2.' Governance and management stay inside reflow2. No sister package, no second binary, no separate vocabulary. The work that follows is INTEGRATION work. ANTHONY'S DIAGNOSIS, and it is the part that changes what happens next: 'it is kind of the late addition, so that is probably why it isn't very well connected/integrated into reflow2 — so we're playing a little bit of catch up.' This reclassifies the evidence rather than dismissing it. Every observation that looked like a case for splitting is re-read as arrears owed by a late arrival: - DesignRule being 'the least-connected type in the schema, which is odd for the one whose whole job is to bind other things' (storyflow trial case, 2026-08-09) is not a sign the type belongs elsewhere. It is a sign the type was added after the edges were drawn. - dec:bl-155's finding that ~17 of the 40 never-called tools are the management/governance/coordination family is not evidence of an unwanted surface. BL-155's own conclusion already said these tools are UNREACHABLE FROM ANY SKILL rather than unwanted, and a late addition is exactly what fails to get wired into the skills that would name it. - reflow2's eight functional systems (dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition) containing no management or governance system is, on this reading, the same debt stated structurally: the decomposition was drawn before the concern arrived and was never revised to hold it. WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A PREFERENCE: it settles what to do with every future governance finding. The question stops being 'does this belong here?' and becomes 'what is it not yet connected to?' — which is answerable from the graph, unlike the first. WHAT IT DOES NOT DECIDE: it does not say governance vocabulary must be mandatory for every project, and it does not rule out the optional-profile shape (option C of the brainstorm) as an INTERNAL organising idea. It rules out the PACKAGE split only. It also does not say the integration is small — the storyflow fleet sized the missing primitives as 'a small declarative field plus a report — not a subsystem', and that estimate is theirs, not confirmed here. CONSISTENT WITH the accepted requirements the split would have cost: req:thin-install and req:no-setup-per-project both survive untouched, which they would not have under a second package. And with proj:reflow2's objective, 'keep a design coherent from concept through operations', which names the whole lifecycle as scope rather than design alone. SUPERSEDES dec:idea-governance-management-split, which stays on the record with all four options so the roads not taken remain visible.		Anthony's word, given directly on 2026-08-09 after the brainstorm was put to him. The reasoning worth preserving is his causal one: governance arrived late, so its poor integration is chronology rather than architecture — which means the fix is wiring, not relocation. Recorded because a later session finding governance badly connected would otherwise be entitled to re-open the split question, and this says it was asked and answered.acceptedGovernance becomes expressible — the four missing primitives and a ledger that can say a record was wrong, grouped so one stamp move pays for all five, A cluster can be declared deliberately separate, so disconnected_community reports undeclared islands instead of one permanent warning, A Decision can state what it binds, and an unstated scope is visible rather than inferred, A node can declare who may change it, so 'what may I change alone?' is answerable from the graph rather than from prose, A rule knows where it is authoritatively stated and where else it is repeated, so an amendment can find its own stale copies, A rule says whether a check is even possible, so 'no detector' splits into debt and accepted limit
The graph handle is an accepted single point of failure
cmp:graph is the single store handle everything else hangs off, and it stays that way. The single_point_of_failure warning on it is accepted as intentional, not resolved by adding redundancy.		The architecture is explicit (AGENTS.md): DesignGraph is 'the single handle everything else hangs off' — one schema-validated CRUD surface so every coherence-loop module speaks to one store one way. Removing it strands schema, search and vocabulary (each with its file) plus the export chain, which is the BL-69 detector telling the truth about the spine. Redundancy is incoherent here twice over: these are modules compiled into one binary (they cannot fail independently of cmp:graph at run time — the same reasoning as the F6 library filter, which cannot see cmp:graph only because it provides no Interface node), and a second graph handle would mean two write paths to one store, exactly the incoherence the single handle exists to prevent. Accepted 2026-07-21 while dispositioning BL-69's corrected findings; sibling of dec:service-spof-accepted.acceptedgraph
OPEN — is a session pointed at a design by editing .mcp.json and reconnecting, or by a graph reference carried per call?
RECORDED AS THE SHAPE QUESTION UNDER `req:a-session-chooses-its-design`. Anthony 2026-08-05 stated a preference — 'I like this approach of just pointing .mcp.json at the graph_id' — which is a lean toward (a), not a settlement, because the trade-off below was not in front of him when he said it. (a) EDIT `.mcp.json` AND RECONNECT. WORKS TODAY WITH ZERO CODE: `--graph-path` is an ordinary argument and accepts an absolute path, so any project's server can be pointed at any store right now. The agent can make the edit — Anthony's own point, 'an agent within a session can usually change files'. Counter: it costs a `/mcp` reconnect, and reconnecting is a step this project has already recorded as the one an autonomous agent CANNOT take ((BL-123)). So the cheap option's cost falls exactly on the case reflow2 most wants to serve. (b) A GRAPH REFERENCE CARRIED PER CALL (the field report's 2a). No reconnect; a session could even read one design and write another. Counter, and it is the strong one: this project already faced the identical shape for seats and went the other way — `dec:stateless-seat-handle` REFUSES a claim without a seat rather than guessing one, because a handle that changes under you is worse than one you must supply. A defaulted graph reference is that hazard with worse consequences: getting a seat wrong misattributes a claim, getting a graph wrong WRITES TO THE WRONG DESIGN, which is the very accident this whole thread began with. ⭐ THE RULE THAT SHOULD SURVIVE WHICHEVER IS CHOSEN, and it is the contribution rather than the choice: DEFAULT WHEN EXACTLY ONE DESIGN IS REACHABLE; REFUSE AND LIST THEM WHEN SEVERAL ARE. That is `dec:no-design-here-never-looked` option (a) and this node's option (b) doing one job at two moments — discovery before creating, refusal before writing. A design chosen by silence is how three graphs appeared on one repo. THE DISCOVERY HALF, WHICH BOTH OPTIONS NEED AND NEITHER PROVIDES. Anthony asked for 'a reflow2 tool to simply return all graph_ids'. MEASURED: that returns ONE PER STORE today — reflow2 opens one graph per store by convention, and his three graphs are three stores. The foundation does support many graphs per store (`{graph_id}\x00{type}\x00{id}`, `keys::graph_prefix`), so the enumeration is real but answers a question nobody currently has. THE USEFUL SHAPE IS THE OTHER ONE: a tool that DESCRIBES THE DESIGN AT A GIVEN PATH — graph id, label, node counts, mint stamp — without binding to it, so an agent that has walked the tree can show the user a menu. Splits cleanly along `dec:agent-navigates-content`: the agent finds the directories, reflow2 says what is in them. ⚠️ THE COMPLICATION NOBODY HAS SOLVED, and it bites (a) and the discovery tool equally: a RocksDB store held by a running server is EXCLUSIVELY LOCKED. Describing a design at a path while another session holds it needs a shared or read-only open. `--shared` exists and this repo's own `.mcp.json` does not pass it, which is separately why the stale-server export replay is needed at every release cut. Any answer here should say what happens when the store is busy rather than discovering it in the field. NOT CHECKED: whether `design_identity` could take an optional path and answer for a store it is not bound to, which would make the discovery half a parameter rather than a new tool.		Kept as a question despite Anthony stating a preference, because the preference was expressed before the reconnect cost was named — and (BL-123) already records that the `/mcp` reconnect is the one step an autonomous agent cannot take, which is a direct argument against the option he leaned toward. Recording his lean AND the counter is what the brainstorm discipline is for; deciding it on the lean alone would be reading agreement into an answer given without the trade-off. The default-when-one, refuse-when-several rule is written as the thing that should survive either choice, because it is the part that actually prevents the observed accident and it is independent of the mechanism. The locking complication is stated because it is the kind of constraint that turns a small tool into a medium one, and it is already known to this project from a different direction.proposedA session names the design it wants by graph_id, and the server maps id to path, DECIDED in the field — a session is pointed at a design by a PROJECT-SCOPED config override, and an absolute path must never enter a global config
A fact may carry its date as a property — the edge stays the truth when there is an epoch, and the property is read when there is not
SETTLED (a) ON ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-16. `valid_from` and `valid_to` become DECLARED date-string properties on TemporalFact, and the readers prefer the `VALID_FROM` / `VALID_TO` EDGE where one exists and fall back to the property where one does not. The edge remains the richer statement; the property stops being a silent no-op.		MEASURED FIRST, DECIDED SECOND. 112 of 205 TemporalFacts carried a `valid_from` PROPERTY the schema did not declare and no code read; 76 carried the declared EDGE to a DesignEpoch; ZERO carried both; 17 carried neither. Full measurement in `fact:defect-half-the-temporal-facts-date-themselves-where-nothing-reads`. ⭐ THE ZERO OVERLAP IS WHAT DECIDED IT. Two populations with two conventions and no node caught between them is not sloppiness — sloppiness would be mixed. It is a MISSING WORD: `VALID_FROM` demands a DesignEpoch, and a writer holding a plain date has nothing to point it at. Everyone who had an epoch used the edge; everyone who had a date invented a property. The corpus was telling the schema what the schema was missing. WHY (b) LOST — keep the edge as the only truth and migrate the 112. It needs 112 DesignEpochs that do not exist, one per calendar date, which floods the time axis with points that mark nothing. That damages the half of the system that WORKS: the roadmap computation reads epochs, and filling that axis with calendar noise makes it worse, not better. Epochs are meant to be named moments. It also cannot fully clean up, because a property once written cannot be removed (`fact:defect-a-property-once-written-cannot-be-removed`). WHY (c) LOST — let `VALID_FROM` point at either an epoch or a date. It keeps one word for one idea, which is attractive, but nothing else in this schema has a polymorphic `to`, and the edge-endpoint guard would carry a permanent special case. A lasting complexity cost for a cosmetic win. WHY (a) SURVIVED THE `dec:edge-orthogonality` OBJECTION, which is the one that mattered. 'Two ways to say one thing' is exactly what that decision argues against — but its test is whether a COMPUTATION READS THE DISTINCTION, and here one would. 'True from this named milestone' and 'true from this date' are different claims: a roadmap wants the first, an audit trail wants the second. The distinction earns its keep. AND IT IS THE ONLY OPTION THAT DESTROYS NOTHING. 112 hand-written dates become readable immediately; nothing migrates; nothing is invented. ⚠️ A CONFLICT OF INTEREST DISCLOSED BEFORE THE RULING AND RECORDED HERE: the agent proposing this had written a share of those 112 the same day, and therefore had a mild stake in the option that says they were fine. Anthony was told this when the options were put to him and chose (a) anyway. CARRIED FORWARD, NOT PART OF THE RULING: TemporalFact's extraction_hint reads 'a satisfaction fact whose VALID_FROM is a later epoch; a dropped requirement = a fact with VALID_TO set' — phrasing that invited the property form the schema did not declare. The guidance and the schema disagreed and the guidance is what a writer reads, so it is corrected under this decision regardless of which option had won.acceptednothing
OPEN — how should reflow2 log which of its own skills and tools a session used, and where does that log live?
ANTHONY'S IDEA, 2026-08-09, close to verbatim: 'adding some type of usage-log tool that captures what reflow2 skills and tools were used in a session would be a nice utility. maybe a tool is not the right option, but something that AUTOMATICALLY logs (maybe store it in project graph?) usage and issues (DOESN'T DIAGNOSE, JUST LOGS).' ⭐ HIS OWN DOUBT IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART AND IT IS CORRECT. **A TOOL IS THE WRONG SHAPE, and self-defeatingly so: a tool must be CALLED, and the population most worth measuring is precisely the one least likely to call it.** An agent that forgets `revise-design` forgets `log_usage`. The measurement would be biased toward the sessions that need no measuring. Every MCP call already passes through the server, so the server can record without the agent's cooperation — which is the only way the number means anything. 'DOESN'T DIAGNOSE, JUST LOGS' IS ALREADY THIS PROJECT'S DOCTRINE, not a new constraint: `dec:report-dont-judge` holds that the confirmation ledger reports claim history and never judges a claim. Same shape, one domain over. --- WHERE IT LIVES: THE QUESTION HE FLAGGED --- (1) BESIDE THE STORE, NOT IN THE GRAPH — the recommendation. The graph is the DESIGN; usage is telemetry about a SESSION and belongs to the process, not to the design. Putting it in the graph means every export carries it (already 4.1 MB), every diff churns with it, and `compare_designs` reports telemetry as design divergence. `rule:per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global` draws the same line from the other side: the test is whether a second design open in the same process would need a different value, and session usage would not. PRECEDENT EXISTS AND IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — reflow2 already keeps session-scoped state beside the store rather than inside it (the shared-mode rendezvous and log; `shared.rs` pins 'log sits beside the store too' and 'rendezvous sits beside the store NOT INSIDE IT'). (2) IN THE GRAPH — what it would buy: usage becomes queryable with the same tools as everything else, and survives in the export. COUNTER: it makes the design record grow with facts that are not design, and the export is the thing consumers merge. ⭐ THE RESOLUTION THAT USES BOTH, and it is an existing pattern rather than a compromise: LOG RAW TO THE SIDECAR, PROMOTE FINDINGS DELIBERATELY. `dec:manifest-derived-is-not-manifest-accepted` already holds that a bulk derivation is not a bulk accept and writes nothing until asked. Raw usage is derivation; a finding worth keeping ('this rule was violated four times') is something a human accepts INTO the design. --- WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS --- **NOBODY HAS EVER MEASURED SKILL USAGE.** `dec:bl-155` measured TOOL calls — 6,095 across 46 retained transcripts — and found 40 of 132 tools never called. There is no equivalent for `get_skill`, which is server-side and trivially countable. So `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` proposes to improve a rate NOBODY HAS EVER OBSERVED, and without this instrument there is no way to tell whether any hint changed anything. ⚠️ AND BL-155'S CAVEAT TRAVELS WITH IT, because it is the trap: absence is WEAK evidence. `set_project_mode` appeared as text in ten transcripts with zero recorded calls despite having been used. A tool can be discussed far more than used; a skill can be FOLLOWED FROM MEMORY without being fetched, which this session did for revise-design. **So a usage log measures FETCHES, not COMPLIANCE, and reporting it as compliance would be exactly the false confidence the loop exists to prevent.** --- OPEN SUB-QUESTIONS --- - Does it log ISSUES as well as usage (his words: 'usage and issues')? A refusal is already visible to the server; recording refusals would surface the enum-rejection class of defect without anyone filing a report. - Is it opt-in? `dec:idea-measure-the-surface` already asks how far usage telemetry may go, and this is that question made concrete. - Retention. `dec:content-growth-is-bounded-by-what-not-by-size` says what bounds a store is WHAT gets stored, not how big it is. NOTHING IS PROMOTED. Recorded so the shape is chosen deliberately rather than by whoever builds it first.		Anthony's idea, with his own doubt about the tool shape carried into the record rather than smoothed away, because that doubt is the part that decides the design. Kept OPEN rather than accepted: the storage question turns on how far telemetry may go, which is already an unanswered decision (dec:idea-measure-the-surface), and answering it here by implication would settle it without him.proposedreflow2 can say which of its own skills and tools a session reached for — recorded automatically, reported without judgement
OPEN — how does a capability say its own status is under challenge, in the window between evidence arriving and someone being ready to restate it?
UNSETTLED. Reported 2026-08-08 by dev_storyflow's sb-boss: they demoted a capability from `realized` to `in_progress` after a failing walk, and between the walk and the demotion the graph went on asserting something false with no way to say so — a window that, on a `--shared` graph, every attached session reads as current. Two shapes, both theirs: (a) a lightweight `contested` marker or status value; (b) let a FAILING `kind=validation` VERIFIES edge automatically flag the capability's status as unsafe to trust. THE SECOND FITS THIS DESIGN'S GRAIN BETTER ON ITS FACE AND THAT IS WORTH STATING, THOUGH NOT DECIDING: dec:passing-is-verified already computes 'verified' from a check that PASSES rather than from a status field, so computing 'contested' from a check that FAILS is the same move inverted, needs no new enum value, and cannot be forgotten the way a marker can. The argument against it is equally real — a failing check does not always mean the claim is wrong, and auto-flagging would make every red test a challenge to the design rather than to the code.		Recorded because demoting early is itself a claim — it asserts a position on work that may turn out fine — so the absence of a middle state pushes a reporter toward one of two wrong assertions. Adjacent and worth reading together: req:blocking-is-partial applies the same instinct to drift rather than to a failing check. Evidence: fact:defect-no-way-to-mark-a-capability-contested.proposednothing
OPEN — should a capability be able to declare that it needs a human INPUT path, so that the absence of one is DETECTABLE rather than diagnosable only by three people failing?
UNSETTLED. dev_storyflow's most-wanted ask, 2026-08-08: express 'this capability needs a surface where a person (or an upstream system) actually writes the data it consumes', so a capability that is realized, built and rendering — but dead because nothing ever writes its input — is caught by a detector rather than by three people producing three wrong root causes. Shapes worth weighing rather than a recommendation: (a) a new edge — cap FED_BY ifc/Actor — with an unrealized_input_path gap when a capability that consumes a field has no writer; (b) a property on the Capability (`needs_input_path: true`) with the detector reading it, which is cheaper and weaker because nothing forces the flag; (c) generalise the existing INTERACTS_WITH by adding a `required` property, so 'an actor interacts with this' can become 'this does not function unless an actor does'; (d) decline it as out of scope, on the ground that reflow2 models the design and not the operational data path. NOTE WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH: req:the-store-is-reachable-from-a-session says 'a capability nothing can call is not delivered — the content store needs a surface', which is exactly this insight scoped to ONE capability and written by hand; nothing generalises it and nothing detects it.		Recorded because it is the one thing the fleet said would have saved the most time, and because it is a VOCABULARY question rather than a detector bug — detect_gaps structurally cannot ask about a surface the design has no way to say is required, which is req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots in its sharpest instance to date. Left `proposed` deliberately: every shape above changes the schema or the detector set, and which one is right is Anthony's call, not a field report's. The evidence is fact:defect-a-realized-capability-can-be-dead-for-want-of-an-input-path.proposednothing
SETTLED — a capture-session skill the user types, chosen as the FIRST STEP because it is the only trigger that does not depend on the mechanism that keeps failing
DECIDED 2026-08-12 by Anthony. OPTION A, knowingly and as a first step. Originally recorded as brainstorming under the question 'should closing a session be a SKILL the user types, when the accepted requirement says the user must never be the trigger?' — that question is now answered. ⭐⭐ HIS DECIDING ARGUMENT, AND IT INVERTS THE TENSION THIS NODE WAS BUILT AROUND. His words: 'I don't mind the capture-session skill being manual and I can use it as I see fit throughout a session. I would prefer it be automatically done by the agent, but as seen elsewhere, then it is dependent upon the agent remembering or placing hooks to do so... so just being able to run this manually myself as a first step is fine with me.' The node above recorded option A as CONCEDING the central clause of `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` ('the user must never be the trigger'). Anthony's reasoning reframes that: options B and C depend on THE AGENT REMEMBERING — and agent forgetting is the documented, four-times-observed failure this whole thread exists because of (`epoch:skill-use-still-needs-reminding`, `chg:user-is-still-the-reminder`, `fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11`, and his own habit). ⇒ THE MANUAL TRIGGER IS NOT THE WEAK OPTION. It is the only one whose reliability does not rest on the thing that keeps failing. A human who types a skill remembers; the mechanism proposed to replace him is the one with the measured defect rate. 📌 THE CLAUSE IS STILL CONCEDED, AND THAT IS RECORDED HONESTLY. `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` remains ACCEPTED and still says the user must never be the trigger. This decision does not amend it, does not weaken it, and does not close it. It ships a manual trigger AS A FIRST STEP while the requirement stands unmet — which is the accurate state, and better stated than papered over. ═══ WHAT THIS DECIDES ═══ A `capture-session` skill the user types, served like every other skill, invocable AT ANY POINT IN A SESSION and not only at the end — his words, 'I can use it as I see fit throughout a session'. That clause was NOT in the original option A and it matters: it directly answers counter-argument ⚠️2 ('session end is the worst moment to ask, and this session is the evidence'), because a skill usable mid-session is capture-as-you-go with a defined contract rather than a closing sweep over a compacted transcript. ═══ WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE ═══ • OPTION C REMAINS THE DESTINATION. 'First step' is his phrasing. The skill defining WHAT capture means is precisely the half C needs; a later hook deciding WHEN sits on top of it without rework. Choosing A does not foreclose C — it builds C's first half. • ⚠️1 WHO JUDGES 'ANYTHING IMPORTANT' is untouched and is the skill's hardest content problem. The skill must STATE ITS CRITERIA rather than ask an agent to introspect on the significance of its own session. • ⚠️3 THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE HAS NO NATURAL NODE — still true, still unresolved, and now load-bearing in a way it was not before: a skill that captures must write SOMETHING somewhere. `cap:session-memory` stays PLANNED. ═══ THE ROADS NOT TAKEN (kept, per brainstorm doctrine) ═══ B — automatic at the Stop hook. Not rejected; deferred. Its mechanism exists and works (it blocked this very session), but it fires per-TURN and cannot tell design-relevant work from any other edit. C — both, split by role. THE DESTINATION, not a rejection. D — build `cap:session-memory` instead. Not taken as a substitute, but the skill must answer D's question — what gets written — before it is worth much.		Captured because the trigger question is genuinely open while the content question is not: dec:idea-is-session-context-already-in-the-graph settled that the connective tissue is what only the session holds, and cap:session-memory has been planned since 2026-07-25 with no trigger. What makes this worth its own node is the tension rather than the idea — req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session is accepted and says the user must never be the trigger, and a skill the user types institutionalises exactly that. Recorded with the counter-arguments beside it, including that this session was compacted, which makes session-end the worst moment to ask for a faithful account of session start.acceptedA user-typed trigger for capturing what only the session holds
OPEN — when a change to a shared upstream is driven by one dependent, how does the OTHER dependent find out? (the diamond: B and D both depend on A, and A's blast radius stops at its own graph)
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, describing what has already happened rather than a hypothetical. THE SHAPE, in his numbering: projectA = **dynograph-foundation**, projectB = **reflow2**, projectC = **flo2**, projectD = **storyflow**. C depends on B; B depends on A; **D ALSO depends on A, and not on B.** A diamond, with A at the point. (projectE = embeddings-rs, and whether it is even a reflow2 project is undecided — recorded as unknown rather than assumed either way.) ⚠️ THE INCIDENT, WHICH IS THE EVIDENCE AND IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Anthony: \'projectB caused changes in projectA, which I implemented real time. **The risk was that the changes that projectB required on projectA might have caused issues with projectA now being able to support projectD** (I thought about it, but really didn't test that anything didn't break in projectD by using an updated projectA).\' ⇒ A change was levied UP one arm of the diamond and shipped, and **nothing checked the other arm.** The owner noticed the risk by thinking, and the check was never run. That is the failure mode, already realised, on the real projects. === WHY THIS IS NOT `dec:who-needs-to-know`, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS STRUCTURAL === That node asks whether notification is SUBSCRIBED or DERIVED from the blast radius, and prefers derived because `propagate_from` already computes who a change impacts. Its recorded counter-argument is: *\'a blast radius is only as good as the edges that exist, so an unrecorded dependency means a silent non-notification.\'* **IN THE CROSS-GRAPH CASE THAT COUNTER STOPS BEING A RISK AND BECOMES A CERTAINTY.** The edge D→A lives in **D's graph**. A's graph does not hold it and cannot. So A's blast radius is not *possibly* incomplete — it is **NECESSARILY TRUNCATED AT THE GRAPH BOUNDARY**, every time, by construction. Derived notification cannot work from the upstream side, and no amount of edge hygiene in A fixes it. ⭐ AND IT IS THE SAME STRUCTURAL FACT `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` already turned on, pointing the other way. There, Anthony's Google-service argument defeated \'the upstream pulls\': a widely-depended-on design **cannot enumerate its dependents**. That killed pull for RECEIVING requirements. Here the identical fact kills push for SENDING warnings — A cannot warn D because A does not know D exists. **One fact, two directions, two different unbuildable mechanisms.** Which is a strong hint that the answer has to live on the CONSUMER side in both cases. === OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN === **(A) THE CONSUMER MIRRORS AND NOTICES.** Each dependent mirrors the upstream's published surface and detects when the mirror drifts from the real one. **The machinery is already built and shipped** — `export_surface` (upstream publishes), `mirror_surface` / `mirrors` (consumer mirrors), `pair_designs`, `seam_report`. FOR: it scales exactly where push fails, because it needs no registry and no knowledge of who depends on you; each consumer looks after itself. It also inverts the burden onto the party who actually cares. COUNTER: it is a PULL, so it only fires when the consumer runs it — D learns it is broken when D next looks, not when A changes. For a project nobody has opened in three months, that is late. **(B) A COMPOSITION RUN ACROSS ALL THE GRAPHS AT ONCE.** `compose_and_analyse` and `pair_designs` exist; `dec:linked-repos-poc` RAN this on reflow2 + flo2 + dynograph-foundation on 2026-08-06 and found \'the linking works, the labelling does not exist.\' **THAT BLOCKER HAS SINCE CLEARED** — reflow2 now declares 9 `required` interfaces, five of them pointed at dynograph (`ifc:req-dyno-*`). FOR: it computes the diamond directly — two consumers requiring the same interface means a change to it touches both — and Anthony HOLDS ALL FOUR GRAPHS, so it is runnable today. COUNTER: it needs somebody with every graph in hand, which is exactly the arrangement the Google-service argument says does not generalise. **Fine for the trial, not the answer.** **(C) THE UPSTREAM KEEPS A REGISTRY OF ITS CONSUMERS.** FOR: A could then warn D. COUNTER: refuted twice already — registration is a write, so pull cannot bootstrap, and a heavily-depended-on design will not maintain it. Retained only for the small-federation case. **(D) NOTHING MECHANICAL; THE OWNER REMEMBERS.** COUNTER: this is what happened, and the record above is what it cost — the risk was identified and the test still was not run. Not because anyone was careless, but because nothing made the omission visible afterwards. === THE FIRST TESTABLE STEP, WHICH COSTS ALMOST NOTHING === **Does storyflow (D) DECLARE its dependency on dynograph-foundation (A) as a `required` interface, the way reflow2 (B) now does?** reflow2's five `ifc:req-dyno-*` interfaces exist; whether D has any equivalent is UNKNOWN AND CHECKABLE. If it does not, no mechanism in any option above can work for D, and declaring it is the prerequisite for all of them. If it does, the diamond is already computable with tools that shipped. 📌 AND THE METHOD IS ANTHONY'S OWN, STATED THE SAME DAY: *\'the best development of reflow2 has been propose something — trial it with a real project — then learn from it — iterate upon the solution and try again.\'* These four projects are that trial, and the diamond is the first thing to run it on. NOTHING IS PROMOTED.		Captured under the brainstorm skill, and kept SEPARATE from two neighbours it would otherwise be merged into — a node holding two questions can only ever be half-answered. `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` is the UP direction (how a dependent levies a need on its upstream); this is the DOWN-AND-SIDEWAYS direction (how a change to a shared upstream reaches a sibling that never asked). `dec:who-needs-to-know` is the SAME-GRAPH version and prefers derived notification; the point of this node is that derivation is structurally impossible across a graph boundary, which that node's own counter-argument anticipates without naming the cross-graph case. Recorded because the failure has already occurred on the real projects and was survived by luck rather than by a check — and because the prerequisite that blocked every mechanism (no labelled seam) cleared three days after it was written down.proposednothing
OPEN — can unmade decisions be ranked as risk to the goal, bounded to what a person can actually decide in a day, when 61 of 83 of them govern nothing and so have no path?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-08-10, in his words: *'is there a way to assess unmade decisions as 'risk' in getting towards the projects goal? like you need to make this chain of decisions before your project can be implemented... almost like the critical path on decision making. for each project (to include reflow2), when I first do where-am-i, I get the critical path of decisions I need to make.'* And the pain behind it, also his: *'I generate many many ideas and really use the brainstorm skill a lot... but I often come up with another idea before making a decision on the previous brainstorming idea. sometimes this is on purpose as I just have a thought and want it captured and I'll decide later.'* THE ANSWER MUST BE BOUNDED TO HUMAN THROUGHPUT, added by Anthony in the same conversation and it constrains every option below: *'many projects have hundreds of decisions and a person can only make a small subset of decisions a day. especially with somebody like me, I think about 25 ideas a minute (exaggerating)... having something that says, these are your top 5 priorities would be great.'* SO THE OUTPUT IS A SHORT RANKED LIST, NOT A FULL ORDERING. This matters more than it sounds: a ranked list of 83 is the same as no ranking, and it is the shape the pile already has. A top-5 also changes what the ranking must be GOOD at — it need only get the head right, not the tail, which makes several of the weaker signals below usable that would be useless for a total order. It also means the cut line is a claim: whatever is at rank 6 is being said not to matter today, and that claim should be visible rather than silent. HALF OF THIS IS ALREADY ACCEPTED INTENT AND MUST NOT BE RE-DECIDED. `req:what-next` (status ACCEPTED, his own earlier words) already says: *'The answer must rank an unmade decision ABOVE the work that waits on it, because being told to build something blocked on a choice only the human can make is worse than being told nothing.'* `cap:what-next` is PLANNED, and its recorded blocker HAS EXPIRED — `cap:derived-completion` reached `verified` and the park was never revisited, which the capability itself notes with 'NOBODY NOTICED'. It also already wants the which-decisions-shape-everything section, with the measured caveat that raw in-degree is the wrong signal because the top hit was a pruning decision governing ten DROPPED requirements. SO THE RANKING HALF IS DESIGNED, AGREED AND UNBLOCKED. What is genuinely new here is the CHAIN, the RISK framing, the BOUND, and putting it at the FRONT of where-am-i. MEASURED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS RECORDED, and it inverts the premise: open (proposed) decisions 83 of those, governing ANYTHING at all 22 of those, governing NOTHING — no downstream, so NO PATH 61 decision->decision precedence edges among open decisions 12 (mostly CONTRADICTS, not precedence) items scheduled into an epoch 23 of those, blocked by an open decision 2 THE CRITICAL PATH IS NOT UNCOMPUTABLE FOR WANT OF AN ALGORITHM — budget.rs already runs Kahn toposort and longest-path, and `cap:bl-150` records that it is hand-rolled there and unavailable elsewhere. It is uncomputable because THREE QUARTERS OF THE PILE HAS NO SUCCESSOR. A path needs something downstream and 61 of these have nothing. ⇒ THE QUESTION THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS, and it is not the one asked: are those 61 ideas genuinely not blocking anything yet — in which case the honest answer is 'your undecided pile carries almost no risk to the goal, and that is why you can safely keep deferring' — or are they blocking things the graph was never told about? THOSE TWO LOOK IDENTICAL FROM INSIDE THE GRAPH AND NEED DIFFERENT ANSWERS. Everything below is downstream of that. THE OPTIONS. (A) BUILD `cap:what-next` AS ALREADY DESIGNED AND STOP. It ranks the 22 that govern something, says plainly that 61 are unranked because they connect to nothing, and leaves it there. Cheapest by far; the intent is already accepted so nothing new needs deciding. WITH THE BOUND, this gets stronger: a top-5 drawn from 22 rankable items is a real answer, where a total ordering of 83 would not be. Counter: it answers 'what should I decide next' only for a quarter of the pile, and the 61 are exactly the ones he feels buried by. (B) ASK ONE QUESTION AT CAPTURE TIME — when a brainstorm is recorded, ask what it bears on, and draw that edge. Converts a musing into something rankable without deciding it. Counter, and it is the serious one: THE BRAINSTORM SKILL IS FRICTIONLESS BY DESIGN AND THAT IS WHY HE USES IT. It explicitly forbids manufacturing links, and adding a question at capture taxes the one habit that is working. It would also often be unanswerable — half-formed ideas frequently do not yet know what they bear on, which is what makes them ideas. (C) DERIVE THE LINKAGE, ASK RATHER THAN ASSERT — use the search index to propose what an idea probably bears on, and surface it as a question at read time instead of an edge at write time. Keeps capture frictionless and fits `dec:ask-not-repair`'s standing shape (a suspicion is a DETECT gap, never a repair). Counter: similarity over prose is exactly the scoring that produced 81-85 scores on unrelated requirements (`fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status`), so the proposals would be noisy — and a noisy proposal at orientation time is the cry-wolf failure this project has now named three times. (D) A REAL CRITICAL PATH, FOR THE 22 THAT HAVE ONE. Declare decision-to-decision precedence (DEPENDS_ON between Decisions already exists, 10 edges design-wide) and run the toposort and longest path budget.rs already implements. Counter: with 12 precedence-ish edges among open decisions, mostly CONTRADICTS, the longest chain today is likely 1-2 hops. A 'critical path' of length two is a list with a promotion. (E) RISK, SCORED RATHER THAN PATHED. Score each open decision by what it blocks — how much is GOVERNED_BY it, how deep the downstream goes, and whether any of it is SCHEDULED into an epoch. That is computable TODAY with no new edges and no new vocabulary, and a score is exactly what a top-5 needs. Counter, and it is the honest one: run it now and the answer is that risk is nearly zero, because only 2 of 23 scheduled items are blocked by an open decision. That may be true and reassuring, or it may mean the schedule is what is under-modelled rather than the decisions. (F) THE PILE'S REAL PROBLEM MAY BE AGE, NOT BLOCKING. Rank by staleness — how long has this been open, has anything touched its region since — rather than by path. `cap:revise-trigger` already exists for surfacing a settled road worth re-opening, and `cap:what-next`'s own expired park is a worked example of a condition nobody watches. Counter: age is not importance, and a stale-first ranking would put genuinely deferred ideas above newly urgent ones. (G) RANK BY ATTENTION RATHER THAN BY CONSEQUENCE — `dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important`, recorded separately the same day. A node the user keeps circling back to may be ripening whether or not it blocks anything. NOT A SUBSTITUTE: a decision can draw attention and block nothing, or block everything and never be searched. Whether the two compose into one ranking, or are two lists, is open in both nodes and settled in neither. WHAT IS NOT AN OPTION: deciding things to shorten the list. Anthony said the deferral is often deliberate — *'sometimes this is on purpose'* — so a mechanism whose success is measured by the pile shrinking would be optimising against how he actually works. The bound makes this concrete: a top-5 that never changes because he keeps not deciding is working correctly, not failing. ONE THING TO SETTLE BEFORE ANY OF THESE, because 'risk to the goal' needs a goal: the Project's objective is one sentence, 'keep a design coherent from concept through operations', and nothing decomposes it. Risk is currently measurable only against EPOCHS, which are the nearest thing to a target the graph holds. Whether the goal itself should be modelled is a separate question this node does not open.		Anthony's idea, recorded as an open question because the measurement changed what the question is. He asked for a critical path; the graph says three quarters of the undecided pile has no successor to path through, so the prior question is whether that disconnection is true or merely unrecorded. REVISED the same session it was created, to fold in the top-5 bound he added minutes later, rather than minting a second node. The bound is a constraint on the answer to THIS question, not a new question — and given that the complaint driving all of it is a pile of 83 open decisions, answering 'how do I triage the pile' by adding another node to the pile would be a poor demonstration. Recorded without a snapshot because the node had not yet been exported or committed and both versions are this session's own capture; a fold after the record ships would need `revise-design` proper. Kept as one node rather than several because all seven options answer the same question — how to triage undecided work — and splitting them would create a set that can only be half-answered. Options are not registered as alternatives, so `undecided_decision_point` stays quiet and the loop says nothing while this is still thinking. No approver edge, deliberately, per the brainstorm discipline: this is thinking out loud, and attaching an approver would make `loop_status` start reporting it as owed. If it becomes a real fork — most likely between (A) and (E), which are both buildable now and compose naturally under a bound — `register_alternative` is what promotes it. Recorded WITHOUT wiring it to `req:what-next` or `cap:what-next`. Those are cited in the text and the relationship is real, but drawing edges from a musing to accepted intent would assert that this idea shapes them, which nobody has decided. That restraint is also the subject of option (B), which makes it worth stating rather than doing silently.proposednothing
OPEN — does a Verification gain structured fields for its BOUNDS and its FINDINGS, and is that the same decision as giving it structured RESULT fields?
UNSETTLED, and it must be settled as ONE question rather than two. Two dev_storyflow reports a day apart ask for different fields on the same node for the same underlying reason — a Verification's qualifications have nowhere to live except its name. (A) 2026-08-07: structured RESULT fields — `exit_code`, `command`, `observed`/`expected` — so the graph can flag `status: passing` beside a non-zero exit as incoherent, and a re-run can be compared mechanically. (B) 2026-08-08: a `bounds`/`caveats` field and ideally a `grade`, plus a `findings`/`report` field, so `name` can go back to being a name and the qualifications become data the loop can reason about. Also on the table, and cheaper than either: truncate `name` in loop_status's rollup, or return `name` + `detail` separately, which fixes the READ cost without touching the schema. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT DESERVES AIRING: reflow2 already has cap:evidence-scope (what a check pinned and swept, on the VERIFIES edge per dec:evidence-scope-on-the-verifies-edge) and reconcile_verification for feeding real outcomes back, so the machinery for 'evidence is structured, not prose' is PARTLY BUILT — and the honest question may be whether these are extensions of it or a second, competing home for the same information.		Recorded as one decision because settling either half alone would put two structured homes for a check's qualifications into the same node type, which is how a schema acquires an overlap nobody can later explain. The urgency is not theoretical: the missing field has already become fleet DOCTRINE at dev_storyflow ('carry the grading and all bounds in the node NAME'), it has made graph_report.top_gaps titles ~2,000-character essays, and reflow2's OWN loop_status digest reads the same way for the same reason. Evidence: fact:defect-a-finding-has-no-bounds-so-grading-goes-in-the-name and fact:defect-verification-evidence-is-prose-so-passing-can-contradict-itself.proposednothing
OPEN — a short generated video explaining reflow2 to someone new, and the tension that it is the one thing on the page that cannot be rendered from the graph
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, in the same breath as settling the page and explicitly flagged as thinking out loud: *'might even be fun to create/generate a small video explaining what reflow2 is for somebody new to it /brainstorm'*. Nothing here is intent. It is his idea and it is recorded so it is not lost, not so it is claimed. DISTINCT FROM the page decision on purpose: that one is SETTLED and covers what the page renders. This is an unsettled question about a different artefact, in a different medium, with a different failure mode. Folding it in would have made a decided node read as half-decided. ═══ ⭐ WHY IT IS BETTER THAN 'A NICE EXTRA', AND WORTH KEEPING EVEN IF DECLINED ═══ It plausibly answers the cost he accepted one sentence earlier. `dec:idea-what-is-on-reflow2s-public-page` rules that the page carries ONLY renderings, which means **it cannot carry a hand-written 'here is what reflow2 is'** — so a newcomer meets a systems-engineering view before knowing what they are looking at. **An explainer is the orientation the ruling removed.** That is not why he suggested it, and the connection is recorded as an observation rather than attributed to him. ═══ ⚠️ THE TENSION, RECORDED BESIDE THE IDEA RATHER THAN AGAINST IT ═══ **A video is the least renderable artefact there is.** The page's whole claim is that its contents come out of the graph and are periodically refreshed. A video is hand-made, expensive to remake, and therefore **the one thing on that page guaranteed to go stale** — and it would sit there asserting, by adjacency, the same provenance as the renderings around it. That is the exact failure `dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph` was opened about, in the medium where it is hardest to fix. ⇒ Not an argument against it. An argument that **if it ships, it must be visibly a different KIND of thing from the renderings** — or the renderings' credibility pays for it. OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) **A HAND-MADE VIDEO.** Best quality, highest staleness cost, remade by hand every time reflow2 moves. (b) **A GENERATED WALKTHROUGH DRIVEN BY THE GRAPH** — a scripted tour whose narration and visuals are projected from the same source as the views, so it re-renders with them. Closest to the page's own doctrine; unclear that the tooling exists. (c) **NOT A VIDEO — AN ANIMATED OR INTERACTIVE RENDERING.** The loop, drawn from the graph and stepped through. `docs/loop-dag.html` already exists as a rendered page and is the nearest thing to a starting point. Keeps the only-renderings rule intact. (d) **NOTHING, AND LET THE CONFESSIONS DO THE TALKING.** The page's honesty is the pitch; a newcomer who does not get it was not the audience. Cheapest, and consistent — at the cost of the orientation gap being real. 📌 NOT ASSESSED: whether anything in reach can actually generate (b). Nothing in reflow2 renders video, and no attempt was made to find out — recording the idea is not the same as scoping it. ⇒ SEQUENCED AFTER THE RELEASE, like the page. Nothing here is started.		Recorded under the brainstorm skill because he marked it as one. The skill's rule is followed exactly: the idea is not argued down, and the objection — that a video is the one artefact on that page which cannot be re-rendered — is recorded BESIDE it as an option-shaping constraint rather than used to dismiss it. An idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning; recorded with its objection, it keeps both. Split from the page decision rather than appended to it, per the skill's rule that several unrelated questions mean several Decisions — and because that one is now settled, so anything unsettled living inside it would make a ruling look tentative. The connection to the orientation gap is the one thing here he did not say. It is attributed as an observation, not to him, so a later reader can tell his idea from the reason it might matter.proposednothing
OPEN — what does reflow2 look like at 1k / 100k / 1M tenants each holding their OWN design, and what must not be foreclosed now?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-09, about using reflow2 behind a web app. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen. DISTINCT FROM dec:live-tier, and the distinction is the whole point: that decision is about MANY WRITERS ON ONE DESIGN (the state-funeral case — thousands replanning one echeloned plan, which needs consensus and would mean replacing single-writer RocksDB). This is the opposite shape: N TENANTS, EACH WITH THEIR OWN graph_id AND ONE WRITER. No write contention, no consensus, no shared-store rewrite. The two cases share a tier and share almost none of their difficulty. THE SCALE STEPS ARE NOT EVENLY SPACED. 1k is a deployment problem and the design already points at it: cap:graph-registry (planned) specifies a bounded, evict-when-idle map from graph key to open design, and cap:select-graph-by-id (unrealized) lets a session name what it wants. Hold a few hundred designs hot, evict the rest. THE STEP CHANGE IS 1k TO 100k, and it is forced by one measured number: reflow2's OWN design is 1,828 nodes = a 3.8 MB export and a 33 MB store on disk — roughly 9x inflation, being RocksDB plus the tantivy index. At 100k tenants that is ~3.3 TB if all were resident, so the hot set is necessarily ~1% or less, which INVERTS the problem: cold open stops being an edge case and becomes the steady state. shared.rs budgets 30 SECONDS for a cold open today. The engineering question changes from 'hold many designs' (which the registry answers) to 'make opening a design cheap' (which it does not address at all). 100k TO 1M IS THEN HORIZONTAL: ~4 TB of cold blobs is unremarkable for object storage and the hot set grows with concurrency, not with registrations. A FIFTH ROAD, alongside dec:live-tier's four, and it fits what reflow2 already believes: OBJECT STORAGE HOLDS THE EXPORT AS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH, a node HYDRATES a RocksDB+tantivy cache on demand, and eviction is free because the cache is derived. This dissolves placement (any node can serve any tenant), dissolves durability (the object store's problem), and makes an idle tenant cost a ~3.8 MB cold blob instead of a 33 MB live store. reflow2 already has the primitive: the export is deterministic, sorted, content-hashed and self-contained — that IS a per-tenant blob, and the store is already derived rather than authoritative. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING TODAY, recorded as unbuilt rather than merely absent: cap:graph-registry is planned and nothing builds it; cap:select-graph-by-id is unrealized and unverified; ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design is PLANNED, and dec:one-process-many-stores was accepted CONDITIONAL on it, so that condition is half met; and dec:live-tier names 'no identity or authorization', which at this scale is not a gap but the product. THE FOUR WAYS TO FORECLOSE, all cheap to avoid now: (1) PROCESS-GLOBALS THAT ARE REALLY PER-DESIGN — cap:graph-registry's own text already lists graph_path, content_path, identity and write_gen as things that must become per-graph; every new static that is secretly per-design is a future migration. (2) PATH AS IDENTITY — cap:select-graph-by-id frames it correctly as 'the server maps id to path', id primary and path derived; sidecar files beside the store (.id.json, .sync.json) want to become object metadata resolved by a resolver. (3) A WHOLE-DOCUMENT WRITE ON A HOT PATH — the export being whole-document is correct for an archival action and fatal on a per-change path, which also makes BL-198 (stop serializing defaults) a SCALING decision rather than tidiness, since blob size is hydrate time. (4) BUILDING MULTI-TENANCY BEFORE PROVING ISOLATION — at this scale that is a security boundary, and retrofitting one into a running multi-tenant system is the sequencing mistake that cannot be walked back. WHAT IS NOT A PROBLEM, worth stating because it is counter-intuitive: the scaling axis is the NUMBER OF TENANTS, not the size of one design. A tenant's graph is small, so full scans, Leiden, modularity and every detector remain cheap per tenant. Single-writer-per-design is a FEATURE here rather than a limit — it is what makes N tenants embarrassingly parallel — so the box would be removing it, not keeping it. THE ONE MEASUREMENT WORTH TAKING NOW, while nothing depends on the answer: hydrate-and-index time as a function of design size (200 / 2k / 20k nodes, import to first query). Under a second for a typical tenant and the cache model is routine engineering; seconds and a read model in front becomes necessary — and that is better known before designing around the opposite assumption.		Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent. Kept SEPARATE from dec:live-tier rather than appended to it, because one node holding two questions can only ever be half-answered and these two differ in their hardest part: many-writers-one-design needs consensus, many-single-writer-tenants needs cheap hydration. Worth keeping even if none of it is built, for three reasons: the 9x store-to-export ratio is a measured anchor that decides the architecture and was not previously written down anywhere; the fifth road follows from a primitive reflow2 already has rather than from new invention; and the four foreclosures are cheap now and expensive later, which is exactly the class of thing a design graph exists to hold. Anthony's framing was explicitly about not painting into a corner rather than about building this, and the record should keep that distinction.proposednothing
A planned increment is identified by what it DELIVERS; the version number is assigned at the cut, from what actually shipped
ACCEPTED on Anthony's word, 2026-08-08 — shape (a), and he named why it is the right one: it is the only option where the question STOPS EXISTING rather than being answered. No plan ever holds a number it can lose, so neither slipping nor inserting is a problem. THE RULE: a planned increment's identity names its CONTENT (`epoch:planned-read-half`, `epoch:planned-status-accounting`). The version number is not part of the plan at all. At cut time the number is derived from what actually shipped, by the CHANGELOG's own bucket table — patch for fixes, minor for a change to the shape of the tool surface or the schema. WHAT IT DISSOLVES: (1) The id churn. An id cannot be renamed, so a version-named plan guarantees either a lying id or a node replacement that breaks the snapshot trail `dec:arrival-delta` reads plan movement from. A content-named plan never needs renaming, because content is what the plan IS. (2) The slip-versus-insert question entirely. `dec:an-unplanned-cut-slips-every-later-increment-by-one` (accepted an hour earlier) and `dec:idea-an-unplanned-cut-takes-an-in-between-number` were competing answers to 'what happens to the planned numbers when unplanned work takes one' — and under this rule there are no planned numbers to disturb. The slip rule is not WRONG; its subject ceases to exist. Recorded with an OBSOLETES edge rather than by un-accepting it, per dec:reopen-supersedes: an accepted Decision is never un-accepted. (3) The pressure to mislabel. With numbering decided at the cut from shipped content, semver stays honest by construction — nobody is tempted to call a shape change a patch to protect a planned number, which is the concrete harm the in-between-number idea carried (the CHANGELOG's own table says patch means the consumer updates blindly). THE OBSERVATION UNDERNEATH, which generalises past versioning: a version number is assigned LAST, at the cut, and a planned increment exists LONG before that. Baking it into the identity records a GUESS as a NAME. That is the same shape as `ver:plan-increments`' finding that a plan's content lived in an epoch's NAME as prose rather than as structure — both are a plan carrying, in its identity or its label, something that belongs elsewhere. COMPOSES WITH THE HYBRID rather than competing: content-named plans plus semver-honest numbering at cut time is the same destination reached from two directions, which is why `dec:idea-an-unplanned-cut-takes-an-in-between-number` stays recorded rather than rejected — its numbering instinct survives, only its premise (that plans own numbers) is gone. NOT CHOSEN: (b) a `version` property on DesignEpoch — smaller, but it leaves the misleading ids in place; (c) redefining the pre-1.0 buckets — cheapest to write, most expensive to be wrong about, since it weakens the one signal consumers act on blindly; (d) keeping version-named ids and reading them as birth numbers — makes every id a small trap for a future reader.		Raised immediately after applying the slip, because the cost was concrete rather than theoretical: four planned epochs needed renaming and none could have its id corrected, so the graph now holds ids whose numbers are one behind their content. Recorded rather than fixed — changing how the plan is ADDRESSED is a bigger act than the slip Anthony asked for, and picking (a) would re-point every future reference.acceptedPLANNED — one honest write surface. Largest and least urgent; nothing here blocks anyone. BL-202 (L) collapses the two write surfaces the typed constructors created — they reach 44% of declared properties and are the single cause behind BL-129 and BL-183. BL-198 stop serializing defaults, but measure the cost to compare_designs and the merge driver FIRST. BL-197 + BL-204: the words we ship stopped matching the code we ship. NO VERSION NUMBER BY DESIGN (dec:idea-a-planned-increment-is-named-by-content-not-by-number). Supersedes epoch:v0280-planned., PLANNED — 'The graph can be READ at the size it has reached.' The OUT half. WIDENED 2026-08-05 on Anthony's word from 'the loop tells the truth about what it is owed' to the whole out half (dec:the-transition-is-two-halves-and-reads-are-the-unscheduled-one, accepted). THE MEASUREMENT THAT FORCED IT: of 33 collection-returning read tools, THREE let the caller bound the result and only scan_nodes can page; reviewed_gaps returned 130,922 characters and had to be read with jq. Today a document BEATS the graph for making a decision, and that is a fair fight the graph loses — so no capture improvement is worth anything until this lands. CONTENTS: BL-194 open_questions all-clear; BL-192 enums name legal values; BL-195 the bridge a ruling forbids; BL-201 wire or retire Requirement.concern; BL-203 an unexercised type is visible; generalise scan_nodes' envelope (total/returned/omitted/next_offset/capped_by + payload budget) to the other 30 tools, since it already solved this and was adopted by exactly one; dec:gap-reporting-when-most-intent-is-unbuilt (accepted), because 300 captured ideas produce 300 identical gaps. JOINED 2026-08-08 from dev_storyflow: scan_nodes has no status filter and get_node returns no edges, which cost a lane its stated bound — and a filtered count MUST name its predicate, or it becomes the fifth number in their four-counts report. BL-205 is DONE (shipped early in #70). NO VERSION NUMBER BY DESIGN (dec:idea-a-planned-increment-is-named-by-content-not-by-number): the number is assigned at the cut from what actually ships. Supersedes epoch:v0250-planned., PLANNED — seams, the frontier the instruments already name. maturity_report puts seams at 0% (0 of 73 couplings declared through a contract) across 23 releases, and Interface has 3 instances with the 5 spec properties set on none. BL-193 a CONSUMED interface with no spec fires no gap; BL-190 the stewardship edge joins it because a new edge type is a schema change and pairing keeps it to one bump. NO VERSION NUMBER BY DESIGN (dec:idea-a-planned-increment-is-named-by-content-not-by-number). Supersedes epoch:v0270-planned., PLANNED — status accounting: WHEN was this true? The biggest conceptual gap either source found, and EIA-649 names it. BL-187 external anchor and BL-185 test-first both add Verification properties (ONE schema touch), BL-189 the retirement half. Evidence: half of one corpus pins to commits no longer ancestors of main; 11 of this project's own verifications sat green on one two-day-old run. NO VERSION NUMBER BY DESIGN (dec:idea-a-planned-increment-is-named-by-content-not-by-number). Supersedes epoch:v0260-planned.
OPEN — should a requirement that is satisfied AND demonstrated become tuple-like: still changeable, but not without specific confirmation?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12. HIS WORDS: 'I think the 'immutability' of satisfied requirements should be a big safety measure of reflow2 projects (including itself, which is a reflow2 project). I mean it shouldn't be impossible to change a satisfied requirement or capability, but there should be safety checks in place that make it hard to change without specific confirmation. maybe once a requirement is satisfied, particularly if it had been tested and demonstrated, should basically become a python tuple.' ⭐ THE FIELD EVIDENCE IS A SECOND USER, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING. His brother Alex, evaluating reflow2 for his own work: 'Yes potentially. As long as it doesn't mess with the core functionality.' Anthony's read of the concern: 'he really likes using reflow2 and he's concerned that we'll somehow change reflow2 away from what it currently is and what he likes.' That is `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` arriving on its own terms — the worry is not deletion, it is DRIFT. ⚠️ WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, AND WHY THIS IS NOT IT. `req:inviolable-intent` is ACCEPTED and covers the same family: 'intent that no downstream decision may trade away — a key performance parameter... COMPUTE a violation rather than rely on anyone remembering... A KPP that nothing checks is a comment.' But a KPP is DECLARED — opt-in, stated up front, about a THRESHOLD VALUE. Anthony is describing something EARNED — a requirement acquires protection by having been satisfied and demonstrated, retrospectively and automatically, and it is about the requirement's TEXT and STATE rather than a numeric threshold. The KPP protects what you said mattered; this would protect what you have already built and proven. Alex's concern is the second one, and it has no mechanism. ═══ WHAT PROTECTION ACTUALLY EXISTS, MEASURED 2026-08-12 ═══ accepted requirements 110 with a satisfier carrying a PASSING check 102 (92%) unproven_capabilities (built, no passing check) 0 unexamined_claims 0 STRONG, AND REAL: delivery is COMPUTED from the golden thread rather than asserted (`req:completion-computed`), so breaking the code reds a check and removing the capability fires `unsatisfied_requirement`. And `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` means no agent can move a requirement off `accepted` — which is the guarantee that matters most while reflow2 is built by agents. 🛑 BUT THE HOLE IS EXACTLY WHERE ANTHONY IS POINTING, and it was measured rather than supposed. In this session an agent appended **+4,770 characters** to `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` — more than doubling its statement — and afterwards: ChangeEvents pointing at it .... 0 Snapshots of it ............... 0 status ........................ still `accepted` throughout ⇒ **STATUS IS GUARDED AND CONTENT IS NOT.** A satisfied requirement can be reworded, narrowed, hedged or quietly scoped down while continuing to read as satisfied, and nothing signals it. That is precisely the drift Alex fears, and 'immutable' is not currently the right word for it. 📌 A SECOND, WEAKER-THAN-IT-LOOKS SIGNAL: 37 of 139 verifications have NEVER RUN. reflow2's own tripwire says why that matters — 'a status is a property any hand can set to `passing` in a single call, and a failing test is not.' So freezing on `verified` would sometimes freeze on a claim rather than a result, and 'tested and demonstrated' needs to mean the run, not the field. ═══ THE OPTIONS, none taken ═══ A — REFUSE AND NAME, on revising a requirement that is accepted + satisfied + carrying a passing check. The two-sided accept shape already used by `set_artifact_checksum` and by the search-first guard: the write is refused, the refusal names what it protects and the deliberate route through. CHEAP, and it reuses a pattern this project has shipped twice. EXPENSIVE, and the lesson is recent and hard-won: search-first's own record says 'a check that refused often would be routed around, and a rule people route around is worse than no rule.' Legitimate sharpening happened SIX times in this session alone; a wall would have blocked all of it. B — SNAPSHOT-FIRST, ENFORCED. Do not block the change; require that it leave a trace — a Snapshot and a ChangeEvent — so a reworded requirement is visible and attributable. `revise-design` already prescribes exactly this and nothing enforces it, and `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` already establishes that a revision with no snapshot is COMPUTABLE FROM GRAPH STATE ALONE. So the machinery exists and is simply not wired to requirement text. CHEAPEST HONEST OPTION, and it answers Alex's actual worry ('will I be able to SEE it') rather than the stronger one nobody asked for. C — A STORED MUTABILITY CLASS, literally the tuple: a property marking a requirement frozen. Explicit and readable. EXPENSIVE: it is stored state that can disagree with reality, which `dec:certainty-derived` argues against — and it would need setting, which is one more thing to forget. D — DERIVE THE CLASS, never store it: 'protected' IS accepted + satisfied + verified-by-a-check-that-has-actually-RUN. Automatic, no new vocabulary, no opt-in, and it degrades honestly — a requirement whose check never ran is simply not protected yet, which is true. Fits `dec:certainty-derived` exactly. EXPENSIVE: it makes protection a moving target, so the same edit is refused today and allowed tomorrow depending on a check's last run. ⇒ B AND D COMPOSE, and are probably the shape: derive the class (D), and let it govern how loudly a change must announce itself (B) rather than whether it is allowed at all. ═══ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea ═══ REFLOW2 DEVELOPS ITSELF, AND SHARPENING SATISFIED REQUIREMENTS IS NORMAL, VALUABLE WORK. Six requirements were legitimately extended in this session — with measurements, field evidence and cross-references that made them better. Any mechanism that treats 'the text changed' as suspicious will fire constantly on exactly the work that improves the design, and the project's own history says such a rule gets routed around. The distinction that has to be drawn, and it is not obvious: SHARPENING (adding evidence, narrowing ambiguity, recording what was learned) versus WEAKENING (removing a clause, lowering a bar, scoping out something that was promised). Nothing in the graph can currently tell those apart, and an agent asserting which one it just did is exactly the self-report this project distrusts everywhere else. NOT DECIDED. The narrow question worth answering first is much smaller than the framing: **should a revision to a satisfied requirement be required to leave a trace?** That is option B alone, it needs no new vocabulary, and it turns 'nothing can break it silently' from a claim into a checkable property. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ SHARPENED SAME DAY — THE UNIT IS THE THREAD, AND THE TRIGGER IS OPERATIONAL ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony corrected the framing above, and the correction is the substance: 'when I'm describing a immutable satisfied requirement, I'm discussing the whole 'chain' as a thread becomes immutable. say I brainstorm an idea, then it leads to an accepted proposal which leads to a requirement which leads to a design to meet that requirement which leads to implementation which leads to test which leads to fielded implementation. basically the whole thread should be immutable or heavily guarded against any changes to it because the thread has been confirmed as 'operational'.' ⭐⭐ TWO THINGS CHANGE, AND BOTH MAKE IT A BETTER IDEA THAN THE ONE ABOVE. (1) THE UNIT IS THE THREAD, NOT THE NODE. Not 'this requirement is frozen' but 'this Decision → Requirement → Capability → Artifact → Verification → fielded deployment is frozen, as one thing'. That is the golden thread reflow2 already computes, extended at the far end into `cmp:fielded` / DEPLOYED_TO / Environment. It is ALREADY TRAVERSABLE: `propagate_change` walks exactly this structure to compute a blast radius, so 'what is in this thread' needs no new machinery — only a state. (2) THE TRIGGER IS OPERATIONAL, NOT SATISFIED. And this ANSWERS THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT recorded above rather than dodging it. The objection was that sharpening satisfied requirements is normal, valuable work — six were extended in this session alone. But almost all of that sharpening happens on intent that has NOT been fielded: recording what was measured, narrowing an ambiguity, cross-referencing. Once something is running in front of users, the calculus genuinely inverts, and the friction stops being a cost and starts being the point. ⭐ THIS IS BASELINING, AND IT IS ANTHONY'S OWN DISCIPLINE. In acquisition terms a fielded thread is a configuration item under a product baseline: changes stop being edits and become change requests. reflow2 ALREADY HAS BASELINE VOCABULARY and it stops short of this exact thing — `epoch_type: baseline` on DesignEpoch, and 'an Anchor is a checksummed baseline epoch'; `as_checksum`, 'frozen at cut time, so later baseline moves do not rewrite what a past release contained'; `Artifact.checksum`, the baseline drift detection compares against. So reflow2 baselines EPOCHS, ARTIFACT CONTENT and RELEASE MANIFESTS — three things — and has no notion of a baselined THREAD OF INTENT. That is the gap this names, and it is the SE-native framing of it. ═══ THE MEASUREMENT THAT SIZES IT, taken 2026-08-12 on reflow2's own design ═══ accepted requirements 110 thread complete AND shipped in a deployed release 67 <- would be frozen thread complete but not in a deployed release 4 incomplete thread 39 deployed releases 1 (v0.28.0) · artifacts shipped 228 🛑 SO THIS IS NOT A CHEAP RULE. **61% of accepted intent would come under configuration control immediately**, not the handful I assumed when I speculated it would cost almost nothing. That cuts both ways and both are worth stating: the safety net would cover the majority of the design from day one, which is what makes it worth having — AND the friction is real, immediate and unavoidable rather than something that arrives gradually as the design matures. 📌 AND THE FRIENDLY READING OF THAT NUMBER: it is high because reflow2 SHIPS. A design that never released would have zero frozen threads and would feel unconstrained — which is correct, because it has promised nobody anything yet. The rule's cost scales with how much you have actually fielded, which is the right shape for a safety measure. ═══ WHAT THIS STILL DOES NOT ANSWER ═══ - WHAT COUNTS AS OPERATIONAL. Above, 'shipped in a release whose status is `deployed`' was used as a proxy. Whether that is the right bar, or whether it needs an Environment of a particular kind (`env:production` versus `env:dev`), is undecided — and reflow2's own design lists `env:dev`, `env:ci` and `env:container`, so the proxy would freeze threads that only ever ran on a laptop. - WHAT A CHANGE TO A FROZEN THREAD ACTUALLY COSTS. Refusal with a named override, a required Snapshot and ChangeEvent, a second approver, or simply a loud finding. The four options above still apply, now scoped to the thread rather than the node. - WHETHER FREEZING PROPAGATES INWARD. If a thread is frozen, is its Artifact frozen — i.e. does the CODE become harder to change too? That is either the most valuable part of the idea or the point at which it becomes unusable, and nothing here settles which. - AND THE SHARPENING-VERSUS-WEAKENING PROBLEM IS UNCHANGED. Even on a frozen thread, adding a measurement is not the same act as removing a clause, and the graph still cannot tell them apart. NOT DECIDED. The narrow first question recorded above — should a revision to a satisfied requirement leave a TRACE — remains the cheapest thing that moves toward this, and it is a prerequisite either way: a thread cannot be shown to have changed if its nodes can change without recording it.		Captured from Anthony's tuple framing and from Alex's concern, which is field evidence from a second user evaluating reflow2 for real work — the worry is drift rather than deletion. It is recorded as a new node rather than folded into req:inviolable-intent because that requirement covers DECLARED inviolability (a KPP, opt-in, about a threshold) and this is EARNED (automatic, retrospective, about a requirement's text and state). The load-bearing measurement is that status is guarded and content is not: a satisfied requirement's statement grew by 4,770 characters in this session with zero ChangeEvents and zero Snapshots recording it. SHARPENED the same day by Anthony's correction that the unit is the THREAD and the trigger is OPERATIONAL, which answers the counter-argument rather than dodging it: sharpening happens before fielding, and the calculus inverts after. Measured on reflow2's own design, 67 of 110 accepted requirements have a complete thread shipped in a deployed release — so this would place 61% of accepted intent under configuration control immediately, which is far more than the handful assumed when the cost was first guessed at.proposednothing
OPEN — should .mcp.json name SEVERAL graph_ids so one session reasons across reflow2 + flo2 + dynograph-foundation at once, and how does that sit against one-session-one-graph?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-06: 'maybe a .mcp.json could have the graph_id for reflow2, dynograph-foundation, and flo2...so when any design decision is made, reflow2 can utilize all 3 graphs?' ⭐ EXTENDED THE SAME DAY, AND THE EXTENSION IS WHAT MAKES IT AN ARCHITECTURE RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE. Anthony's second pass: 'projectC is dependent upon projectB which is dependent upon projectA and these are all managed by user1. say user2 is responsible for projectD which is dependent upon projectC. user2's .mcp.json should only have the graph_id for projectC and projectD, while user1's .mcp.json should have projectA, B and C. theoretically, you could link huge projects together with multiple users only managing their respective set of projects.' THE RULE THAT FALLS OUT OF HIS OWN EXAMPLE, and he did not state it explicitly: projectC appears in BOTH configs. So a graph_id in a config does not mean one thing — THE SAME GRAPH IS WRITABLE FOR ITS OWNER AND READABLE FOR ITS CONSUMER. user1 owns C and may write it; user2 depends on C and may only read it. The set a user holds is therefore {the graphs I own → writable} ∪ {the graphs I directly depend on → readable}, and that is not a flat list of equals — it is a list with a role per entry. THIS RESOLVES THE TENSION THIS NODE WAS RECORDED TO NAME. Option (b) below was written as the conservative choice — one writable graph, N readable. Anthony's federation makes it the GENERAL one: N writable (the ones you own) and M readable (the ones you depend on), which degenerates to (b) for a single-project owner and to today's behaviour for someone with no dependencies. Option (a) — a flat list where every graph is equal — stops being the simple choice once the roles are visible, because it is the only one that has to answer 'which of these three does this write land in'. ⭐ THE SCALE PROPERTY, which is the real content of 'link huge projects together': NOBODY HOLDS THE WHOLE DAG. Each user holds a LOCAL CUT of it — their own subtree plus one hop outward — and the cuts overlap exactly at the ownership seams. That is why it composes to arbitrary size without any user, machine or process ever loading the whole federation, and it is a materially different claim from 'one process holds many graphs' (dec:one-process-many-stores), which is about a SERVER holding tenants. This is about a PERSON holding a neighbourhood. ⚠️ THE HONEST LIMIT, and it is the thing worth deciding rather than discovering: user2 sees C but NOT B or A. If user2's need in C turns out to require a change in B, user2 cannot see that and cannot even tell that B exists. The requirement has to RELAY — user2 asks C's owner, who then discovers it is really a B problem. Whether that is a feature (bounded blast radius, matching real ownership and real org charts) or a defect (a need can stall invisibly one hop out of view) is a genuine question.
