WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED WHEN THIS IS PICKED UP: `dec:what-lives-where` (the accepted rule and its falsifiable test), `dec:views-are-projections` plus `tools/render_views.py` (the rendering half already exists), (BL-198) (a serialized default is indistinguishable from a choice — the same 'what does the graph actually record' family), and (BL-209) (22 Decisions invisible because `AUTHORED_BY` counts as attachment — a graph-native backlog would land straight into that blind spot and must not).		Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request. The load-bearing content is the taxonomy and the single gap it exposes: three of the four kinds of backlog row already have a node type, and the fourth — a defect in a capability that is built, verified and wrong — has none, which is why those rows have no choice but to be prose. Recording the measurement (581 KB, 6 of 8 rows with zero graph representation, four re-derivations in one session) so the next session argues from numbers rather than from the impression that the file is getting long. Extended 2026-08-04 with the data-model constraint Anthony asked for — free text is unbounded and the schema is additive, but only 52 properties are indexed and `rationale` is not one of them, so the answer turns on how much of a row becomes structure rather than prose. Note the irony worth keeping: this rationale is itself unsearchable.supersedednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 measure a design's BREADTH against its DEPTH and prompt a step back? It is measurable, reflow2's own design is nearly all breadth, and an 'ideal ratio' would be the overfit the idea exists to prevent
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14. ═══ ⭐⭐ ADDED 2026-08-14 (LATER, SAME DAY): HIS INHERITANCE-VERSUS-COMPOSITION FRAMING, WHICH CUTS AGAINST DEPTH AND IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT ON THIS NODE ═══ HIS WORDS: *'it reminds me (of) a python class that inherits another class that inherits another class and on (depth). this is different from composition architectures where there is no inheritance and everything is horizontal. In (that) case, is it good that reflow2 is horizontal or would there be some advantages in making things have some level of depth?'* ⇒ **THE ANALOGY IMPORTS A SETTLED ENGINEERING ARGUMENT, AND IT ARGUES FOR THE SHAPE REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS.** 'Prefer composition over inheritance' is doctrine because deep hierarchies are rigid: the taxonomy has to be right before the work is understood, a change to a base ripples to every descendant, and the ladder is expensive to re-cut once things hang off it. **On that reading reflow2's flat shape is not a deficiency to be corrected but the safer default**, and the burden falls on anyone proposing depth to say what it BUYS. ⚠️ **BUT THE ANALOGY IS IMPERFECT IN ONE SPECIFIC WAY, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS LOAD-BEARING.** In code, inheritance and composition are ALTERNATIVES — two ways to reuse behaviour, and picking one excludes the other. In this graph they are NOT alternatives, because they answer different questions: `CONTAINS` says *what is this made of*, `DEPENDS_ON` says *what does this need*, and a design legitimately has both at once. So 'horizontal versus vertical' is not the same trade as 'composition versus inheritance', and reading it as one would make depth look like a competing architecture when it is an orthogonal axis. ⭐ **WHERE THE ANALOGY DOES BITE, EXACTLY: `DECOMPOSES`.** That edge is the one relation here that behaves like inheritance — a child decomposes a parent and **delivery ROLLS UP**, so satisfying every child satisfies the parent. That is a base-class contract with arithmetic attached, and it is brittle in precisely the way deep inheritance is. **AND THE COST IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL — IT WAS PRICED THE SAME DAY:** `req:decomposition-covers-its-parent` → `cap:decomposition-coverage-is-asked` (built 2026-08-14, PR #181) exists because the roll-up never checks that the children AMOUNT TO the parent, so a requirement split into two children addressing a tenth of it reports `delivered` the moment both close. **Depth buys computable roll-up and costs the risk that the roll-up lies.** That is the trade, stated in one line, and it did not exist on this node before he raised the analogy. 📌 SO THE QUESTION IS NARROWED, NOT ANSWERED: not *'should the design be deeper?'* but **'which of the three depth ladders earns its brittleness?'** — and each is separable. `CONTAINS` (assembly) is cheap and carries no arithmetic. `DECOMPOSES` (requirement roll-up) is the expensive one and now has its counterweight built. `Component.level` / `Capability.tier` are labels that compute almost nothing today. ═══ 🛑 RE-MEASURED 2026-08-14 AFTER HIS QUESTION — AND A THIRD UNUSED LADDER APPEARS ═══ ``` DECOMPOSES ................ 0 (requirement lineage: original 164, decomposed 0, derived 0) Component.level ........... component 48 · subsystem 8 · system 0 · SoS 0 · enterprise 0 Capability.tier ........... operational 147 · UNSET 14 · strategic 0 · tactical 0 <- NEW Component CONTAINS ........ 42 edges over 8 parents (of 56 components) lateral ................... DEPENDS_ON 178 · ALLOCATED_TO 178 · SATISFIES 192 PART_OF_FLOW .............. 0 (zero Flow nodes) ``` ⚠️ **`Capability.tier` WAS NOT ON THIS NODE BEFORE AND IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE: 147 of 161 capabilities carry `operational` and NOTHING carries `strategic` or `tactical`.** A three-value ladder holding one value is not a shallow hierarchy, it is an unused field — and it is the SAME vocabulary Alex's tier request (`dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share`) would reach for. **Measured separately the same day: `Capability.tier` carries no schema description at all**, so nothing tells an agent what it means or how it relates to `Component.level`. Three ladders exist, and all three are close to empty. ⇒ **THE HONEST READING OF ALL THREE NUMBERS: reflow2's design is not flat because someone weighed depth and chose against it. It is flat because the depth vocabulary was never filled in.** That is a different fact from 'horizontal is right here', and it means the composition-versus-inheritance question **cannot be settled from this design's shape** — the evidence is absence of modelling, not evidence of a considered choice. Which is exactly what option (b) below already warned it would be measuring. ════════════ THE ORIGINAL CAPTURE, 2026-08-14 ════════════ HIS WORDS: *'I almost want 'missing the wood for the trees' to be a skill of reflow2. that sometimes somebody becomes so wrapped up in some little detail that they forget the big picture… another way to look at it is 'breadth' vs 'depth' of a design… you can probably error in going too far in one dimension without considering the other dimension - need to find the correct balance. not sure if there is a way to measure in a graph depth vs breadth? if it can be measured, then there probably becomes a ratio of depth-to-breadth that is ideal to maintain. maybe in a graph you can count all the nodes (peer to peer nodes and this is your horizontal score). then count all the components nodes that make up a system (kind of looking at system-of-systems to systems to components and so on) and this is your depth score.'* ═══ ✅ YES, IT IS MEASURABLE, AND HIS PROPOSED SHAPE IS THE RIGHT ONE ═══ Run on reflow2's own export (`c18a4a1`, 2026-08-14): ``` DEPTH BREADTH Components ................ 56 lateral edges ........... 203 component CONTAINS ........ 42 DEPENDS_ON 178 · CONSUMES 15 MAX NESTING DEPTH ......... 2 PROVIDES 6 · INTERACTS_WITH 4 components with no parent . 14 hierarchical edges ...... 122 CONTAINS DECOMPOSES edges .......... 0 + 0 DECOMPOSES Component.level used: component 48, subsystem 8 system 0, system_of_systems 0, enterprise 0 Requirements 164 · Capabilities 161, all at one level ``` 🛑 **REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN IS ALMOST PURE BREADTH.** 164 requirements with **zero** decomposition; 56 components nested at most **two** deep, using two of five `level` values; 14 components parented by nothing. **The project built around `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` — *'nested as deep as the design needs'*, which Anthony called *'one of the primary things I designed it for'* — has a flat design.** ═══ ⚠️ A CORRECTION MADE BEFORE THIS NODE WAS SAVED, AND IT MATTERS ═══ This session first wrote that the blind spot had **doubled from 6 to 14** since 2026-08-07. **That was wrong.** `fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure` already recorded BOTH numbers on the same day — `components_outside_any_subsystem: 6` and `component_roots: 14` — as two different measures, not a before and after. **The truth is less dramatic and arguably worse: the numbers are IDENTICAL a week later.** `hierarchy_issues` 0, roots 14, max_depth 2, `DECOMPOSES` 0 — a fully measured defect, unchanged. 📌 The error was caught by the near-duplicate guard surfacing that node — the same guard this session has documented firing wrongly seven times today. **Here it was right, and it prevented a false claim entering the record.** ═══ WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW HERE, beyond the 2026-08-07 measurement ═══ · `Component.level` uses **two of five** values — nothing is a `system`, `system_of_systems` or `enterprise`. The ladder his idea depends on is three-fifths unused. · **Lateral 203 vs hierarchical 122** — the breadth/depth contrast stated as a single comparison, which is his proposed metric and which nothing computes today. · `DEPENDS_ON` has grown 171 → 178 in the week while `DECOMPOSES` stayed at 0. **The design is getting wider and no deeper**, which is the trend his idea is for and which no report shows. · 📌 **IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCE FOR WORK ACCEPTED EARLIER TODAY:** `cap:decomposition-coverage-is-asked` is planned to ask whether a decomposition's children cover their parent. **With 0 `DECOMPOSES` edges it cannot be dogfooded on this graph at all** — it would ship doing nothing here and nobody would notice. Not an argument against building it; an argument for testing it elsewhere. (BUILT 2026-08-14, PR #181, and it shipped saying exactly this about itself.) ═══ ⚠️ THE 'IDEAL RATIO' IS THE OVERFIT THIS IDEA EXISTS TO PREVENT ═══ **A depth-to-breadth target derived from any one design is exactly the specialisation Anthony warned against in the same message.** A house, a beamline, a shop and an MCP server share no natural proportion, and `req:design-anything` forbids binding the tool to one discipline's habits. Two recorded failures agree: · `evaluate_allocation` reports **modularity 1.0 from `total_internal: 1, total_external: 0`** — a perfect score over ONE dependency while the graph holds 178 `DEPENDS_ON` edges. **A ratio over a starved denominator is that failure again.** · BL-5's lesson, in `detect.rs`: **a loud detector needs a different QUESTION, not a tuned number.** ⭐⭐ **THE ANTIDOTE IS ALREADY BUILT: `granularity_report`.** It answers a structurally identical question — *is the build coarser than the design?* — and its contract says *'IT NEVER SAYS 'monolith', 'too big' or 'split it', carries NO severity… THERE IS NO SIZE THRESHOLD: artifacts are compared against THIS DESIGN'S OWN DISTRIBUTION.'* ⇒ **A breadth/depth measure should report the numbers and the design's own distribution, name what it cannot see, and refuse a verdict.** No universal ideal, no target, no severity. `fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure` reaches the same conclusion from the other side: *'what is wrong is a metric reporting a value at all when its denominator is one, instead of saying it has too little to measure.'* ═══ AND ON THE SKILL ITSELF ═══ ⚠️ **A SKILL ALONE REPEATS A FAILURE THIS PROJECT HAS MEASURED REPEATEDLY.** 'Step back and look at the whole' is exactly what a session under load stops doing; `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` exists because an agent keeps adding nodes while the loop silently stops, and `dec:idea-a-capture-session-skill-the-user-types` settled that the manual trigger is the only one not depending on the mechanism that keeps failing. **A wood-for-trees skill nobody remembers to invoke is the joke telling itself.** OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) **A USER-TYPED SKILL, NO METRIC.** Cheap, reliable trigger (human). Counter: tells the user little they did not already suspect when they typed it. (b) ⭐ **MEASURE + SKILL, ON `granularity_report`'s NO-THRESHOLD SHAPE** — report depth, breadth and this design's own distribution; refuse a verdict; the skill puts the question. Counter: needs an honest answer to *what counts as depth* while `DECOMPOSES` is unused and `Component.level` is three-fifths empty — today it would mostly be reporting **absence of modelling** rather than a property of the system. ⭐ **THE RE-MEASUREMENT ABOVE STRENGTHENS THIS COUNTER: with `Capability.tier` also one-valued, ALL THREE depth ladders are near-empty, so a measure shipped today would report unfilled fields in three places and call it shape.** (c) **A RATIO WITH A TARGET.** Argued against above on this node's own evidence. (d) **NOTHING — `where-am-i` re-orients already.** Counter: it reports what the design SAYS and has no notion of proportion; it surfaced none of the numbers above. 📌 THE HONEST OPEN QUESTION UNDER ALL OF IT: is reflow2's flat shape a DEFECT, or a correct reading of a system that genuinely has 56 peer components and little natural hierarchy? **The measure cannot answer that and must not pretend to** — which is why `granularity_report` refuses a verdict, and why this stays a question rather than becoming a check. ⚠️ **AND THE RE-MEASUREMENT NARROWS EVEN THAT: with three ladders unfilled, the flatness is at least partly unmodelled rather than observed, so this design cannot be the evidence either way.**		Captured under the brainstorm skill and measured on reflow2's own export before anything was written, because the central question — can depth and breadth be counted — is answerable rather than arguable. The measurement confirmed his proposed shape works and showed this design is nearly all breadth despite being built around recursive decomposition. A wrong claim is recorded in the node rather than quietly dropped: this session asserted the unparented-component count had doubled, and the prior fact node showed both figures were taken the same day, so the real finding is that a fully measured defect is unchanged a week later. The 'ideal ratio' half is argued against rather than deferred, since a target derived from one design is the specialisation he raised the idea to avoid, and `granularity_report` already demonstrates the correct pattern — report the distribution, name what cannot be seen, refuse the verdict.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 answer 'what order can this increment be built in, and what is buildable now?'
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled. THE OBSERVATION: capabilities form a DEPENDS_ON DAG that detect_defects insists stays acyclic, and NOTHING ever asks what order it implies. reflow2 can say what is scheduled for an increment (SCHEDULED_FOR) and what is delivered (the golden thread), but not what can be started. THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::topological_sort — Kahn's, deterministic (lexicographically smallest order), returns None on a cycle. Two distinct uses: (a) A SIMPLIFICATION available today: budget.rs:312 hand-rolls Kahn's algorithm in about forty lines with a comment that says so. The foundation exports it. (b) A NEW capability: given the capabilities scheduled for an increment, a valid build order — and the frontier of what has no unbuilt dependency, which is 'what can I pick up now'. WHERE IT LANDS: BL-68 (TRL/MRL readiness gating) is about whether something is ready; this is about whether its DEPENDENCIES are ready, which is the other half of the same question. Also epoch planning. CHEAP for (a). Moderate for (b), which needs a scope (a whole design? one increment? one component's subtree?) and a rendering. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS: (a) is not free — the local version works on string-id arcs while the foundation one needs a Graph built through GraphBuilder, so it trades forty lines of Kahn's for an impedance adapter, and the local one is already tested. (b) risks asserting a schedule reflow2 has no business asserting: a topological order is ONE valid order of many, and presenting it as THE order would be the same overreach dec:report-dont-judge exists to prevent. The honest output is probably the READY FRONTIER (what is unblocked) rather than a full ordering. Filed as a backlog row on Anthony's word (2026-08-01) — the work is tracked; the shape, especially frontier-vs-order, is open.		Found by grepping reflow2 for any existing ordering concept and hitting a hand-rolled Kahn's in budget.rs — evidence both that the need is real and that the foundation function was not known to be there.proposednothing
IDEA — in acquisition work the formal documents ARE the artefact: design reviews, authorisations to proceed, official direction. Could the graph hold them well enough that an organisation trusts it and stops keeping external docs?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-08-15, framed by him as aspiration rather than intent — his own words end \'but I don't think we are there yet\', preserved here as part of the idea rather than trimmed off it.\n\nHIS WORDS: \'in some designs, actual design reviews are done and official direction to proceed and other formal docs are required (coming from the US Air Force and US Space Force, documentation is required — maybe we can eventually get to where the graph tracks authorizations to proceed or other official acquisitions documents are in the graph and organizations trust the graph to hold such docs and therefore, keeping external docs is no longer needed — but I don't think we are there yet).\'\n\nDELIBERATELY DISTINCT FROM `rule:design-information-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-documents`, which the guard named because this node cites it. THAT RULE GOVERNS THIS REPOSITORY and is settled and enforced. THIS IS A QUESTION ABOUT THE PRODUCT, in a domain where a document is not a convenience: a signed authorisation to proceed is what makes work lawful to start, and whether an organisation will rely on a graph instead is a question about trust, audit and legal standing rather than about storage. The rule can hold while this stays open, and it does.\n\nWHAT ALREADY POINTS THIS WAY, so the starting position is not zero: `Contributor` with `AUTHORED_BY role: approver` records whose sign-off a node carries and when (`acted_at`); `Decision` with `status: accepted` records that something was settled and by whose word; `DesignEpoch` records when; and this project has already settled that rendered pages are ONLY projections of the graph rather than documents in their own right. An authorisation is structurally an approver plus a date plus a scope plus a decision — all four of which the schema can already say.\n\nWHAT IS MISSING IS NOT VOCABULARY, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART: it is EVIDENCE and NON-REPUDIATION. The graph can record that somebody approved something; it cannot today demonstrate to a third party that they did, that the record has not moved since, or that the approver had the authority. A `status: accepted` written by an agent and one written by a general are the same bytes.\n\nTHE OPTIONS:\n\n(a) DO NOTHING; FORMAL DOCUMENTS STAY EXTERNAL and the graph points at them with `Artifact.location`. HONEST TODAY, costs nothing, and matches his own concession that a pointer \'might be okay\'. COUNTER: it is exactly the arrangement the no-documents rule was made to end, so the product would be telling consumers to do what this project forbids itself.\n\n(b) THE GRAPH HOLDS THE AUTHORISATION AS TYPED NODES, the signed document stays external as evidence. Cheap, mostly expressible already. COUNTER: it splits the record — authority in the graph, proof in a file — which is the worst of both for an auditor.\n\n(c) THE GRAPH HOLDS THE BYTES TOO. A signed PDF is precisely \'what the graph cannot hold inline\', the sentence `cap:content-store` was built around — BUILT, VERIFIED, AND DISCONTINUED on his word on 2026-08-09 for zero use across three projects (`dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued`). ⭐ THIS WOULD BE THE FIRST REAL USE THAT DISCONTINUATION SAID DID NOT EXIST. COUNTER, and it is his own from that decision: bytes in a repo grow without bound, and in flo2 could reach terabytes needing backup, security and per-project separation — all MORE true, not less, for controlled or classified acquisition documents.\n\n(d) THE DOCUMENT IS DERIVED FROM THE GRAPH — the official record is generated as a rendering, so there is one source and the document is an output rather than an input. Consistent with the settled doctrine that pages are only renderings. COUNTER: a rendering is not a signature. Something must still capture the act of approval by a person with authority, and that act happens outside reflow2.\n\n⚠️ THE HONEST BLOCKER, stated so it is not rediscovered: whether an organisation trusts a graph is not a feature reflow2 can build. It is earned through audit, retention policy, access control and someone accepting liability. Everything above is necessary and none of it sufficient, and a version that shipped the mechanics while implying the trust would be the most damaging overclaim this project could make.\n\nNOT ESTABLISHED: whether any real programme would accept it; what standard would have to be met (none has been named); and whether this is one question or two — TRACKING authorisations, versus BEING the authoritative record.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Started as a new node rather than merged into the rule after the guard named it: the rule governs this repository and is settled, while this asks whether the product could carry legal-weight documents for someone else — different scope, different decider, and merging them would bury a product question inside a house rule. His \'I don't think we are there yet\' is preserved inside the idea, because a later reader would otherwise read the aspiration as a plan.proposednothing
OPEN — when the owner is happy with the current state, can everything not yet accepted or built be cleared in one deliberate act?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12, and he said plainly at capture time that he expects this to stay unaccepted — he wanted it on the record, not enacted. Nothing here is settled. HIS WORDS: 'should we have a 'purge' skill. I'm getting pretty happy with how reflow2 is now. There are a lot of still unrealized ideas and gaps that we still should work through, but say I'm happy with the current state of the project - can I just 'purge' all the additional things not yet accepted or built? It is a destructive action, but sometimes I'd like to continue reflow2 without every decision and thing I've submitted.' ⭐ THE NEED IS REAL AND ALREADY EVIDENCED. `fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input` records that he pours instructions, ideas, feedback and requirements in as they occur to him. That is the tool working as intended, and its cost is exactly what he is describing: the open list grows faster than anyone decides on it, and eventually it stops being a to-do list and becomes noise. ═══ WHAT THIS WOULD TOUCH, MEASURED 2026-08-12 ═══ Decision proposed 104 of 341 carrying 248 edges 2 edgeless Requirement proposed 47 of 156 carrying 151 edges 0 edgeless Capability planned 37 of 151 carrying 150 edges 0 edgeless ───────────────────────────────── 188 nodes, ~549 edges 🛑🛑 AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHOULD DECIDE THIS: **26 OF THE 47 PROPOSED REQUIREMENTS ARE ALREADY SATISFIED BY SOMETHING.** They are built. Their status simply never moved off `proposed`, because status moves only on the owner's word and nobody went back to say so. A purge keyed on 'not yet accepted' would delete more than half its own target set WRONGLY — deleting delivered work along with the speculation. That is not a hypothesis. It is `req:supporting-is-not-conflict` at scale: during the 2026-07-30 prune that requirement was proposed for dropping as 'an orphan in all but name', and checking its single edge revealed it was DELIVERED, by a `realized` capability. The lesson recorded then was 'low edge count was read as low value, and for a requirement that has been built, edge count is exactly backwards'. One hand-check caught one instance; the same reflex applied in bulk would now be wrong 26 times. ═══ THE PART THAT MAY MAKE THIS UNNECESSARY ═══ ⭐ **THE THING HE WANTS MAY ALREADY EXIST, AND IT IS NOT DELETION.** `dec:proposed-requirements-pruned` (accepted, his own word, 2026-07-30) already did this once by hand — nine of twenty-six requirements retired — and its finding is the direct answer here: > 'All are `dropped`, not deleted... `dropped` also stops them raising `unsatisfied_requirement`, so the open list means what it says again.' So the BENEFIT he is asking for — an open list that means something again — is delivered by the STATUS CHANGE. Deletion adds nothing to that and additionally destroys the reasoning. That decision's rationale states the cost of going further: 'Deleting them would erase why the surviving rules are shaped as they are, and would let the same captures be re-made next quarter by someone who could not see they had been weighed.' The `retire-from-design` skill already carries dropped-not-deleted as its central distinction. So what is missing is not the ACT; it is doing it in BATCH, and being prompted when the list has grown enough to be worth doing — the same shape as `dec:idea-the-graph-notices-the-record-moved-without-being-asked`, where the tool existed and the trigger did not. ═══ THE OPTIONS ═══ A — A BATCH DROP, never a delete. A skill that walks the unaccepted set in classes, proposes a disposition per class, and moves status to `dropped`/`deferred` on his word. Reuses existing vocabulary; nothing is lost; the open list clears. EXPENSIVE: it is 188 nodes, and a batch under one shared reason is precisely what `acknowledge_gaps` already REFUSES by design — 'a batch under one shared reason is exactly the erosion the ask-don't-repair rule exists to prevent'. So the batching has to be per-class with a stated reason each, which is what made the 2026-07-30 prune trustworthy and also what made it slow. B — ACTUAL DELETION. What he literally asked for. Cheapest to state, and the only option that genuinely reduces graph size. EXPENSIVE, and the objections are unusually concrete: 549 edges would go with the nodes; the 26 delivered-but-unmarked requirements would go with them; and `dec:ask-not-repair` plus the whole `apply_heal` design exist to stop reflow2 destroying design without a human asserting each case. C — SNAPSHOT-THEN-CLEAR. Export the design first, then drop hard, on the argument that git holds the memory. EXPENSIVE, and this is the one worth thinking hardest about: a design nobody can query is not memory. `search_design` cannot reach a node that only exists in a file, so 'it is in git' means 'nobody will ever find it again'. The whole point of the graph over documents is that the record is QUERYABLE. D — DO NOTHING NEW. `retire-from-design` exists and works; the 2026-07-30 prune proves it. What is missing is a nudge when the unaccepted set crosses some size. Free. EXPENSIVE: he has now asked for this, which is evidence the existing route is not discoverable at the moment he wants it. E — FIX THE UPSTREAM CAUSE INSTEAD. 26 of 47 are stale STATUS, not surplus intent. A pass that asks 'these 26 look delivered — accept them?' would shrink the open list by more than half WITHOUT dropping anything, and would make the remaining list honest. Not a purge at all; possibly the thing that removes most of the felt need. ═══ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea rather than used to kill it ═══ The brainstorm skill's own closing rule is that roads not taken are part of the design's memory — 'recorded as considered, never deleted... a later session that finds an old idea knows both that it was thought of and that it was not chosen.' A purge is the direct negation of that rule. If it is ever built, that rule has to be revisited deliberately rather than quietly broken, because half of what makes this graph worth keeping is that it remembers what was rejected and why. ⚠️ AND A SCOPE NOTE: 'not yet accepted or built' is not one population. A `proposed` Decision that is an OPEN QUESTION is not surplus — it is unfinished thinking, and deleting it discards the question rather than answering it. A `planned` Capability nobody will build is different again. Any version of this has to say which of the three it means; the measurement above keeps them apart for that reason. NOT DECIDED, and expected by its author to stay that way.		Captured on Anthony's explicit instruction to record it without pursuing it — 'I expect this one to stay non-accepted, but I did want to capture.' That is the funnel working exactly as `fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input` describes, and this node is itself an instance of the thing it proposes purging, which is worth noticing. The measurement is what makes it worth keeping rather than merely polite: 26 of 47 proposed requirements are already satisfied, so the felt problem is substantially STALE STATUS rather than surplus intent, and option E addresses more of it than any purge would. The 2026-07-30 prune already established dropped-not-deleted and recorded that `dropped` alone restores the open list — so the benefit sought here is reachable without the destruction.proposednothing
OPEN — how should a corpus like dev_storyflow's 1,124 documents actually be mass-ingested?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-04, while BL-186 was mid-build: 'maybe we setup an exploratory brainstorm and branch discussing the various ways that we could mass-ingest something like in dev_storyflow. then we can systematically test some different strategies and observe/measure which performs the best.' Nothing here is chosen, and no option below has been costed by running it. THE CASE, MEASURED (dev_storyflow, `/home/ajs7/project/dev_storyflow`, read-only): 1,124 markdown files, 22 MB, ~6M tokens of source text. 17 files at depth 1 and 1,107 below it, so a non-recursive ingest reads 1.5% of the corpus and reports nothing missing. docs/archive 333 files / 16.2 MB (73% of the volume, dated superseded board snapshots); memory/ 380; docs/evidence 195 md + 744 binaries; the plausibly design-bearing remainder is 216 files / 3.3 MB. The fleet's own survey (`reflow2_feedback.md`, api-boss 07426210) read samples rather than filenames and found docs/evidence is at least FIVE types, and that 102 of 334 memory files are unbuilt product intent that reflow2 already models — so a filename-level exclusion of memory/ would be wrong. (a) INGEST EVERYTHING, RECURSIVELY, NO SELECTION. Cheapest to specify, and the only option needing no human judgement. Expensive to run (~6M tokens before the per-pass multiplier) and the yield is poor: a design dominated by 333 superseded archives. Counter-argument that is specific rather than general — the archives are dated snapshots of the SAME few boards, so they are near-identical to each other, and the DUPLICATES bridge built for corpus-scale asking would turn them into thousands of standing questions. The mechanism that makes batched asking possible is the same one that makes an unselected corpus unusable. (b) PLAN THEN INGEST (directory triage). Walk the tree, group by directory, report counts + bytes + sample names, put THAT to the user as one batched ask about scope before any document is extracted. Cheap, one round, and it puts the judgement where it belongs — reflow2 cannot know that `archive/` is superseded, and hardcoding a skip-list is the 'shaping the model until the tool goes quiet' failure docs/sharpening.md names. Honest counter-argument: directory-level judgement is wrong at file level, and the fleet's own deeper read proves it — docs/evidence holds 5 runbooks and 50 root-cause memos that are knowledge, not evidence, and excluding the directory loses them. (c) CLASSIFY THEN ROUTE. A cheap per-document classification pass first (design intent / evidence / archive / doctrine / hazard), then route by kind: intent gets the full extraction, evidence becomes an Artifact with an anchor, archive is skipped or marked pending_expansion. More calls but each tiny, and it matches what the corpus actually is rather than what its folders are named. Counter-argument: it adds a classifier whose errors are invisible, and it is the option most likely to quietly mis-file the thing you care about. (d) EXPLOIT THE CORPUS'S OWN SELF-LABELLING. It already declares itself: 102/334 memory files say FUTURE/parked, evidence files pin commit SHAs, grounding docs are headed 'READ-ONLY GROUNDING (no code, no build)'. Zero model cost for the signal. Counter-argument, measured: 117 of 334 memory files declare no type at all, and the fleet's filename convention and its frontmatter schema already disagree (`tech_` is 67 by filename and 6 by declared type) — so the labels cover most of the corpus and are silent exactly where it is messiest. (e) HIGH-VALUE-FIRST, INCREMENTALLY. Ingest docs/architecture (20), docs/decisions (6), docs/grounding (34), briefs and the root planning docs — the 216-file remainder — measure the design that results, then decide whether more is worth it. Fastest to first value, and it composes with the resume story already settled on BL-186 (the graph IS the resume point; sweep the folder, diff against registered Fragments, the remainder is the work left). Counter-argument: it answers 'is this useful' and not 'does this scale', which is the question BL-186 exists to answer. WHAT A TRIAL WOULD HAVE TO MEASURE, since none of the above is decidable by argument: documents ingested per unit cost; nodes created against merge candidates raised (signal to noise); how many candidates a HUMAN then has to rule on; coverage_report claimed against unclaimed; and the only test that actually matters, which the scope doc already states — 'whether an agent reading 500 heterogeneous markdown files produces a design a human recognises is a trial, not an argument, and it should be run on a real folder before anyone promises this to a user.'		Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the options survive as options. Anthony proposed trialling several strategies and measuring which performs best; this node holds the strategies, and dec:idea-trial-driven-choice-skill holds the separate question of whether reflow2 should have a way to run that kind of trial at all. Measurements of dev_storyflow are exact greps taken 2026-08-04; the type judgements are the fleet's own from reflow2_feedback.md, not mine — my earlier filename-level read of memory/ was wrong and is corrected above.proposednothing
OPEN — should a finding say HOW two nodes are coupled, not only that they are?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled. THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::shortest_path (unused) returns the actual Path between two nodes. Two readings on a design graph: (a) surprising_connections reports that two things bridge separate communities. It does not say through what. The path is the explanation a human needs before acting. (b) 'Why is this node in my blast radius?' propagate reports hop distance and impact direction; a named path is the artifact a person can read and check. CHEAP: exact, already a dependency, and both call sites already hold the network. WHERE IT LANDS: this is the BL-114 family again from a third direction — a finding that states a conclusion without stating the evidence it walked. BL-141(a) has just done exactly this for circular_dependency (name the contracts the cycle ran through), and that change was small and immediately useful on real data. The same argument applies here. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a shortest path is not necessarily the RESPONSIBLE path — several may exist, and showing one implies a causal story that may not be the operative one. BL-141(a) sidestepped this by naming the SET of contracts involved rather than a single route; the equivalent here might be 'the edge types this coupling runs through' rather than one path. Worth deciding which before building.		Grouped with the explain-what-you-walked family (BL-114, BL-141a) rather than presented as a new idea, because that is what it is — the third instance of the same shape.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 federate heterogeneous designs across organisations the way OpenMBEE does, rather than composing exports?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a FIRST-PASS REVIEW OF openmbee.org — the website, the GitHub org listing and one (truncated) architecture page. Nothing here rests on reading their source or running it. Anthony intends to clone the repo for a deep review, and every reading below should be re-tested then. THE OBSERVATION: OpenMBEE's stated purpose is 'an open source collaborative engineering system' that 'enables engineers to work in the language of their choice and easily share and document their work across other tools', with the tagline 'Edit once, use everywhere'. Its answer to multi-organisation, multi-tool work is LINKED DATA — an RDF quadstore where the fourth term is a named graph, so many contexts coexist in one repository, plus transclusion so one source of truth appears in many places. WHY THIS IS THE AREA WHERE THEY ARE PLAINLY AHEAD OF reflow2, and it is not a small one: it is precisely the operating context Anthony described — several organisations with competing, partially-built, differently-motivated designs that must be made to interoperate although they were never designed to. reflow2 has `req:design-composes`, `compose_and_analyse`, `pair_designs` and `mirror_surface`, and `dec:linked-repos-poc` has sat PARKED since it was filed. Those compose EXPORTS — whole documents, pairwise — where OpenMBEE federates a live graph across repositories. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is strong: reflow2 already decided against the architecture that makes their approach possible. `dec:repo-file-embedded` (the graph lives as a repo file, embedded, not a service) and `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (many writers keep the repo file and merge on pull — no hosted service) are the opposite answer to the same question, taken deliberately. A quadstore federation is a service, and adopting the capability may mean reopening those. NOTE ALSO that `dec:central-host` and `dec:live-tier` are BOTH still proposed in this design — OpenMBEE is a fairly complete picture of what saying yes to them costs and buys, which makes it evidence for those two questions whether or not this one is ever answered. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether federation can be had at the EXPORT seam — `export_surface` and `mirror_surface` already publish a subset — rather than requiring a live shared store.		Recorded through the brainstorm skill because this is an idea from a landscape review, not intent Anthony has stated. He asked for the areas where OpenMBEE is stronger to be captured as proposed ideas ahead of a deep review, in those words. DELIBERATELY LEFT UNLINKED: `describe_schema {from: Decision, to: Decision}` reports that NO edge type models the pair and that the seventeen which validate do so only through a `*` wildcard — 'validating is not the same as meaning what you intend… prefer leaving the edge out to asserting one that is wrong'. So this will surface as an `orphan_node` info finding, exactly as `dec:linked-repos-poc` does, and that is the true description of a parked idea rather than a defect to route around.proposednothing
OPEN — how should two designs be paired: declared pair types, a shared contract artifact, or (SETTLED) the user asserting the correspondence and reflow2 refining it?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-13, extending his own RNA analogy. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen. HIS WORDS: 'going back to the RNA pairing discussion, can we have each project have a set of defined pair types that could facilitate the combining if two projects in a much faster manner?' — and, earlier in the same message, the shape he was reaching for: 'not sure if one project carries a set of one side of the pairs and that would allow the other project to only line up with its corresponding pair on the other side.' ⭐ THE ANALOGY IS PRECISE ABOUT WHY PAIRING IS FAST, and that is the real content of the idea. Four bases, two valid pairs, an alphabet fixed by chemistry. Matching is a LOOKUP, not a comparison. reflow2 today does comparison: `req:complementary-pairing` keys on `medium` PLUS `transport_security` PLUS `auth`, then falls back to fuzzy name resolution with a reported middle band a human must answer. Declared pair types would replace the fuzzy step with an exact one. 🛑 AND THE ANALOGY ALSO NAMES ITS OWN LIMIT, which is the honest counterweight. Bases pair by an alphabet that chemistry fixes GLOBALLY and nobody negotiates. Two organisations have no chemistry. A shared pair-type vocabulary requires prior agreement between the parties — and working WITHOUT prior agreement is exactly what the attribute key buys, in exactly the cross-organisation context reflow2 states as its operating breadth. The idea's power and its limit come from the same property. ═══ THE OPTIONS ═══ A — NOTHING. The attribute key already pairs two designs that never coordinated. Faster matching is not obviously the constraint. CHEAPEST, and the null hypothesis. B — A DECLARED PAIR-TYPE VOCABULARY, his idea literally: each project publishes named types, and combining is a type-name join. FASTEST when both sides share the vocabulary; USELESS when they do not, and worse than useless if two orgs use one name for different contracts — a false pair is more dangerous than no pair, which is the failure the dynograph-foundation trial already produced once from the provider side. C — ⭐ USE `SPECIFIES`, WHICH ALREADY EXISTS AND HAS NEVER BEEN DRAWN. The schema carries it: 'A machine-readable contract artifact defines an entity — an OpenAPI / protobuf / JSON-schema / IDL file SPECIFIES an Interface (its authoritative contract)', with a `format` property. MEASURED 2026-08-13: **zero SPECIFIES edges in reflow2's design.** If two designs' Interfaces are both specified by the SAME artifact, matched on content hash, that is exact pairing with NO vocabulary to negotiate — THE HASH IS THE AGREEMENT. It is the ICD made first-class, which `Interface.designation` already gestures at when it cites 10 U.S.C. 4401 and 'what an ICD publishes'. Needs no new node type, no new edge type, no enum change, and no stamp move. D — HYBRID, AND THE ONE THAT DEGRADES HONESTLY: exact when a shared contract artifact is present, attribute-key-plus-fuzzy-name when it is not. Two designs that have agreed get a precise seam; two that have not still get today's answer. Costs a second matching path and a rule for which wins. ═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══ ⚠️ 1. THE STRONGEST — SPEED IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT, AND MAY NEVER BE. reflow2's own frontier reads seams 0% : ZERO of 73 component couplings run through a declared Interface. There is nothing to pair yet. Optimising the matching step while nothing is labelled is optimising past the actual blocker, which is that boundaries are unclassified. 📌 STATUS 2026-08-13: PARTLY ADDRESSED. `cap:undeclared-seam-is-named` shipped (PR #167) and now NAMES those 73 pairs as one aggregate gap. It does not declare them — it asks. The blocker is now visible rather than silent. ⚠️ 2. THE FUZZY MIDDLE BAND IS NOT A DEFECT TO REMOVE. Asking a human about an uncertain name match is `dec:ask-not-repair` working as designed. Replacing it with exact lookup removes the question by removing the cases that raise it — which is only an improvement where the shared vocabulary is real. ⚠️ 3. A SHARED VOCABULARY IS A COORDINATION COST, and this project spends heavily to avoid exactly that: `dec:identity-out-of-band` refuses a registry that hands out ids, `dec:advisory-concurrency` refuses a lock manager. A pair-type registry is the same shape as the things twice rejected. ⚠️ 4. `SPECIFIES` IS UNUSED, SO THE SUBSTRATE IS UNTESTED. Zero edges means option C's mechanism has never run on real data, and every linking defect this project has found came from running the thing rather than reading it. 📌 WHERE THE IDEA IS STRONGEST, and it is narrower than 'a vocabulary': WITHIN ONE OWNER'S NEIGHBOURHOOD. Ten reflow2 designs live under ~/project, all Anthony's. A shared pair-type vocabulary across designs one person controls is entirely achievable, needs no negotiation, and would make combining them mechanical. It is the cross-ORGANISATION case that cannot assume it — so the honest question may be whether reflow2 supports both, with the vocabulary as an optional accelerator over an attribute-based floor. That is option D. ═══════════ SHARPENED 2026-08-13, SAME SESSION ═══════════ Anthony then described the combining PROCESS step by step: 'can first filter out interfaces in a graph. secondly, of the interfaces, can they be labeled as publisher, subscriber, or both. then you kind of have 3 RNA pairs. the agent then has the job of mapping publishers with subscribers (one RNA pair) and both with both. if the agent is unable to pair based on reason, you now have a gap or issue to solve.' ⭐⭐ THE FIRST FINDING IS THAT HE RE-DERIVED THE BUILT ALGORITHM, and this is recorded as a NON-finding on purpose rather than filed as new. Verified against `crates/reflow2-core/src/seam.rs:464` rather than assumed: `offers = published | both`, `needs = required | both`. Three labels, four valid combinations — published↔required, published↔both, both↔required, both↔both — never like-with-like, which `two_publishers_never_pair_with_each_other` pins as a test. And the unpairable DO become findings, in five buckets: `paired` (the seam), `unmet_needs` (a subscriber nothing publishes), `dead_surface` (a publisher nobody subscribes to), `conflicts` (role-compatible but cannot connect on medium/transport_security/auth), `candidates` (the fuzzy middle band — the code comment reads 'worth a human's attention, never acted on'). The RNA analogy was his on 2026-07-27 and produced `req:complementary-pairing`. Reasoning from it again nine days later reproduced the same algorithm from a different starting point. THAT IS CORROBORATION, NOT REPETITION — an analogy that regenerates the same structure twice is doing work rather than decorating a decision already made. 🛑 AND THE ONE GENUINE DELTA: 'if the agent is unable to pair BASED ON REASON'. His version has an AGENT JUDGEMENT step. The built version has none — pairing is a computed key end to end, and no LLM is consulted at any point. That opens three further options: E — THE AGENT PROPOSES ON `candidates`, THE GRAPH STILL COUNTS, THE HUMAN STILL DECIDES. Let an agent argue for or against each middle-band pair in prose, ATTACHED to the candidate rather than resolving it. Exactly `dec:three-party-checks` — 'the LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides' — applied to a band that currently arrives with a score and no argument. A score says HOW CLOSE two names are; it never says WHY they might be the same contract. F — 📌 THE AGENT REASONS OVER `conflicts` INSTEAD, and this is the strongest narrow form. A conflict today says 'you publish REST/JWT/TLS, I need REST/none/none, we cannot connect' — true, and silent on whether that is a real incompatibility or one side simply never filled in `auth`. An agent that has read both designs can tell 'they left it unspecified' from 'these genuinely disagree', and those need opposite actions. This is the one place a computed answer is PROVABLY incomplete, because `unspecified` is the honest default on three of the key's fields and the key cannot distinguish silence from disagreement. G — THE AGENT PAIRS OUTRIGHT where the key is silent. RECORDED AS REJECTED-LEANING so it is not re-proposed by someone who has not read the trial: a false pair is worse than no pair, and the dynograph-foundation session already produced one from the computed side — 'I require REST' matching an unauthenticated liveness probe. An LLM guessing would be the same failure with less traceability. ⚠️ 5. A FURTHER COUNTER-ARGUMENT ON E: the candidate band exists precisely so a HUMAN decides. Putting an agent between the score and the person risks the band being cleared by argument rather than by judgement, which is the erosion `dec:ask-not-repair` is written against. ⚠️ 6. AND `unlabelled` MUST STILL BE COUNTED whatever is chosen. `req:complementary-pairing` already requires it: a boundary nobody classified must not read as `internal`, or a design that never did the labelling pairs with nothing and reports a clean seam. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ SHARPENED AGAIN 2026-08-13, AND THIS ONE MOVES THE QUESTION: LINKABILITY IS THE USER'S ASSERTION; REFLOW2'S JOB IS REFINEMENT ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ ANTHONY'S WORDS, and they settle what pairing is FOR: 'maybe it is too much for two+ projects just to be linked kind of in an ad-hoc approach (something like a user saying 'link projectA and ProjectB' and just turning it over to reflow2 and the agent to figure out how. in defining flo2, I knew from the get go that it was going to have to use reflow2. it became a much more measured/deliberate approach of having flo2 read the reflow2 code and graph and then identifying (the agent) how it'd interface' and then, decisively: 'I think the deliberate part of purposefully linking two projects is the user's responsibility that two projects can actually be linked. if projectA was a design for a house and ProjectB was design a python service for accounting, that is a failure on the user and ad-hoc/automatic linking can't occur (unless we do some very creative linking). I knew when I designed flo2 that it was going to use reflow2 - is the interface spec perfect? no, it is still in work, but I know the two projects can roughly interface with each other and precisely the point of all this is to use reflow2 to make a clearly defined and fully specified interface' ⭐⭐⭐ **THE CORRESPONDENCE IS AN INPUT, NOT AN OUTPUT.** That inverts the framing every option above assumed. reflow2 is not being asked whether a house design and an accounting service relate — asserting linkability is the USER'S job, and getting it wrong is a user error rather than a tool failure. What reflow2 is for is taking a roughly-known, still-in-work correspondence and driving it to a **clearly defined and fully specified interface**. ⇒ **WHICH MAKES `seam_report` THE LOAD-BEARING TOOL AND `pair_designs` THE CONVENIENCE**, and today the documentation has that backwards. `seam_report`'s own parameter doc reads: *'`pair_designs` computes these from complementary roles since 2026-07-30; supply them by hand only when a design has not declared its roles yet'* — treating the hand-supplied pair as a FALLBACK. Under Anthony's model the hand-supplied pair is the PRIMARY and correct input, and computed pairing is an accelerator for the case where nobody has asserted anything yet. ═══ MEASURED THE SAME DAY, AND IT SETTLES WHICH TOOL ANSWERS THE GOAL ═══ Full run recorded in `fact:reflow2-flo2-seam-measured-2026-08-13`. The two halves: COMPUTED (`pair_designs`, both designs as they stand) paired 0 · conflicts 10 · unmet_needs 5 · dead_surface 2 · candidates 1 and with the role corrected in memory, the TRUE seam scores 64 while a WRONG match (ifc:graph-export, sharing the word 'design') scores 81 and outranks it. ASSERTED (`seam_report`, pair supplied by hand: ifc:mcp-tools ↔ ifc:reflow2-design-api) agreed 3 · incompatible 0 · differs 0 · UNSTATED BY NOBODY 5 → auth, transport_security, operations, error_model, payload_schema ⇒ **THE ASSERTED PAIR PRODUCES EXACTLY THE ANSWER HIS GOAL ASKS FOR** — the two projects are compatible as far as anything is stated, and five named axes stand between 'roughly interfaces' and 'fully specified'. The computed path produced nothing usable on the same seam. That is the strongest evidence yet for the reframe, and it was obtained by RUNNING the two projects at each other rather than by reasoning about them. 🛑 AND IT CAUGHT REFLOW2 BEING THE UNDER-SPECIFIED SIDE. flo2 states `auth: none` and `transport_security: tls`; reflow2's own PUBLISHED `ifc:mcp-tools` states NEITHER — *'the side that assumed less finds out in production'*. Only a cross-project check surfaced it, which is an argument for linking as a DESIGN INSTRUMENT rather than only as a delivery step. ═══ WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT A/B/C/D, none of them yet taken ═══ · **A (nothing) is weakened.** Computed pairing found 0 on the one real seam and ranked a wrong match first; it is not currently sufficient for the deliberate case. · **B (pair-type vocabulary) is answered rather than chosen.** Anthony's own framing supplies what B was reaching for without a registry: the user ASSERTS the pair. No shared alphabet is negotiated because the assertion is per-link, not per-vocabulary. · **C (`SPECIFIES`) is now empirically motivated**, and is the durable form of the assertion: recording 'this boundary of mine IS that boundary of yours' at the moment it is authored, with the content hash as the agreement, rather than re-deriving it from names later. · **D (hybrid) survives unchanged** and is probably the shape: assertion first, computation as the accelerator. 📌 THE UNBUILT PIECE THIS EXPOSES: **there is no way to RECORD the correspondence.** flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api` exists BECAUSE someone read reflow2's `ifc:mcp-tools`; nothing in either graph says so, and the pair had to be re-supplied by hand at every run. `mirrors` on reflow2 returns 0, so the built mechanism for 'I designed against your published surface, pinned at this version' has never been used on the pair of projects that most obviously calls for it. **The pairing information was free at design time and thrown away.** NOT DECIDED.		Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent, and kept separate from the graph_id question because the two are unrelated. Worth keeping for one measured fact and one connection: SPECIFIES exists in the schema with a format property and has zero edges in reflow2's own design, so the mechanism for exact contract-based pairing is already built and never exercised; and the RNA analogy, which has already earned its place once by predicting that compatibility needs more than one point of contact, here argues BOTH ways — a fixed alphabet is why base pairing is fast AND why two organisations cannot borrow the trick. ⭐ THE AGENT-REASONING BRANCH IS SETTLED, 2026-08-13, ANTHONY'S WORD: 'I agree with the approach without an agent 'reasoning'.' Options E, F and G are CLOSED — no LLM enters the pairing loop, on candidates, on conflicts, or anywhere else. Pairing stays a computed key end to end. WHAT THAT COSTS, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATER AS A SURPRISE: option F was the strongest of the three and it named a real hole. A `conflict` says 'you publish REST/JWT/TLS, I need REST/none/none' and CANNOT distinguish a genuine disagreement from one side never having filled in `auth` — because `unspecified` is the honest default on three of the key's fields. That gap does not close by itself. It now has to be closed some other way, if it is closed at all: by a detector that reports HOW MUCH of a conflict rests on unspecified fields, by the pairing report naming which side was silent, or by a human reading the two boundaries. Declining the agent does not make the computed answer complete; it means the completion must be computed or asked, never inferred. WHY THIS IS CONSISTENT WITH THE PROJECT RATHER THAN A NARROWING OF IT: `dec:three-party-checks` gives the LLM the speaking role, not the counting one, and everything reflow2 computes is deliberately verdict-free — `granularity` refuses to call an observation a defect, `maturity` refuses to grade a band, `ility_report` refuses a score. An agent arguing a pair into or out of existence would be the LLM doing the counting. ⭐⭐ SHARPENED AGAIN 2026-08-13 AND THE QUESTION MOVED: Anthony settled that ASSERTING TWO PROJECTS CAN BE LINKED IS THE USER'S RESPONSIBILITY, not something reflow2 discovers — 'if projectA was a design for a house and ProjectB was a design for a python service for accounting, that is a failure on the user.' reflow2's job is refinement: taking a roughly-known correspondence and making it 'clearly defined and fully specified.' The correspondence is an INPUT. That was then MEASURED against flo2 the same day (fact:reflow2-flo2-seam-measured-2026-08-13) and the measurement backs it: computed pairing returned 0 paired and ranked a wrong match above the right one, while the hand-asserted pair returned 0 incompatible, 3 agreed and 5 axes stated by nobody — exactly the punch-list his goal asks for. It also caught reflow2's own published boundary being the under-specified side. A/B/C/D remain open, but B is answered rather than chosen (a per-link assertion needs no negotiated vocabulary) and C is now the durable form of the assertion rather than a theoretical preference.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 detect OWNERSHIP orphans: well-connected, realized, shipping, and nobody accountable?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, relayed via dev_storyflow's api-boss: \'If nothing else, we'll see what areas of the graph are not claimed by anyone (orphans). Not sure reflow2 has this feature to detect orphans in ownership.\' ⭐ IT IS A DIFFERENT AXIS FROM orphan_node, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT. orphan_node structurally disconnected — nothing says what it is FOR. ownership orphan well-connected, realized, verified, SHIPPING — and nobody accountable. ⚠️ A NODE CAN BE STRUCTURALLY PERFECT AND GOVERNANCE-ORPHANED, and that is the more dangerous state precisely because NOTHING ABOUT IT LOOKS WRONG. Every existing detector would pass it: it satisfies a requirement, a component holds it, an artifact realizes it, a check verifies it. The only thing missing is a person, and no detector asks about people. IT IS ALSO THE THIRD MEMBER OF A FAMILY THIS PROJECT FOUND TWICE TODAY, which is why it is worth naming as a class rather than a feature: - req:the-design-says-what-was-built-and-never-used — built, and NOTHING CONSUMES IT. - req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read — declared, and NOTHING READS IT. - this one — shipping, and NOBODY OWNS IT. Every existing gap asks what is MISSING FROM A NODE. All three of these ask what is missing AROUND a node, and none of the seven capability gaps can express that shape. STRICTLY DEPENDENT ON THE EDGE. There is nothing to detect the absence of until ownership is expressible — dec:idea-ownership-is-the-third-who-axis holds that question. Recorded separately for exactly that reason: the edge can exist without the detector, the detector cannot exist without the edge, and a single node holding both could only be half-answered. ⚠️ THE HARD PART, AND IT IS A DESIGN INPUT RATHER THAN A SETTING — api-boss's, and it is the strongest objection on the table: WHICH NODE TYPES ARE OWNABLE? In their 1,127-node graph most nodes legitimately have no owner; their example is exact — \'a Constraint about prose rendering is nobody's in the accountability sense.\' A naive detector therefore fires on the MAJORITY of a mature graph and becomes a signal trained to be ignored, which is the permanently-red-check failure this project has now written down three times. But in a two-person project the design is probably mostly partitioned, so the same detector is nearly silent and genuinely useful. ⇒ OWNABILITY LOOKS LIKE A PER-PROJECT DECLARATION, NOT A FIXED RULE, and the same feature behaves very differently at those two scales. THE SHAPES, with counters beside rather than argued down: (A) A GAP — `unowned_region`, one per ownable node with no owner. Appears in the loop where people already look. COUNTER: the ownability problem above hits this hardest, because a gap that fires on the majority is worse than no gap. (B) A REPORT — an ownership census: what is owned, by whom, and what is not, reported as a FACT the way granularity_report and surprising_connections are. Cannot nag. COUNTER: a report nobody runs is invisible; it would need a line in graph_report to be seen. (C) A COVERAGE NUMBER — \'N of M ownable nodes have an owner\', one line, the same shape as the trajectory bands and the certainty line. Cheapest to read, hardest to ignore, and it degrades gracefully at both scales because a low number in a fleet graph is a true statement rather than N nags. COUNTER: a number says nothing about WHICH, so it needs (B) behind it to be actionable. (D) SCOPED TO A DECLARED PARTITION — a project declares which types are ownable, and the detector only speaks about those. Answers the hard part directly. COUNTER: it is a new declaration to maintain, and an unmaintained one silently narrows the detector to nothing, which is the same class as an unread marker. ⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, and it is the trap all three of today's findings share: shipping the marker without the computation that reads it, or shipping a computation that fires on correct work. reflow2 has now met the first failure eight times over in its own edge vocabulary and has doctrine against the second in dec:read-hint-shape. NOTHING IS PROMOTED. Anthony raised the question and said he was not sure the feature existed; it does not.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill: `proposed`, options with counters, nothing promoted, and separated from the edge question it depends on so neither can be half-answered. Worth stating why this one is recorded at all when it cannot be built yet: it is the third instance in one day of a shape reflow2 has no vocabulary for — absence AROUND a node rather than absence IN it — and the other two were captured as intent this session. Recording it keeps the family visible; whether it becomes a fourth requirement is Anthony's call, not a consequence of the first three.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 detect DECLARED-BUT-UNREACHED vocabulary, when its own accepted rule that a distinction must earn its keep is itself unread?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, on being told that two retirement edges exist and neither is read: \'these are a new type of orphans that I never thought about and curious why until now haven't they surfaced? ... should reflow2 have something that detects these class of orphans, and are there other orphan developments (actually implemented design) that nothing detects or surfaces?\' ⚠️ PROVENANCE CORRECTION FIRST, because he asked what search produced the SUPERSEDES claim and the honest answer is NONE. It was read out of dec:one-retire-edge, which records a schema sweep another session ran on 2026-07-28. It was relayed as though freshly measured. THE MEASUREMENT BELOW WAS THEN ACTUALLY RUN, and it is what this node is for. === THE MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-09, against reflow2's own 1,869-node / 7,051-edge design === Method, stated because the first cut of it was too crude to trust: an edge type counts as REACHED if it is instantiated in this design, OR named in `structural_rule`'s propagation table (11 edges), OR named anywhere in non-test Rust outside its own `pub const` declaration. Anything failing all three is declared vocabulary with nothing behind it. EIGHT OF SIXTY EDGE TYPES ARE DECLARED AND UNREACHED ON EVERY TEST: COMPLIES_WITH · CONTAINS_EPOCH · EVOLVES_INTO · IMPOSES · MITIGATES · SUPERSEDES · SUPPLEMENTS · VIOLATES_RULE SEVEN OF TWENTY-NINE NODE TYPES HAVE ZERO INSTANCES HERE: Anchor · DimensionAssessment · DimensionObservation · EnvironmentRule · Flow · QualityGate · ReadinessAssessment FIVE MORE EDGE TYPES ARE INSTANTIATED BUT REACHED ONLY GENERICALLY — not in the propagation table, never named in code: ABOUT_ENTITY (117 instances), CAUSES (9), INTERACTS_WITH (4), OPERATES_IN (3), VALID_TO (2). These are not dead; they are unnamed, which means nothing would notice if they stopped working. ⭐ THREE OF THESE ALREADY HAVE INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, which is why this is a class and not a curiosity: - VIOLATES_RULE — dev_storyflow filed it HOURS before this measurement: `describe_schema{from:Component, to:DesignRule}` returns 17 candidates and VIOLATES_RULE is not among them, so a session doing the documented thing cannot discover the edge named for the job. They used VIOLATES instead and said it is presumably wrong. - QualityGate — dev_storyflow's governance trial, item ⑦: \'I could not find an honest use, and I think that is informative... Recording the decline, because 'the type exists and nobody instantiated it' is otherwise indistinguishable from nobody having tried.\' - Anchor — dec:anchor-retire-or-implement is already OPEN on exactly this: \'superseded by Snapshot but still advertised: retire it or implement it?\' === WHY IT NEVER SURFACED, which is his real question === EVERY DETECTOR IS INSTANCE-LEVEL AND THIS IS A VOCABULARY-LEVEL FACT. detect_gaps computes over nodes and edges that EXIST — unsatisfied_requirement needs a Requirement, disconnected_community needs a cluster of two or more, orphan_node needs a node. A declared type with zero instances produces NOTHING for any of them to anchor on. The blind spot is not an oversight in any one detector; it is that no detector asks a question ABOUT THE SCHEMA rather than about the design. ⭐⭐ AND THE SHARPEST PART: THE RULE ABOUT UNREAD THINGS IS ITSELF UNREAD. dec:edge-orthogonality is ACCEPTED and says a vocabulary distinction earns its keep ONLY IF A COMPUTATION READS IT — it is the decision that retired VALIDATES and ENABLES on precisely this reasoning. Nothing computes it. So the principle was applied ONCE, by hand, and the eight above accumulated afterwards with nobody to notice. === ARE THERE OTHER UNSURFACED ORPHAN DEVELOPMENTS? YES, AND ONE IS ALREADY OPEN === dec:bl-155 (OPEN): \'40 of 132 served tools were never called in the retained sample, and reflow2 cannot tell 'unused' from 'unreachable'.\' That is the same shape one level out — built surface nobody reaches — and it has the same cause: reflow2 measures how well the DESIGN covers the SYSTEM, and never how well anything covers the SURFACE reflow2 itself ships. THE OPTIONS, with what is cheap or expensive about each: (A) A CENSUS REPORT, NOT A GAP — a `vocabulary_census` naming declared-but-unreached types, reported as a FACT the way granularity_report and surprising_connections are. CHEAPEST, and it cannot false-positive into nagging. COUNTER: a report nobody runs is the same failure one level along; it would need a line in graph_report to be seen. (B) A GAP AT LOW SEVERITY — `unreached_vocabulary`, one per declared type with nothing behind it, acknowledgeable. Makes it appear in the loop where people already look. COUNTER, AND IT IS SERIOUS: a demonstrator legitimately does not use Flow or ReadinessAssessment, so this would fire on correct work in every young design — the exact thing dec:read-hint-shape and the phase-nudge doctrine were built to avoid. Firing on the SCHEMA (a fixed 60/29) rather than on the user's design might dodge that, since it is reflow2's own vocabulary being judged rather than the consumer's modelling. (C) SCOPE IT TO THE SHIPPED SURFACE ONLY — make it reflow2's own maintenance instrument (a tools/ script, like toolsnap), not a served capability. Honest about who the finding is for: a consumer does not care that reflow2 declares SUPPLEMENTS, and rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party would ask what the CONSUMER gets. COUNTER: the consumer DOES get something — describe_schema offers them these types, and VIOLATES_RULE proves a consumer can waste time on one. (D) DO NOTHING NEW AND JUST PRUNE — decide dec:one-retire-edge and dec:anchor-retire-or-implement, delete what loses, and accept that the next accumulation goes unnoticed too. COUNTER: this is exactly what happened after dec:edge-orthogonality, and eight more arrived. ⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, whichever is chosen: another marker nothing reads. That is the finding this node is about, and it would be a fourth instance of it. BOUND, stated rather than glossed: this measured ONE design — reflow2's own. A type with zero instances HERE may be in daily use in dev_storyflow or flo2, and the census would need to be per-design to mean anything to a consumer. The 8 unreached-on-every-test edges are the stronger claim, because those have no code behind them anywhere and that is a property of the SHIPPED BUILD rather than of this graph. NOTHING IS PROMOTED.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted without Anthony's word. The provenance correction is inside the decision text rather than only in conversation, because the claim that started this thread was relayed from another session's sweep as if freshly measured, and a later reader deserves to know which parts were measured today and which were quoted. The measurement in this node WAS run today, with its method stated so it can be re-run or disputed. Kept separate from dec:one-retire-edge (which asks which of two edges survives) and dec:bl-155 (which asks the same question about served TOOLS): this one asks whether the class should be DETECTED at all. Linked to both rather than merged, because a node holding all three could only ever be part-answered.proposednothing
OPEN — should a git diff be a direct input to impact analysis, given reconcile_artifacts already returns propagation_seeds and nothing drives it from a commit?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 research, specifically Understand Anything's 'diff impact analysis that shows what a given change touches'. STILL OPEN. THE IDEA: reflow2's impact analysis runs design-first — add_change_event then propagate_change, seeded by the design node you are about to touch. The survey's tools run it code-first: here is a diff, here is what it touches. Those are opposite directions, and the code-first direction is the one a developer actually has in hand at review time. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, and this was checked rather than assumed: reconcile_artifacts takes observed artifact hashes and returns `propagation_seeds` — 'the design nodes the changes land on' — explicitly documented to be fed to propagate_from. So the code-to-design hop is BUILT. The composition is: changed files, to registered artifacts by hash, to REALIZES edges, to capabilities and upward. Nothing is missing in the core. WHAT IS THEREFORE ACTUALLY OPEN, and it is smaller than the survey makes it sound: (a) nothing computes the hashes from a commit — reflow2 performs no file I/O by design, so a caller must do it, and no caller currently does it from a git diff; (b) the CI gate checks the committed export for drift and open gaps, not 'what does this commit touch upstream'; (c) the answer is only as complete as artifact registration, and an unregistered file lands on nothing at all, which would read as 'this change is safe' rather than 'this change is unmapped'. That last one is the real risk and it is the same failure mode as the release-manifest problem: silence that looks like a pass. WHAT IS CHEAP: a driver script over `git diff --name-only` plus hashing, calling reconcile_artifacts then propagate_from. That is wiring, in the same family as tools/reflow2_check.py, and needs no core change. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a per-commit blast radius is only as trustworthy as REALIZES coverage, and an incomplete golden thread turns it into a confident understatement — which is worse than no answer, because a reviewer will believe it. If this is built, the honest version must report unmapped files as UNMAPPED and loudly, not fold them into a clean result. The existing unrealized_capability gap is the design-side half of that problem; this is the artifact-side half and there may be nothing that detects it.		Recorded as an idea rather than a gap because the machinery it asks for already exists and only the driver is absent, which makes it a small increment rather than a design question — except for the unmapped-file silence, which is a design question and is the reason this is worth a node at all.proposednothing
OPEN — should the depth axis compute CORRELATION between dimensions, not just drift within one?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled. THE OBSERVATION: reflow2 uses exactly TWO functions from dynograph-vector — mean and linear_regression_slope, both in dimensions.rs. The depth axis records DimensionObservations and computes drift as a slope WITHIN one dimension over time. THE IDEA: pearson_correlation and spearman_rank_correlation (unused) would answer a question the axis cannot currently ask — do two dimensions move TOGETHER across components? 'Does complexity track defect count?' 'Does coupling track change frequency?' Spearman is the rank version, so it survives non-linear but monotone relationships and is the safer default on small samples. CHEAP: pure functions, already a dependency, and the observations are already stored. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, and there are two. First, this is the most SPECULATIVE idea in the batch — no backlog item asks for it and no trial has reported wanting it, so it is a capability looking for a user. Second and more serious: correlation invites causal reading, and a design brain reporting 'complexity correlates with defects' will be read as 'complexity causes defects'. The schema already takes this seriously — the CAUSES edge carries a `basis` enum (observed / correlational / causal / spurious) with the instruction 'do not assert causal without a mechanism' — so the vocabulary for the caveat exists, but the report would have to carry it loudly.		The only genuinely unexplored idea in dynograph-vector; the rest of that crate is either already used (mean, slope), already a parked question (embeddings), or thin (softmax, percentile).proposednothing
OPEN — should the content store be discontinued outright, with design artifacts kept as ordinary files in the repo?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, leaning towards discontinuing rather than phasing out: \'I don't think anybody is actually fully utilizing it anyways, so not a big deal I think if we just discontinue it now versus phasing it out.\' HIS ARGUMENT, in his words and not improved on: (1) the bytes cannot fully live in a repo because it would become a huge object rapidly; (2) dev_storyflow's 700+ documents have been actively ingested into the graph and \'those documents are no longer really needed\' — the documents that would have been put in the blob; (3) maybe the better approach is important design artifacts directly in the git repo in something like a design_artifacts folder and forget blob altogether; (4) it is another feature that must be maintained and must grow with the rest of reflow2; (5) in flo2 the blob could end up being terabytes that has to be backed up, secured, and somehow separable per project. ⭐ MEASURED BEFORE ANY OPINION WAS FORMED, and it is the strongest thing in this node. REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN USES THE CONTENT STORE ZERO TIMES: no `--content-path` is configured in .mcp.json, no `.reflow2/content` directory exists, and 0 of 148 Fragments carry a `content_ref`. This is a 1,867-node graph that has been dogfooded harder than any other. The feature is built, tested (ver:content-surface, 5 cases), documented, and unused by its own author's primary project. That is evidence for his (4) rather than a coincidence. CORROBORATING, from the consumer side: every dev_storyflow locator complaint filed on 2026-08-09 is about `Artifact.location`, `Fragment.title` and path resolution — a worker even wrote scripts/records/locator_validator.py because \'location is the join key between a corpus and the design and nothing validates it.\' NOBODY COMPLAINED ABOUT CONTENT HASHES, because nobody is using them. They are joining on PATHS. ⭐ AND AN ARGUMENT NOBODY HAS MADE YET, which strengthens his case: dec:where-content-lives settled on a content-addressed store whose blobs are COMMITTED TO THE REPO. GIT IS ALREADY A CONTENT-ADDRESSED STORE. So the current design is a content-addressed layer inside a content-addressed system — the dedup and the integrity hash are both things git already provides for anything committed. A `design_artifacts/` folder would not be giving up content addressing; it would be using the one underneath. WHAT THIS WOULD RE-OPEN, stated so nothing is decided by accident: dec:where-content-lives (accepted), dec:what-lives-where (accepted), dec:content-growth-is-bounded-by-what-not-by-size (accepted), dec:content-store-implementation and dec:content-manifest. Per dec:reopen-supersedes a re-opening mints a NEW decision that obsoletes the old one; the accepted ones are never un-accepted. ⚠️ AND IT WOULD ANSWER dec:what-lives-where's OWN FALSIFIABLE TEST — which is the most interesting thing here. That decision wrote its own refutation condition: \'IF REFLOW2 WORKS, STORYFLOW WOULD NOT HAVE NEEDED dev_storyflow. One repo, code native, the design in the graph, the sources in the store. If a user still ends up splitting their repo to stay sane, reflow2 has not delivered what this decision claims.\' Anthony's observation is a DIFFERENT and sharper result than that test anticipated: it is not that the split was still needed, it is that ONCE THE DOCUMENTS WERE MINED THEIR ROLE WAS SPENT. If what mattered became nodes with Fragments recording provenance, the bytes are archival — and a repo folder (or the existing dev_storyflow repo) already archives them. THE OPTIONS, with what is cheap or expensive about each recorded beside rather than argued down: (A) DISCONTINUE NOW — remove content_put/content_get and the store, keep nothing. Cheapest to maintain, and honest given zero usage here. COUNTER: content_manifest answers a real question (\'I was handed this design on its own — what does it point at that I do not have?\'), and that question survives the store's removal; it would need re-pointing at repo paths rather than deleting. (B) DEPRECATE, KEEP THE READS — stop accepting new content, keep content_get/exists/manifest so an existing store still resolves. COUNTER: Anthony's own point is that phasing costs more than discontinuing when the user count is zero; this buys compatibility nobody needs. (C) KEEP IT, NARROW IT — retain for the one case a repo folder genuinely cannot hold (very large or non-diffable binaries) and say so. COUNTER: that is the status quo with better documentation, and the status quo has zero users; \'it might matter later\' is what the no-foreclosure rule exists to make a deliberate choice rather than a default. (D) REPLACE WITH A CONVENTION — a `design_artifacts/` folder plus a Fragment/Artifact `location` pointing into it, no new machinery. Uses git's own content addressing. COUNTER, and it is the real one: `location` is the field dev_storyflow just filed FOUR defects about (unvalidated paths, a literal ellipsis that matched nothing, title-vs-source ambiguity, no way to ask \'is this path already in the graph?\').
