Moving weight onto `location` without fixing it moves weight onto the weakest join in the schema. That is an argument for fixing `location` FIRST, not against (D). WHAT NOBODY HAS ESTABLISHED, and it should not be guessed: whether any OTHER consumer has a populated store. This project has none; flo2 was checked and has no .mcp.json content path; dev_storyflow was not checked. A discontinue is cheap if the answer is nobody and expensive if it is somebody, and it is one call (content_manifest) per project to find out. NOTHING HERE IS PROMOTED. Anthony stated a lean, not a decision, and the options above are recorded as considered.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, options in the prose with counters beside them, nothing promoted to intent without Anthony's word. Deliberately NOT recorded as a re-opening of dec:where-content-lives yet — that would assert the choice has been made and would obsolete an accepted decision on a lean rather than a decision. If he settles it, dec:reopen-supersedes says the re-opening mints its own node then. Kept separate from dec:external-blob-store-pressure, which asks whether committed blobs should move to an EXTERNAL store — the opposite direction, and it assumes the store exists. This asks whether it should exist at all, and one node holding both could only ever be half-answered.proposednothing
DECIDED — a Decision OBSOLETES what it withdrew, and three detectors plus delivery now read it
DECIDED 2026-08-11 on Anthony's word. NO NEW VOCABULARY WAS NEEDED, and finding that out is the whole result. THE ANSWER: a Decision `OBSOLETES` the thing it withdrew. PUT THE DECISION AT THE SOURCE. That dissolves the objection this node was opened over. Point (3) above says both retirement edges 'presume a successor to sit at the source end. A discontinued thing with no replacement has NOTHING TO PUT THERE. You cannot draw OBSOLETES from nothing.' True — but a discontinuation ALWAYS has a decision behind it even when it has no replacement, so the decision is the honest source. `OBSOLETES` is already `* -> *` in schema/inference.yaml and its hint already reads 'source makes target redundant or deprecated'. So: no edge type, no enum value, NO SCHEMA STAMP MOVE, and no upgrade doc — none of which option (A) or (B) could have claimed. ⭐ AND IT ANSWERS `dec:one-retire-edge`'S REAL QUESTION AS A SIDE EFFECT. That decision asked, since July, what SHOULD consult a retirement edge — 'retiring something marks it and changes nothing. A retired capability still counts in every rollup, still raises its gaps, still appears in delivery arithmetic.' Four readers now exist, which is four more than either retirement edge has ever had: · `unmotivated_capability`, `unrealized_capability`, `unverified_capability` fall silent · delivery arithmetic stops counting a discontinued capability as a satisfier So OBSOLETES is no longer a marker nothing reads. Whether SUPERSEDES survives at all is still `dec:one-retire-edge`'s to settle, and it is now a smaller question: one of the two words has a job. ⚠️ ONLY AN ACCEPTED DECISION DISCONTINUES ANYTHING. A `proposed` withdrawal has withdrawn nothing; the thing keeps counting until somebody with the authority says so. That is `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` applied to the retire path, and it is pinned by a test that fails if the check is dropped. ⚠️ THE CASCADE IS DELIBERATE. Withdrawing the thing that met a need does not meet the need, so the requirement it served drops back to UNSATISFIED and is asked about again — 'covered, deferred, or dropped?'. Without that, a discontinuation would be invisible one hop away and the design would keep reporting a need as met by something that no longer exists. Applying this to the content store surfaces exactly that, and the two requirements it served are now open questions for Anthony rather than silent claims. ⚠️ AND THE NUMBERS SAY WHY THEY MOVED. `DeliveryCoverage.satisfied_only_by_discontinued` counts the skipped edges, because a discontinuation that made delivery fall with no mention is the silent-drop failure this project forbids everywhere else: the count drops, nothing explains it, and a reader concludes the design regressed. WHAT IS STILL OPEN AND IS NOT CLAIMED HERE: · `dec:idea-does-a-capability-need-a-cancelled-state` (Alex's) is NOT closed by this. It covers the ABANDONED case; it says nothing about a WISH NOBODY EVER AGREED TO, which has no decision behind it to be the source of an OBSOLETES edge. That half is still `dec:exploratory-staging`'s. · A Verification whose code was deleted still reads `passing`. `ver:content-store` is the live instance. Nothing here fixes that, and marking the verification obsoleted does not change its status field. · Nothing reads discontinuation for Components, Interfaces or Artifacts. Only the capability detectors and delivery consult it today, which is stated rather than left to be discovered.		Anthony asked on 2026-08-09 for a way to say 'we built this and then decided against it'. Searching before building found that the vocabulary already held it, in a direction nobody had tried: the objection was that a discontinued thing has no successor for the source end of a retirement edge, and the answer is that the DECISION is the source. That costs nothing — no schema change, no stamp move, no upgrade doc — and it gives OBSOLETES its first reader in the process, which is the question dec:one-retire-edge has been waiting on since July. Shipped WITH its readers deliberately: this project has now found three markers nothing reads (enforced, SUPERSEDES, OBSOLETES itself), and a fourth would have been the defect rather than the fix.acceptednothing
OPEN — should surprise and severity be reported as distributional positions rather than absolute scores?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled; recorded as a minor idea with a real objection. THE IDEA: percentile and median (unused, in dynograph-vector::stats) would let surprising_connections report 'the top 5% most surprising couplings in THIS design' rather than everything over a fixed score. A distributional cut self-calibrates to the graph it is run on; an absolute one does not, and a design with 100 nodes and one with 10,000 do not have the same natural scale. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is the projects own lesson: BL-23 established that when a detector punishes correct work, the answer is A DIFFERENT QUESTION, not a tuned threshold. A percentile is still a threshold — it just moves rather than sits still. Worse, a top-N-percent rule ALWAYS returns something, so a design with no surprising couplings at all would still be handed a list, which is exactly the false-signal failure the noise-floor work (BL-42) was about. WHERE IT MIGHT STILL HELP: not as a cut, but as CONTEXT on a finding already made — 'surprise 2.56, which is the highest in this design' is more useful to a reader than a bare number, and asserts nothing extra.		Kept deliberately small and recorded with the objection first, because the naive form of this idea contradicts an established lesson and a later session should meet the objection at the same moment as the idea.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2's viewpoints become a document product, the way DocGen is for OpenMBEE?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a first-pass review of openmbee.org — website and repository listing only, deep review pending. THE OBSERVATION: OpenMBEE's Model Development Kits 'implement DocGen language for dynamic, model-based document generation using view and viewpoint concepts'. Document generation is not a side feature there; it is half the value proposition, and the tagline 'Edit once, use everywhere' is largely a claim about documents — write the model once, and every specification, review pack and report derives from it rather than drifting from it. WHERE reflow2 STANDS, and the gap is narrower than it first looks: reflow2 already has the same underlying idea. `docs/viewpoints.md` is DoDAF-informed, `dec:views-are-projections` states that a view is a pure projection of the graph and that renderer fill-ins are DEFECTS, and `tools/render_views.py` projects six viewpoints and CONFESSES anything a view needs that the graph cannot supply — with every confession counted as a finding (BL-40). That confession discipline is arguably stronger than DocGen's, because it makes the gaps in a document visible instead of filling them. THE HONEST DIFFERENCE IS PRODUCT, NOT CONCEPT: `render_views.py` is a probe in the tools directory, run by developers of reflow2. DocGen is something an engineering organisation hands to its systems engineers to produce the artefacts a programme is contractually required to deliver. reflow2 has never claimed the second, and `req:no-se-knowledge` ('the user never needs systems engineering') suggests it may not want to. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a document generator is a large surface with a long tail — templates, formats, numbering, review states — and every hour of it is an hour not spent on the coherence loop, which is the thing nobody else is building. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether the projections reflow2 already computes are close enough to what a real programme must deliver that the remaining distance is rendering rather than modelling.		Recorded through the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request, ahead of a deep review against a clone of OpenMBEE's repository. The strength claim is deliberately hedged: reflow2 holds the concept (views as projections, confessions as findings) and OpenMBEE holds the product. Which of those is 'stronger' depends entirely on whether the user is a programme owing deliverables or a builder owing a coherent design, and reflow2 has so far chosen the second. Anthony's own position sits across both, which is why this is worth asking rather than assuming.proposednothing
DECIDED — no cancelled state, ever: abandonment is an OBSOLETES edge, and whether the vocabulary fix was enough is a MEASUREMENT owed by Alex's fleet, not a further decision
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD: NO `cancelled` VALUE IS ADDED TO `Capability.status`, NOW OR LATER.** Abandonment is recorded by an accepted Decision drawing `OBSOLETES`, which computes `discontinued`. The question this node was opened under is answered; what remains is a measurement and a separate, narrower question, both named below. ⭐ **AND THE DETECTOR IS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT YET — THAT IS THE PART OF THE RULING WORTH KEEPING.** Three ways to make an agent find `OBSOLETES` were on the table: a hint on `set_capability_status`, a DETECTOR for abandonment words in description prose, and the command coverage. **The vocabulary fix shipped in v0.31.0** (`Capability.status` and the `OBSOLETES` hint now name each other, pinned by tests) **and has never been in front of an agent** — Alex's fleet has not seen it. Building the detector now would be guessing that the cheap fix failed before observing whether it did, and it is the only option with a false-positive cost: a capability legitimately describing that it REPLACED something dropped would fire. 🎯 **WHAT IS OWED IS THEREFORE A MEASUREMENT, AND IT IS FREE.** Alex's fleet is the only place 'DROPPED in prose' was ever observed. **If it stops appearing there after v0.31.0, the vocabulary fix worked and the detector is unnecessary; if it continues, the detector is justified by evidence rather than by fear.** Same discipline Anthony applied to the allocation question — do not reason about it, measure it. ⚠️ **THE RESIDUAL IS REAL AND BELONGS ELSEWHERE, NOT HERE:** a capability **nobody ever agreed to** has no decision to hang an `OBSOLETES` edge from, so neither this ruling nor the 2026-08-11 one reaches it. That is `dec:exploratory-staging`'s, and closing this node does not close that. ════════ THE REASONING THAT PRODUCED THE RULING ════════ 🛑 **ANTHONY, 2026-08-14, CHALLENGING THE PREMISE: 'we already have an obsolete with discontinued or something like that — are we playing semantics with cancelled?' CHECKED AGAINST THE CODE AND THE GRAPH RATHER THAN ARGUED. HE IS RIGHT FOR THE ABANDONED CASE, AND THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY DECIDED THREE DAYS EARLIER.** `dec:idea-discontinued-is-a-first-class-state` was **DECIDED on his word 2026-08-11**: a Decision `OBSOLETES` what it withdrew, the decision itself being the source. No enum value, no edge type, no schema stamp move, no upgrade doc. **IT IS NOT THEORETICAL — IT IS LIVE IN THIS GRAPH.** `dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued` (accepted) obsoletes `cap:content-store` and `cap:content-manifest` (both stored `realized`) and `cap:session-artifacts` (`verified`). And `is_discontinued` has FOUR readers: `unmotivated_capability`, `unrealized_capability` and `unverified_capability` fall silent, and delivery arithmetic stops counting a discontinued capability as a satisfier (`DeliveryCoverage.satisfied_only_by_discontinued`). ⇒ **ADDING `cancelled` WOULD BE A SECOND WAY TO SAY WHAT THE GRAPH ALREADY COMPUTES — and worse than redundant, because a STORED status can disagree with the COMPUTED one.** The stored status deliberately keeps saying what was BUILT; that is why `get_node` carries `discontinued` separately and warns to read it. ═══ ⭐ WHAT ACTUALLY BIT ALEX IS DISCOVERABILITY, NOT A MISSING STATE ═══ His agents typed 'DROPPED' into description prose while the mechanism existed and worked. Measured via `describe_schema`, which the served routing table tells an agent to use for exactly this lookup: `Capability.status` carried **no description at all** — four bare values and no fifth — while every neighbouring property carried a teaching one; and `OBSOLETES`'s entire hint read *'Source makes target redundant or deprecated'*, naming neither the retirement job, nor the Decision as source, nor `discontinued`. **So an agent did everything right and still had nowhere to put the fact except prose.** Both descriptions shipped in v0.31.0, with no schema stamp move. ════════ THE ORIGINAL REPORT, KEPT ════════ Alex's fleet, 2026-08-09: 'Requirements: deferred / dropped. Capabilities: no equivalent — agents stuff DROPPED into description text.' CONFIRMED AGAINST THE SCHEMA: Requirement.status is (proposed, accepted, deferred, dropped, met); Capability.status is (planned, in_progress, realized, verified). WHY IT IS THE WEEK'S OWN DEFECT CLASS AGAIN: a state that cannot be expressed does not disappear — it gets smuggled into prose.		Raised by a second consumer project rather than found here, which is the useful part: reflow2's own graph never hit it because this project retires capabilities rather than cancelling them. Kept as a decision point rather than built because it is a schema enum change that would move the stamp and therefore owe an upgrade doc — the first this week that would — and because it touches an already-open question about retirement being modelled in two places. Anthony's to settle.acceptednothing
OPEN — chain_reflow's six nuggets audited: does a MIRRORED DESIGN occupy a rung on Component.level, or is the cross-graph black box outside the ladder forever?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony pointed at chain_reflow, 2026-08-12, while working out bottom-up system-of-systems: 'made me think of chain-reflow... might be worth re-analyzing that repo and doing a search for what reflow2 already has in this topic.' ⚠️ THIS NODE IS THE INGEST OF `docs/chain-reflow-nuggets.md`, which is one of the four nuggets files on Anthony's ingest-then-delete list (inward-facing docs become graph, then go). It held reflow2's adoption plan for chain_reflow and NOTHING IN THE GRAPH RECORDED IT — searching for 'chain reflow nuggets touchpoint matryoshka' returns nothing above 12.5, all of it unrelated. A stale inward-facing tracker holding knowledge the graph does not have is exactly why that list exists. ═══ THE AUDIT, 2026-08-12: six nuggets, planned vs actual ═══ MATRYOSHKA / MISSING-INTERMEDIATE adopt (now) ✅ BUILT — hierarchy.rs; `missing_intermediate_level` fires in both hierarchy_issues and detect_gaps CORRELATION VS CAUSATION adopt (now, schema) ✅ BUILT — `basis` + `validation_status` on inference edges, and the schema still credits chain_reflow by name CREATIVE LINKING (guarded healer) adopt (concept) 🛑 BUILT as `generate_bridge`, then RETIRED 2026-08-10 SoS TOUCHPOINT DISCOVERY adopt (MEDIUM) ⬜ the word 'touchpoint' appears NOWHERE in the codebase ORTHOGONALITY ASSESSMENT later ⬜ INTERACTIVE EXECUTOR later ⬜ ═══ FINDING 1 — TOUCHPOINT DISCOVERY IS HALF SHIPPED UNDER OTHER NAMES AND HALF OUTLAWED ═══ The nuggets doc specifies it as: 'allow Project↔Project links, and a touchpoint-discovery pass that PROPOSES cross-project `Interface`/`DEPENDS_ON` edges (standard technical matching first; creative linking only for orthogonal, guarded). The merged graph is then diagnosed/healed like any other.' ⭐ THE 2026-07 PLAN IS PARTLY FORBIDDEN BY A 2026-08 RULE. `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` (accepted, shipped v0.28.0) removed `generate_bridge` precisely because proposing an edge that asserts a relationship nobody stated is fabrication. A pass that PROPOSES cross-project DEPENDS_ON edges is that, across an ownership boundary, where it is worse — the asserted relationship is between two designs whose owners never agreed to it. BUT THE PERMITTED HALF EXISTS, under two different names: - 'standard technical matching first' -> `pair_designs`, which reports `candidates` and states outright that uncertain name matches are 'CANDIDATES to ask about, never actions'. - 'the merged graph is then diagnosed like any other' -> `compose_and_analyse`, which imports theirs alongside yours in memory and runs the ORDINARY checks over the whole, attributing findings ours / theirs / seam. ⇒ TOUCHPOINT DISCOVERY IS NOT UNBUILT THROUGH NEGLECT. Its safe half shipped as two differently-named tools and its unsafe half was deliberately outlawed. That is a better outcome than the plan, and it should be recorded as such rather than sitting on a roadmap as a debt. 📌 CREATIVE LINKING'S COMPLETE ARC IS WORTH KEEPING: adopted as a concept (2026-07), built as `generate_bridge`, retired as fabrication (2026-08-10). heal.rs still carries the comment 'NO SUGGESTION, DELIBERATELY. `generate_bridge` used to sit...' — an idea taken from another project, built, and then argued back out on a rule the receiving project later derived. Chain_reflow also carries `validate_merged_architecture.py`, written because 'Chain Reflow workflows create merged architectures but lack automated validation' — the same job `compose_and_analyse` now does, which confirms the merged graph was always meant to be validated AS A WHOLE. ═══ FINDING 2 — THE ACTIONABLE ONE: A MIRRORED DESIGN OCCUPIES NO RUNG ═══ `Component.level` already runs `component ▸ subsystem ▸ system ▸ system_of_systems ▸ enterprise`. SO SYSTEM-OF-SYSTEMS IS ALREADY A MODELLED RUNG, and `missing_intermediate_level` is pure level arithmetic over CONTAINS/DEPENDS_ON **between Components**. 🛑 BUT A MIRRORED DESIGN ARRIVES AS A **PROJECT** CONTAINING COMPONENTS (measured 2026-08-12: 1 Project, 6 Components, 5 Interfaces, 1 Artifact, with 5 CONTAINS edges from `proj:flo2`). **A PROJECT OCCUPIES NO RUNG ON THAT LADDER.** So the cross-graph black box sits outside the level system entirely, and matryoshka detection structurally CANNOT see across an ownership boundary — not because the analysis is missing, but because the thing on the far side is not levelled. ⇒ THE QUESTION, and it is one sentence: **does a mirrored Project present as a Component at some level, or does the ladder extend to Projects?** Answer it and matryoshka recurses across ownership boundaries using the detector that already exists. This is also exactly what `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` demands in its own closing line — 'an arbitrary-depth nesting that is exercised beyond two levels' — and the two had never been connected. OPTIONS, none taken: A — A MIRRORED PROJECT PRESENTS AS A COMPONENT at a stated level, chosen by the mirroring side. Cheapest: no schema change, the existing detector works immediately. EXPENSIVE: the level is the HOST's judgement about someone else's design, which is an assertion about them they never made — the same class the fabrication rule guards. B — EXTEND THE LADDER TO PROJECTS, so level arithmetic spans node types. Truthful — a Project genuinely is a bigger box than a Component. EXPENSIVE: a schema change touching the one property the matryoshka detectors are built on. C — THE MIRRORING SIDE DECLARES THE RUNG ON THE MIRROR, not on the foreign node — a property of the LINK rather than of either design. Fits 'foreignness is a property of the node' and keeps the host's judgement on the host's side of the line. EXPENSIVE: the link is not yet a first-class object, which is gap 1 of the linking audit. D — LEAVE IT. Cross-graph composition is analysed by `compose_and_analyse` and needs no levels. EXPENSIVE: then `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` is satisfiable within a graph only, and the bottom-up SoS reading Anthony is reaching for stays out of scope. NOT DECIDED.		Captured because pointing at chain_reflow turned up an adoption plan that existed only in an inward-facing doc slated for deletion, and auditing it against the code changed two statuses: touchpoint discovery is half-shipped under other names and half-outlawed by a rule derived after the plan was written, and creative linking has a complete adopted-built-retired arc worth keeping. The actionable residue is one sentence — a mirrored design occupies no rung on Component.level, so the matryoshka detector cannot cross an ownership boundary — which is the precise blocker under the cross-graph reading of req:recursive-black-box-decomposition.proposednothing
OPEN — should comparing the live graph against the committed record be part of a session's opening move, when the comparison cannot yet tell a default from a decision?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is chosen; the options are ideas with their honest counter-arguments beside them, and the road not taken is kept on purpose. THE PROMPT. I suggested (2026-08-10) that `compare_designs` against the committed export belongs at the OPEN of a session rather than being run when trouble is already suspected, because it was the only thing that found a record diverging from the graph on main. Anthony asked for it to be thought through rather than acted on. WHAT SEARCHING FIRST DID TO THE QUESTION — it inverted it. The same session then found `fact:correction-the-export-loses-nothing-the-108-were-serialized-defaults`: a 2026-08-08 session ran exactly this comparison, got 108 property-level findings, concluded `export_graph` was silently dropping design, wrote that into a PR body and a handoff note, and retracted it after one probe. They were serialized schema defaults. I had just made the same false claim on the same data, 95 findings instead of 108, without having read theirs. SO THE OBSERVED RECORD OF THIS INSTRUMENT AT ORIENTATION TIME IS TWO RUNS, TWO FALSE DEFECT CLAIMS, TWO RELEASES APART, BY DIFFERENT AGENTS. That is not an argument against comparing; it is an argument that the question is not 'when do we run it' but 'what does it have to be able to say before running it earlier makes anyone better off'. THE OPTIONS. (A) DO NOTHING — the null option, and it is stronger than it looks. `where-am-i` ALREADY names `compare_designs` as its first gather step. The failure on 2026-08-10 was not that the step was skipped; it was run, and misread. Adding a ritual does not fix a reading problem, and this project has already rejected the ritual shape twice (`dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written`: build the view, not the document; `dec:read-hint-shape` rejected option B because boilerplate on every return trains the agent to skim). Cheap: costs nothing. Counter: it leaves the actual observed harm — the record was wrong on `main` for an unknown number of PRs and `reflow2_check` is structurally incapable of noticing, since it reads artifact checksums and anchored gaps and never node properties. (B) COMPUTE IT, DO NOT PRESCRIBE IT — extend `dec:read-hint-shape`'s already-chosen option C (state-derived hint, riding the orientation-shaped reads, fire-on-change) to carry DISTRIBUTION debt alongside coherence debt: 'the record and the graph disagree' surfacing at the moment of attention, only when true. This is flo2's F5 filed 2026-08-09 — `loop_status` tracks what COHERENCE is owed and nothing tracks what DISTRIBUTION is owed. Fits the strongest precedent in the design and needs no new vocabulary. Counter, and it is decisive as things stand: a hint that fires on phantom findings is a hint that teaches you to ignore it. Building B before C or D would ship the cry-wolf failure into the one mechanism that currently works. (C) FIX THE INSTRUMENT — make a property difference able to say WHICH SIDE MEANT IT, so a default never appears as a change. The 2026-08-08 correction already argues this and names the precedent: 'a comparison that cannot say which side meant it is the same shape as an edge that cannot say who asserted it (DUPLICATES `basis`, which cost dev_storyflow ten proposed deletions) — the fix there was to make provenance explicit rather than to tune the detector, and the same argument applies.' Most expensive; also the only option that makes the finding trustworthy rather than quieter. Counter: property-level provenance is a large surface, and `dec:certainty-derived` would argue it should be DERIVED rather than stored — which may make (D) sufficient. (D) FINISH BL-198 — 'do not serialize a value equal to the default, so an absent property honestly means nobody said'. Cheaper than C, kills the noise at its source, and the exporter has evidently begun doing it already (0.25.0 wrote defaults, 0.27.0 does not) while `fact:bl-198` is still listed PLANNED in `epoch:planned-one-write-surface`. Counter, and it is the trap both incidents actually fell into: suppressing defaults does not remove the disagreement, it MOVES it to the transition. Two builds one release apart still differ on every default, and that window is exactly what produced both false claims. So D makes the steady state clean and the upgrade moment worse — which is an argument for D plus a version-aware comparison, not D alone. (E) WRONG TRIGGER ENTIRELY — the record diverging matters when it is PUBLISHED, not when a session starts. Put the check at export/commit/CI time, where something is about to be shipped, and leave session-open alone. Cheap and well-precedented (`ci-gate` exists). Counter: it cannot catch what is already committed and wrong, which is the case actually observed here; and it inherits the same default-vs-decision blindness, so it would go red on a version bump for no reason. WHAT IS NOT AN OPTION, said plainly so nobody re-derives it: tuning a threshold so the phantom findings fall below it. That silences the true findings at the same rate as the false ones, and it is the 'reduce a SET to a SCALAR' failure this project has already written down. THE ORDERING THAT FALLS OUT, offered as a finding and not as a decision: C or D before B, and A is a legitimate resting place if neither is worth the spend — because the value of running the comparison earlier is bounded above by the comparison's ability to be believed, and right now it has a 2-for-2 record of not deserving to be.		Recorded as an open question rather than an answer because the brainstorm materially changed what the question is. I opened arguing for a session-opening step; the design's own memory then supplied a two-instance record of that step producing confident false defect claims — one of them mine, an hour earlier. An idea that is weaker after searching is worth keeping in exactly that state, with the evidence that weakened it attached, so a later session does not re-propose it fresh and pay for the discovery a third time. Kept deliberately open, and NOT registered as alternatives: each option here is a paragraph, not a design, so `detect_gaps` stays quiet (`undecided_decision_point` fires only on two or more registered alternatives). If one of these grows a design of its own — most likely C, which needs a property-provenance shape — `register_alternative` is what makes it a real fork, and being nudged to choose would then be correct. The counter-arguments are recorded beside the options rather than used to kill any of them, including against my own opening position. (A) is listed first and honestly rather than as a foil: this project has twice chosen the computed form over the prescribed one, and 'the step was already prescribed and was run and was misread' is a real answer to 'should we prescribe the step'.supersedednothing
IDEA — `change_type` has no value for an as-built defect. Add one, alias an existing one, or split the axis it is actually conflating?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's idea, from the Opportunities section of his 2026-08-14 session (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md), in his words: 'Add `change_type` for as-built defects (`defect_fix` / `as_built_fix`), or officially alias `test_failure_fix`.' DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM `fact:defect-change-event-has-no-type-for-a-field-reported-defect`, which the near-duplicate guard correctly surfaced: that node MEASURES the problem and counts its five occurrences; this one holds the UNMADE CHOICE about the shape of the fix. Merging them would put an open question inside a settled measurement, and the fact would then read as though it had proposed its own answer. WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN ITS ONE LINE: the evidence is now five forced choices, not one — two maintainer sessions, one fleet, Alex, and the very edit that recorded his corroboration, each picking a different least-wrong value. THE OPTIONS: (a) ADD `defect_fix` (or `field_report_fix`) — exactly what he proposed. CHEAP: enum values are not counted by the version stamp, so it is not a schema break. COUNTER, and the reason this is a question rather than a task: the five forced choices needed at least THREE different missing meanings — a defect fix, 'an open question was settled' (`chg:arrival-delta-decided`), and 'the design's knowledge moved while the thing did not'. One value fixes the loudest instance and leaves the pattern. (b) OFFICIALLY ALIAS `test_failure_fix` — his cheaper alternative: document that this is the bucket. CHEAPEST, no schema move. COUNTER: it makes a structured field permanently mean something other than its name, and the project rejected that reasoning once already — `baseline_established` exists precisely because forcing a record-only change through a code category 'writes a fiction into the ledger that exists to prevent fiction'. (c) SPLIT THE AXIS — carry a `subject: system | record` alongside a narrower type. MOST HONEST: `baseline_established`'s own doc comment already names the axis — 'every other variant answers why the thing changed; this one says the thing did not change and only the design's knowledge of it did' — then leaves it with one member, reserved. COUNTER: a real schema property on a type with a lot of history, and every existing ChangeEvent would carry an unstated subject, which is the 'absent means nobody said' problem again. (d) A STRUCTURED `reported_by` / `found_by` PROPERTY — the other half of Alex's own suggestion. Keeps how-it-was-found structured rather than narrated. COUNTER: orthogonal to the gap; it records provenance of the discovery, not the kind of the change, so (a) or (c) would still be owed. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the three missing meanings are all of them, or only the three that happen to have been hit.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, options with their counters beside them, nothing promoted. Started as a new node rather than merged into the measuring fact after the near-duplicate guard named it — a measurement and an unmade choice are different acts, and folding the second into the first would make the fact appear to answer itself.proposednothing
OPEN — does every served skill get a slash command, or is the shortfall the wrong thing to fix?
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD — OPTION A: ALL TWENTY SERVED SKILLS GET A SLASH COMMAND, AND THE COVERAGE IS PINNED BY A TEST.** Raised the same day after `/capture-session` came back `Unknown command` on his work computer. At the time nine of twenty skills were fronted by a command and eleven by nothing. He was given three options and took A over B (fix discovery instead) and C (cover only what people type by name). **TWO THINGS MOVED THE ARGUMENT, and both are dated later than the reasoning that originally held the set at eight:** 1. **THE CLUTTER OBJECTION HAD ALREADY BEEN PAID DOWN.** The case against widening was Alex's *'inserted several things into my project'*, which is why `dec:idea-init-asks-which-harness-and-installs-only-that` narrowed the install. But that shipped in PR #178 on 2026-08-14: `init` now ASKS which harness and writes `.claude/commands` for Claude Code ONLY. An OpenCode or VS Code project receives none of them, so the cost that argued against twenty files is no longer paid by the projects that complained. 2. **MEASURED THE SAME DAY — COMMANDS ARE THE CHANNEL THAT ACTUALLY GETS USED.** `fact:skill-use-measured-two-channels-2026-08-14`: across every retained transcript, `where-am-i` was invoked **37 times as `/where` against 4 `get_skill` calls**. 55 of 63 sessions invoked a skill by command or Skill tool; 35 used `get_skill`. People type shortcuts; they rarely instruct an agent to fetch a skill. **A skill with no command is reachable only by the weaker of the two channels.** ⭐ **AND THE MEASUREMENT CUTS BOTH WAYS, WHICH IS WHY THE TEST IS PART OF THE RULING.** A skill WITH a command is invoked locally and vanishes from `get_skill` counts; a skill WITHOUT one can arrive by no other route. So widening coverage will make `surface_usage.py` report LOWER apparent skill use unless it learns to count both channels. That is a measurement artefact, not a regression, and it must not be read as one. ═══ WHAT IS OWED, AND THE SECOND HALF IS THE DURABLE ONE ═══ · Eleven new command files for capture-session, ci-gate, impact-check, ingest-corpus, link-artifacts, link-projects, parallel-work, plan-increments, report-friction, retire-from-design, revise-design. · **A TEST THAT PINS COVERAGE.** `skill_lint` already fails a command naming a skill that does not exist; **nothing fails a skill that no command names**, and nothing pins the count — which is how `dec:commands-are-the-exception`, `chg:commands-ship` and `ver:install-reaches-the-agent` all still say EIGHT while eleven ship. Without this half the set silently falls behind again the next time a skill is added. · The three records above should be corrected to the shipped number rather than left saying eight.		THE OPTIONS, WITH WHAT EACH COSTS. None is recommended here; the measurement is the contribution. **A — ship all twenty.** Consistent, and it is the option `dec:commands-are-the-exception` already argues for: each command is four lines of pointer with no version-coupled content, so twenty rot no faster than eight. COST: twenty files in a consumer repo. Alex, 2026-08-14, on init: it *'inserted several things into my project'* — and that report is why `dec:idea-init-asks-which-harness-and-installs-only-that` narrowed the install. **Widening the command set runs directly against the complaint that was just settled**, and these are Claude-Code-only files, so an OpenCode project gets twenty it cannot read. **B — ship none of the missing eleven, and fix DISCOVERY instead.** The server instructions already list every skill; the failure is that a user reaches for `/name` and gets a flat `Unknown command` from the HARNESS, which reflow2 never sees and cannot answer. COST: does nothing for the person typing the slash. Nothing in reflow2 can intercept it. **C — cover the skills a user REACHES FOR by name, and say so.** capture-session is the demonstrated case. COST: the criterion is taste, and the current eleven were chosen by the same unstated taste — which is how the shortfall went unnoticed. **WHAT IS NOT OPTIONAL EITHER WAY, and is the cheaper half:** the guard is asymmetric. `skill_lint` fails a command naming a missing skill; **nothing fails a skill that no command names**, and nothing pins the count, so the record still says 'eight' while eleven ship. Whichever option wins, the intended coverage should be asserted somewhere a test can read it — otherwise the next skill ships uncovered in silence exactly as these eleven did. **THE STANDING TRAP:** this is invisible from inside the checkout. `.claude/skills/` holds all twenty as compile sources, so Claude Code resolves every skill as `/name` HERE and on no consumer install. Any judgement about command ergonomics made in this repo is made in the one environment where the shortfall does not exist.acceptednothing
OPEN — the user asked for '2+' projects and what shipped is pairwise; should link-projects handle N, or say plainly that it handles two?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised 2026-08-13 while putting `req:linking-two-projects-is-a-served-process` to Anthony, flagged before he accepted it, and he accepted anyway — so the requirement stands and this stays open beneath it rather than blocking it. HIS ASK USED '2+': *'a process that we can reuse when a user wants to link 2+ reflow2 projects'*. THE SKILL THAT SHIPPED IS PAIRWISE, and does not say so. WHAT THE TOOLS ACTUALLY DO, checked rather than assumed: · `seam_report` takes a LIST of pairs, so it already composes across many boundaries in one call. · `pair_designs` takes exactly ONE other design. Three projects therefore means three runs (or six, if every pair is checked), and **nothing aggregates the results** — no report says 'these five designs, taken together, have these seams and these unmet needs.' ⇒ THE GAP IS NOT IN THE PROCESS BUT IN WHAT COLLECTS IT. Each pairwise answer is correct; there is no whole-neighbourhood view, and a user with five interrelated designs would have to hold that in their head. 📌 THIS IS WHERE `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` LIVES — ten reflow2 designs sit under `~/project`, all Anthony's, which is exactly the N-project case and the one place a shared vocabulary needs no negotiation (see the 'strongest narrow form' note on `dec:idea-defined-pair-types-so-two-projects-combine-by-lookup`). And `req:many-people-and-many-projects-compose` already says the two axes must hold TOGETHER, which neither accepted requirement states. THE OPTIONS, none taken: A — SAY IT PLAINLY. One line in the skill's 'Honest limits': it links two designs at a time, and N projects means N-1 or N(N-1)/2 runs with no aggregation. Cheapest, honest, and consistent with every other skill stating what it cannot do. **Does nothing for the user with five designs.** B — LET THE SKILL LOOP. Prescribe running the pairwise process over each pair and collating by hand. No code, but it puts on the user exactly the bookkeeping a tool should carry, and it will be skipped. C — A NEIGHBOURHOOD REPORT. Something that takes several designs and answers once — seams, unmet needs, dead surfaces across the set. Real work, and it needs the correspondence to be RECORDED rather than re-asserted per run, which is the same unbuilt prerequisite step 7 names. D — NOTHING YET. Wait for a real three-project case. reflow2↔flo2 is the only pair anyone has actually linked, and building an N-way view off a sample of one is the mistake the pairing measurements already warn about. ⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO MY OWN FLAG: I generalised 'distrust the name matcher' from a single pair, and D says the same caution applies here. A neighbourhood report designed before anyone has linked three real projects would be designed from imagination. ⇒ A IS OWED REGARDLESS AND COSTS ONE LINE — a skill whose ethos is stating its own limits currently does not state this one. C is the interesting one and should wait for evidence.		Recorded so a flag the user moved past is not lost. He asked for '2+', the shipped skill is pairwise, and the skill does not admit it — which matters more than usual because that skill's whole ethos is naming what it cannot do. The measurement underneath it: seam_report already takes a list of pairs and composes; pair_designs takes one other design and nothing aggregates across a set. So the gap is in what COLLECTS the answers, not in the process itself. Kept separate from dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects (where the graph lives for one owner with many projects) and from the pairing-mechanism decision, though both are adjacent — this one is narrowly about whether a shipped skill overstates its own scope. NOTE ON THIS NODE'S OWN HISTORY: the first write of it carried a malformed tail in this field, absorbed from a broken tool call. Corrected in place the same minute; the decision text was unaffected.proposednothing
OPEN — reflow2's GUIDED paths do sequence function before structure; the open question is whether anything makes a design SHOW it followed one
UNDECIDED — RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-16. ⚠️ THIS NODE'S FIRST VERSION WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. It said reflow2 has 'no SEQUENCE or GATE' and offered 'stay a vocabulary and a set of detectors' as the status quo. BOTH ARE FALSE, and I wrote them before reading the skills. Corrected the same day, on the same question. ⭐ WHAT THE GUIDED PATHS ACTUALLY DO, quoted rather than characterised: GENESIS enforces exactly the predecessor's order and uses its own labels: 'Seed the brief into P0/P1 — and stop there … `add_requirement` for each thing that must be true (P0) … `add_capability` for each thing the system does (P1) … **Do NOT create Components (P2) yet.** Leaving structure unspecified is deliberate: the first DETECT round will surface `concept_without_design`, which is the right next question ('how should this be structured?'). Answer it *with the user*, not by guessing.' The detector is real (`GapSource::ConceptWithoutDesign`). It also sets `mode` (`flexible` = design evolves with the build; `rigid` = design is the source of truth) at scaffold time — the predecessor's dial, with the predecessor's meaning, at the moment it matters. ADOPT is stricter and is the path a brownfield user takes. Five phases — Gather, Scan, Analyze (static then dynamic), Recover, Validate — and its central discipline is the SE one that matters most: 'NEVER INFER A REQUIREMENT FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION THAT SATISFIES IT. A requirement backed out of the code is satisfied by construction — it can never contradict anything, so a graph of those can never say anything.' It demands BOTH SIDES OF EVERY CONTRACT, keeps recovered requirements at `proposed` until the user's word, and closes with `coverage_report` to say what the design has never heard of. ⇒ REFLOW2 IS NOT A BARE VOCABULARY. It ships a sequenced, opinionated process on both the greenfield and brownfield paths, and the sequence is function-before-structure. WHY THE SELF-HOST IS NOT EVIDENCE AGAINST IT: reflow2 has no genesis epoch from a brief and was never taken through adopt. Its graph records organic growth with good bookkeeping — not a guided design. THE EXPERIMENT ANTHONY IS WORRIED ABOUT HAS NOT BEEN RUN ON REFLOW2 ITSELF. (And its functional decomposition WAS deliberate — `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition`, accepted 2026-07-23, derived with the user.) ⚠️ THE ONE PLACE THE SELF-HOST IS A FAIR INDICTMENT, and it is narrower than 'no process': reflow2's own graph VIOLATES ADOPT'S OWN INSTRUCTION. 'Both sides of every contract' — and there are 73 coupled module pairs with ZERO declared interfaces. THE QUESTION THAT REMAINS, and it is Anthony's real one restated: HOW DOES A USER GAIN CONFIDENCE THAT THE PROCESS WAS FOLLOWED? Nothing today records which skill a session used, at which phase, or reports when a design departed from the sequence. THE OPTIONS, revised: (a) NOTHING FURTHER. The guidance is good and the field reports support it — music_graph's own wins list says 'coverage_report is the single best thing in the adopt flow' and 'unmotivated_capability IS the design-recovery engine, exactly as the skill claims'. AGAINST: it leaves confidence resting on testimony rather than on anything the graph can show. (b) MAKE THE DESIGN SAY WHICH PROCESS PRODUCED IT — record the skill and phase a session worked in, so 'was he guided' becomes a fact rather than a hope. Cheap. AGAINST: it records the claim, not the conformance; a session can say `adopt` and do anything. (c) REPORT DEPARTURES FROM THE SEQUENCE — 'Components exist but no Capabilities', 'allocated before anything was decomposed', 'this boundary has no contract'. Every input is already computed, and it is the house style (`dec:report-dont-judge`). AGAINST: `undeclared_seam` has reported reflow2's own missing contracts all along, at severity 0.45, under the gate — a report nobody must act on is how the self-host drifted. (d) THE REAL EXPOSURE MAY BE NEITHER: skills are SERVED but must be REACHED FOR. `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` is ACCEPTED and says the user must never be the trigger — and it is NOT BUILT. The risk to a new user is not a flawed process; it is a session that never loads `adopt` and starts writing Components on day one. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether (d) is the dominant risk. Nobody has measured how often a consumer session actually invokes a skill.		Recorded as brainstorming on Anthony's `/brainstorm`, 2026-08-16, and CORRECTED the same day after reading the genesis and adopt skills — the first version asserted reflow2 had no process, which was my error from not reading before characterising. His question and framing throughout; the measurements and the correction are mine. The self-host half is `dec:idea-should-reflow2s-own-design-be-re-derived-through-a-principled-se-process`. Nothing is promoted; that is his word.proposedA user can see that reflow2 guided them through a principled process, rather than having to take it on trust
OPEN — should `unmotivated_capability` grade on whether the thing is BUILT, rather than only on provenance?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — thinking out loud with Anthony, 2026-08-11, from his question 'should reflow2 allow something to proceed without a requirement?' Nothing here is intent. THE MEASUREMENT THAT PROVOKED IT, taken on reflow2's own graph. 148 Capabilities, 18 with zero outgoing SATISFIES: 16 `imported` BL-nnn backlog rows none realized — wishes nobody has built 1 `authored`, not realized — a half-finished thought 1 `authored`, REALIZED BY AN ARTIFACT — cap:governance-proposal: SHIPPED CODE All eighteen scored 0.55 with the same wording: 'satisfies no requirement — what need does it serve, or should it go?' The one instance of shipped-but-unrequested in the entire design is indistinguishable from a parked backlog row. WHAT THE DETECTOR CURRENTLY GRADES ON (detect.rs:1269-1300): `provenance`. `inferred` → 0.70 with 'is built and running, but no requirement justifies it — is there a need nobody wrote down, or is this dead code?'; everything else → 0.55. The docstring is explicit that the bump exists to catch a feature in production during an ADOPTION pass. ⭐ THE OBSERVATION: `provenance` answers 'where did this node come from' (recovered from a real system vs written into the design). It does NOT answer 'does code exist for this'. On the adopt path those coincide, which is why the split works there and was never wrong. On the GENESIS path — a design under control where somebody builds an unrequested feature, which is Anthony's scenario — the capability is `authored` because a person wrote it in deliberately, AND realized because they shipped it. It lands at 0.55 with wording that reads like tidying up an idea. IDEAS, unranked: (a) Add REALIZES-presence as a second axis: authored+realized reads at the higher severity with the 'built and running' wording, because the cost of a wrong answer is a maintenance burden rather than a stray node. (b) Leave severity alone and change only the WORDING when realized, so the reader can tell shipped from unbuilt without the ranking moving. (c) Do nothing — 0.55 already surfaces it and the reader can look. COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside rather than suppressed: the current 0.70/0.55 split was tuned so that `inferred` 'clears `unsatisfied_requirement`'s 0.60 default exactly on the graph where the trial wanted it to and nowhere else' (detect.rs:1265-1268). Adding a second way to reach 0.70 changes a threshold that was set against a real trial, and nobody has re-run that trial. Option (b) is the version that costs nothing here. ALSO UNRESOLVED: no detector reads Project.mode at all (`project_mode` is read in genesis.rs and heal.rs, never in detect.rs). Whether mode SHOULD enter this is a separate question — provenance may already be carrying it adequately.		Anthony asked whether reflow2 should allow a capability with no requirement. It does, and reports it — but the report cannot distinguish shipped code from a parked wish, which are the two ends of exactly the judgement he was worried about.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 adopt embeddings and the HNSW index, or stay on lexical search?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced by the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review, but NOT a new idea: this question already exists as PROSE in docs/requirements-coverage.md ('Note: are embeddings (an embeddings-rs sidecar) actually needed?'). Recording it here moves it from a document into the graph, which is the direction dec:what-lives-where argues for; it does not settle it. STILL OPEN. WHAT IS AVAILABLE AND UNUSED: dynograph-vector ships an HNSW approximate-nearest-neighbour index (HnswConfig / HnswIndex / SearchResult, with filtered, batch and snapshot-persisted search) plus SIMD cosine similarity and the whole distance family. reflow2 uses none of it. search_design is BM25 lexical, and the schema carries embedding_field declarations on several node types that nothing populates. THE CASE FOR: semantic search would find a requirement whose words differ from the query's. It would also strengthen resolution — the duplicate-detection path already has a fuzzy_then_vector strategy declared in the schema with the vector half unimplemented. THE CASE AGAINST, and it is why this has stayed parked: embeddings need a MODEL, and reflow2-core is deliberately LLM-free and deterministic. An embedding provider at the core would break that, and putting it at the seam means a sidecar to install, version and keep in sync — which cuts against req:thin-install and the whole served-not-installed posture. Determinism is also load-bearing here: two runs of a detector must agree, and an ANN index is approximate by construction. --- 2026-08-04, re-examined while building BL-186 (cap:corpus-ingest). Four things are now MEASURED rather than supposed, and one distinction is offered against the case-against. The question is still open and this update does not settle it. --- 1. THE PRODUCER EXISTS AND IS ANTHONY'S OWN. `embeddings-rs` (github.com/sligara7/embeddings-rs, local at a990e4d v0.1.1) is a Rust/ONNX parity sidecar for nomic-embed-text-v1.5 with a code-derived, drift-gated OpenAPI contract, written to pair with dynograph-foundation. That matters to the case-against: 'a provider dependency' and 'a local, self-hosted, contract-frozen sidecar you maintain' are not the same risk, and the deferral's stated reason was avoiding an external LLM provider. 2. THE WHOLE PATH EXISTS AND IS INERT — VERIFIED, not read from the earlier note. dynograph-storage has an embeddings column family with set_embedding / get_embedding / delete_embedding / scan_embeddings_by_type. dynograph-vector really does ship HNSW (crates/dynograph-vector/src/hnsw.rs) and SIMD cosine (distance.rs). reflow2's own schema declares embedding_field on Capability, Requirement, Question and others. reflow2's source contains exactly two matches for 'embedding': a bidi-sanitizer comment and a doc comment saying 'no embeddings'. So the missing piece was never the model or the index — it is reflow2 calling any of it. embedding_field is another declared-and-read-by-nothing field, this time spanning four components. 3. NOT NEEDED FOR cap:corpus-ingest, AND ANTHONY SCOPED IT OUT ON 2026-08-04: 'keep BL-186 lexical and ship it.' The cost half of the corpus problem is candidate generation, which the BM25 index already in the served binary answers; embeddings would ADD a round trip per node, not remove one. The ordering half was a naming bug, fixed lexically. The folder driver needs no vectors. 4. WHERE IT WOULD ACTUALLY EARN ITS KEEP, and this is the honest limit of the lexical answer: req:corpus-ingest requires that 'the same component named in forty specifications must converge on one node'. Forty authors do not merely reorder tokens, they choose different words. token_sort_ratio cannot see 'Read Cache' ~ 'Local Store' at all — that is not a low score, it is invisible. The cases the scope doc names (Auth Service / Authentication Service = 84, Gateway / API Gateway = 74) are the EASY ones because they still share tokens. So shipping BL-186 lexical satisfies the requirement's ordering clause and its cost, and leaves its convergence clause satisfied only for documents that happen to share vocabulary. That limit should be stated to a user pointing reflow2 at a heterogeneous corpus rather than discovered by them. 5. THE DISTINCTION OFFERED AGAINST THE CASE-AGAINST: determinism is treated above as one blanket objection — 'two runs of a detector must agree, and an ANN index is approximate by construction'. That is strong for search_design and for anything feeding a gate. It is materially weaker for INGEST RESOLUTION, because under dec:ask-not-repair that path's output is a merge_candidate a human rules on, not a verdict. Approximate retrieval feeding a QUESTION is a different risk from approximate retrieval feeding a GATE. So the answer may not be a single yes/no: 'yes, on the ingest resolution path only' would leave req:deterministic-core intact. Offered as a distinction to consider, not as advocacy — the req:thin-install objection stands unchanged either way, since a sidecar to install, version and keep in sync is a real change to the one-binary deployment story. --- 2026-08-06: FIRST EXTERNAL EVIDENCE. Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 survey of the 'graph brain' ecosystem (relayed by Anthony), recorded here because it bears on the case-against and on nothing else in the node. Does not settle the question. --- 6. EVERY COMPARABLE SYSTEM IN THE FIELD IS HYBRID, NOT LEXICAL. Mem0 combines vector search with graph relations and key-value storage; Cognee's pipeline is ingest, chunk, entity/relationship extraction, then vector DB plus graph DB plus relational, queried by hybrid graph-and-semantic similarity; Zep/Graphiti, Letta, LangMem and LlamaIndex Memory all rest on vector retrieval. Not one of the surveyed systems is retrieval-lexical-only. That does not make lexical wrong — none of those systems has reflow2's determinism requirement, because none of them feeds a GATE, which is precisely the distinction drawn in point 5 — but it does mean the case-against can no longer include 'nobody needs this': everyone building in this space has paid for it. The question narrows to whether reflow2's gate-feeding, one-binary posture is worth the retrieval quality it costs, and that is a real trade rather than an oversight. 7. WHAT THE COMPARISON DOES NOT SHOW: none of those systems has to answer a query the same way twice, and none of them exports a byte-stable artifact a CI gate diffs. So their unanimity is weak evidence about reflow2's core and strong evidence only about the ingest-resolution path — exactly where point 5 already located the weaker objection. The external evidence therefore sharpens the existing distinction rather than adding a new argument.		Captured because the review found the HNSW index entirely unused and the question live only in prose. The honest status is 'already parked, now visible' rather than 'newly proposed'. Updated 2026-08-04 after BL-186 forced the question in practice: the findings above are measured against the local checkouts of embeddings-rs and dynograph-foundation rather than recalled, and the per-path determinism distinction is new. Anthony's scoping call — BL-186 ships lexical — is recorded here so the decision to defer is visible on the node itself rather than only in the increment that deferred it. Updated 2026-08-06 with the first EXTERNAL datum: the whole comparable field is hybrid graph-plus-vector, which removes one leg of the case-against without touching the determinism or thin-install legs.proposednothing
OPEN — every reflow2 project uses a git repo, so should reflow2 PROMPT each one to shape its own workflow governance rather than wait for someone to state them?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Anthony, 2026-08-11: 'since every reflow2 project will use git repo, then a project needs to shape its own governance rules for that project.' ⭐ THE ARGUMENT IS UNIVERSALITY, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THIS A PRODUCT QUESTION RATHER THAN REPO HYGIENE. `req:persistence` is ACCEPTED — the design lives in-repo alongside the code — so a git repository is not one deployment choice among many, it is the substrate every reflow2 project stands on. That makes the QUESTIONS predictable even though the ANSWERS are not: who may merge, what may land on the main line, when the design export is written, whether breaking any of it should stop a build. Every project will face them; each will answer differently. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, and the gap is in the TRIGGER rather than the vocabulary: · `cap:governance-proposal` — BUILT and shipping. Asks what breaking a rule should cost and writes `enforced` explicitly in both directions. But it is REACTIVE: it fires when somebody happens to state a rule. Nothing asks the question first. · `DesignRule` + three-state `enforced` + `unverified_enforced_rule` — the layer is there. · `req:a-project-records-how-it-ships` (proposed, Anthony 2026-07-31) — ADJACENT AND NOT THE SAME. That is the ordered RELEASE PROCEDURE, and its own text says the steps are not derivable from the graph. This is workflow AUTHORITY and TIMING, which is a different question with the same property: not derivable, project-specific, and currently unrecorded until someone volunteers it. · `genesis` captures deployment and platform context as Requirements — target platforms, the driving agent — and captures NOTHING about how the project's work reaches its main line. · `req:a-node-can-say-who-may-change-it` (proposed) — node-level authority, not merge authority. 📌 AND HIS OWN 2026-08-08 FRAMING ALREADY NAMED MERGING, in the entry that produced reflow2's governance layer: 'every project will be managed differently and have differing sets of people running it with their own practices and POLICIES ABOUT MERGING AND WHO CAN MERGE and other governing mechanisms — but allowing reflow2 to setup a generic set of nodes/edges that allow a user or set of users to define their own project management policies/governance in graph form is something that I think would be really helpful.' The capture half of that shipped. The half that would make a project actually reach for it did not. ⭐ WHY REACTIVE CAPTURE IS NOT ENOUGH, measured rather than argued. reflow2 itself has run for weeks with `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly` stated NOWHERE in its design until 2026-08-09 — that rule's own text records it: 'it lived in an agent's memory file and in Anthony's head, and it was followed twice that day by a session reading it from neither.' A reactive mechanism cannot capture a rule nobody thinks to state, and a rule everybody follows is exactly the one nobody states. IDEAS, unranked: (a) ASK AT GENESIS/ADOPT. A short set of workflow questions alongside the deployment ones, each landing as a DesignRule with its consequence stated. Reaches every project once, at the moment the repo is being set up anyway. (b) ASK WHEN THE EVIDENCE APPEARS, not at bootstrap. A design that has gained a Release, or a second Contributor, or a second seat, has demonstrably reached the point where merge authority matters — and at genesis nobody has an opinion yet, which is the same objection that makes asking for feedback consent at INSTALL read worse than at UPDATE. (c) SHIP A STARTER SET as advisory DesignRules the project edits or deletes — reflow2's own four, generalised. Fastest to value and the most dangerous: a default rule is an opinion nobody chose, which is precisely what `cap:governance-proposal` exists to prevent, and `req:defaults-do-not-assert` forbids. (d) Nothing. The vocabulary is there; a project that wants governance can state it, and prompting risks manufacturing policy nobody needed. ⚠️ THE STRONGEST OBJECTION, and it is Anthony's own from a different day: `dec:proposed-requirements-pruned` dropped two requirements as 'backlog hygiene dressed as product requirements', with the test being whether a requirement changes what anyone BUILDS. A prompt that produces four DesignRules nobody enforces has changed nothing and added four nodes. What would save (a) or (b) from that is the CONSEQUENCE question — governance-proposal's actual contribution — because a rule with a stated, chosen consequence does change what the build does. ⚠️ SECOND: the questions are only universal if they stay in PURE GIT. 'Who may merge' is a forge concept on GitHub and a filesystem-permission concept on a bare remote; 'what lands on the main line' is expressible in plain git and survives both. See dec:idea-should-reflow2-carry-its-own-git-discipline, where reflow2's own rule is stated entirely in GitHub's vocabulary and is partly unfollowable without one. ⚠️ THIRD, the scale objection: a solo project and a seven-session fleet need different answers, and asking a solo developer to state merge authority is asking him to gate himself — which is exactly why Anthony made reflow2's own branch-then-PR rule ADVISORY rather than enforced ('there is nobody to stop'). Any prompt must be able to accept 'nobody, it is just me' as a real answer rather than an incomplete one.		Git is the substrate every reflow2 project stands on, which makes the governance questions predictable even though the answers differ per project. The capture half shipped and is reactive; nothing asks first. reflow2's own experience is the evidence that reactive is insufficient — its branch-then-PR rule existed nowhere in its design for weeks while being followed daily, because a rule everybody follows is the one nobody thinks to state.proposednothing
OPEN — a collaborator clones, writes feedback into the graph, pushes; the other pulls and has it. Four steps make that work and three of them fail silently — how much should be automatic?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-13, after taking a pile of Alex's feedback over the phone. HIS WORDS: *'I told him to just git clone the repo and then run via his agent/session to add the feedback directly into the graph. Then he should git push. My idea would be that next time I git pull, I should have all his feedback in the graph?'* ⭐ **THE ANSWER IS YES, AND IT IS WHAT THE DESIGN IS BUILT FOR** — `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (no server, the file is the transport), the three-way merge, and the `parallel-work` skill all exist for exactly this. It is not a new mechanism; it is the intended one. 📌 SEPARATE FROM `dec:central-host`, which asks whether reflow2 gains a hosted MCP surface ALONGSIDE the repo file. That question is about REPLACING or supplementing the transport; this one is about whether the transport we already have is DEFENDED. A hosted surface would make all four steps below moot, which is an argument for that node rather than an answer to this one. 🛑 **FOUR STEPS HAVE TO HAPPEN, AND THREE ARE SILENT IF MISSED.** Checked against the repo rather than assumed: 1. **ALEX MUST IMPORT FIRST, BEFORE HE WRITES ANYTHING.** A fresh clone has no `.reflow2/`, so his first reflow2 use MINTS A NEW DESIGN with a new `graph_id` — and his export would then be a different design that merely looks similar. Measured on the v0.30.0 cut: importing into an EMPTY store prints *'this store was empty, so it takes the imported design's name (reflow2)'*, so importing first preserves identity and writing first does not. **Silent either way.** 2. **ALEX MUST EXPORT TO `docs/design/.json` BEFORE PUSHING.** `.reflow2/` is gitignored, so his graph writes are invisible to git; pushing without exporting sends NOTHING and the push succeeds. ⇒ **THIS IS THE EXACT DEFECT HE HIT TODAY** (`fact:second-user-first-run-report-2026-08-13`): he could not find the committable record because a fresh install never made one. **His feedback plan depends on the thing that was broken, and would have failed silently before this morning's fix.** 3. **HIS CLONE WILL NOT HAVE THE MERGE DRIVER.** `.gitattributes` declares `docs/design/reflow2.json merge=reflow2`, but its own comment says the driver *'needs (to be) defined once per clone (git deliberately does not let a repository configure an executable)'*. MEASURED: it IS configured in this clone, and **`tools/reflow2_init.py` does not install it** — grep for `merge.reflow2` / `gitattributes` in the installer returns nothing. So Alex gets git's LINE-BASED text merge on a 5 MB JSON graph document. The `.gitattributes` comment calls that *'safe — it just means you resolve the JSON by hand'*, which is true and is not a thing anyone will do. 4. **ANTHONY MUST IMPORT AFTER PULLING.** `git pull` updates the FILE; the live graph is a separate store. `sync_status` reports `behind` and names the missing ids — and it **deliberately never auto-imports**, because *'import is an upsert and an unasked one would silently overwrite live work'* (`dec:ask-not-repair`). So the last step is a conscious act by design, and it is at least LOUD. ⇒ **THE PLAN IS RIGHT AND THE PATH IS UNDEFENDED.** Three of the four steps produce a successful-looking outcome when skipped: mint-instead-of-import, push-without-export, and a text merge on a graph. ═══ THE OPTIONS, none taken ═══ A — **NOTHING. Tell people the four steps.** The `parallel-work` skill already prescribes most of it. CHEAPEST; and this session is the evidence against it, because the skill exists and Alex still hit step 2 head-on. `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` says a catalogue cannot deliver a discipline that applies mid-flow. B — **THE INSTALLER CONFIGURES THE MERGE DRIVER.** `reflow2_init.py` already writes `.mcp.json`, hooks and `.gitignore`; two `git config` calls close step 3 entirely. **The narrow, obviously-good one.** Costs: it must point at a binary path that exists on THAT machine — the same absolute-path problem `.mcp.json` already has and already solves. C — **IMPORT-ON-FIRST-USE.** If a store is empty and a committed export sits beside it, adopt rather than mint. Closes step 1, and it is the behaviour the import path ALREADY has once somebody thinks to call it. ⚠️ Adopting a design because a file happened to be present is the silent inference `describe_designs` refuses; it would have to say loudly what it did. D — **A PULL-SIDE NUDGE.** `sync_status` already computes `behind` with the ids; the loop hint could say it on the first call of a session rather than waiting to be asked. Closes step 4's discoverability without touching its deliberate manual-ness. E — **A `sync` SKILL** covering all four steps as one named workflow, the way `link-projects` now covers linking. Cheap, and the same shape that just worked for a process nobody could reconstruct. ⚠️ **THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT WORTH KEEPING, AND IT ARGUES AGAINST C SPECIFICALLY:** every step here is silent-when-skipped, and the instinct is to automate all of them. But step 4 is deliberately manual on `dec:ask-not-repair`'s reasoning — an unasked upsert can overwrite live work — and step 1 has the same shape from the other side. **Automating an act because forgetting it is expensive is exactly how a tool starts making design decisions on somebody's behalf.** B and D add no inference and are safe; C infers. 📌 A PRACTICAL NOTE THAT IS NOT PART OF THE DESIGN QUESTION: Alex pushing to `main` directly would collide with `dec:export-once-per-pr` and the branch-then-PR practice. Either he opens a PR, or his feedback lands on a branch Anthony merges — worth telling him before he tries, since a rejected push is a discouraging first experience of contributing.		Recorded under the brainstorm skill: Anthony asked whether a plan would work rather than deciding anything, and the plan turns out to be the design's intended path with three undefended steps in it. Worth keeping for the measurements rather than the idea, which is not new: the merge driver is declared in .gitattributes but NOT installed by reflow2_init.py (grep confirms), so a fresh clone silently falls back to git's line merge on a 5 MB JSON graph; and a fresh store mints a new graph_id unless the export is imported first, measured on the v0.30.0 cut when an empty store reported taking the imported design's name. The connection worth not losing: step 2 of Anthony's plan is precisely the defect Alex reported this morning. His feedback route depends on the committable record existing, and before today's fix it did not — so the plan would have produced a successful push carrying nothing. Kept separate from dec:central-host because that asks whether to add a hosted surface alongside the repo file, which would make these four steps moot; this asks whether the transport already in use is defended. Options B and D are recorded as the safe ones and C as the risky one on purpose. Automating a step because forgetting it is expensive is how a tool starts inferring intent, and step 4's manual-ness is a decision (dec:ask-not-repair), not an oversight.acceptednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 ask, once, whether a project wants to send feedback back, and record that consent in the graph?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Alex's idea (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-11; his input is ADVISORY per rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word. HIS WORDS: 'You should put in an update that asks me if I want to collect feedback and store my decision in the graph or something. And put the skill in your skills. That way you get what you want.' TWO HALVES, AND ONE IS ALREADY DONE. The skill half is satisfied: `report-friction` is served and ships in the kit, one of eighteen — that he asked for it is itself recorded as evidence under fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11, because a user asking for an installed capability is the sharpest form of `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`. THE NEW HALF IS CONSENT: nothing in reflow2 asks whether a project is willing to send anything back, and nothing records the answer. Grepped 2026-08-11 — no consent, opt-in-to-feedback or telemetry machinery exists anywhere in the core or the surface. ⭐ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT COLLECTION. Every piece of field evidence reflow2 has was carried back by hand, by two people who happen to talk to each other. dec:idea-field-evidence-is-a-prioritisation-input asks whether that evidence should reach prioritisation; this asks whether the evidence ARRIVES AT ALL from anyone outside that circle. A prioritisation input with a single-digit number of sources is not a prioritisation input, and weighting by SOURCE INDEPENDENCE — the honest version of that idea — is impossible while every source is the same two households. ⭐⭐ AND ALEX'S FRAMING IS THE DESIGN, not a nicety. 'ASKS ME... AND STORE MY DECISION IN THE GRAPH.' Not a config flag, not an env var, not a default: a decision, asked once, on the record, revisitable. That is `cap:governance-proposal`'s shape applied to the consumer relationship rather than to a build rule, and it is exactly what `req:defaults-do-not-assert` demands of anything with a substantive default — silence must not read as yes, and it must not read as no either. WHERE IT WOULD LIVE. `req:frictionless-update` is accepted ('install is one command, update is one word', modelled on Claude Code). The update path is the natural moment to ask: it already exists, it is already a place a human is present and consenting to something, and `reflow2 update` is queued work. Asking at INSTALL rather than UPDATE was considered and reads worse — at install nobody has used the tool yet, so there is nothing to have an opinion about. IDEAS, unranked: (a) A one-time ask at update, recorded as a Decision in the graph with the user's word. Revisitable, visible in the design, and it costs nothing when declined. (b) Ask, but record it OUTSIDE the graph (a config file). Keeps the design clean of tooling state and loses the thing Alex specifically asked for — a decision he can see and change later. (c) No ask. Keep `report-friction` as the only route and make it more discoverable instead. Cheapest and it does nothing about arrival rate. (d) Ask, and additionally make the reporting one command. Alex's whole framing is 'that way you get what you want', which reads as him volunteering — the bottleneck he is naming is that nobody asked him, not that he lacked a tool. ⚠️⚠️ THE HOLE THIS LANDS ON IS ALREADY NAMED AND STILL OPEN. `docs/partnership.md` lists DATA-PRIVACY MARKING among the three uncovered failure modes: 'local-first by decision, and report-friction redacts by design; but NO FIELD IS MARKED SENSITIVE, so nothing can enforce redaction mechanically.' A consented feedback channel makes that hole load-bearing. Consent to send is not consent to send ANYTHING, and today the redaction is a skill's discipline rather than a property the graph can check. This must not ship ahead of that. ⚠️ SECOND: consent recorded in a design that gets EXPORTED and committed is consent that travels. Whose consent is it when a second contributor pulls the repo? `req:a-node-can-say-who-may-change-it` (proposed) is the adjacent unbuilt piece, and this is a concrete case for it. ⚠️ THIRD, and it cuts against the whole idea: reflow2 is local-first by decision (`dec:repo-file-embedded` weighs 'the user's design on a machine they do not control' AGAINST a service). Any channel that sends anything anywhere is in tension with that, and the honest version may be a channel that only ever produces a FILE the user chooses to send — which is what report-friction already does.		Every piece of field evidence reflow2 holds arrived by hand from two related sources, which is precisely why the prioritisation idea recorded beside it cannot weight by source independence. Alex's framing — ask once, record the decision in the graph — is the right shape and matches how this project already handles a rule's consequence. The blocker is that it lands squarely on the data-privacy-marking hole partnership.md names as uncovered, where redaction is a skill's discipline rather than anything the graph can enforce.proposednothing
OPEN — should MEASURED FIELD EVIDENCE (friction reports here, test reports in any project) be an input to what to work on next?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-11. Nothing here is intent. HIS FRAMING, in his words: 'feedback that I've been giving back to from various projects... is clear demand signal of what needs prioritized... Obviously, this is demand signal for reflow2 itself; perhaps, in a general project, this would be akin to 'test reports', which should help prioritize which things need fixed immediately versus other desirements.' And the sharpening that prompted it: two items in a fresh external report were things ALREADY ACCEPTED and unbuilt, so the report did not propose them — it CONFIRMED them, which is a different and more actionable signal. THE MEASUREMENT, taken 2026-08-11 on this design: TemporalFact nodes 133 of fact_type `defect` 123 — every one basis: measured of those, whose text describes RECURRENCE 70 (instance / recurred / third time / two projects / again) ranking computations that read any of them 0 `what_next` scores connectedness only: governed nodes (+1 each), those scheduled into an increment (+2), CONTRADICTS an accepted Decision (+2). `crates/reflow2-core/src/what_next.rs` never references TEMPORAL_FACT. The only readers anywhere are nodes.rs (constants), temporal.rs (the writer), preserve.rs (classification) and readiness.rs (forecasts). So reflow2 holds a corpus of 123 measured field observations and cannot let one of them move a priority. ⭐ THE WORKED EXAMPLE IS FROM TODAY AND IT COST FORTY MINUTES. `fact:defect-rebuild-strands-the-shared-server` (2026-08-07) recorded a defect at basis `measured`, confidence 1, WITH ITS FIX WRITTEN IN ITS OWN EVIDENCE FIELD. A sibling fact counted three instances across two projects and two machines and noted the third 'landed on the maintainer'. A fourth instance hit on 2026-08-11 and blocked every graph tool. Between the diagnosis and the fix, FOUR DAYS, during which nothing ranked it — because a TemporalFact is not a Decision and `what_next` scores Decisions. The issue it was filed under was CLOSED with the finding unfixed. ⚠️⚠️ THE DECISIVE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS ANTHONY'S OWN, AND IT IS ALREADY ACCEPTED. `dec:proposed-requirements-pruned` (2026-07-30) DROPPED `req:friction-has-a-severity-bar` and `req:friction-has-a-baseline` with this reason: 'Both are backlog hygiene dressed as product requirements: THE ANSWER TO UNCONVERTED FRICTION REPORTS IS TO ACT ON THEM, NOT TO MODEL THEM.' His stated test was whether a requirement changes what anyone BUILDS, and 'how the project manages itself' does not. Any version of this idea has to answer that or it is a re-litigation. THE ARGUMENT THAT IT IS NOT THE SAME THING, offered so he can judge it rather than be persuaded by it: the dropped pair were about REFLOW2 MEASURING ITSELF — a usability baseline, and a threshold at which reflow2's own friction becomes reflow2's own scheduled work. That is process. THIS is about whether ANY user's design can let measured field evidence — test reports, incident records, trial findings — reach the thing that says what to work on next. That is a product capability with a code citation, which is exactly what survived his prune. The honest counter to the counter: it is also convenient for me to say so, and he is the one who drew the 'backlog hygiene' line in the first place. IDEAS, unranked: (a) Give `what_next` a term for measured evidence: a Decision or Requirement that a `defect` TemporalFact is ABOUT scores higher, and higher again when independent instances accumulate. Small, reuses the existing vocabulary, changes a ranking nobody has to trust. (b) Do not touch the score; add a BAND. `what_next` already separates `marked` / `ranked` / `unexplored` / `shaping` precisely because they answer different questions. A fifth band — 'things the field has told you about' — reports the evidence without pretending it is commensurable with connectedness. (c) Model the confirmation case only, which is the narrow half Anthony actually pointed at: when external evidence lands on something ALREADY ACCEPTED AND UNBUILT, say so. That is a much smaller claim than ranking, and it is the one his example supports. (d) Nothing. Act on the reports.
