This is his 2026-07-30 answer and it has not been shown to have failed — the spawn defect was not unranked because ranking was missing, it was unbuilt because nobody picked it up. ⚠️ THE TRAP, AND THE GRAPH ALREADY NAMED IT. `fact:the-stale-server-defect-recurred-to-the-people-who-wrote-it-down` carries its own caveat: 'recurrence is not automatically corroboration — these three share a CAUSE rather than a METHOD, so they add weight to the COST, not to the diagnosis.' A naive instance count would have read three findings-by-the-same-route as three independent confirmations. Whatever counts here must distinguish *found the same way twice* from *found two different ways*, or it manufactures confidence — the same failure as `dec:` on BM25 scores not being relevances. SECOND TRAP: a count of reports is gameable by whoever writes the most reports, and reflow2's field evidence currently comes from a small number of closely-related sources. Weighting by SOURCE INDEPENDENCE is the honest version and is much harder than counting. NOTE ON WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this is not built twice: `report-friction` writes the reports, `TemporalFact` holds them with `basis`/`confidence`, and the reconcile family (`reconcile_artifacts` / `_verification` / `_deployment`) already turns observations into findings. The gap is not capture and not vocabulary. It is that nothing carries any of it forward into what to do next.		reflow2 holds 123 measured defect facts, 70 describing recurrence, and no ranking reads any of them — while a fully-diagnosed defect with its fix already written down sat four days and recurred. The generalisation to test reports is sound. What it must answer is Anthony's own accepted decision that friction prioritisation is backlog hygiene rather than product, and the graph's own warning that recurrence by the same method is not corroboration.proposednothing
OPEN — how does a downstream owner levy a requirement on an upstream design they do not own? (Anthony leans: write-only-at-proposed, carried by git)
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-06: 'having somewhat independent reflow2 projects linked allows for requirements from one project to flow naturally to another without a user specifying we need to update package x because package y has a gap that only package x can fix. having reflow2 be able to do this automatically would be great.' THE WORKED EXAMPLE IS THIS REPOSITORY, AND IT WAS ENTIRELY BY HAND. flo2 hit a wall it could not climb from inside itself — a proposed Decision that nothing reported — and the fix had to land in reflow2. What carried it across was a human writing a markdown proposal in the flo2 repo, a human reading it, and an agent re-typing it as reflow2 nodes (chg:flo2-proposal-multi-graph-hosting). NOTHING IN EITHER GRAPH KNEW. ⭐ SHARPENED 2026-08-06 BY A CONCRETE CASE AND A SCALING ARGUMENT THAT CHANGES THE ANSWER. Anthony: 'say my brother, who only has read access for reflow2, needs place a requirement upon reflow2 in order for flo2 to properly function... should my brother have the ability to add proposed ideas to reflow2 (write only for proposed, else read only) or should my brother place the external requirement in flo2 and when I open all 3 of my projects, it'll (the agent) see this requirement in the flo2 graph. I'm leaning towards the prior because say projectA (the one being depended upon) is huge and has multiple other projects dependent upon it and don't actually track any of the dependent projects/graphs, then option B may not function... think of it like a Google service is project A...they are not going to load every graph that is dependent upon them.' ⭐ THAT ARGUMENT DEFEATS OPTION (C) BELOW, WHICH THIS AGENT HAD RECOMMENDED, AND THE REFUTATION IS RECORDED RATHER THAN THE RECOMMENDATION QUIETLY WITHDRAWN. 'The upstream pulls rather than the downstream pushes' rests on the upstream being able to ENUMERATE ITS DEPENDENTS. A widely-depended-on design cannot: it does not know who depends on it, and would not load their graphs if it did. And DISCOVERY OF DEPENDENTS IS ITSELF A PUSH — either the upstream somehow learns of every consumer, or consumers register, and registering is a write. Pull cannot bootstrap itself. It survives only in the SMALL federation case Anthony described earlier (C's owner asking who declares a dependency on C, finding exactly D). ⭐ THE ANALOGY IS AN ISSUE TRACKER, NOT PUB/SUB. Anthony reached for 'socket publish/subscribe'. Pub/sub is the right shape for the OTHER direction and already exists: the upstream publishes its surface (export_surface, built), consumers mirror it (mirror_surface, built). The REVERSE channel in every real ecosystem is a tracker: you do not get write access to Google's codebase, you file an issue. ANYONE MAY FILE; ONLY MAINTAINERS TRIAGE. That is precisely 'write only for proposed, else read only', and it scales because the upstream keeps ONE inbox rather than N graphs. ⭐⭐ IN SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING TERMS THIS IS NOT EXOTIC, IT IS THE NORMAL DIRECTION. flo2 is a CUSTOMER of reflow2; reflow2 is the SUPPLIER. A customer levying a requirement on a supplier is the most ordinary transaction in the discipline. Framing it as 'writing into a design you do not own' made an unremarkable act sound like a violation. ⭐⭐ THE VOCABULARY IS ALREADY THERE, WHICH THIS AGENT PREVIOUSLY GOT WRONG BY NOT LOOKING. Checked against describe_schema, a Requirement already carries every field this needs: `source` ('who/what stated it — a user, a regulation, a stakeholder'), `provenance` with an `imported` value, `designation` published/internal so the downstream can mark what it publishes, `status` starting at `proposed` with only the owner's word moving it off (set_requirement_status), and AUTHORED_BY carrying role author/reviewer/approver. A levied requirement is expressible TODAY as: add_requirement (lands proposed) + authored_by role=author + source '' + provenance imported. NOTHING IN THE SCHEMA NEEDS TO CHANGE. ⭐ AND IT IS ALREADY REPORTABLE, BY WORK MERGED THE SAME DAY. loop_status gained `unsettled_assigned_decisions` (PR #81, 2026-08-06) — a Decision left proposed while carrying an approver edge. The identical shape answers 'a proposed Requirement from an external source is waiting on you'. THE INBOX IS ALREADY COMPUTABLE; it has never been pointed at this case. SO WHAT IS MISSING IS TWO THINGS: (1) TRANSPORT — how a node gets from their machine into this graph; (2) ENFORCEMENT — nothing stops a writer doing more than filing, because reflow2 HAS NO AUTHENTICATION and cannot acquire one without becoming a different product. ⭐ TRANSPORT ALREADY EXISTS, AND IT IS **GIT** — NOT ANY ONE PROVIDER. ⚠️ CORRECTED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-06, and the correction matters because the first version of this node named GitHub: 'we can probably use GitHub for this example, but not every project will use GitHub. every project is designed to use a git repo though so other git providers like gitlab can also work.' The mechanism is a BRANCH CARRYING A PROPOSED-STATUS NODE IN THE COMMITTED EXPORT, offered to the owner, who merges it or does not. Every primitive that needs is plain git — a branch, a diff, a merge — and reflow2's own three-way merge driver already operates on the export FILE, provider-agnostic by construction. A hosted forge (GitHub pull request, GitLab merge request, Gitea, Bitbucket) is one CONVENIENT UI over those primitives and supplies the review gate and audit trail for free; NONE OF IT IS REQUIRED. With no forge at all the same exchange works by `git format-patch` and email, `git request-pull`, or a shared bare repo over SSH — which is also what makes it usable where a forge cannot go, including the disconnected case dec:idea-need-to-know-compartments cares about. THE LOAD-BEARING FACT: dec:multi-writer-architecture (accepted) already made the repo file the unit of exchange, and req:persistence puts the design inside the consumer project. So 'the design travels as a file in a git repo' is not a workaround adopted for this feature — it is the architecture, and this transport falls out of it for free. ZERO NEW REFLOW2 CODE. ITS LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: it requires the filer to have a clone and a git workflow, which is exactly what flo2's non-technical contributors do not have — so for the HOSTED case flo2's own layer must be the mailbox, and that lands back on req:reflow2-consumable-as-an-image and dec:one-process-many-stores. OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN — REORDERED BY THE ARGUMENT ABOVE. (A) ⭐ ANTHONY'S LEAN: WRITE-ONLY-AT-PROPOSED. A consumer may create nodes at `proposed`, attributed and sourced, and may do nothing else — no accepting, no editing, no deleting. Expressible in today's schema, reportable by today's loop, transportable by plain git, and it scales because the upstream keeps one inbox rather than N graphs. Counter, and it is the honest one: reflow2 cannot enforce it. 'Write only for proposed' is a property of WHATEVER HOLDS THE MAILBOX — a forge's branch permissions, a maintainer's judgement, or flo2's own layer — and calling it a reflow2 feature would be the same overclaim dec:idea-need-to-know-compartments warns about. (B) THE REQUIREMENT STAYS IN THE DOWNSTREAM GRAPH and the upstream owner sees it when they open both. Anthony's own counter is decisive at scale: a heavily-depended-on design will not load its dependents' graphs and does not know who they are. Still fine for the two-brothers case, and it is what the composition machinery already supports with no new anything. (C) THE UPSTREAM PULLS. Refuted above as a general mechanism. Retained for the small federation case only. (D) A THIRD, PROGRAM-LEVEL GRAPH holding cross-project intent, with the others as composed children. dec:nested-graphs and cap:derived-completion anticipate the shape. Answers 'where does shared intent live' rather than 'how does a need travel', and adds a design to maintain. ⚠️ THE PREREQUISITE THAT STILL BOUNDS ALL OF IT: dec:linked-repos-poc was RUN 2026-08-06 and found reflow2 declares NO `required` interface at all, so nothing pairs across any seam. The channel this node is about has no labelled boundary to run along. ⚠️ AND THE CONSTRAINT FROM dec:idea-need-to-know-compartments: an automatic cross-graph write is a channel between compartments, and the safe direction is defined against SENSITIVITY, not against the dependency arrow. Option (A) is materially safer than any automatic flow precisely because a human files it and a human accepts it — the write is deliberate at both ends.		Captured under the brainstorm skill 2026-08-06, then SHARPENED twice the same day. ⭐ THREE CORRECTIONS TO THIS AGENT ARE PRESERVED IN THE NODE rather than edited away, because each was a different failure worth keeping visible. (1) Option (C), upstream-pulls, was RECOMMENDED here and is refuted by Anthony's Google-service argument: pull requires enumerating dependents, a widely-used design cannot, and discovery of dependents is itself a push, so pull cannot bootstrap. (2) This node previously implied the graph could not express a levied requirement. describe_schema shows it already can — `source`, `provenance: imported`, `designation`, `status: proposed` and AUTHORED_BY roles are all present. Same failure dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs corrected on 2026-08-05: asserting an absence from a summary instead of reading the surface. READ THE SCHEMA, NOT THE SUMMARY. (3) The transport was first written as 'a pull request... enforced by GitHub'. Anthony corrected it: not every project uses GitHub, but every project uses a git repo. The distinction is not pedantic — coupling reflow2's answer to one vendor's feature would narrow a product whose whole persistence story (req:persistence, dec:multi-writer-architecture) is already vendor-neutral, and would exclude exactly the disconnected and self-hosted environments where the file-and-merge model is the ONLY workable one. The primitives are branch/diff/merge; a forge is a UI over them. Kept SEPARATE from dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs (ACCESS — which graphs a session can see) because this is AUTHORITY — who may write what, and at which status. The federation node localises this question to each ownership seam; this node is what happens at one. The reframe worth keeping even if every option here is rejected: this is a CUSTOMER REQUIREMENT LEVIED ON A SUPPLIER, the most ordinary transaction in systems engineering.proposednothing
OPEN — would genesis on reflow2's own requirements rebuild reflow2? The measured answer is no, and the gap is 18 capabilities and 389 decisions
UNDECIDED — RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's hypothetical, 2026-08-16: 'take every requirement we've defined, and start a new project called reflow3 and run /genesis with those requirements (would we end up with the same product?)'. DISTINCT FROM ITS SIBLING: the adopt hypothetical asks what reading the CODE recovers. This asks what reading the REQUIREMENTS produces. One tests recovery, the other tests SUFFICIENCY — whether the recorded intent determines the product. They point in opposite directions and neither answers the other. ⭐ THE MEASURED ANSWER IS NO, AND THE GAP IS COUNTABLE (2026-08-16): Requirements 175 (115 accepted · 47 proposed · 9 dropped · 4 deferred) Capabilities 162 Decisions 389 (247 accepted · 131 proposed · 10 superseded · 1 rejected) GOVERNED_BY 901 edges, of which 877 LAND ON A DECISION ⇒ THE DESIGN IS GOVERNED MORE THAN TWICE AS HEAVILY BY DECISIONS AS BY REQUIREMENTS. Genesis takes a brief → Requirements → Capabilities. IT DOES NOT TAKE DECISIONS AS INPUT. So reflow3 would re-litigate every shaping choice from nothing: `dec:report-dont-judge`, `dec:certainty-derived`, `dec:edge-orthogonality`, `dec:views-are-projections`, `dec:agent-navigates-content`, `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition`. There is no reason a fresh pass lands the same way on any of them, and those are what give reflow2 its CHARACTER rather than its feature list. THREE CONCRETE DIVERGENCES, all measured: (a) 18 CAPABILITIES THAT NO REQUIREMENT ASKS FOR — 11% of the product, invisible to a requirements-only genesis. This is exactly what `unmotivated_capability` detects, the detector music_graph independently called 'the design-recovery engine'. (b) 43 REQUIREMENTS NOTHING DELIVERS — so reflow3 would have them in scope from day one and might come out MORE complete on that axis. (The 43 includes dropped and deferred, so the live backlog is smaller.) (c) THE REQUIREMENTS ARE THEMSELVES DOWNSTREAM OF DECISIONS. `req:key-interfaces` and `req:modularity-computed` exist because `dec:mosa-conformance` was thought through. Feed only the outputs and you lose the reasoning that generated them — and, worse, the reasoning that would generate the NEXT ones. ⭐⭐ WHAT THE QUESTION ACTUALLY TESTS, and it is the sharpest form of the concern Anthony raised all day: IS THE DESIGN A SUFFICIENT SPECIFICATION OF THE PRODUCT? Measurably, not quite — the gap is 18 capabilities plus 389 decisions. That is not obviously a flaw in reflow2 so much as a true fact about design; what is unusual is that reflow2 can SHOW THE SIZE OF THE GAP rather than leaving it a feeling. THE VARIANT WORTH MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL, and nothing in the design has considered it: GENESIS FROM REQUIREMENTS **AND** DECISIONS. That is a real question about whether reflow2's own record is self-sufficient, and it is a far stronger claim if it holds — 'this graph is enough to rebuild the product' is the strongest statement a design brain could make about itself. Genesis takes a brief; whether decisions can be seeded alongside is unexamined. A PREDICTION, recorded so it can be wrong: reflow3 would be recognisably the SAME KIND of thing and differ in nearly every SPECIFIC. Which is itself an answer to whether reflow2 produces principled designs — it produces a design that determines the product's PROPERTIES, not its SHAPE. THE OPTIONS: (a) leave it hypothetical — the measurement above already answers the interesting part without spending the effort; (b) run the requirements-only version as a cheap sufficiency probe and count what is missing; (c) run the requirements-AND-decisions version, which is the one that tests the graph's self-sufficiency; (d) do neither and instead treat '18 capabilities no requirement asks for' as a to-do — close the gap rather than measure it. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the 18 unmotivated capabilities are an honest backlog or already acknowledged as deliberate. Nobody has read them. That single check would change which option is worth taking.		Recorded as brainstorming on Anthony's hypothetical, 2026-08-16, at his instruction to capture it. His question and his framing ('would we end up with the same product?'); the counts, the divergences and the prediction are mine. Kept at `proposed` rather than promoted — he asked it as a hypothetical, and the requirements-and-decisions variant is my suggestion rather than his. Its sibling is `dec:idea-run-adopt-on-reflow2-itself-as-a-ground-truth-test`.proposednothing
OPEN — should management/governance stay inside reflow2, or split into a sister package?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony raised this at the very end of 2026-08-09 and it got no thinking because the session was out of context. Nothing below is intent; the options are recorded so the roads not taken survive. ANTHONY'S QUESTION, and he brought the strongest counter himself: should reflow2's management and governance surface (rules, enforcement, claims/seats, epochs, releases, readiness, budget, ownership) live where it does, or become a sister package? HIS OWN COUNTER-ARGUMENT: **UAF does not separate them** — Architecture Management, Project, Standards and Strategic are all viewpoints inside one framework. That counter is strong and is engaged below rather than waved at. --- OPTION A — STAY UNIFIED (status quo, no work) --- One package, one vocabulary, one graph. FOR: proj:reflow2's objective is already 'Keep a design coherent from concept THROUGH OPERATIONS' — the whole lifecycle is the stated scope, so a split narrows an objective held since genesis. The management surface is DEFINED BY READING DESIGN STATE: dec:release-trigger computes a cut from what is delivered, req:readiness-gates-the-roadmap computes the epoch from readiness rather than declaring it, req:plans-move-honestly puts plan movement on the record. None of that is a layer on top; it is a reader of the coherence graph, so a sister package would need full read access anyway — at which point ask what was actually separated. AGAINST: this is also the option that requires nobody to think, which is not the same as being right. --- OPTION B — SPLIT INTO A SISTER PACKAGE --- A second crate / MCP server with its own vocabulary, sharing the graph. FOR, and this is the real evidence: dec:bl-155 measured 40 of 132 served tools never called, and roughly SEVENTEEN of those forty are the management/governance/coordination family (claim_region, claim_report, release_claim, mint_seat, apply_merge, merge_designs, recall_resolutions, plan_epoch, set_epoch_status, arrival_delta, budget_report, add_flow, part_of_flow, performed_in, add_resource, add_environment, set_project_mode). The management half is measurably the least-exercised part of reflow2. Also: the natural users differ — governance's natural consumer is an agent fleet, design coherence's is a person designing. AGAINST, and it is the same datum read the other way: BL-155's own conclusion is that these tools are UNREACHABLE FROM ANY SKILL, not unwanted — 'a capability nobody can find is worth what an absent one is worth'. Packaging is not the cause of the non-use, so packaging is not the cure; a split would make them less reachable, not more. SECOND COST, concrete: a sister package collides with two ACCEPTED requirements — req:thin-install ('after setup, a project never has to change again for reflow2 to move') and req:no-setup-per-project ('setting up a project is not a step'). The split is not free; it is paid for in install friction the design already refused once. --- OPTION C — SPLIT THE VOCABULARY, NOT THE PACKAGE --- One binary; governance/management becomes a declared, optional PROFILE a project opts into. FOR: this is what UAF actually does, and it is where Anthony's counter is sharper than it first looks. UAF unifies VIEWPOINTS in one framework; it says nothing about whether one piece of software ships them. So the UAF precedent argues for one VOCABULARY and is silent on one PACKAGE — which suggests the question is a packaging question wearing a vocabulary question's clothes, and that separating the two axes may dissolve it. AGAINST: reflow2 has no profile mechanism today, so this is the option with the most unbuilt machinery behind it. --- OPTION D — NEITHER: THE LINE IS MECHANISM vs POLICY --- Not a package boundary at all. Mechanism lives in reflow2; policy lives in each project's own graph and reflow2 stays ignorant of it. FOR: this is the line the storyflow fleet drew after a month of operations, with the test 'could a solo hobbyist, a two-person team and a regulated enterprise each express THEIR governance with this, without reflow2 having an opinion about which is right?' Their verdict sizes the missing work as small: 'reflow2 models the DESIGN well and the DECIDING poorly — it does not know who may decide, what a decision covers, which rules can even be checked, or where else a rule is written down. Those four are what a governance layer is, and each is a small declarative field plus a report — NOT A SUBSYSTEM.' You do not split a package off four fields. AGAINST: the same report notes DesignRule is 'the least-connected type in the schema, which is odd for the one whose whole job is to bind other things' — so governance here is an underfitted corner, and calling the remaining work small may be measuring the part already understood. --- WHAT THE GRAPH ITSELF SAYS, checked rather than assumed --- reflow2's own functional decomposition (dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition, 'reflow2's systems are functional, not its file tree') holds EIGHT systems — Agent Surface, Coherence Loop, Documentation, Human Channel, Intake, Design Store, Time & History, Vocabulary — and NONE of them is management or governance. There is no existing seam to split on. That cuts both ways and the honest reading of both is recorded: it means a split must invent a boundary the design never drew, and it means the absence of that boundary may be exactly why the area is tangled. RELATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED: dec:idea-package-versus-shared-server asks a different packaging question (shared server vs self-contained package) on the same axis; rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party governs how any answer must be judged — by what it does for a consumer's project, never for this repo.		Recorded as brainstorming at Anthony's request (/brainstorm, 2026-08-09). Searching the graph first changed the shape of the question three times: proj:reflow2's objective already claims concept-through-operations, so a split narrows a stated scope; dec:bl-155's never-called list turns out to be ~17/40 management tools, which is the strongest datum on either side and reads both ways; and req:thin-install + req:no-setup-per-project give the split a concrete, already-accepted cost. The storyflow fleet's trial-case report (2026-08-09, api-boss 05af57c1) supplies option D from a month of live operation. No option is recommended and none is promoted to intent.supersedednothing
OPEN — HEAL's defect catalogue is 8 of 13, one deferral's blocker has EXPIRED unnoticed, and the module comment recording the gap is itself stale
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced 2026-08-11 checking `docs/requirements-coverage.md`'s deferrals against the code rather than trusting its status column. Nothing here is intent. WHAT WAS MEASURED. HEAL-3 says the catalogue is 8 of 13, with `unreachable`, `weak_connection`, `missing_link`, `missing_entity` and `missing_embedding` deferred. Grepping the core: the only hits for those five are a MODULE COMMENT at `crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs:27-29` and unrelated `unreachable!()` macros. So the five are genuinely absent — confirmed, not assumed. ⭐ BUT THAT COMMENT IS ITSELF STALE, WHICH IS THE SHARPER FINDING. heal.rs:27-29 reads: 'Deferred (need `dynograph-graph` or the LLM): dead_end / unreachable / disconnected_community / weak_connection / single_point_of_failure / missing_link…'. Three of those — `dead_end`, `disconnected_community`, `single_point_of_failure` — ARE BUILT and were being proposed as fixes until PR #147 narrowed them this same session. A comment naming what is missing has kept naming things that arrived. ⭐⭐ AND HEAL-14'S BLOCKER HAS EXPIRED. The row reads '⬜ Missing-intermediate Component for hierarchy — matryoshka (needs `Component.level`)'. `Component.level` EXISTS: 3AX-9 is ✅, `hierarchy_issues` and `MissingIntermediateLevel` are in `crates/reflow2-core/src/hierarchy.rs` (5 references), and `missing_intermediate_level` is surfaced as a gap by `detect_gaps`. So the DETECTOR fires and the REPAIR was never written — `heal.rs` has zero references to it. The stated reason for deferring is gone and nothing noticed. This is the same shape as `cap:what-next`, whose blocker also expired unnoticed and which turned out to be buildable the moment anyone looked. ⚠️ THE COUNTERWEIGHT, and it is not optional: PR #147 (merged today) REMOVED HEAL's ability to propose `generate_bridge`/`generate_owner` for `disconnected_community`/`dead_end`/`orphan`, because inventing a relationship nobody designed is not a repair. A `generate_component` for a missing intermediate level is EXACTLY THAT SHAPE — inventing a subsystem to sit between a system and a part. So HEAL-14 may not be 'unblocked and buildable'; it may be 'unblocked and now forbidden by a rule accepted hours ago'. `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` is accepted. That tension is the actual question here and it did not exist when the row was written. IDEAS, unranked: (a) Fix the stale module comment and the stale HEAL-14 blocker note — pure record-keeping, costs nothing, and stops the next reader inheriting both errors. (b) Decide HEAL-14 on the anti-fabrication rule: either the missing-intermediate repair is legitimate (the level is derivable from the two endpoints, not invented) or it is forbidden and the row should be RETIRED rather than left ⬜ forever. (c) Retire the five never-built categories from the catalogue. The project's own test is 'unused AND redundant → retire; unused AND not-redundant → defer, and say so' — nobody has re-asked which of the five is which since 2026-07-22. (d) Nothing. 8 of 13 has been enough for every trial so far, and no friction report has asked for the missing five. 📌 THE META-POINT, which is the reason this node exists at all: `requirements-coverage.md` carries a BINDING deferral discipline — 'a deferral that isn't written down is a silent stub, which this project treats as the same integrity breach as a silent drop.' Three rows were checked today and three were wrong: SP-3b says ingest cannot be called from a session (it can), GS-17 says the polished PROMPT step is deferred (`gap_to_prompt` does it), 3AX-5 says TemporalFact usage is deferred (133 instances). The table goes stale in BOTH directions, and nothing computes on it. That is the argument for deferrals living where a detector can reach them — and equally the argument against trusting this table as the source for what to build.		Checking three deferrals against the code found three stale rows and one expired blocker, plus a module comment that has kept naming built features as missing. The HEAL-14 question is genuinely live and genuinely changed: its blocker cleared, and hours later this session accepted a rule that may forbid the repair outright.proposednothing
OPEN — the triage findings are TemporalFacts and schedule_for takes only a Requirement or Capability, so nothing today can be planned. What becomes the plannable thing, and how many of them are there?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's question, 2026-08-16: 'we used to have a planned capabilities increment / planned epochs within reflow2 — can we use these features within reflow2 to map out the triage fixes?' The reconnaissance and the options are mine. THE SHORT ANSWER IS YES, THE MACHINERY EXISTS AND WORKS. Measured today: `plan_epoch` (future) is distinct from `add_epoch` (happened); `schedule_for` carries `modality: expected | required` with real teeth; `arrival_delta` computes five outcomes and stores none; 11 planned epochs and 27 SCHEDULED_FOR edges already exist. `arrival_delta` on `epoch:governance-becomes-expressible` returned six outstanding requirements AND volunteered 'nothing is scheduled `required` … so there is no obligation to miss and it is NOT ready to cut. An increment that promises nothing has not been scoped.' The tools are healthy and opinionated. ⭐ BUT THERE IS A BLOCKER THE QUESTION DOES NOT ANTICIPATE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE DECISION: `schedule_for` accepts `Requirement` or `Capability` ONLY. EVERY triage finding is a TemporalFact. So not one of them can be scheduled as it stands. The plan-increments skill says why this is correct rather than a limitation — 'a plan is not intent … an item scheduled but never captured is a promise with no requirement behind it' — so the missing step is CAPTURE, not scheduling. 📌 AND THE SKILL ALREADY NAMED WHAT I WAS DOING: 'if you are maintaining a numbered list of upcoming work in the conversation … that is a delivery plan living outside the graph.' My ranked what-next list was exactly that, twice today, and it would have died with the session. ⚠️ EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS WORTH DOING PROPERLY RATHER THAN QUICKLY — reflow2's OWN plan has drifted, in precisely the shape the skill's §4 warns about. Of 27 SCHEDULED_FOR edges, ELEVEN still point at `rel:v0190`, `rel:v0200` and `rel:v0210`, all long shipped. Planned epochs sit at sequence 250–267 while arrived epochs reach 343. So the plan looks present and is answering nobody. Any new plan laid on top inherits that unless the stale half is dealt with. THE OPTIONS FOR WHAT BECOMES PLANNABLE. (a) A CAPABILITY PER FIX, at `status: planned`. Faithful to how features are tracked. ⇒ AGAINST: most of these are repair, not new function — 'propose_heal stops mislabelling its scope' is restoring intended behaviour, and filing it as a capability inflates the capability count with maintenance and makes `unrealized_capability` noisier for months. (b) A REQUIREMENT PER FIX, capabilities beneath where one is genuinely new. Faithful to the vocabulary: a fix is a statement about what must be true. ⇒ AGAINST: roughly a dozen findings would become a dozen requirements, which is a lot of intent minted in one act, and some are small enough that a requirement overstates them. (c) ⭐ A REQUIREMENT PER THEME, several findings beneath each — and today's findings cluster harder than they look. At least four are ONE statement: 'a report says whether a check was EXERCISED or had NOTHING TO EXAMINE.' That covers propose_heal's vacuous zero, and it is not new doctrine — `chg:a-null-and-a-vacuous-zero-now-say-which-they-are` already did exactly this for scoped `detect_gaps`, and dev_storyflow named it a WIN. A second theme is 'a reply says what it did not recognise', covering the undeclared property and the nearest-name suggestion. ⇒ AGAINST: theming is a judgement, and grouping wrongly buries a finding under a heading nobody searches. (d) SCHEDULE NOTHING; leave them as facts and let the loop surface them. ⇒ AGAINST, and this is measured rather than argued: across this entire session `loop_status` reported the same 80 gaps and 16 defects and NEVER ONCE surfaced a triage item, because a defect FACT is not a gap. Doing nothing means they stay invisible to the loop that exists to say what is owed. (e) EXTEND `schedule_for` TO ACCEPT A TemporalFact. Removes the blocker directly. ⇒ AGAINST: a fact is an observation, not work. Scheduling an observation is a category error, and it would let the design promise to deliver a measurement. AND THE SECOND QUESTION, WHICH IS SEPARABLE: HOW MANY EPOCHS? One 'triage fixes' epoch is easy to reason about and hard to argue with; two or three themed epochs (the detectors that misdescribe themselves, the write surface that accepts what it should question, the loop that cannot scope itself) carry more meaning and cost more to keep honest. `arrival_delta`'s own note argues for at least one `required` item per epoch, or it is not scoped. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the stale SCHEDULED_FOR edges to shipped releases should be cleaned first, retired deliberately, or left as the historical record they arguably are — that is its own decision and re-pointing them silently would erase the slip, which the tool explicitly warns against.		Anthony's idea; the blocker, the drift measurement and the five options are mine. Recorded rather than acted on because the choice mints intent. ⭐ SETTLED 2026-08-16 ON HIS WORD: 'one triage fixes epoch, requirement per theme.' That is option (c) for the plannable unit and ONE epoch for the container. WHAT THAT RULES OUT, recorded because the roads not taken are the useful half: (a) a Capability per fix is declined — most of these are repair rather than new function and would inflate the capability count with maintenance; (b) a Requirement per fix is declined — roughly a dozen at once is too much intent minted in one act; (d) leaving them as facts is declined, and the measurement is why: `loop_status` reported the same 80 gaps and 16 defects all session and never once surfaced a triage item, because a defect FACT is not a gap; (e) extending `schedule_for` to accept a TemporalFact is declined as a category error — a fact is an observation, not work. AND HE CHOSE ONE EPOCH over two or three themed ones — easier to reason about and harder to argue with, at the cost of the increment carrying less meaning in its name. ⚠️ WHAT THE RULING DOES NOT DECIDE, and was not asked: nothing is scheduled `required`. Every item goes in `expected`, because `required` is an obligation whose miss is a computed violation rather than a slip, and the plan-increments skill says to ask rather than assume. ⇒ `arrival_delta` will therefore report this epoch NOT ready to cut until somebody names at least one obligation. That is the tool being right, not a defect, and it is the next question for him. AND THE STALE HALF IS STILL OPEN: eleven SCHEDULED_FOR edges still point at releases shipped long ago. This ruling adds a new plan beside them and does not clean them, deliberately — re-pointing them silently would erase the slip.acceptedfact:feedback-triage-status-across-three-sources-2026-08-16
OPEN — what makes the reflow2→flo2 link a STANDING subscription rather than a run somebody remembers to do?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09: \'how can we link reflow2 and flo2 — flo2 is dependent upon reflow2; we've discussed publisher → subscriber type relationships.\' WHAT SEARCHING FIRST CHANGED, and it changed the question rather than answering it: most of the linking machinery is DESIGNED AND BUILT, and it has already been RUN on exactly this pair. dec:linked-repos-poc (executed 2026-08-06) composed reflow2, flo2 and dynograph-foundation in a throwaway in-memory graph and found ONE true positive unprompted — ifc:core-api (ours, `library`) against flo2's ifc:model-provider-api (`REST`), 80/100 name match, \'very likely the same contract, but they cannot be connected as either is currently built.\' Nobody told it the answer. So the publisher/subscriber SHAPE is not the open question; dec:pairing-role-placement settled where the role lives, cap:publish-surface and cap:mirror-surface are built, and dec:nested-graphs settled that separately-owned designs are separate graphs. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN IS THE TENSE. Every link so far has been a THING SOMEBODY RAN — a manual composition into a temporary graph, discarded afterwards. A subscription is a standing relationship: flo2 would be continuously answerable to what reflow2 currently publishes, and would learn when it moved. Nothing in the design says how that happens, and the two projects are on different machines, different release cadences and different owners. THE OPTIONS, in Anthony's framing and with what is cheap or expensive about each recorded beside it rather than argued down: (A) PULL AT THE EXPORT. flo2 vendors reflow2's committed export (or its published surface via export_surface) and re-composes on each reflow2 release. Cheapest by far, needs nothing new, and rides git which both already use. COUNTER: it is a snapshot, so flo2 learns about a moved contract whenever it next remembers to pull — which is the failure mode this whole question is about, one level up. (B) PULL AT THE RUNNING SERVER. Once one process holds many designs (cap:graph-registry, reflow2_updates #1), flo2 could hold both graph_ids and ask across them live. COUNTER: gated on the largest outstanding piece of work, and dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs is still proposed. Also flo2's graph_id is `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2` — an opaque mint beside two readable labels — so the addressing story needs a human-facing name first. (C) A DECLARED DEPENDENCY EDGE BETWEEN DESIGNS, not just between nodes. reflow2 already has req:design-dependencies-declared (accepted, verified) for library versions; the analogue for designs would let a consumer say \'I depend on reflow2's published surface at version X\' and make a stale subscription COMPUTABLE rather than remembered. COUNTER: it is new vocabulary, and dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs and dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency are both still open about what may legitimately cross a design boundary at all. (D) THE SEAM AS A GATE. flo2's CI composes against reflow2's published export and fails when a contract it consumes has moved — the ci-gate pattern pointed across a boundary instead of inward. COUNTER: it makes reflow2's release able to break flo2's build, which is a real coupling decision and Anthony's to make, not a technical detail. ⚠️ THE BLOCKER IS THE SAME FOR ALL FOUR, AND IT IS ONE MISSING LABEL. dec:linked-repos-poc found it and deliberately did not fix it: REFLOW2 DECLARES NO `required` INTERFACE ANYWHERE. Pairing matches complements, so with nothing required, nothing can ever pair — paired=0 on BOTH pairs, 15 of dynograph-foundation's interfaces and 5 of flo2's landing in dead surface. Its most dangerous number was `unmet_needs: 0`, which reads as \'nothing is missing\' and means \'we never said we needed anything\'. Until reflow2 says what it requires, every option above links two designs that cannot be compared. That PoC called declaring them \'the cheapest next step\' — a handful of nodes — and left it to Anthony's word because it is design about reflow2's own boundaries. AND A SECOND THING NO OPTION ADDRESSES, from reflow2_updates.md #7 (NOT DESIGNED): there are TWO version axes at this seam and only one negotiates. The MCP protocol version negotiates per connection; reflow2's 149-tool surface does not. The toolsnaps stop a surface change landing silently IN THIS REPO and tell flo2 nothing. Whatever subscription shape is chosen has to carry that, or \'clean module\' quietly becomes \'vendored fork\' — which dec:open-reflow2-as-core-module already names as the crux, with the cost falling on @ajs. NOTHING HERE IS PROMOTED. The options are recorded as considered; the one decision genuinely waiting is whether to declare reflow2's `required` interfaces, which is small, unblocks all four, and is not an agent's to make. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ ANSWERED IN PART 2026-08-12 BY A BACKTEST — THE SUBSTRATE IS NOT THE DESIGN EXPORT ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ This node said the SHAPE was settled and only the TENSE was open. A backtest shows a third thing was open and unnoticed: WHAT THE SUBSCRIPTION WATCHES. THE METHOD, and it is reusable: rather than build a mechanism and hope, replay real history against failures with KNOWN answers. `reflow2_updates.md` — flo2's hand-written tracker, the manual version of this subscription — went stale in two specific, dated ways. Each was given a window and three candidate signals were scored against it. Read-only; nothing was built. §4 CONTRIBUTOR-SCOPED loop_status. The doc was CORRECT when written (2026-08-09 10:21, against v0.26.1 — `loop_status_for` genuinely absent). It landed 3h later in PR #126 and shipped in v0.27.0. The doc became WRONG at its 2026-08-11 re-check. Window: v0.26.1 → v0.27.0. §7 THE SEAM CHANGES. `HealIssue.suggested_fix_type` went `&'static str` → `Option`, and five capture tools began REFUSING near-duplicates. Both v0.28.0-only. Window: v0.27.0 → v0.28.0. RESULTS: signal | §4 input contract | §7 capture refusals | §7 result shape design export diff | 1 hit in 70 | 12 hits in 103 | NO — only 'art:heal changed' toolsnap diff | DECISIVE | DECISIVE | STRUCTURALLY BLIND ⭐ THE TOOLSNAP DIFF WINS OUTRIGHT ON INPUT CONTRACTS. For §4 it is mechanical and needs no interpretation: `inputSchema.properties` went `{}` → `{contributor_id: …}`. For the capture refusals, `distinct_from` appears with a description that explains the new refusal. 🛑 NOTHING SEES OUTPUT SHAPE. Toolsnaps record `annotations, description, inputSchema, name` — THERE IS NO OUTPUT SCHEMA. So a result-shape change is invisible to every signal reflow2 has, and it is exactly the half most likely to break a generated client. 🛑🛑 AND THE DESIGN EXPORT ACTIVELY LIES. `cap:owed-to-a-contributor` reads `in_progress` at v0.26.1, v0.27.0 AND v0.28.0 — three releases after the capability shipped — because status moves only on the owner's word and nobody went back. A subscription built on design-export status would have told flo2 'still in progress' about working code. THAT IS WORSE THAN SILENCE, and it fully explains how the hand-written doc went wrong: it was not carelessness, the design export AGREED WITH IT. ⇒ **DIFFERENT CONSUMERS NEED DIFFERENT SUBSTRATES.** flo2 calls reflow2's TOOLS; its contract is the tool surface. A sibling consuming reflow2's INTENT would want the design export. Treating 'link two designs' as one thing conflates them, and option (A) above (pull at the export) would have watched the wrong artefact. ⚠️ AND THE WINNING SIGNAL IS NOT OBTAINABLE ACROSS THE SEAM. The toolsnaps ship in NEITHER `release.yml` NOR the kit. flo2 has already registered them as `art:reflow2-toolsnaps` with location 'github.com/sligara7/reflow2 — tools/toolsnaps/*.json', i.e. GO READ THEM OUT OF OUR REPO. The strongest available signal requires a checkout of the upstream, which defeats consuming a released artifact. TWO CHEAP FOLLOW-ONS THE BACKTEST EARNED: publish the toolsnaps as a release asset, and record OUTPUT schemas in them. ═══ THE PAIRING TRIAL, same day — first time it computed on this pair ═══ `pair_designs` reflow2 → flo2: **paired 0, conflicts 10, unmet_needs 5, dead_surface 2, candidates 1, unclassified 2 ours / 1 theirs.** The blocker this node's PoC recorded (reflow2 declared no `required` interface) cleared in PR #130; reflow2 now declares 9. (a) ZERO PAIRS, NOT FOR A FIXABLE REASON. flo2 models `cmp:reflow2-service` as a component it CONTAINS. Pairing matches complements ACROSS a boundary; flo2 drew reflow2 INSIDE its boundary, so there is none. A legitimate model that makes the seam permanently uncomputable by pairing. (b) TEN CONFLICTS, NEARLY ALL SPURIOUS. reflow2's dynograph LIBRARY requirements name-matched flo2's REST endpoints at 62–83/100. The one true correspondence scored 61 and landed in `candidates`. Fuzzy names PROPOSE; only a person DISPOSES. (c) TWO DESIGNS CAN AGREE BY BEING IDENTICALLY WRONG. Both label the shared boundary `medium: REST`; both MEAN MCP and both say so in `spec` prose. Had roles been complementary they would have PAIRED on a shared falsehood. The tool defends against `unspecified` reading as agreement and has NO defence against two sides stating the same wrong value. A seam check verifies LABEL EQUALITY, never interoperability. ═══ THE GAPS IN LINKING, generalised so they apply to any two reflow2 projects ═══ 1. THE LINK IS NOT A THING. Nothing in either graph records the other exists. A link happens when a human hands two files to a tool: no identity, no owner, no pinned version, no lifecycle. `req:design-dependencies-declared` covers LIBRARY versions and has no analogue for DESIGNS. 2. CORRESPONDENCE IS INFERRED, NEVER ASSERTED. No shared identifier space, so matching falls back on fuzzy names and re-guesses every run. A human should be able to say 'my X IS your Y' and have it stick. 3. AGREEMENT IS NOT INTEROPERABILITY (see (c) above). 4. THE LINK IS A RUN, NOT A RELATIONSHIP — the tense problem this node opened with. 5. THE COMPARISON HIDES ITS OWN SKEW. A 0.27.0 flo2 export was compared against a 0.28.0 reflow2 and nothing said so. ⭐ `dec:fix-the-comparison-before-pointing-it-earlier` step 2 ALREADY DECIDED 'a comparison discloses its own confound' for the single-project case and has never been pointed at the cross-project one, which has the same confound and a worse one — the two sides are on different release cadences by construction. 6. ONLY INTERFACES CROSS. A decision in A that invalidates a capability in B, a shared constraint, readiness gating — the vocabulary for crossing is one node type wide. 7. READING IS SAFE; WRITING IS NOT. A comparison touches neither store. A propagated gap writes into a graph its owner never agreed to. The git-diff transport survives BECAUSE it never opens the store — a safety property, not an implementation detail. 8. THE PRECONDITION IS BILATERAL AND NOBODY BUDGETS FOR IT. A seam is only as good as the least-labelled side, `internal` is the DEFAULT so an unlabelled project reports a confidently empty seam, and neither party gets value until both have paid. This is why the whole linking layer has zero instances. 9. N > 2 IS QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT AND ALREADY MEASURED. `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface`: reflow2 and dev_storyflow both depend on dynograph, one as a Rust library and one as REST. A naive pairwise check between the siblings reports ALL-CLEAR — confidently and wrongly — because the conflict lives BELOW both published surfaces. Shared-dependency conflict is a property of the graph, not of any pair in it. Linking N designs is not N-choose-2 links.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, options in the prose, nothing promoted to intent without Anthony's word. Kept SEPARATE from dec:linked-repos-poc because that node records a RUN and what it proved; this one asks what the relationship should be going forward, which the PoC explicitly did not answer. Kept separate from dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs and dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency because those ask WHAT may cross a design boundary, while this asks WHEN and BY WHAT MECHANISM — one node holding both could only ever be half-answered. PARTLY ANSWERED 2026-08-12 by a backtest against two dated failures with known answers: the substrate for a TOOL consumer is the toolsnaps, not the design export, whose status field lagged three releases behind a shipped capability. The method — replay real history against failures whose answer is already known — is more reusable than the finding.proposednothing
OPEN — how does a design register a source document that lives OUTSIDE its own repository?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — found 2026-08-11 by breaking CI with it. Nothing here is intent. WHAT HAPPENED, and it is the cleanest possible demonstration. `cap:capture-registers-its-source` shipped, and the first thing it was pointed at was the document that actually drove reflow2's governance work: `dev_storyflow/reflow2_feedback.md`, in a SIBLING REPOSITORY. Registered as `art:storyflow-reflow2-feedback` with `location: ../dev_storyflow/reflow2_feedback.md`, plus DOCUMENTS edges to the seven governance requirements. Local gates passed. CI FAILED: FAIL DRIFT art:storyflow-reflow2-feedback: missing_artifact CI checks out reflow2 alone, so the path resolves to nothing. `tools/reflow2_check.py` (line 615) reads `location` and FALLS BACK TO `name` when it is absent, then joins against `--root` — so there is NO WAY to register an out-of-repo source without failing the gate. Dropping the location does not help; it makes the check try the name as a path instead. ⭐ THIS IS `req:content-reaches-every-seat` FIRING ON THE THING BUILT TO SATISFY `req:no-idea-goes-quiet`. 'A pointer resolves for everyone holding the design, not only for the machine that wrote it.' A relative path into a sibling checkout resolves on exactly one machine. The two accepted requirements pull against each other in this case, and neither names the other. ⚠️ THE CASE IS NOT EXOTIC — IT IS ANTHONY'S NORMAL. His operating context is several partially-built designs across repositories and organizations, with the source material for one living in another. `req:many-people-and-many-projects-compose` (proposed) is the axis; this is a concrete instance of it landing on the artifact layer rather than the design layer. IDEAS, unranked: (a) An `external: true` / `reachability` marker on Artifact that tells `reconcile_artifacts` the file is deliberately not part of this checkout, so ABSENCE is expected rather than drift. Mirrors what `volatility` already does for expected CONTENT change — this is the same move for expected ABSENCE. Risk: absence is the one finding `set_artifact_intent` deliberately keeps at full severity, so this weakens the strongest signal in the reconcile family and needs its own argument. (b) COPY the driving excerpt into this repo as a dated, attributed source document and register that. Honest, resolves everywhere, and is what `req:sources-are-kept-not-just-parsed` (accepted) arguably already implies — keep the source WITH the design. Cost: a copy can drift from its original, and nothing would detect that. (c) Treat the other repo as a DESIGN rather than a folder, and reach it through the cross-design machinery (`req:design-dependencies-declared`, accepted) instead of the artifact layer. Cleanest conceptually; costs the most, and dev_storyflow's feedback file is not a design. (d) Do nothing, and accept that a source outside the repo simply cannot be traced. Cheapest; it is also the status quo that made Anthony hand-point an agent at the file in the first place. WHAT WAS DONE MEANWHILE: the artifact and its seven DOCUMENTS edges were REMOVED so the gate is honest, and the backward trace is once again absent. That is a retreat, not a fix, and it is recorded here so the retreat is visible rather than quiet. `cap:capture-registers-its-source` remains correct for the in-repo case, which is the case its own description scoped it to — it says nothing about reachability, and that silence is the actual defect in it.		The capability shipped and its first real use broke CI, because the only source document that mattered lives in a sibling repo. Two accepted requirements — no-idea-goes-quiet and content-reaches-every-seat — pull in opposite directions here and neither names the other. Recording the fork rather than picking one, because option (a) weakens the strongest signal the reconcile family has and option (b) crosses a repo boundary; both are Anthony's calls.proposedCapture FROM a document registers that document and links what came out of it, so the backward half of the thread exists by construction
OPEN — how does a project record what it DECIDED about work that was built without a requirement: maintain, delete, or accept?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony's question in his own words, 2026-08-11: 'now the project has things that weren't supposed to be built - should they maintain, delete it accept the work done without a requirement?' Nothing here is intent. THE SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM. Those three are a real disposition with real cost attached, and the graph has nowhere to put them. The two moves the tooling currently offers both lose information: (1) WRITE A REQUIREMENT FOR IT. The detect-and-ask skill warns against this in its own table: 'The wrong move is to invent a requirement from the capability's own description: a requirement backed out of the thing that implements it is satisfied by construction and can never contradict anything.' A retro-fitted requirement makes the gap disappear and makes the design lie. (2) `acknowledge_gap`. Files it under 'reviewed and fine'. Cannot tell 'we accept this and will maintain it' from 'we accept this and it is now debt somebody owns' from 'this is scheduled for deletion' — three different futures, one record. IDEAS, unranked: (a) A disposition property/edge on the acknowledgement itself: accepted-and-maintained / accepted-as-debt / scheduled-for-removal, with an owner. Cheap if it rides on the existing acknowledge_gap Decision. (b) Reuse the retire-from-design path for the delete branch and leave the other two to acknowledge_gap. Cheapest — no new vocabulary — but the accept-vs-debt distinction stays unexpressed. (c) Treat it as an ordinary Decision the user writes by hand, governed by nothing new. Zero build cost; costs the ability to ASK 'what unrequested work are we carrying?' across a design. ⭐ WHY THIS IS NOT A NICHE CASE, and it is Anthony's actual working context rather than a hypothetical: at NSLS-II he evolves a ~10-year-old bluesky stack where several organizations built partially-overlapping things because they could not wait for each other. Unrequested-but-built is the NORM on the brownfield path, not the anomaly. `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (proposed) is the adjacent capture; this is what to DO once it is captured. RELATED BUT DISTINCT, so it is not folded in here: `req:the-design-says-what-was-built-and-never-used` (proposed) surfaces implemented effort nothing depends on. That is BUILT-AND-UNUSED. This is BUILT-AND-UNREQUESTED. A capability can be either without the other, and conflating them would produce a detector that answers neither question. COUNTER-ARGUMENT: reflow2 is a design-coherence tool, not a project-management tool. dev_storyflow's own feedback rejected importing PMBOK/WBS structure for exactly this reason — 'importing PM artifact structure would add a second, competing spine next to the golden thread.' A disposition vocabulary is close to that line, and (c) is the option that respects it.		Anthony named three futures for unrequested work and the graph collapses all three into one acknowledgement. Recording the question keeps his framing intact; the ideas differ mainly in how much new vocabulary they cost.proposednothing
OPEN — a finding that corroborates another has to say CONTRADICTS to do it, and two code paths then filter that back out. Leave it, widen an unused edge, or make corroboration something reflow2 computes?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony asked how to choose this after a capture pass hit it; nothing here is intent, and the options are mine unless marked otherwise. MEASURED FIRST, because it changes the question. In reflow2's own graph today: 198 TemporalFacts, and SIX TemporalFact→TemporalFact edges — ALL of them CONTRADICTS, and FIVE of the six carry `alignment: supporting`, i.e. corroboration rather than conflict. Five earlier sessions independently reached for a negation type to say two findings AGREE. This is not one author's routing quirk. AND THE CURRENT ARRANGEMENT IS CORRECT, which is the strongest argument against touching it. Both computations that read CONTRADICTS skip `supporting` deliberately — `heal.rs:917-923` and `report.rs:1751-1766` — and report.rs carries a comment naming the bug that once existed: reading only the edge TYPE 'turned every recorded corroboration into a structural defect'. So there is NO live defect. The cost is a word that says the opposite of its meaning, and an author who must find a property to negate the type they just chose. THE TEST THAT SHOULD DECIDE IT IS ALREADY ACCEPTED DOCTRINE: `dec:edge-orthogonality` — 'a vocabulary distinction earns its keep only if a computation reads it'. So the real question is not which word is nicer. It is: SHOULD REFLOW2 COMPUTE CORROBORATION? 'This finding is independently corroborated by N sources' is the same evidence-strength signal the design already cares about everywhere else (`basis: measured`, `confidence`, the whole verification doctrine), and the five supporting edges cluster on exactly the findings that recurred to different people. If that number should be reportable, the relation earns a type. If not, it is documentation and the cheapest option wins. THE OPTIONS. (a) LEAVE IT. CONTRADICTS + `alignment: supporting`. Cheapest, five precedents, twice defended in code with a comment recording why. ⇒ Against: every future author reaches for a negation to express agreement, and only finds the escape hatch by reading the schema — which is how this came up. (b) WIDEN `SUPPLEMENTS`. It already exists and is declared `from: Fragment, to: Fragment` (build.yaml:133). A from/to list edit is the exact shape of #198 (VERIFIES admits Constraint), which shipped this increment, and it does NOT move the stamp — type counts and names are unchanged, so no upgrade doc is owed and nobody is locked out. ⇒ Against, and it is serious: SUPPLEMENTS has ZERO edges anywhere in this design, and its documented meaning is narrow and different (an LLM-as-SME supplementary-analysis Fragment augmenting its source). Nothing computes it. So this moves corroboration from an edge that IS read-and-correctly-skipped to one nothing reads at all — arguably backwards by `dec:edge-orthogonality`'s own test. (c) A NEW EDGE TYPE (`CORROBORATES`). Cleanest semantics, and the only option where the word matches the meaning. ⇒ Against: edge_types 61 → 62 MOVES THE STAMP, which owes an upgrade doc and makes older binaries refuse newer graphs. That is a real consumer cost for what may be documentation — and it only pays for itself under the computation test above. (d) SPLIT `alignment` OUT of CONTRADICTS ENTIRELY, so conflict and corroboration are separate types. Most honest model. ⇒ Against: same stamp cost as (c) PLUS a migration of the five existing supporting edges, and it would delete a working distinction to replace it with an equivalent one. (e) LEAVE THE SCHEMA AND FIX DISCOVERABILITY. CONTRADICTS's hint mentions the supporting case only as a trailing parenthetical — '(or, with alignment=supporting, reinforce)'. Lead with it instead. ⇒ Zero schema risk, zero stamp movement, and it addresses the ACTUAL failure, which was an author not finding the mechanism rather than the mechanism being absent. Weakest if the answer to the computation question is yes. WHAT NOBODY HAS MEASURED, and it would settle (c) vs (a): whether any consumer design has fact→fact corroboration at all, or whether this is a self-host pattern produced by reflow2 being the only project that records its own defects as TemporalFacts. If it is self-host-only, that is an argument for (a) or (e) on `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` grounds. RELATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FOLDED IN: `dec:one-retire-edge` is the same shape one axis over — two edge types for retirement, neither consulted, and still open. If these are answered separately they may drift apart; whether edge-vocabulary questions should be settled as a batch is itself a question.		Not a proposal and not a ranking. The five-of-six measurement is the part worth keeping whatever is decided: a corroboration relation is being expressed through a negation type, five times, by different sessions, and the code correctly filters it back out in two places. Anthony asked how to choose; the honest answer is that `dec:edge-orthogonality` already supplies the test, and applying it needs one thing nobody has decided — whether 'independently corroborated by N sources' is a number reflow2 should report. ⭐ THE OUTSTANDING MEASUREMENT WAS THEN TAKEN, 2026-08-16, AND IT LEANS HARD. The decision text asks whether any CONSUMER design has fact→fact corroboration. Measured across every committed export on this machine — dev_storyflow, dynograph-foundation, flo2, music_graph, quantum_benchmarking_initiative, storyflow — the answer is not 'no fact→fact edges'. It is ZERO TemporalFacts, in all six, full stop. ⇒ THIS IS A SELF-HOST-ONLY PATTERN. reflow2 is the only project recording its own defects as TemporalFacts, because it is the only project whose subject is reflow2. That is `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` pointing the other way for once: normally the self-host lags what it teaches; here it has invented a usage no consumer has reached for. ⇒ WHICH RE-RANKS THE OPTIONS, though it does not settle them. (c) a new edge type and (d) splitting `alignment` both move the stamp — an upgrade doc owed and older binaries refusing newer graphs — and would be paying a CONSUMER cost for a relation no consumer uses. (b) widening SUPPLEMENTS was already argued against on `dec:edge-orthogonality` grounds and this weakens it further. (e) fixing CONTRADICTS's hint so the `supporting` case leads rather than trails costs nothing, breaks nothing, and addresses the failure actually observed — an author not finding a mechanism that was already there and already correct. ⚠️ THE BOUND ON THAT MEASUREMENT, stated rather than glossed: these are COMMITTED EXPORTS, which may trail those projects' live stores — music_graph's is dated 2026-08-01, and F23 is precisely a case of a committed export being behind. So this reads 'zero in the record I can see', not 'zero in existence'. Six-for-six at zero is still a strong signal, and it would take only one consumer starting to record findings to overturn it.proposednothing
OPEN — is a human newcomer asking 'why does this exist' a first-class reader of the graph, when req:driving-agent says the human is reached only through the agent?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: the SECOND half of Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 exchange, relayed by Anthony 2026-08-06. In Alex's own words, the use case is: 'I have a ton of domain/tribal knowledge about my project, beyond the code itself. For example, I know why certain UI sections were created or have talked with the users and want a better way to document this information for junior devs on my project. I'd like to brain dump a bunch of this info in a way that other devs can query it using an AI prompt.' STILL OPEN. WHY THIS IS WORTH A NODE RATHER THAN A NOD: Alex described reflow2's use case almost exactly — rationale, who asked for it, what constraint drove it, kept beside the code and queryable in natural language — and the research answered him with Notion AI, Confluence/Rovo and Cognee. reflow2 was not a candidate in an answer to the question reflow2 exists to answer. Whatever else is true, that is a finding. WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS FOR IT: add_decision with a rationale, authored_by (whose word this is), the golden thread from requirement to capability to artifact, and search_design over all of it. Against a wiki it has one property no wiki has: a rationale in reflow2 can be shown to have gone STALE, because the thing it justified is linked and drift is computed. A Confluence page saying 'the legacy report screen stays because finance uses it monthly' stays confidently wrong forever after finance stops. That is the same normative property recorded in dec:idea-normative-vs-descriptive-graph, seen from the tribal-knowledge angle. THE TENSION, and it is with an ACCEPTED requirement, not a soft one: req:driving-agent states that the primary consumers are coding agents and 'the human is reached only through the agent'. Alex's junior dev is a human asking a question with no build task attached and no design intent to capture. Serving that reader well means a read-optimised, question-answering surface — closer to Q&A over the graph than to the capture-detect-ask-decide loop — and the loop is what the current skill kit is built around. It is a different product surface on the same store, which is either a natural projection (dec:views-are-projections would allow it, since answering from the graph invents nothing) or a second product, and those have very different costs. WHAT IS CHEAP: nothing new is needed to try it. An agent with the existing read tools can already answer 'why does this exist' from a well-populated graph. The cheap experiment is to have someone who did not build the design ask it questions and see what it cannot answer. WHAT IS EXPENSIVE, AND THE HONEST OBJECTION: this reader wants to BRAIN DUMP first and get structure later, which is the opposite of the capture loop's order. cap:ingest and cap:corpus-ingest exist for exactly that shape, so the primitive is there — but the loop's habit of asking about gaps at capture time is precisely what a brain-dumping user will experience as friction, and the brainstorm skill's own rule (do not run detect-and-ask over material the user deliberately left soft) exists because of that. Whether a dump-then-structure mode is a mode, a skill, or a different reader's whole path is unsettled. A CONCRETE DOGFOODING OPPORTUNITY, recorded because it is testable rather than arguable: Alex has the project, the tribal knowledge and the junior devs. Pointing reflow2 at his brain dump would test cap:ingest, the newcomer-query path and the tribal-knowledge story at once, on a design nobody in this repo authored. Anthony's word needed on whether that is wanted.		Recorded as an idea because the tension is with an accepted requirement and therefore cannot be resolved by an agent — either req:driving-agent is narrower than it reads, or this reader is out of scope, and only Anthony can say which. Also recorded because the finding that prompted it (reflow2 absent from an answer to its own question) is the kind of thing that vanishes from a conversation and cannot be rediscovered.proposednothing
DECIDED — `init` ASKS which harness you use and installs only that one's files (option c), settling init's two contradictory install policies in favour of the narrow one
DECIDED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY: **OPTION (c) — INIT ASKS.** Alex's literal request, taken over the recommendation recorded on this node, which was (b) *'apply the instruction-pointer policy to MCP configs'*. He chose with (b)'s argument and (c)'s stated costs both in front of him. ⭐ THE STRONGEST CASE FOR HIS CHOICE, which the pre-decision text under-weighted: **(b) GUESSES, AND A WRONG GUESS IS SILENT.** Detection reads a fresh repo that has no signal, falls back to the primary harness, and hands an OpenCode user a `.mcp.json` their tool never opens — with nothing to tell them anything is missing. Asking is the only option on the list that cannot be silently wrong, and a silent wrong install is the exact failure class this project keeps finding (`cap:degraded-surface`'s diagnosis not reaching a by-name caller; the loop nudge registered against a script that is not there; the pointer written into a file the harness never reads). **A question costs one prompt; a silent miss costs a user who concludes reflow2 does not work.** ⚠️ WHAT IT COSTS, RECORDED SO NOBODY IS SURPRISED LATER: the one-liner install becomes a conversation, which is in tension with `user-iterative-release-preference` (*one-liner install, one word to update*). So the non-interactive path is not optional garnish — it is part of the requirement: a flag must carry the answer, and a non-tty must never hang. CI, scripted installs and `adopt` runs are the common path, not the exception. 📌 WHAT (c) DOES NOT SETTLE: the instruction-pointer policy stays as it is (already narrow and correct), and the loop-nudge asymmetry is a separate open question (`dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only`) where the problem runs the other way — too little, not too much. Option (d), labelling the generated files, was not chosen but composes with (c) and remains available. ═══ THE ANALYSIS THIS WAS DECIDED FROM, kept because `req:roads-not-taken` says the roads not taken are part of the record ═══ RAISED AS BRAINSTORMING by Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14. HIS WORDS: *'`reflow2 init .` for a project should be more like a CLI wizard that asks you what agent harness you are utilizing (Claude, Grok, ChatGPT, open code, etc.) and only installs the necessary file changes based on your choice. It needs the correct mcp setup, the graph artifact that can be git committed and the agents.md reference.'* ✅ HIS THREE NAMED ESSENTIALS ARE ALL ALREADY PRODUCED on HEAD (`cbb1a19`): the MCP setup, the committed export at `docs/design/.json` (since PR #172), and the `AGENTS.md` reference. **Nothing he needs is missing — the complaint is that things nobody asked for arrive alongside them.** ⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT REFRAMED THE QUESTION: `tools/reflow2_init.py` ALREADY IMPLEMENTS ALEX'S PRINCIPLE — for instruction files — AND THE OPPOSITE ONE FOR MCP CONFIGS, ABOUT 150 LINES APART. Both deliberate, each carrying its reasoning in a comment, and they contradict each other. · INSTRUCTION POINTERS (`pointer_targets`, `CREATE_IF_NO_INSTRUCTION_FILE`) — appends only to instruction files the project ALREADY OWNS; when it owns none, creates just `CLAUDE.md`. The comment rejects the alternative in as many words: *'writing GEMINI.md, .cursorrules and the rest into a repo that asked for none of them is **spam**, and the sidecar we create (AGENTS.md) already IS the agents.md convention that the others increasingly follow.'* · MCP CONFIGS (`MCP_CONFIGS`) — writes `.mcp.json`, `opencode.json` AND `.vscode/mcp.json` unconditionally: *'One generator, several files — a project opened in a different tool should just work.'* ⇒ So the question was never 'should init ask?' but 'which of init's two existing policies is right?' — and (c) settles it toward the narrow one, by asking rather than by inferring. THE OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD. (a) LEAVE IT — extras are inert. Counter: init's own code calls that spam one screen away, and a first-time user read it as clutter. (b) APPLY THE POINTER POLICY TO MCP CONFIGS — detect, falling back to the primary harness. No prompt, internally consistent. **Counter that decided it: detection has no signal on a fresh repo, which is exactly when init runs, so it guesses — and guesses silently.** (c) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — ASK, with `--harness=…` for non-interactive use. (d) INSTALL ALL, BUT LABEL each file with which tool reads it and that deleting it is safe. Not chosen; composes with (c). (e) ASK ONLY WHEN AMBIGUOUS — detect, prompt when detection is empty. Not chosen; two code paths, and behaviour that differs between a fresh and an established repo. 📌 SCOPE, because it makes the change smaller than it sounds: most of what `init` writes is HARNESS-NEUTRAL and untouched — `AGENTS.md`/`REFLOW2.md`, the committed export, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`. The harness-specific surface is the three MCP configs, the instruction pointer (already policy-correct), and the loop-nudge hook. ⚠️ VERSION CAVEAT: two of Alex's five notes describe defects already fixed, so he is probably on an older kit (`fact:second-user-notes-2026-08-14-two-items-already-fixed`). Measurements here are against HEAD; an older `init` may have written a different set of files than what he saw.		Raised under the brainstorm skill and settled the same day on Anthony's word. Two things are deliberately on the record rather than smoothed away: that the choice went AGAINST the option this node recommended, and the reason his choice is nonetheless the stronger one — detection guesses, and a wrong guess about which harness will open a repo produces a silent failure, which is the failure class this project has now hit four separate times. The pre-decision text is kept in full beneath the outcome because `req:roads-not-taken` makes the rejected options part of the record, and because the instruction-pointer contradiction it documents is a real finding about `reflow2_init.py` that survives whichever option was taken.acceptedThe install asks which agent harness this project uses, and writes harness-specific files for that one only
OPEN — a published surface already carries designated REQUIREMENTS; should DECISIONS cross a design boundary too?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Surfaced 2026-08-05 by Anthony's multi-project question. ⚠️ CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART. This node first claimed 'everything reflow2 has built for crossing a design boundary shares CONTRACTS... NOTHING CARRIES A DECISION OR A REQUIREMENT ACROSS.' THAT IS WRONG ABOUT REQUIREMENTS, and it was wrong for the ordinary reason — the claim was made from the capability's one-line description ('the contracts others may rely on, and nothing internal') rather than from the code. Reading `export_surface` shows a second, deliberate half: `published_promises()`, behind `req:publishable-promise` (ACCEPTED — 'a published surface must be able to carry a behavioural promise, not only structure'). Its own comment says why: 'a structural surface says what the boundaries ARE and cannot say what any of them undertakes to DO — 'fails loud rather than falling back', 'ordering is preserved' — because a behavioural commitment lives in a Requirement and every Requirement was withheld. FOUND BY A REAL TRIAL, where the promise ended up asserted in a comment in the CONSUMER's build file, on the wrong side of the seam.' SO THE ACTUAL STATE, verified in `crates/reflow2-core/src/export.rs`: a published surface carries INTERFACES designated `published`, the artifacts that SPECIFY or REALIZE them, REQUIREMENTS the owner designated `published`, and the Project so a recipient knows whose surface it is. Everything else is withheld AND COUNTED. Opt-in throughout — designation is a deliberate act, never a default. ⭐ SO THE REAL GAP IS NARROWER AND SHARPER THAN FIRST WRITTEN: WHAT CANNOT CROSS IS THE **DECISION** — the reasoning. A consumer can learn WHAT this design promises and WHERE its boundaries are. It cannot learn WHY. 'We settled that outdoor units send cumulative totals, so a lost reading heals itself' is exactly the thing a sibling project should inherit, and there is no way to publish it. AND THE MECHANISM FOR THE PARENT DIRECTION ALREADY EXISTS: `cap:derived-completion` is VERIFIED, and `dec:nested-graphs`' second obligation names it — 'a parent's view of a composed child must derive from the child's own evidence or a requirement satisfied inside the child fires unsatisfied in the parent forever'. So a program-level design holding intent that child designs satisfy is ANTICIPATED and BUILT, not missing. OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) NOTHING MORE CROSSES — interfaces and designated promises are the boundary, and reasoning stays private by design. Defensible and cheapest; the counter is that a sibling project then re-derives a ruling its neighbour already made, which is this project's most expensive recurring failure. (b) DECISIONS BECOME DESIGNATABLE, the same opt-in shape requirements already have. Small and consistent — the machinery, the designation vocabulary and the withheld-and-counted reporting all exist. Counter, and it is the hard one nobody has answered: IS A MIRRORED DECISION BINDING ON THE MIRRORING DESIGN, OR ONLY VISIBLE TO IT? A Decision that governs nothing on the far side is a note; one that governs is an authority claim across a boundary the whole rule exists to draw. (c) A STANDING 'HOUSE RULES' DESIGN every project mirrors — one design holding what its author carries everywhere. Fits `dec:nested-graphs` cleanly because that design IS separately owned and shared. Counter: nothing models a design with no build, and it overlaps option (d) on `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects`. (d) DO NOT SOLVE IT IN THE GRAPH. Counter: 'the person remembers' is what `req:no-idea-goes-quiet` (accepted the same day) exists to reject. ⚠️ THE PREREQUISITE THAT BOUNDS ALL OF IT, unchanged by the correction: reflow2's own `maturity_report` puts SEAMS at 0 OF 73. Not one coupling in this design runs through a declared Interface. So `publish-surface` and `mirror-surface` are `verified` by their own tests and have NEVER been exercised on the design that ships them — the same shape that hid (BL-176) for eleven releases and produced (BL-213) this morning. `dec:linked-repos-poc` is the trial that would fix that, and it has been parked since 2026-07-27. THE METHOD NOTE, because this is the second time today: I asserted an absence from a capability's DESCRIPTION and the code said otherwise. The description was not wrong — 'nothing internal' is true of what it withholds — it simply was not the whole surface. READ THE EXPORT, NOT THE SUMMARY.		Corrected an hour after it was written, on the same day, because the first version asserted an absence it had not checked — and an absence is exactly the kind of claim that hardens into folklore. The correction is kept in the node rather than silently replacing the text so the failure mode stays visible: I read a capability's one-line description and reported it as the whole mechanism. Kept separate from `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` because that node asks WHERE the boundary goes and this asks WHAT MAY CROSS IT. The remaining question genuinely narrowed rather than closed: requirements already cross, so the open part is Decisions, and the hard sub-question — binding or merely visible — is now the thing worth Anthony's word rather than the broad 'should intent cross'.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 model multi-organisation interoperability as a normal-form game?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. The most interesting idea in the batch and the least evidenced. Nothing here is settled. THE CRATE: dynograph-game is not even a dependency of reflow2 today. It is closed-form normal-form analysis — per-player dominant strategies, pure Nash equilibria, Pareto-optimal outcomes, the interior 2x2 mixed equilibrium, and a headline classification `nash_is_pareto_suboptimal` with the Pareto outcome that dominates each suboptimal equilibrium. THE FIT, and it is to a context Anthony has stated rather than one invented here: his real operating environment is several organisations with competing, partially-built, differently-motivated designs — A wants X, B wants Y, C built its own because it could not wait — and the job is making them interoperate when they were never designed to. That is a normal-form game. Players are organisations. Strategies are {adopt the shared interface, build our own}. And `nash_is_pareto_suboptimal` is exactly the interoperability tragedy: every organisation behaves rationally, every one builds its own, and the system of systems is collectively worse. The crate names both the equilibrium and the outcome that dominates it. ADJACENT: dec:mosa-conformance is open, and MOSA is fundamentally an argument about the incentives to use open interfaces rather than about the interfaces themselves. THE CONFLICT TO BE CLEAR ABOUT: the OBVIOUS application is analysis of alternatives — score the options, compute the equilibrium. That would CONTRADICT dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable, which is accepted and says 'alternatives are unranked forkable siblings; the human judges in hindsight, not a stored score'. Computing an equilibrium over design alternatives IS a stored recommendation. This must not be done without reopening that decision explicitly (dec:reopen-supersedes gives the mechanism).
