The interoperability reading does NOT conflict, because reflow2 would be reporting a structural property of an incentive situation a human described, not preferring a design — the same posture as dec:report-dont-judge. THE HARD COST: payoffs are not in the graph and cannot be invented. This needs new vocabulary (players, strategies, payoff matrix) and a capture path, so it is M-to-L, not a spike. It is a product question about what reflow2 is for, and wants a conversation and a Decision before any code.		Recorded because the fit to the stated multi-organisation context is unusually good, and recorded WITH the conflict against dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable stated in the same node, so nobody can pick this up later without meeting the objection.proposednothing
PARKED, TRIGGER NAMED — is 100% allocation against 0% declared seams an inversion? Unanswerable until allocation timing is recordable at all
🕐 **PARKED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD, SPLIT OUT of `dec:idea-allocation-waits-for-the-last-responsible-moment` so that its two SETTLED halves could be accepted without this one holding them open.** ✅ **APPROVER DROPPED 2026-08-14 ON HIS WORD, AND THE PARK IS UNCHANGED — READ THIS BEFORE CONCLUDING THE EDGE WAS LOST.** The `AUTHORED_BY role=approver` edge to `who:ajs` was REMOVED DELIBERATELY, taking `loop_status`'s own second option: *'decide, or drop the approver if nobody was actually asked.'* **WHY, and it is not a downgrade of the question:** an approver edge asserts that a named person was asked to SETTLE something, and this cannot be settled by anybody. It is blocked on DATA THAT DOES NOT EXIST, not on judgement. Leaving the edge made it read as outstanding work owed by him, and the only act available to him would have been to rule without evidence — which is precisely what he refused to do when he asked for the measurement first. **A question nobody can answer is not debt; carrying it as debt teaches the loop's reader to discount the list.** ⇒ THE QUESTION IS STILL OPEN, STILL PARKED, AND STILL FINDABLE. The re-ask trigger below does the remembering. **Re-attach an approver when the trigger fires** — at that point there IS something to settle. THE QUESTION: reflow2's own design is ~100% allocated while `maturity_report` puts seams at 0% (0 of 73 couplings declared through a contract). OPEN — is reflow2 already a CP store behind an AP record, and is that seam where its recurring bugs live?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12, asking whether CAP/PACELC applies to reflow2's own design. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen. ⭐ THE FINDING THAT MAKES THIS WORTH KEEPING: reflow2 HAS ALREADY MADE THESE TRADE-OFFS, REPEATEDLY AND DELIBERATELY, AND HAS NEVER NAMED THEM AS ONE CLASS. Checked against the graph rather than asserted: THE STORE IS CP. One RocksDB store, single-writer by construction. A second writer is refused rather than served — `cap:degraded-surface` exists precisely to explain that refusal, and `dec:read-while-held-mechanism` settled what a locked-out seat gets: 'a read-only view as of open, not a catchable-up secondary'. That is textbook CP with a stale-read escape hatch. `cap:stale-seat-refusal` and `req:stale-seat-knows` are the write half: refuse rather than clobber. THE RECORD IS AP. `docs/design/reflow2.json` travels by git. Everyone works offline, diverges freely, reconciles later — `cap:merge-designs`, `cap:git-merge-driver`, `cap:portability`, three-way merge with rerere. Nobody blocks. `cap:the-record-moved-is-surfaced` and `sync_status` are, precisely, an eventual-consistency staleness detector: they tell a seat the shared record moved ahead of it and name what arrived. AND `dec:advisory-concurrency` IS AN EXPLICIT AP CHOICE WITH EMPIRICAL BACKING. Its words: 'seats coordinate by announcement and provable order, NEVER BY EXCLUSION… when two claims cross, the winner is whichever landed first in git history, and both parties can verify that independently.' It names what it rejected — 'a coordination service or lock manager' — and why: 'a lock is exactly what took FIVE OF SIX SESSIONS OFFLINE on 2026-07-25.' That is choosing A over C after measuring the cost of C, which is the CAP decision made properly and never called by its name. ⇒ SO THE CANDIDATE READING IS: reflow2 is PC/EC in the store and PA/EL in the record. In normal operation it does not block on syncing the record — you work locally and export later, which is choosing L. PACELC's actual contribution here is that second half: the store-versus-record tension is NOT rare-failure behaviour, it is what every ordinary session does all day. 🛑 AND THE SHARP PART, WHICH IS WHY THIS MIGHT BE MORE THAN A RELABELLING: THE SEAM BETWEEN THE CP STORE AND THE AP RECORD IS WHERE AN UNUSUAL SHARE OF THIS PROJECT'S BUGS HAVE LIVED. Not a claim about all bugs — a pattern worth testing: · 'the design graph does NOT branch with git' — one store serves every branch, so an export carries another branch's writes. Caught once as four phantom drifts that would have merged cleanly. · The whole export procedure — restore from origin/main, export exactly once, verify prev_content_hash — is a HAND-OPERATED RECONCILIATION PROTOCOL between the two models, and every one of its documented traps is a reconciliation bug. · The mirror-refresh defect (v0.12.0 → v0.29.0): a stale pin reporting FRESH after a failed refresh is a staleness-register lie, which is the classic AP failure mode. · 2026-08-12, this session: creating nodes after exporting silently put the record behind the graph. Nothing prevented it; only a later `compare_designs` would have caught it. ═══ THE OPTIONS ═══ A — NOTHING. Record the observation and stop. CHEAP, and possibly correct: nothing would compute differently, and the choices are already made, individually, with better-reasoned rationales than 'CAP says so.' B — USE IT AS A LENS ONLY, in prose. Name the store/record split in AGENTS.md so a newcomer meets it once instead of rediscovering it through the export traps. Cheap, no code, no schema. C — MAKE THE SEAM A FIRST-CLASS THING THE GRAPH KNOWS. If the record and the store are two replicas with a hand-run reconciliation protocol, then the protocol deserves to be modelled — the traps are currently memory and prose, not structure. Most expensive, and the one where something could actually compute. D — TREAT IT AS A REQUIREMENTS SOURCE. Ask what reflow2's own availability target IS. It has never been stated, and `dec:read-while-held-mechanism` answered a CAP question without one. ═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══ ⚠️ 1. CAP IS ABOUT REPLICATED DATA UNDER NETWORK PARTITION, and reflow2's 'partition' is mostly a HUMAN and PROCESS boundary — git branches, separate sessions, a person on a plane. Borrowing a theorem outside its domain is how architectures acquire vocabulary they cannot cash. The single strongest objection. ⚠️ 2. THERE IS NO REPLICATION PROTOCOL HERE. CAP's interesting cases begin with replicas that must agree. reflow2 has one writer per store and delegates the distributed half wholesale to git — so 'reflow2 is AP' may be a statement about GIT, correctly, and nothing about reflow2. ⚠️ 3. THE CHOICES ARE ALREADY MADE AND ALREADY BETTER-ARGUED. `dec:advisory-concurrency` rests on a measured outage of five of six sessions. Relabelling that as 'we chose AP' is strictly less information than what is recorded. ⚠️ 4. NOTHING WOULD COMPUTE DIFFERENTLY under A or B, and this project's own bar — `dec:exploratory-staging`, the ility work — is whether a distinction changes a computation. 📌 A FAIR POINT FOR THE IDEA: the export traps keep being rediscovered, session after session, and live in a memory note rather than in the design. If naming the seam is what makes them explicable rather than a list of superstitions, that is worth something even under option B.		Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent. Kept because the descriptive half is verifiable today against existing nodes — dec:advisory-concurrency, dec:read-while-held-mechanism, cap:stale-seat-refusal, cap:the-record-moved-is-surfaced — and because it offers a single explanation for a family of recurring export and staleness bugs that are currently carried as procedure rather than as design. The counter-arguments are recorded beside rather than against; the strongest is that reflow2 delegates the distributed problem to git, which would make this a statement about git.proposednothing
OPEN — if every decision an agent makes is already in the graph, is capturing session context moot? (No, but the part that isn't moot never needed a blob)
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, on why he built the content store in the first place: \'one of the primary reasons I had also developed the blob was to capture actual agent session context. from my limited understanding, an agent is stateless because it can't recall previous session's context. by storing in the blob, I thought I could make a session 'stateful'. ... however, every decision that an agent makes and implements is already embedded in the graph because it is already using reflow2, therefore, ingesting session context is moot or not needed?\' ⭐ THE QUESTION HAS A RECORDED ANSWER ALREADY, and it is sharper than either yes or no. cap:session-memory (PLANNED, framing settled by Anthony himself on 2026-07-25) states it directly: \'Decision.rationale and ChangeEvent already capture fragments of the why; WHAT LIVES ONLY IN THE SESSION IS THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE — what was tried, what was rejected and on what grounds, which findings turned up while doing something else.\' So the split is: MOOT — the design content. Decisions, their rationale, requirements, changes, snapshots, questions and answers all land in the graph as they happen. Storing a transcript to preserve those would be a second copy of something already held better. NOT MOOT — the connective tissue. What was attempted and abandoned, what failed and why, what cost more than expected, what was noticed sideways. None of that is design intent, so none of it has a natural node, and it is precisely what a later session needs in order not to repeat the work. ⭐⭐ THIS SESSION IS THE EVIDENCE, and it is self-implicating rather than hypothetical. 2026-08-09 produced a great deal of design content, all of it now in the graph. It also produced process knowledge that is in NONE of it: hashing an artifact before the last edit FIVE times (because every mandatory gate — fmt, a clippy fix, a skill_lint trim — mutates the file AFTER the work looks finished); piping a gate into `tail` so the pipe returned tail's exit code and a red gate was pushed past; merging a four-PR stack in one loop so three PRs landed in already-squashed base branches and were stranded while GitHub reported all four as MERGED. **Every one of those lives in a markdown memory file OUTSIDE reflow2 entirely.** That is the connective tissue cap:session-memory names, currently housed in exactly the kind of file dec:what-lives-where was written to retire. === AND THE PART THAT BEARS ON THE BLOB === THE STORE WAS NEVER THE RIGHT MECHANISM FOR THIS, AND cap:session-memory ALREADY SAYS SO: \'a pointer to a 3 MB transcript is a RECEIPT, not documentation: leaning on it recreates the markdown problem one level down, since 'it is all in the transcript' is the same excuse as 'it is all in the backlog file'.\' Its actual design needs no content store at all: session takeaways as FIRST-CLASS GRAPH CONTENT, written when they happen, anchored to the session's epoch, queryable afterwards. The transcript is modelled as a Fragment carrying the session UUID as portable identity — A POINTER, NOT BYTES — with the absolute path explicitly demoted to a machine-scoped hint, because a path stored as identity resolves for one person and silently misses for everyone else. ⇒ SO THE SESSION-CONTEXT JUSTIFICATION FOR THE BLOB DOES NOT SURVIVE, but not for the reason the question proposes. It is not that session context is worthless — it is that ITS VALUE IS IN DISTILLED NODES, WHICH NEED NO STORE. Storing the transcript would preserve the receipt and lose the documentation. THE FRAMING THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN CLEANUP, and it is Anthony's own from 2026-07-25: a session's context IS documentation — the how-and-why record of a design's evolution — and documentation is part of the product. That changes the standard rather than the mechanism: \'a convenience can be skipped under load, a deliverable cannot.\' === WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN === (1) IS THE STATELESSNESS PREMISE ALREADY ANSWERED? reflow2's whole pitch is that the graph is the memory (req:persistence). If so, a transcript store would be a SECOND, lossier memory competing with the first — and two sources of truth is the failure this project designs out everywhere else. That reading says the blob's session justification was solving a problem reflow2 already solves. (2) WHAT FORCES THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE TO BE WRITTEN? cap:session-memory names this as its load-bearing gap: \'the existing handoff enforcement watches the modification time of MARKDOWN files, so the only mechanism forcing a session to leave takeaways behind POINTS AWAY FROM THE GRAPH.\' That is still true today — it is why this session's process findings are in a memory file. Fixing it is a nudge/hook question, not a storage question. (3) DOES PROCESS KNOWLEDGE BELONG IN A DESIGN GRAPH AT ALL? Honest counter, recorded beside rather than argued down: \'I hashed before running fmt\' is not design intent. It may belong to the harness or to a project's own working notes, and forcing it into the design graph could make the graph a log — which is the failure mode dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written warns about from the other direction. cap:session-memory's answer is the documentation reframe; whether that reframe holds for PROCESS failures as well as DESIGN reasoning is genuinely unsettled. NOTHING IS PROMOTED. Anthony asked a question; cap:session-memory remains PLANNED and unchanged.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, counters beside the options, nothing promoted. Deliberately NOT folded into cap:session-memory, and not used to edit it. That capability already holds the answer to the moot question and its framing is Anthony's own; this node records that the question was asked again, what the existing answer is, and the one part that genuinely bears on the content-store decision — that the session-context justification for the blob does not survive, because the value is in distilled nodes rather than stored bytes. Linked to dec:idea-discontinue-the-content-store because it removes one of that decision's stated motivations, which is a material change to the argument rather than a footnote.proposednothing
IDEA — external feedback arrives undifferentiated: an idea, a test result, or the boss's word. Should reflow2 have a `feedback` skill that determines what it is and routes to the skills that already exist?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-08-15, in his words: 'maybe reflow2 needs a /feedback skill to insert feedback into the graph. we have a few capture type skills already and we've used a brainstorm at times, and we have mass ingest. the thing with feedback is you don't know if it is an idea or test results or maybe it's a word by your boss on something — my point being, the feedback skill needs to determine intent/content to properly address. like I said, we have a lot of already existing skills, so this probably isn't a create-from-scratch effort, but a question of how to quickly capture external feedback in the graph.' DELIBERATELY DISTINCT FROM THE THREE NODES THE GUARD NAMED, all of which are about feedback LEAVING: `dec:idea-agent-to-agent-feedback-is-a-formal-channel` (should agents write reports for other agents), `req:agent-authored-feedback-is-reproducible-and-never-leaves-unasked` (nothing leaves without the human's word), `fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11` (one such report's content). THIS IS THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION — somebody else's report arriving, and what it becomes once it is here. Nothing in the design covers intake. ⭐ EVIDENCE FROM DOING IT BY HAND, TWICE, TODAY. This session processed two external feedback documents — a Grok session's 14 items and a US-government genesis session's 4 — and INVENTED THE SAME ROUTING BOTH TIMES with nothing to consult: verify each claim against the running build; `search_design` for an existing node before writing; defects to `TemporalFact` per `dec:defects-are-temporal-facts`; open questions to `proposed` Decisions; ideas via brainstorm; provenance via Fragments and `YIELDED`. That is knowledge re-derived per session — the exact failure `fact:defect-a-pre-served-skills-install-is-stranded` names as reflow2's own reason to exist. It is also the shape that produced `link-projects`: a process performed ad hoc, noticed, and made a served skill. ⭐⭐ THE SHARPENING, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THE QUESTION ASSUMES. He frames the discriminator as CONTENT — idea vs test result vs boss's word. Measured against what actually happened, the harder discriminator is AUTHORITY. The same sentence routes differently depending on who said it: 'this should be civil-date, not UTC' from a user is an observation; from the design's owner it MOVES A STATUS. Moving a status is precisely what an agent may not do on its own (`dec:certainty-derived`). reflow2 already models this — `Contributor`, and `AUTHORED_BY` with `role: author | reviewer | approver` — and NOTHING READS IT AT INTAKE. A skill routing on content alone would take a boss's ruling and file it as somebody's opinion. ⭐⭐ AND THE FIRST STEP IS NOT RECORDING, IT IS VERIFYING. Of the 18 items processed today, FOUR were wrong as stated: `get_instructions` truncating (it was the client's cap), the export needing the server stopped (it does not), `Constraint` requiring numeric fields (it does not — and that error had already cost that project eleven permanently-open gaps), and a claim of mine that `VIOLATES` was read by nothing. A skill whose first move is 'record what they said' would have written four false facts into the graph, each carrying a real source's authority. NO EXISTING CAPTURE SKILL HAS A VERIFY STEP, because `capture-intent` takes the user's words AS intent by definition — right for intent, wrong for a report about a system that can be checked. THE OPTIONS: (a) A NEW `feedback` SKILL THAT ROUTES — a triage front door: verify what is checkable, search for the node that already holds it, then hand off to `capture-intent` (new intent), `brainstorm` (an idea), `governance-proposal` (a rule), `revise-design` (a change to something recorded), `reconcile_verification` (a test result), or a `TemporalFact` (a defect found by use). CHEAPEST TO DESCRIBE, and it matches his read that this is composition rather than new machinery. COUNTER: a router that only routes leaves the two hard steps — verify, and read authority — to judgement, which is exactly where today's four errors would have come from. (b) A SKILL THAT DOES THE WHOLE JOB: verify → attribute authority → search → record → link provenance → report what was refuted. STRONGEST, and it captures what was actually derived twice. COUNTER: it duplicates chunks of four existing skills, and this project has been bitten before by instructions drifting out of step with the tools they describe. (c) NO NEW SKILL; EXTEND `capture-intent` with a triage section. No 21st skill, and capture-intent is already the front door people reach for. COUNTER: capture-intent's contract is that the user's words ARE intent; bolting 'first check whether they are true' onto that changes what the skill IS. (d) DO NOTHING — the mapping table in `capture-intent` plus judgement covers it. COUNTER, measured: judgement produced the right answer twice today at considerable cost in re-derivation, and the same judgement also produced four claims that survived only because they were checked. ⚠️ COST THAT MUST BE WEIGHED: twenty skills already ship, and eleven had no slash command until recently. A 21st has to earn its place against the context every session pays. ⚠️ AND IT INHERITS AN UNRESOLVED PROBLEM: feedback usually arrives AS A DOCUMENT, and `rule:design-information-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-documents` is now enforced while `Fragment.content_ref` is explicitly a pointer 'rather than inlining' the text. Until that is scoped, a feedback skill cannot say where a report's un-distilled remainder goes. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether feedback volume justifies a skill at all — three external reports in eight days is either a trend or a coincidence.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Started as a new node rather than merged after the guard named three near matches — all three concern feedback LEAVING the project, and this is intake, which is the opposite direction and shares only the word. The two sharpenings — that authority rather than content is the harder discriminator, and that verification precedes recording — are findings from this session's measured work, stated as findings rather than as answers.proposednothing
OPEN — should a Requirement/Capability carry lifecycle dimensions from the moment it is written, so fielding is thought about at the start?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-11, thinking out loud — nothing here is settled and nothing should be quoted back as intent. HIS IDEA, IN HIS WORDS: 'attach some type of additional parameters to each requirement or capability node. something that accounts for the full lifecycle of that requirement/capability. for instance, have fields for: develop-using, development-test-plan, operational-test-plan, production-plan, operational-deployed. there might be other 'dimensions' to a requirement node, but having something at the very beginning of design that already has an agent/user thinking from the get-go how it will eventually be fielded in an operational environment is good to have upfront. many of the things may be unknown-at-this-moment or N/A, but at least something is there to drive the thought process.' ⭐ THE GOAL IS THE PROMPT, NOT THE FIELD. Read his last sentence: the value he names is that the question gets ASKED early, and he expects most answers to be empty. That is a statement about when a thought happens, not about where a value is stored — and it is what separates the options below. An option that stores five mostly-empty fields but never asks anything would miss the point entirely; an option that asks all five questions and stores nothing until there is an answer would meet it. WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY HOLDS, so a later reader is not re-deciding settled ground. Each of his five axes already has machinery, but scattered and edge-shaped rather than gathered on the node: - development-test-plan / operational-test-plan — `dec:idea-verification-is-planned-with-the-requirement` is ALREADY OPEN and asks almost exactly this: 'should reflow2 guide a project to plan HOW a need will be verified when the need is stated, rather than only asking for a check once something is built?' His two test-plan axes are that question, split into a development arm and an operational arm — which is a V-model distinction that open question does not currently draw. - operational-deployed — Environment nodes, `deploy_to`, `reconcile_deployment` and `cmp:fielded` already model where something actually runs. - production-plan / readiness to field — the Readiness layer (TRL/MRL, ReadinessAssessment, GATED_ON with a required `min_level`) already models whether a thing is mature enough to field, and `SCHEDULED_FOR` models when it is due. - develop-using — nothing obvious models this. It is the one axis with no existing home. - Requirement already carries a five-state lifecycle (proposed/accepted/deferred/dropped/met) of which THREE ARE UNUSED — recorded in `chg:bl104-derived-completion` as 'the requirement lifecycle is 3/5 unused'. Any new lifecycle vocabulary has to answer why it would fare better than the one already there and unused. THE OPTIONS, with what is cheap and what is expensive about each. A — PROPERTIES ON THE NODE, his literal proposal. Five enum/string fields on Requirement and Capability. Cheapest to build (schema YAML), and the fields are visible in every export and every view, so they nag by existing. EXPENSIVE: BL-198 has just spent this month REMOVING stored defaults — 3,207 of them across 59% of nodes — because a value written by the tool rather than by a person makes `compare_designs` unable to tell a default from a decision. Five fields defaulting to 'unknown' on every node is that exact shape, freshly re-introduced. And 'N/A' written by an agent is a judgement about scope, which `dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement` says the tool does not get to make on the user's behalf. B — ASK THE FIVE QUESTIONS, STORE NOTHING UNTIL THERE IS AN ANSWER. A gap detector in the existing detect-and-ask loop that asks, of a requirement, 'how will this be developed / checked in development / checked in operations / produced / fielded?' No schema change; nothing is stored until somebody answers, so silence stays silence and never becomes a stored 'unknown'. Matches the goal he actually stated, since the thought is what he wants triggered. EXPENSIVE: the loop already owes 67 unasked gaps, and five new questions on every requirement would swamp it — this needs a rule about WHICH requirements deserve the questions (and when), or it drowns the thing it is added to. C — EDGES TO REAL NODES, which is what reflow2 does today. A test plan is a Verification, a production plan is a Release/DesignEpoch, fielding is an Environment. Nothing new at all. CHEAP and already queryable end to end. EXPENSIVE, and this is Anthony's actual complaint: it only ever happens when somebody REMEMBERS to draw the edge, so the thinking never gets prompted at the start — which is the whole thing he is asking for. D — A SIDE NODE PER AXIS, on the DimensionAssessment pattern that already exists for cross-cutting concerns. Keeps the requirement clean, lets an axis carry its own provenance and date, and extends to 'other dimensions' without another schema change each time — which is the extensibility his aside asks about. EXPENSIVE: a node per axis per requirement is a lot of graph for something usually empty, and it is the heaviest of the four. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO THE WHOLE IDEA, recorded beside it rather than used to kill it: a checklist filled with 'unknown-at-this-moment' on every node teaches people to skip it, and then reflow2 holds five more fields nobody reads — the exact failure already measured twice here, in the 3-of-5 unused requirement lifecycle and in the two evidence-quality axes used zero times. Whatever is chosen has to say what READS the answer, because a marker nothing reads is a comment. NOT DECIDED, and deliberately not ranked. B and C are not exclusive — B could be the prompt that leads to C's edges, which would need no new vocabulary at all.		Anthony's, 2026-08-11: 'having something at the very beginning of design that already has an agent/user thinking from the get-go how it will eventually be fielded in an operational environment is good to have upfront.' The design's V-model has both arms and no rungs, and this is a proposal for rungs stated at the top of the left arm — which is why it is worth recording even though four of the five axes already have scattered machinery.proposednothing
OPEN — should a project hold SEVERAL graph_ids in one store and operate on whichever the question needs, which is a linking mechanism nested-graphs never considered?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-05: 'just curious if it is a hard limit for a project to be limited to one graph_id? for instance, could a project say, could list 3 different graph_ids and be able to do reflow2 operations on whichever or multiple based on the question. this would be a different way of linking multiple graphs, which was an idea that we had discussed previously.' ⭐ FIRST, THE MEASURED ANSWER, BECAUSE THIS ONE IS CHECKABLE AND WAS CHECKED. IT IS NOT A HARD LIMIT AT THE STORAGE LAYER. - Storage keys are `{graph_id}\x00{type}\x00{id}` (`dynograph_storage::keys`), so one store namespaces many graphs by construction. - `DesignGraph::with_graph_id` (graph.rs:191) IS A FIELD ASSIGNMENT — `self.graph_id = id.into()`. Rebinding a handle to another graph in the same store is FREE: no reopen, no lock churn, no cost. Its own doc comment says the intent out loud: 'to host several designs in one storage instance'. - `open_in_memory_as(graph_id)` already exists for the same reason. So 'list 3 graph_ids and operate on whichever' is architecturally CHEAP TODAY. What blocks it is the SERVER, not the store: the MCP service holds one `Arc>` bound at launch, and no tool takes a graph argument. ⭐⭐ SECOND, AND IT IS THE PART THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS IS 'LINKING' AT ALL: EDGES STILL CANNOT CROSS GRAPH_IDS, EVEN INSIDE ONE STORE. `create_edge` (graph.rs:276) resolves BOTH endpoints through `self.get_node(kind, id)`, which is scoped to the bound `graph_id` — so an edge to a node in a sibling graph is refused as `NodeNotFound`. That refusal is deliberate and well-argued (a dangling edge 'is not a judgement call the user might reasonably disagree with… it is a graph that cannot be walked'), and it applies here without having been written for this case. SO THE HONEST FRAMING OF WHAT THIS BUYS: co-location gives CHEAP SWITCHING and ONE PLACE TO LOOK. It does NOT give cross-graph edges, so it does not by itself answer (BL-214) — the prose cross-references that `detect_gaps` and `propagate_change` cannot see. What it DOES do is make cross-graph edges a much shorter path IF they are ever wanted, because the key encoding already namespaces and the endpoint check is one scope decision rather than a storage redesign. ⭐ WHY THIS IS A GENUINELY NEW OPTION RATHER THAN A RESTATEMENT. `dec:nested-graphs` (accepted 2026-07-25) weighed exactly three: (a) one graph, zoom by level; (b) a graph per system; (c) a graph per ownership boundary, which it took. ALL THREE ASSUME ONE GRAPH PER STORE — the store/graph distinction was never in play, so 'many graphs, one store, switchable' was not among the roads taken OR the roads not taken. It sits between (a) and (c): more separation than one graph, less ceremony than federation, and it costs none of the three obligations (a coordinate, an evidence roll-up, a freshness check) that the accepted rule says every seam must pay — because there is no seam, only a scope. OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) LEAVE IT — one graph per store, federate across stores as `dec:nested-graphs` prescribes. Counter: that is what produced prose cross-references and three stores on one repo, and federation's costs are being paid by one person with no authority boundary to justify them. (b) SEVERAL GRAPHS IN ONE STORE, ONE BOUND AT A TIME — the cheapest real change: a graph reference selects which, edges stay within a graph, reads and writes stay scoped. Counter: it makes 'which design am I writing to' a per-call question, which is `dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design`'s hazard exactly — and getting it wrong writes to the wrong design. The refuse-when-several rule recorded there applies here unchanged. (c) SEVERAL GRAPHS, QUERIED TOGETHER — 'operations on multiple based on the question', Anthony's stronger reading. Counter: EVERY read is `self.engine.scan_nodes(&self.graph_id, …)`, so this is not a parameter, it is a change to how every analysis is scoped, and the reports would need to say WHICH graph each finding came from or become unreadable. (d) SEVERAL GRAPHS AND EDGES MAY CROSS THEM — the full version, and the only one that answers (BL-214). Counter: it reopens `create_edge`'s endpoint invariant, which currently guarantees every reader a walkable graph, and it needs an answer to what a cross-graph edge MEANS when one side is exported and the other is not. ⚠️ AND THE CONSTRAINT THAT CUTS ACROSS ALL OF THEM: `req:persistence` says 'the design persists in-repo alongside the code' and `dec:repo-file-embedded` says the graph lives as a repo file. A single store holding several projects' designs lives in ONE repo or in none — so (b), (c) and (d) all need that requirement revisited rather than quietly contradicted. That is the same tension `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` option (d) hit, and it is the real price here, not the code. WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED: `with_graph_id` is free and already intended for this; `create_edge` refuses cross-scope endpoints and the refusal is deliberate; the MCP server binds one graph at launch; and `dec:nested-graphs` never considered this shape, so taking it is an addition to that decision rather than a contradiction of it. NOT CHECKED: whether the export/import path carries `graph_id` in a way that would let one store's several graphs be exported separately — `export_graph` writes the bound graph, and `import_graph` 'adopts the document's own graph_id', which suggests it would work, but nobody has tried it.		Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request, and the mechanical half was CHECKED IN THE CODE BEFORE ANY OF IT WAS WRITTEN — deliberately, because three times earlier the same day this agent asserted a mechanism from a description and was wrong each time. The three facts that matter here (with_graph_id is a field assignment, create_edge scopes both endpoints, the server binds one handle) are cited to file and line so the next session argues from them rather than re-reading. Recorded as its own node rather than folded into `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` because that node asks WHERE the boundary goes and this one asks WHAT A STORE MAY HOLD — they interact but are separately answerable, and one node holding both could only be half-answered. The observation that `dec:nested-graphs` never considered this shape is the load-bearing part. That decision is accepted and its reasoning is sound; this is not a challenge to it but a fourth option it did not have, and saying so plainly is what stops a later reader treating this as reopening a settled question.proposednothing
OPEN — may an exploratory fork build without requirements, and is the motivation gate at the WRITE or at the MERGE?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Anthony, 2026-08-11: 'there have several times where I've forked off somebody's repo and tried something just to see if it was possible... do we allow users of reflow2 to 'fork' off a main design and explore without having the requirement for anything they build to have 'requirement' linked to it. then if the exploratory fork off main design works, is there a way to 'merge' into main?' His own lean, recorded as his: 'can something merge into main design without a requirement associated with it (I'm kind of leaning towards no)'. ⭐ THE QUESTION SHARPENS TO ONE THING: WHERE THE GATE SITS. Nobody is proposing that unmotivated work be invisible — `unmotivated_capability` fires today and should. The open question is whether it should be SILENT IN A FORK and BINDING AT THE MERGE, which is a different placement, not a different rule. ⚠️ THE COST OF THE CURRENT PLACEMENT IS MEASURED, and it is in `dec:exploratory-staging`: a Capability at `planned` with no Requirement raises THREE gaps — `unmotivated_capability`, `unrealized_capability`, `unverified_capability` — 'THREE GAPS EACH, FOREVER, BY CONSTRUCTION'. On 2026-08-10 that was 34 of 73 open gaps, 47% of the list, from backlog rows that were wishes nobody had agreed to. An exploratory fork is the same shape at speed: every spike accrues three gaps, and a fork built to answer 'is this even possible' would be all noise by the end of an afternoon. 📌 SO THE FORK CASE MAY BE THE MISSING EVIDENCE `dec:exploratory-staging` IS WAITING FOR. That decision's closing question is 'DOES A NOT-YET-AGREED WISH BELONG IN THE DESIGN AT ALL?' and its options (b) a `proposed` Capability status and (c) route wishes to a Decision are both about giving unagreed work a silent home. A fork is a place where unagreed work is not merely tolerated but is THE POINT, which is a stronger argument for a silent home than a backlog row ever was. These should be read together. IDEAS, unranked: (a) GATE AT THE MERGE, NOT THE WRITE. The fork writes freely; `apply_merge` refuses to land a Capability with no incoming SATISFIES unless the merger states one or explicitly accepts it as unmotivated. This is EXACTLY the shape `apply_merge` already has — `dec:merge-three-way` makes it refuse, writing nothing, until every conflict is decided — so the mechanism is a second refusal reason rather than a new mechanism. It also matches Anthony's lean. (b) SILENCE THE DETECTORS IN A FORK by marking the design exploratory, so gaps stay quiet until it is merged. Cheap, and it hides real findings: a fork that is quietly incoherent looks identical to one that is fine, which is the false-green class this project keeps finding. (c) DO NOTHING. Explore in a fork, tolerate the gap noise, and let the merge be an ordinary merge. Zero build cost; the noise is the cost, and it is the cost `dec:exploratory-staging` already measured at 47% of a real gap list. (d) REQUIRE MOTIVATION AT THE WRITE EVEN IN A FORK — the status quo. Honest and it forbids the thing Anthony is describing: you cannot try something to see if it is possible if you must first say why you want it. ⚠️ THE ARGUMENT FOR HIS LEAN, stated because it is stronger than it first looks. What lands in the primary design becomes what the golden thread computes delivery from. `req:completion-computed` (accepted) derives delivery FROM the thread rather than from a status field, so a Capability merged in with nothing behind it silently degrades the one number the design is supposed to be able to state honestly. A fork can afford incoherence because nothing computes from it; the primary design cannot. ⚠️ THE ARGUMENT AGAINST IT, equally real. `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (proposed) exists because a body of intent that contradicts itself is still a design, and `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` says the target is a consumer's project — where brownfield reality is that things get built and the requirement is written afterwards, if ever. A merge gate that admits no unmotivated work forbids adopting the very case `adopt` exists for. Whatever is chosen must let a merger say 'yes, this is unmotivated, and I am taking it anyway' and have that recorded rather than blocked — which is what makes (a) a two-sided accept and not a wall. ⚠️ AND THE HONEST WARNING FROM THE SAME FAMILY: the detect-and-ask skill forbids inventing a requirement to close `unmotivated_capability` — 'a requirement backed out of the thing that implements it is satisfied by construction and can never contradict anything.' A merge gate that demands a requirement will produce exactly those unless the accept-it-anyway route is first-class and cheap.		The question is not whether unmotivated work is visible but where the gate sits. Gating at the merge lets a fork do what a fork is for while keeping the primary design's delivery number honest, and it reuses apply_merge's existing refuse-until-decided shape rather than inventing one. The fork case is also stronger evidence for dec:exploratory-staging's open question than the backlog rows that raised it, since in a fork unagreed work is the point rather than a leftover.proposednothing
OPEN — should real usage telemetry be a standing instrument for shaping the surface, and how far may it go?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony's idea, 2026-08-01, and the first run has already paid (BL-153/154/155). What is open is not whether the measurement is useful, but how far it should go and what it must never become. WHAT WAS DONE, and it is now `tools/surface_usage.py`: read the retained Claude Code transcripts, count tool calls, build the tool-to-tool transition graph, and run PageRank over it with self-loops removed. 46 sessions, 6,095 calls, 10 projects. WHY THE GRAPH OPERATION EARNS ITS KEEP: it disagrees with raw counts. Volume puts `release_includes` first (1,008 calls, bookkeeping in 7 sessions); PageRank puts `detect_gaps`, `loop_status`, `export_graph`, `detect_defects` first — the coherence loop's read side, which is what workflows route THROUGH. High-volume-low-PageRank is a batching defect; high-PageRank is load-bearing. One measurement, two questions, and the tool that tops one does not top the other. THE OPEN QUESTIONS, none answered: (a) HOW FAR DOES IT GO? Today it is a manual, offline, read-only probe over transcripts a developer happens to have. The tempting next step is telemetry FROM the server — and that is a different product with different consent, privacy and trust properties. A design brain that watches its users is not obviously the same thing as one that keeps their design coherent. (b) MAY ANY OF IT REACH THE GRAPH? `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` says loop debt is computed from graph state and never from run history, and 'looking is not writing' is a standing rule. That decision is about DEBT specifically, not about whether usage telemetry may exist at all — but nobody has ever said so out loud, and this is the moment to decide rather than to assume. The instrument as written writes nothing, which keeps the question open rather than answering it by accident. (c) WHAT IS THE HONEST UNIT? Self-loop share proxies for a missing bulk form, and it worked. But a design brain optimised for fewer tool calls is not obviously optimised for better designs, and BL-23's lesson is that a number which punishes correct work needs a different question rather than a tuned threshold. There is no target self-loop share and there should not be one. (d) OTHER PROJECTS' TRANSCRIPTS ARE OTHER PEOPLE'S WORK. Reading Anthony's own machine is one thing. If this ever runs over a consumer's sessions it needs their word first, and probably needs to never leave their machine. THE HONEST LIMIT ALREADY FOUND: absence is weak evidence. `set_project_mode` appears as text in ten transcripts with zero recorded calls, so a tool used before the retention window is indistinguishable from one never used. Any 'unused' verdict from this instrument is a question, not a finding.		Recorded as an idea rather than a capability because the measurement is already built and useful while the QUESTIONS it raises — server-side telemetry, whether any of it may become graph state, consent over other people's transcripts — are genuinely undecided and would each be a different product. Anthony's idea; the first run produced three backlog rows.proposednothing
OPEN — should adopt extract code STRUCTURE mechanically (tree-sitter style) and reserve the agent for intent, when reflow2 has already decided decomposition is functional and not the file tree?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 research (relayed by Anthony 2026-08-06), specifically Graphify (Tree-sitter static analysis plus LLM semantic extraction) and Understand Anything (multi-agent pipeline over every file, function, class and dependency, with architectural-layer and business-domain views on top). STILL OPEN. THE IDEA: the adopt skill currently recovers an existing system by having an agent read it. The survey's tools do the structural half MECHANICALLY and deterministically — files, functions, classes, imports, calls, API surfaces, DB models — and spend the LLM only on summaries. Splitting adopt the same way would make the cheap half cheap and exact, and leave the agent doing only what the artifact cannot tell you: why it was built that way, who asked for it, what is now vestigial. It would also make link-artifacts and reconcile_artifacts far cheaper to keep true, since registering artifacts and their hashes is precisely a mechanical sweep. WHAT IS CHEAP: the extraction itself is a solved problem with off-the-shelf parsers, and it is deterministic, which sits well with req:deterministic-core. WHAT IS EXPENSIVE: a parser per language, kept current — and Anthony's real operating context is a ten-year-old Python stack (bluesky, tiled) plus beamline analysis code, so the language surface is not small and much of it is dynamic, where static analysis is weakest. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is the strong one, from reflow2's own record: dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition already decided that reflow2's systems are FUNCTIONAL, not its file tree. Mechanical extraction from source produces exactly the decomposition that decision rejected — a Component per module, an Interface per public signature — which is a map of the repository, not of the design. Feeding that in would populate the graph with structure at the wrong altitude, and the wrong altitude is harder to fix than an empty graph because it looks finished. Understand Anything's 'architectural layers (API, service, data, UI)' is an attempt at the same altitude problem, and it solves it by guessing, which is what dec:views-are-projections forbids reflow2 from doing. A NARROWER VERSION THAT MAY SURVIVE THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: extract only ARTIFACTS and their content hashes, not Components or Interfaces. That is the layer whose identity genuinely IS the file, so no altitude claim is being made, and it is the layer reflow2 already models as files (art:*, set_artifact_checksum, cap:link-artifacts). The mechanical pass would then answer 'what exists on disk and has it changed' and say nothing about what the design means. Offered as a distinction to consider, not as advocacy. RELATED, NOT THE SAME QUESTION: whether reflow2 should CONSUME an existing code-graph tool's output rather than build extraction itself. The survey's tools all expose their graph over MCP, which would make them an ingest source rather than a rival. Unexplored.		Recorded as an idea because the mechanical/intent split is a genuinely good shape that the adopt skill does not currently have, and recording it with dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition named beside it is the point — the objection is what makes this idea usable later, and an idea killed in conversation would have lost it.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 propose MISSING edges from neighbourhood overlap, as a question rather than a repair?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled. THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::link_prediction_all / link_prediction_from (unused) score non-adjacent node pairs by how much their neighbourhoods overlap — common neighbours, Jaccard, or Adamic-Adar (which down-weights hubs). Read on a design graph: 'these two look like they should be connected and are not — is there a missing SATISFIES, or DEPENDS_ON?' WHERE IT LANDS: BL-114's unsolved half. That item records that disconnected_community SUGGESTS adding a bridge while its suggestion does not know the detector's own selectivity, so the advised bridge's only correct forms are edge types the measurement excludes. Link prediction would propose WHICH bridge, on evidence rather than on a template. IT MUST BE AN ASK, NEVER A REPAIR. dec:ask-not-repair (suspected duplicates are asked, never merged) and dec:report-dont-judge both apply directly, and apply_heal already proposes-and-stops in rigid mode. A predicted edge written into the graph would be reflow2 inventing design. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it may be fatal: a golden thread is largely a TREE. Trees have very few common neighbours, so neighbourhood-overlap scores may be near-zero almost everywhere and the signal may simply not exist on this shape of graph. That is measurable BEFORE any build — run it over reflow2's own 1179-node export and see whether anything scores. docs/sharpening.md is exactly the discipline for that, and this should not be built until the instrument says there is a signal.		Included because it is the only unused foundation function that addresses BL-114's open half; recorded with its likely-fatal objection attached rather than argued down, so a later session inherits both.proposednothing
OPEN — is the per-user graph scope a convenience or a COMPARTMENT, and what must reflow2 promise (and refuse to promise) if designs are separated by clearance?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-06, extending the federation idea into his own professional domain: 'in the military, when you have a clearance, there is a 'need to know' and a person only gets what they need to know. often SAP/SAR programs are like this. reflow2 could support both this mechanically by user1 being the only person to projectA... then user2 who does not have a need to know only has access to projectB... and their projectC. mechanically, they'd have to have access to some machine that could hold the graph for the different clearance levels.' NOTE ON THE EXAMPLE: Anthony flagged immediately afterwards that he had muddled which made-up project sat at which level ('oops, I think I goofed up the clearance levels of my made up projects, but hopefully the point is still valid'). It is. Nothing below rests on the specific levels — only on the SHAPE: user1 holds {A, B}, user2 holds {B, C}, and B is the overlap. The levels are deliberately not restated here, because the slip turned out to expose a real error in the first version of this node. See the correction below. THE STRUCTURAL ANALOGY IS EXACT, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS DANGEROUS. The federation shape recorded in dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs — each person holds their own subtree plus one hop outward, cuts overlapping at ownership seams — is, drawn on a whiteboard, indistinguishable from need-to-know compartmentation. The overlap graph is the shared compartment. Nothing about the picture is wrong. ⚠️⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT BE READ INTO IT, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS NODE: reflow2 IS NOT AN ACCESS CONTROL AND MUST NEVER BE DESCRIBED AS ONE. It has NO AUTHENTICATION OF ANY KIND — recorded already in req:a-session-cannot-reach-another-designs-graph, and --http-allow-host is Host-header allowlisting for DNS-rebinding protection, not authentication. A list of graph_ids in a config file is a CONVENIENCE SCOPE: it says which designs a session bothers to load, not which designs a person is permitted to read. Anyone with filesystem read access to the store reads the entire design, config or no config. In most domains that distinction is pedantic. In THIS one it is the difference between a tool and an incident, and it is precisely the permission-versus-convenience question left open on the federation node — now with real consequences attached. THE REAL SEPARATION IS THE ACCREDITATION BOUNDARY, NOT THE APPLICATION. Anthony said the mechanical part himself — 'they'd have to have access to some machine that could hold the graph for the different clearance levels.' The enclave, the system-high accreditation and whatever guard moves data between them are the controls. reflow2's honest role is to be COMPATIBLE with that separation, never to implement it. ⭐ AND HERE THE FEDERATION SHAPE EARNS ITS KEEP FOR A REASON THAT HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH CONVENIENCE. Because nobody holds the whole DAG — each person holds a local cut — the design CAN be split across enclaves at all. A design brain that required the whole federation resident in one process to answer a question would be unusable above unclassified, full stop. The local-cut property is what makes cross-enclave design possible, and that is an architectural argument for it independent of anything about laptops and subtrees. ⭐ THE FILE-BASED MODEL IS THE ONE THAT SURVIVES AN AIR GAP, AND IT IS NOT LEGACY. dec:multi-writer-architecture (ACCEPTED) keeps the design as a graph-in-a-repo-file with many writers merging on pull, and its product is an EXPORT — a single, complete, content-hashed, deterministic file, with a three-way merge that can reconcile two divergent copies. FILES ARE WHAT A CROSS-DOMAIN TRANSFER PROCESS CAN ACTUALLY MOVE. The hosted always-on server of dec:one-process-many-stores — flo2's model, proposed the previous day — is not that, and could not be. So reflow2 now has TWO deployment shapes serving genuinely different worlds: hosted, for flo2's non-technical browser collaborators; file-and-merge, for anything behind an accreditation boundary. Recording this because the hosted work could easily be mistaken for the direction of travel, and for this class of user the repo-file model is not the old way — it is the only way. ⚠️⚠️ THE DIRECT COLLISION WITH THE FEATURE ANTHONY ASKED FOR AN HOUR EARLIER. dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency proposes that a gap in one design automatically become a requirement in the design it depends on. IN A COMPARTMENTED SETTING, AN AUTOMATIC CROSS-GRAPH WRITE IS A CHANNEL BETWEEN COMPARTMENTS. And it is worse than the content: the mere EXISTENCE and TIMING of activity on one side can be inferable from the other — a node id, a timestamp, a counter that ticks, 'someone is blocked on this' — none of which is the sensitive fact and all of which can carry it. AGGREGATION compounds it: two designs each individually releasable may not be releasable together. ⭐⭐ CORRECTION, 2026-08-06, PROMPTED BY ANTHONY'S OWN SLIP ABOUT THE LEVELS — and it changes the engineering conclusion, so it is recorded rather than quietly edited. The first version of this node said 'upward may be fine, downward is spillage.' THAT CONFLATED TWO DIFFERENT AXES. Dependency direction (who consumes whom) and classification direction (what is more sensitive) are INDEPENDENT, and assuming they align is exactly the mistake the muddled example accidentally surfaced. In the example as loosely written, the most sensitive project happened to also be the most upstream, so 'flows upstream' and 'flows to higher classification' looked like the same sentence. THEY ARE NOT, AND REFLOW2'S OWN REAL CASE IS THE OPPOSITE ONE: dynograph-foundation is the most upstream design and the least sensitive — a public library — while its consumers are the things that could carry sensitivity. So a gap in a classified consumer flowing UP into an unclassified foundation is a flow toward LOWER classification, which is the dangerous direction. The feature's most natural and most useful direction is, in the realistic configuration, the unsafe one. THE CONSTRAINT THEREFORE HAS TO BE STATED AGAINST THE SENSITIVITY LATTICE, NOT AGAINST THE DEPENDENCY GRAPH — 'one-directional by construction' is not enough, because the design cannot know which direction is safe without being told something it currently has no vocabulary for. Which loops back to option (b) below: SOME marking axis may be unavoidable, not because reflow2 should enforce anything, but because without it the tool cannot tell the safe direction from the unsafe one and must therefore refuse to flow anything automatically at all. That is a defensible answer — refuse rather than guess is this project's standing doctrine — and it should be reached deliberately rather than by omission. THERE IS NO MARKING VOCABULARY, AND `designation` IS NOT IT. Searched before writing: the only thing resembling a marking is `designation` on Requirements and Interfaces, whose values are `internal` / `published`. That is the SHAPE of a marking — an opt-in, per-node, computed-upon label, withheld by default and counted when withheld — but it is about PUBLICATION BOUNDARIES, not sensitivity, and reading it as a classification would be a category error. Whether reflow2 should gain a real marking axis is a schema question and therefore at least a minor version, per the CHANGELOG's own rule. OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) REFLOW2 MODELS NOTHING ABOUT CLASSIFICATION. The enclave separates; reflow2 is just a design tool that happens to run inside one. Cheapest, most honest, impossible to misread. Counter: the user still has to mark things somewhere, and it will end up in prose inside node text — the shadow-list failure again, and here an unmarked-but-sensitive statement sitting in a `statement` field is a genuine problem. AND, per the correction above, this option forecloses automatic cross-graph flow entirely, because a tool with no sensitivity vocabulary cannot know which direction is safe. (b) A DESCRIPTIVE MARKING AXIS — a sensitivity label per node or per design, never enforcing, so an export can SAY what it contains and an automatic flow can at least refuse to run toward a lower label. Counter, and it is severe: a marking that does not enforce invites exactly the misreading warned about above, and a WRONG marking is more dangerous than none, because people act on it. (c) REFLOW2 PROMISES ONLY NEGATIVE PROPERTIES, and says so plainly: never requires the whole federation in one place, never initiates a message (already true and verified against the service — proxy.rs), never phones home, and its export is a complete, self-describing, content-hashed file a human can inspect before it crosses anything. Marketed as COMPATIBLE WITH an accreditation boundary, never as implementing one. Cheap, truthful, and very nearly the current state already. (d) CROSS-GRAPH FLOW IS DIRECTIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION AND EVERY CROSSING IS AN AUDITABLE EVENT — with the correction above attached: the direction must be defined against sensitivity, which (a) cannot express. Worth having on its own merits even with no classification involved, because 'which design wrote into mine, when, and why' is a question any consumer wants answered. WHAT IS NOT RECORDED HERE BECAUSE ANTHONY HAS NOT SAID IT: whether this is a real requirement he intends reflow2 to meet, or an observation that the shape happens to fit a world he knows well. He called it 'just another spinoff of this idea', which reads as the latter — and the difference matters enormously, because (b) and (d) are real work and (a) and (c) are mostly writing down what is already true.		Captured under the brainstorm skill, 2026-08-06, as the third node in one conversation — kept separate from the ACCESS question (dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs) and the AUTHORITY question (dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency) because it asks a third thing: what reflow2 may TRUTHFULLY CLAIM about separation, which is a question about the product's promises rather than about its mechanism. CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE CORRECTION IS KEPT IN THE NODE rather than silently replacing the text — the same discipline dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs used on 2026-08-05, and for the same reason: the failure mode should stay visible. The first version asserted 'upward may be fine, downward is spillage', which quietly assumed the dependency ordering and the sensitivity ordering run together. They do not, and reflow2's own dependency chain is a counterexample — dynograph-foundation is simultaneously the most upstream and the least sensitive design in it. The error surfaced only because Anthony flagged that he had muddled the levels in his own example, which forced a re-read; a tidier example would have hidden it. Recorded as chg:classification-and-dependency-are-orthogonal. Written with a deliberate bias toward what reflow2 must NOT say. Anthony is a Space Force systems engineer and this is his working domain, so the failure mode here is not that reflow2 lacks a feature — it is that a structural resemblance between 'per-user graph scoping' and 'need-to-know' gets read as a security property by someone who then relies on it. The node therefore leads with the disclaimer rather than the opportunity, and the disclaimer is drawn from intent the design already holds rather than from caution: req:a-session-cannot-reach-another-designs-graph states in its own text that reflow2 has no authentication and that authorization belongs to the layer in front. Also recorded because it re-values something that could otherwise look superseded: the repo-file-plus-merge model (dec:multi-writer-architecture, accepted) is the ONLY one of reflow2's two deployment shapes that can cross an air gap, since its product is a complete deterministic file and a three-way merge. The hosted multi-graph work of the previous day is additive, not a migration, and this is the clearest statement yet of who each shape is for.proposednothing
OPEN — is reflow2's differentiator that the graph can be RIGHT when the code is WRONG, and what should follow from defending that line?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 research on the emerging 'graph brain around the codebase' ecosystem, relayed by Anthony 2026-08-06. STILL OPEN. WHAT THE SURVEY SHOWS. The field has converged on two families, and reflow2 is in neither: (1) CODE-AS-GRAPH — Graphify, Understand Anything, Sourcegraph/Cody. The graph is DERIVED from the code by static analysis plus LLM summarisation. It answers 'what depends on this', 'what breaks if I change this function'. (2) AGENT MEMORY — Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta (MemGPT), Cognee, Supermemory, LangMem, LlamaIndex Memory. The graph is DERIVED from conversation and execution traces. It answers 'what did we say before', 'what worked last time'. THE READING OFFERED, and it is the agent's own analysis rather than anything Alex or the research says: both families are DESCRIPTIVE, and the property they therefore cannot have is disagreement. A graph re-derived from the code can never contradict the code — if the code drifts from intent, the graph drifts with it and reports nothing. A memory layer never contradicts anything either; it recalls. reflow2's graph is AUTHORED and sits UPSTREAM of the code, which is what lets it say the code is wrong: drift, gaps, defects, unrealized capabilities, a failing gate. That is not a feature the survey's tools lack by oversight — it is unavailable to anything whose graph is a function of the artifact. THE OPEN QUESTION, which is a design question and not a marketing one: if that is the line reflow2 defends, several current tensions resolve one way rather than the other. Retrieval quality (dec:idea-embeddings-adoption) becomes a convenience rather than the product. The gates, drift detection and the coherence loop become the core rather than the overhead. And 'reflow2 as a memory layer you sprinkle on' becomes the wrong shape, because a layer that plugs into somebody else's agent framework has no standing to refuse. Conversely, if the line is NOT defended, the honest conclusion may be that several of these tools already do most of what a user wants at a fraction of the adoption cost. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: every tool in the survey is a LAYER — it plugs into LangGraph/LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel or Claude Code, and the user keeps everything else they had. reflow2 is a whole system: its own store, schema, skill kit, gates and vocabulary. Being normative is exactly WHY it cannot be a thin layer, so the differentiator and the adoption cost are the same fact seen twice. req:thin-install and req:frictionless-update are pushing on this, and a one-line install does not by itself make a coherence loop cheap to adopt. Whether there is a legitimate smaller entry point — read-only, query-only, no loop — or whether that entry point would be a dishonest version of the product, is part of what is open here. WHAT IS ALSO WORTH NOTING AND IS NOT A QUESTION: Sourcegraph exposing its graph to agents over MCP is the pattern reflow2 already implements. That is validation, not a gap. Mem0's 'organizational memory' tier (knowledge many agents share) is the same territory as req:many-designs-one-service and dec:central-host, which are already in flight — also validation.		Recorded because there is currently NO node anywhere in the design that says what reflow2 is that comparable tools are not, and a differentiator nobody wrote down cannot be defended when a build decision quietly trades it away. The specific value of the survey is that it is the first external evidence of what the alternatives actually do, so the comparison is against real systems rather than a supposed rival.proposednothing
OPEN — where does the graph live when ONE PERSON works many interrelated projects, which is the case dec:nested-graphs' rule was not written for?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-05, in his own words: 'one idea that I've come across is that I work many inter-related projects. it seems like a reflow2 project/graph is limited to one git repo. curious if we should remove this constraint? then I can use the reflow2 graph in one project (project_x) and still use it to guide a closely related project (say project_y). the benefit of this is that a set of projects done in this manner can all influence each other. another option is to build the reflow2 graph in the parent folder of a bunch of interrelated projects. for instance, all my individual projects are in a folder called git_projects - maybe this is the appropriate place to build the graph versus within each project.' ⭐ FIRST, THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD, AND THAT MATTERS BEFORE ANY OPTION IS WEIGHED. There is NO CONSTRAINT TO REMOVE. `--graph-path` is an ordinary CLI argument; this repo's `.mcp.json` passes `./.reflow2/graph` and that is a CONVENTION, not a binding. Verified the same day by creating graphs at arbitrary filesystem paths outside any repository during the corpus trial. `dec:install-once-per-machine` already states the position: 'reflow2 installs once per machine; the in-repo half is optional and only for repos you share.' So the question is not CAN the graph live elsewhere — it can, today, with no change — but WHERE IT SHOULD, which is a design question about authority rather than a limitation to lift. SECOND, THE PLACEMENT RULE IS ALREADY DECIDED AND IT DISPOSES OF ONE OPTION OUTRIGHT. `dec:nested-graphs` (ACCEPTED, Anthony, 2026-07-25): 'A design is its own graph when something at that level is separately OWNED, separately RELEASED, or separately SHARED — and a subtree of one graph otherwise. THE HIERARCHY DOES NOT DECIDE; AUTHORITY DOES.' A `git_projects/` parent folder is a filesystem convention with no authority attached, so under the accepted rule it is NOT a reason to put a graph there. If those projects share a graph it must be because they share an owner, a release train or a recipient — never because they share a directory. ⭐ THIRD, AND THIS IS WHY THE QUESTION IS GENUINELY OPEN RATHER THAN ALREADY ANSWERED: THE RULE WAS WRITTEN FOR FEDERATION BETWEEN OWNERS, AND ANTHONY'S CASE IS ONE OWNER WITH MANY RELEASE TRAINS. The discriminator is a three-way OR — owned, released, OR shared — so 'separately released' alone sends his projects to separate graphs. But every cost the rule cites for a seam (a coordinate, an evidence roll-up, a freshness check) is a cost of crossing an AUTHORITY boundary, and there is no authority boundary here. He is paying federation's price to solve a filing problem. The rule is not wrong; his case sits on a seam in it that multi-org federation never presented. OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) ONE GRAPH FOR THE FAMILY, levels inside it. The accepted rule already blesses this 'for everything inside one ownership boundary' and `cap:scoped-analysis` delivers per-level reading, so nothing new is needed. Counter, from the rule's own text: what one graph cannot give is separate write locks, separate release trains, or a way to share ONE project without shipping the others — and his projects DO release separately, which is exactly the case (a) was said not to cover. (b) A GRAPH PER PROJECT, MIRRORED. What the accepted rule prescribes, and the linking half is BUILT (`cap:mirror-surface`, `cap:publish-surface`). Counter: `dec:linked-repos-poc` names the blocker — 'reflow2 structures roughly one and a half of the six characteristics an interface spec needs and puts the rest in one free-text string, so today two graphs can be linked and still not be comparable' — and reflow2's own `maturity_report` puts SEAMS at 0 of 73, so the mechanism this option rests on is the least-exercised thing in the design. (c) A GRAPH IN THE PARENT FOLDER. Ruled out by `dec:nested-graphs` as stated, but worth keeping visible because it is what Anthony reached for and the reason it fails is not obvious: a folder is where things SIT, not who decides them. (d) ONE GRAPH FOR INTENT, SEPARATE GRAPHS FOR BUILD. Not previously considered: the shared thing across his projects is what he is trying to achieve, and the separate thing is what each repo ships. Counter: reflow2 has no vocabulary for a design that holds only intent and no build, and `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` is the closest thing — which is about a corpus, not a standing hub. (e) DO NOTHING; the constraint he wanted removed does not exist, and he can point `--graph-path` wherever he likes today. Counter: that answers the mechanism and ignores the question, which is what SHOULD be one design. WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED WHEN THIS IS PICKED UP: `dec:nested-graphs` and its four stated obligations (the coordinate, the roll-up, freshness, the seam), `dec:linked-repos-poc` and its dependency on `req:interface-spec-complete`, `req:design-composes` and `req:composed-analysis` (both accepted), and `cap:mirror-surface`/`cap:publish-surface`/`cap:composed-analysis` (all built). The LINKING half exists; the COMPARING half does not. NOT CHECKED, and it bears directly on (b): whether `mirror_surface` and `compose_and_analyse` have ever been run on two real designs. `dec:linked-repos-poc` is one of the two parked Decisions that `detect_defects` has been reporting as governing nothing all session, which suggests not.		Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request, and the search he asked for was run first — he said 'I know we've discussed linking projects in the past, so there should already be some discussion on this,' and he was right. Recording what already exists BEFORE recording the new question is the whole point of the exercise, and this project has spent a session establishing that the expensive failure is re-deriving what is written down. The premise correction is on the node rather than left in conversation because it is the most perishable part: 'the graph is limited to one git repo' is a reasonable thing to believe from the outside, it is false, and nothing in the repo says so plainly. If that correction lives only in a chat it will be believed again. Deliberately NOT registered as formal alternatives — that would make this a fork the loop starts asking him to choose between, which is exactly what a brainstorm should not do. Kept separate from dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs because that one asks what may cross a boundary and this one asks where the boundary is; one node holding both could only ever be half-answered.proposednothing
OPEN — is betweenness the right centrality, or should closeness / eigenvector / clustering also be read?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Recorded for completeness; this is the WEAKEST of the ideas in this batch and is written down mainly so a later session knows it was considered and not chosen. THE UNUSED FUNCTIONS: degree_centrality (with DegreeMode), closeness_centrality, eigenvector_centrality, and clustering (local clustering coefficient). All exact, all already available. WHAT EACH WOULD MEAN HERE: closeness = how near a node is to everything else, so 'how quickly does a change here reach the whole design'. Eigenvector = importance by association with important nodes. Clustering coefficient = how tightly a node's neighbourhood is interconnected, a possible signal for over-coupled subsystems. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, which is why this ranks last: betweenness is the RIGHT measure for the question reflow2 asks — how much of the golden thread routes THROUGH this node — and the others answer questions nobody has asked yet. Degree is already computed locally in structure.rs and needs no crate. Adding measures because they exist is how a report becomes a dashboard nobody reads, and reflow2 has an explicit instinct against that (dec:report-dont-judge, and BL-42's noise-floor lesson). IF ANY: clustering coefficient is the only one with a question attached that reflow2 does not already answer — 'is this subsystem more tangled inside than the design says it should be?' — and even that overlaps leiden communities.		Recorded deliberately as a considered-and-not-chosen idea. The brainstorm skill's rule is that roads not taken are part of the design's memory; without this node a later reviewer would rediscover four unused centrality functions and re-litigate them.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2's outward-facing docs be RENDERED from the graph by the agent, rather than hand-written prose that goes stale?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-11, in his words: 'reflow2 has a capability to return to the agent any systems engineering data (not view) and the agent can render it. would like to actually demonstrate this in the docs of these examples of different views of reflow2 using this rendering type construct.' Nothing here is intent. ⭐⭐ THIS IS ALREADY THE RECORDED DIRECTION, AND IT IS UNBUILT. `docs/viewpoints.md` §'Direction (the rest of BL-40)' says it almost exactly: 'once the catalogue's shape has settled here, move the projection data into core as typed read tools on the MCP surface (the `flow_report` shape — facts plus confessions — is the template), so the in-session agent renders views deterministically instead of re-deriving them through an LLM, which is exactly where extrapolation would creep back in.' Same shape as `req:what-next` last month — accepted intent, blocker unexamined, nobody built it. This is not a new idea to decide; it is an old idea to finish. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, measured 2026-08-11: typed report-shaped read tools on the MCP surface 15 (graph_report, flow_report, maturity_report, granularity_report, ility_report, readiness_report, evidence_report, coverage_report, seam_report, budget_report, release_report, confirmation_ledger, changelog_view, claim_report, graph_report_markdown) tools/render_views.py 44 KB, renders 10 DoDAF-informed viewpoints docs/design/views.html 323 KB of rendered output So the DATA side is largely built and the RENDER side exists as deterministic Python that writes one HTML file nobody links from the reading order. ⭐ THE EVIDENCE FOR DOING IT IS FROM TODAY, AND IT IS DAMNING. Every one of these is a hand-maintained claim ABOUT THE GRAPH that the graph could have answered: · `docs/overview.md:52` says the schema has 60 edge types. The export stamp says 61. · `docs/three-axes.md` says axis Z is 'MISSING'. The graph holds 111 DesignEpochs, 133 TemporalFacts, 114 Snapshots and 362 ChangeEvents. The doc that would tell a reader whether time is modelled says it is not. · 3 of 4 deferrals spot-checked in `requirements-coverage.md` were wrong (SP-3b, GS-17, 3AX-5). · `crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs:27-29` lists dead_end, disconnected_community and single_point_of_failure as deferred. All three are built. A rendered doc cannot make any of these mistakes, because it has no opinion of its own. ⚠️⚠️ THE CENTRAL RISK, and it is this project's own doctrine pointed at the proposal. `viewpoints.md` rule 1: 'A projection may sort, group, count and draw — it may not infer, default, or improvise.' An LLM's default behaviour IS to improvise, and Anthony's own standing position (UAF/DoDAF-trained: views must be pure projections; a renderer fill-in is a reflow2 defect) makes an improvised sentence in a rendered doc a DEFECT REPORT, not a cosmetic issue. The existing Python renderer cannot improvise by construction. Moving rendering to the agent trades staleness for extrapolation — and the doc's own Direction paragraph names that trade explicitly as the reason to move the DATA into typed tools first, so the agent has less room to invent. ⚠️ SECOND RISK: DETERMINISM AND THE DIFF. A committed file rendered by an LLM churns on every regeneration — different wording, same facts — so `git diff` stops meaning 'the design changed'. `render_views.py` is deterministic and byte-stable; an agent is not. ⚠️ THIRD, AND IT IS A JUDGEMENT CALL NOT A BUG: confessions become PUBLIC. Every renderer here is also a probe, and what it cannot project it confesses. Rendering the outward-facing docs means reflow2's adoption surface carries reflow2's own gaps to a first-time reader. `partnership.md` argues credibility is decided at the front door. A confessing doc reads either as unusually honest or as unfinished, and which one it is depends on the reader, not on us. IDEAS, unranked: (a) LIVE ONLY — the agent renders a view on demand from the typed tools; nothing is committed. Never stale by construction. Costs the browsable artifact: a stranger on GitHub sees no docs, and docs ARE the adoption surface. (b) COMMITTED + CHECKED — render into committed files and add a CI step that re-renders and diffs, so a stale doc fails the build. Turns doc staleness into a gate, which is the actual disease. Needs determinism, which argues for keeping the renderer deterministic (Python/Rust) rather than an LLM. (c) HYBRID — prose docs that EMBED rendered sections between markers, regenerated and diff-checked. Smallest change; keeps the argument-shaped docs intact and puts the facts under the gate. Every number that went stale today lives in an embeddable section. (d) DEMONSTRATION ONLY — pick two or three docs, render them as worked examples of the capability, leave the rest prose. This is closest to what Anthony literally asked for, and it is the cheapest way to find out whether the output is any good before committing the whole doc set to it. 📌 SEQUENCING FINDING, recorded because it changes what to do NEXT. Anthony asked in the same breath for `genesis.md`, `artifact-linking.md`, `impact-propagation.md`, `gap-surfacing.md` and `heal-process.md` to be rewritten as outward-facing prose. Those five describe what `genesis`, `link_artifact`/`reconcile_artifacts`, `propagate_from`, `detect_gaps` and `propose_heal` DO AND RETURN — which makes them the FIRST candidates to become projections, not prose. Hand-rewriting 661 lines into a format that may be replaced is the wasteful order. Deciding (d) first costs one doc's worth of work and tells you whether the other four should be written at all.		Four hand-maintained claims about the graph were found wrong in a single day, and every one was answerable from the graph. The data side is 15 typed tools already built and the direction is already recorded in viewpoints.md as the rest of BL-40. What is genuinely open is who renders — an LLM buys freshness and risks the extrapolation this project treats as a defect; deterministic code keeps the doctrine and keeps the diff meaningful.proposednothing
OPEN — the condition dec:ownership-reads-claims-before-adding-an-edge set has now been met: are CLAIMS shown insufficient, and does OWNED_BY become justified?
