RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. ⭐⭐ THE HEADLINE: AN ACCEPTED DECISION SET A CONDITION, AND THE CONDITION HAS NOW BEEN MET BY EXACTLY THE EVIDENCE IT ASKED FOR. dec:ownership-reads-claims-before-adding-an-edge (ACCEPTED, Anthony's word 2026-08-08) says: build the first cut from CLAIMS rather than a new edge, and \'DECIDE ON OWNED_BY ONLY AFTER THAT IS BUILT AND SHOWN TO BE INSUFFICIENT.\' Its rationale names the disqualifying evidence in advance: \'If claims turn out to model the wrong thing (THEY ARE TRANSIENT WORK-IN-HAND, WHILE OWNERSHIP IS DURABLE AND SURVIVES THE SESSION), that is a real distinction and the edge becomes justified on evidence rather than on anticipation.\' ONE DAY LATER, dev_storyflow filed precisely that distinction, and Anthony supplied the use case himself (2026-08-09, relayed by api-boss 05af57c1): \'As my brother and I collaborate on another project, there are areas of the design that are his and areas that are mine. This is probably a different 'ownership' of something than the claim_region type descriptor... it is probably DURABLE, SURVIVES EVERY SESSION, and SHOULD NEVER BE RELEASED.\' ⭐ THE FRAMING THAT MAKES IT LEGIBLE — reflow2 has two of the three WHO axes: AUTHORED_BY who WROTE this past tense · historical · never changes CLAIMS who is IN it RIGHT NOW transient · advisory · released at checkout ??? whose AREA this is durable · standing · never released WHY CLAIMS CANNOT BE STRETCHED TO COVER THE THIRD, which is the \'shown to be insufficient\' the accepted decision demanded, and it is operational rather than theoretical: claim_region's own description says ADVISORY and session-scoped; the parallel-work skill says release at checkout; on a shared server a claim reads `unknown` rather than `live` and NEVER EXPIRES ON ITS OWN. So standing ownership claims would permanently drown the tool's actual job — showing who is ACTIVELY in your ground. api-boss noted they hold one claim, released and re-took it once today purely to fix its note, and asked what three permanent graph-wide claims would do to that surface. ⚠️ AND THE FLEET RETRACTED ITS OWN COUNTER-ARGUMENT, which is worth more than the ask. They had argued that recording ownership in the graph duplicates their PROTOCOL.md ownership matrix and would rot the way six of their copied rules already have. Their retraction: \'That objection is specific to an organisation that ALREADY writes ownership down. A PAIR OF COLLABORATORS HAS NO MATRIX — the knowledge lives in their heads and in habit. For most projects the graph would be the FIRST place ownership was ever recorded, not the second, and the duplication risk is simply absent.\' They kept only the narrow fleet-specific form. ⭐ AND THE REFRAME THAT MATTERS MOST FOR SCOPE: every earlier version of this ask was framed around an AGENT FLEET, which invites the reply \'that is exotica\'. The two-person case is not exotica. It is two people splitting a design, which is the ORDINARY case of collaborative design work. === WHERE THIS SITS AGAINST WHAT SHIPPED TODAY === cap:owed-to-a-contributor shipped `loop_status(contributor_id)` on 2026-08-09. IT IS NOT THE FIRST CUT THAT ACCEPTED DECISION SPECIFIED: it attributes via the AUTHORED_BY `role=approver` edge, not via CLAIMS. That is already recorded honestly — the SATISFIES edge to req:ownership-is-an-edge-so-debt-has-an-addressee carries `coverage: partial` and says so: \'its chosen first cut answers 'what has a named person been asked to settle', not 'which gaps are in the part of the system I own'. The fleet's ask is the second one.\' ⇒ SO THE CLAIMS-BASED FIRST CUT WAS NEVER BUILT, and the question is whether it still should be. Two readings, both honest: (a) The decision's build order stands: build the claims-based cut, THEN judge. The insufficiency argument above is about claims as a DURABLE record, and a claims-scoped debt report might still be useful for its actual purpose without ever being ownership. (b) The insufficiency is already established by inspection — claims are advisory, session-scoped and released by doctrine, so building a durable ownership view on them would be building on a foundation whose own description forbids it. Under this reading the condition is met and the edge is justified now. AND IT FITS WHAT SHIPPED: loop_status's scoped answer deliberately attributes ONLY assignment and reports everything else under `scope.not_attributable`. AN OWNED_BY EDGE IS EXACTLY WHAT WOULD LET THE REST BECOME ATTRIBUTABLE. The restraint shipped today is waiting for this. === THE SHAPES, with counters beside rather than argued down === (A) AN OWNED_BY / ACCOUNTABILITY EDGE — Contributor → any node, explicitly NOT in the decomposition spine and NOT a traceability edge. THE PRECEDENT EXISTS TWICE: AUTHORED_BY and CLAIMS are both already deliberately excluded from impact propagation (nodes.rs structural_rule), so this would be the third of a kind rather than a novelty. COUNTER, and it is this project's own: dec:ownership-reads-claims-before-adding-an-edge warns that adding an edge type is the most expensive and least reversible change to this schema, and today's measurement found EIGHT of sixty edge types declared and reached by nothing. An unused OWNED_BY would not be a novel failure here; it is the common one. (B) REUSE CLAIMS WITH A DURABILITY FLAG — a `durable: true` property that exempts a claim from release and from the overlap report. Cheapest, no new edge type. COUNTER: it makes one edge mean two things whose lifecycles are opposite, and the tool's descriptions would have to say both. That is how a vocabulary rots — the same sentence dec:one-retire-edge uses about two words for one relationship, running the other way. (C) OWNERSHIP AS A PROPERTY ON THE NODE — an `owner` field. Cheapest of all to read. COUNTER: it cannot express shared or partial ownership, cannot carry a note about WHAT is owned, and puts a person's id inside design content where every export and every merge has to reconcile it. ⚠️ THE HARD PART, WHICH IS A DESIGN INPUT RATHER THAN A SETTING, and it comes from the fleet: WHICH NODE TYPES ARE OWNABLE? In their 1,127-node graph most nodes legitimately have no owner — \'a Constraint about prose rendering is nobody's in the accountability sense\' — so a naive detector fires on the majority and becomes a signal trained to be ignored. In a two-person project the design is probably mostly partitioned. ⇒ OWNABILITY LOOKS LIKE A PER-PROJECT DECLARATION, NOT A FIXED RULE, and the same feature behaves very differently at those two scales. NOTHING IS PROMOTED. The accepted decision's condition may now be met; saying so is Anthony's to do, and dec:reopen-supersedes says a re-opening mints its own node rather than un-accepting the old one.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill: `proposed`, options with counters, nothing promoted. Kept SEPARATE from dec:ownership-reads-claims-before-adding-an-edge rather than editing it, because that decision is ACCEPTED and dec:reopen-supersedes is explicit that a re-opening mints a new Decision which obsoletes the old one — the accepted one is never un-accepted. This node is the evidence arriving that its own condition named; whether that closes it is Anthony's call. Separated from the ownership-orphan detector question (dec:idea-detect-ownership-orphans) because the edge could exist without the detector and the detector cannot exist without the edge — one node holding both could only be half-answered.proposednothing
OPEN — does collaborating on a shared server cost the self-contained package, or does it only flip which way the default points?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-05, closing the session and naming a tension he has been circling all day: 'The initial vision was, using a house as the delivered product, was that when you gave the house to somebody else, they would also get all the blueprints and design decisions (this would be the reflow2 graph). This would all come in a nice package that anybody else could take from there and see why you made the decisions you made and take it from there. In a code based project, your repo = implemented code + reflow graph object + other artifacts in a reflow blob storage. This would all come in one nice and complete package. However, in retrospec, this could have been done differently. The discussion earlier is more about collaboration and using multiple graphs, which somewhat break this wholistic/complete package that I had originally developed. Theoretically, there is no reason that you couldn't create a common/shared server that hosts the reflow2 mcp and everybody in the organization could access it. Not only that, a project could just point to the graph_id (or multiple graph_ids) and everybody could work collaboratively. Additionally, if people were assigned subsections of a big project, they could just point their .mcp.json at the master graph in their project and take on their subsection. So I guess what I'm stating is that to increase collaboration, we may have to remove the 'nicely wholistic combined package' that I had originally developed.' ⭐ FIRST, MEASURED: BOTH HALVES ARE ALREADY ACCEPTED REQUIREMENTS, AND THE SHARED SERVER IS ALREADY BUILT. - `req:persistence` (ACCEPTED) — 'The design persists in-repo alongside the code.' The package. - `req:design-reachable-without-the-repo` (ACCEPTED) — 'Someone without the repo can reach a design, read it, and contribute to it.' The collaboration. - `req:content-reaches-every-seat` (ACCEPTED) — 'a pointer resolves for everyone holding the design, not only for the seat that stored it.' - `dec:central-host` — ACCEPTED (its NAME still reads 'OPEN — does reflow2 gain a hosted surface…', which is stale in the same way `dec:skills-served`'s was; worth a rename, not a re-decision). - AND `--http` SHIPS TODAY: `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/main.rs` carries `--http`, `--http-allow-host` and `serve_http`, and its own comment says '`--http` already lets several sessions share one design, and it works.' So this is not a road not taken. The design committed to BOTH and the transport exists. ⭐⭐ SECOND, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: THE DICHOTOMY IS FALSE, BECAUSE THE PACKAGE AND THE WORKING MEDIUM WERE NEVER THE SAME ARTIFACT. The live store (`.reflow2/graph`) is GIT-IGNORED and always has been. What ships in the repo is `docs/design/reflow2.json` — the deterministic, self-contained, mergeable EXPORT. The house-with-blueprints has always been the export, never the store. So collaborating on a shared store does not touch the package: the package is what you export FROM it. ⚠️ THIRD, AND THIS IS WHERE HIS INSTINCT IS RIGHT AFTER ALL. The loss is real, and it is a DEFAULT rather than a capability: - With a per-repo store, the design is IN the repo by default and you must work to lose it. - With a shared server, the design is OUT of the repo by default and you must work to KEEP it. That flip is the actual cost of collaboration, and it is not fixed by having an export format — it is fixed by something making the export happen. Which is why (BL-215) is the same finding from the other end: the hxm_program session found `.reflow2` git-ignored, and every captured decision had to be HAND-COPIED into markdown for teammates, 'double bookkeeping, and only the prose copy is shared.' That team already lost the package, on a per-repo store, with no shared server involved — because nothing told the project to commit its export. OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) KEEP THE PER-REPO STORE AS THE DEFAULT and treat the shared server as the exception — today's shape. Counter: it is the shape that produced three stores on one repo and prose cross-references, and it makes the collaboration requirement something you configure your way into, which `reflow2_init.py`'s own comment already argues against for `--shared` ('a capability you have to reconfigure your way into is one most users never reach'). (b) SHARED SERVER AS THE DEFAULT, EXPORT AS THE DELIVERABLE — collaboration is normal, and committing the export becomes an explicit, prompted, possibly gated act. Counter: the export is only as fresh as the last person who ran it, so the package's completeness becomes a discipline rather than a property, and a stale export is a COMPLETE document that merges cleanly and silently drops work (`req:stale-seat-knows` names exactly this). (c) BOTH, WITH THE EXPORT AUTOMATED — a session-end hook or a CI job keeps the committed export fresh, so the package survives whichever medium the work happens in. Cheapest thing that preserves both accepted requirements, and it is (BL-215)'s own suggestion. Counter: nobody has said what happens when the automated export and a human's differ, and an export that writes itself is one more thing that can silently break. (d) THE PACKAGE IS THE POINT AND COLLABORATION SHOULD BEND TO IT — keep everything per-repo and solve sharing by merging exports, as `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (ACCEPTED) already says: 'Many writers keep the repo file and merge on pull — no hosted service.' Counter: that decision predates the field evidence, and one person on one machine already ended up with three stores and a markdown side-channel under it. WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED: `--http` exists and works; `req:persistence` and `req:design-reachable-without-the-repo` are BOTH accepted; the live store is git-ignored and the export is the shipped artifact; `dec:multi-writer-architecture` chose merge-on-pull over a hosted service and has not been revisited since the field reports; and `dec:central-host` is accepted despite a name that still says OPEN. NOT CHECKED, and it bears on (b) and (c): whether a shared `--http` server can serve SEVERAL graph_ids at once, or is bound to one like the stdio server is. `dec:idea-many-graphs-one-store` measured that `with_graph_id` is free and the store namespaces by id, but nobody has looked at what the HTTP path does with that.		Captured at Anthony's request as the session's closing thought, and the mechanical half was checked first — which changed the answer twice. He believed he was describing a road not taken; both halves are accepted requirements and the transport ships. He believed collaboration would cost the package; the package is the export and was never the working store. What survives his concern, and is recorded as the load-bearing sentence, is the DEFAULT flip: per-repo you must work to lose the design, shared you must work to keep it. That is a real cost, it is not an architectural one, and it is already being paid on a per-repo store by the team in (BL-215) — which is the strongest evidence that the threat was never the shared server. Deliberately not registered as alternatives, so the loop does not start asking him to choose. He asked for this to be the last activity of the session and to keep nothing promoted; four options with their counters is the state he asked for.proposedreflow2 is consumable as a pinned, versioned container image, so a consumer needs no Rust toolchain and reflow2 needs no knowledge of their deploy
IDEA — reflow2 models who holds what and whether you are behind the record, but gives one seat no way to SAY anything to another. The most valuable work a three-boss fleet did in a day travelled over a markdown file reflow2 cannot see.
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Filed by dev_storyflow's dragon Boss (`853732df`) on 2026-08-15 AT ANTHONY'S EXPLICIT DIRECTION, and his framing is the better one: 'if reflow2 is going to work in an environment where multiple sessions are running simultaneously (on the same computer here, but could also be across several machines), may need to make cross-talk an enduring part of reflow2 — maybe not use B.md, but some way for sessions to collaborate cleanly.' DISTINCT FROM THE TWO NEIGHBOURS THE GUARD WOULD NAME. `dec:idea-the-loop-only-sees-what-an-agent-hand-carries` asks whether the loop should SUBSCRIBE TO REALITY — CI, telemetry, the outside world. `dec:idea-agent-to-agent-feedback-is-a-formal-channel` asks whether an agent should write a REPORT for another agent to read later. THIS is neither: it is seat-to-seat exchange DURING work, where the value is in the minutes rather than the record. ⭐ THE OBSERVATION, STATED SO IT IS NOT READ AS 'ADD CHAT': reflow2's multi-seat STATE model is unusually good and they list it — `mint_seat`, `claim_region`/`release_claim`/`claim_report` (advisory, seat-stamped, liveness computable), `OWNED_BY` for durable ground against `CLAIMS` for transient holding, `sync_status`, `arrival_delta`, `compare_designs`, and the whole pairing family. WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT STATE, IT IS EVENTS. The graph can say who holds what and whether you are behind the record. It has no way for one seat to SAY something to another, and no way for a seat to be TOLD. ⭐⭐ THE SHARPEST FORM, and it is an argument from reflow2's own surface rather than from their inconvenience: THE TOOLS KEEP HANDING OFF TO A CONVERSATION THEY CANNOT HOST. `sync_status`'s own description declines to answer 'what will I publish that is not mine'. `export_graph` publishes every attached seat's in-flight work. `add_decision` refuses a near-match and asks a human to judge it. `acknowledge_defect` demands a reason a person must supply. Every one of those ends by requiring a human exchange, and none of them can carry it. WHAT THEY MEASURED, and it is the part that makes this more than a wish — nine exchanges in ONE day, three bosses, no workers, each producing something no single seat could: · A PEER CORRECTED A PRESCRIPTION WITHIN THE HOUR — one seat's retrofit was replaced by another's prevention, and 'a maintainer reading ⑨ alone would have built the weaker fix'. · A WARNING ARRIVED BEFORE THE DAMAGE: a peer was about to mint 25 Verifications across two graphs and replied 'your warning arrived before I minted a single Verification'. Hours apart it is a retrofit; minutes apart it is free. · A PEER'S ONE-LINE CHECK RETIRED MOST OF A FEATURE REQUEST — `set_decision_status` already takes `rejected`, so a claimed missing feature was a DISCOVERABILITY failure, and the fix collapsed from a schema change to one sentence in two skills. ⭐ CROSS-TALK STOPPED A WRONG FEATURE REQUEST FROM REACHING THE MAINTAINER, which is a saving in reflow2's own backlog. · THREE SEATS INDEPENDENTLY HIT ONE MISSING CONCEPT from three unrelated directions — 'deliberately out of scope', 'proposed and refuted', 'deferred with a promotion trigger'. One hole, not three requests, AND THE CORROBORATION IS THE EVIDENCE: any one of them filed alone reads as an edge case. · A PEER'S FINDING MADE A SEAT RE-AUDIT WORK IT WOULD NEVER HAVE RE-OPENED, producing a defence now stated explicitly: after any `distinct_from`, run a same-type `search_design` yourself, because the guard's silence is not the check. · ONE HAZARD CAUGHT FROM ALL THREE DIRECTIONS IN A DAY — the `--shared` export cross-carry, caught receiving, caught writing, and caught pre-emptively — turning a written rule into observed practice. THE OPTIONS: (a) DO NOTHING; THE FLEET'S OWN FILE IS THE ANSWER. B.md works, and it is theirs to shape. CHEAPEST and it respects that not everything belongs in the tool. COUNTER: every boss hand-rolled a 20-second `awk` poller, reflow2 is blind to the most valuable output of the day, and Anthony has now asked twice for cross-talk to be an enduring part of it. (b) A MESSAGE OR EVENT LAYER IN THE GRAPH — seats post, seats read, delivery is recorded. Most direct reading of the ask. COUNTER, and it is severe: the graph is a DESIGN record, and a design brain that becomes a chat log acquires an unbounded write volume with no coherence meaning. `dec:defects-are-temporal-facts` was accepted partly because it added NO new node type; this would add a whole axis. (c) MAKE THE HAND-OFFS FIRST-CLASS RATHER THAN BUILDING A CHANNEL — the tools already know the exact moments a human exchange is needed, and `open_questions` already models 'somebody was asked and has not answered' for the gap→user case. Extending that shape to seat→seat is narrow, uses vocabulary that exists, and carries only exchanges the design cares about. COUNTER: it would not have carried six of their nine examples, which were warnings and corrections nothing in the design had asked for. (d) NOTIFICATION WITHOUT CONTENT — a seat can learn that another seat wrote in its claimed region, and go look. Cheap, uses `CLAIMS` and `sync_status` machinery that exists, and adds no message store. COUNTER: it delivers the least valuable half; their examples were about MEANING ('this remedy is already possible'), not about the fact that a write happened. ⚠️ THE BOUND THEY STATE THEMSELVES, and it should survive: 'I did not exercise the claim family this session, so I am describing the surface, not testing it.' The state model is being praised from its documentation rather than from use. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether cross-machine is in scope (Anthony raises it, nothing measures it); whether a channel would be used by a SOLO user, who is still the common case; and whether any of this belongs in reflow2 rather than in the harness that runs the seats.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Kept distinct from the subscribe-to-reality and agent-to-agent-report questions after reading both: this one is about exchange DURING work between seats on one design, where their measured value was in minutes rather than in the record. The nine examples are summarised rather than quoted whole because the corroboration pattern — three seats reaching one hole from three directions — is the evidence, and it is invisible in any single one of them.proposednothing
OPEN — `req:design-anything` is accepted and the DELIVERY is still software-shaped; what closes the gap between a neutral vocabulary and a toolchain full of code?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14. HIS WORDS: *'I don't think it should be focused on a specific topic like software engineering as I'd like to use it for other projects like my shop.'* 🛑 THE INTENT IS ALREADY ACCEPTED, SO THIS IS NOT A NEW REQUIREMENT. `req:design-anything` (ACCEPTED): *'Software, hardware, a document, a process — the vocabulary stays neutral.'* What Alex hit is not the vocabulary — it is EVERYTHING WRAPPED AROUND IT. The served instructions and skills assume a codebase throughout: Artifacts are source files with checksums, `link-artifacts` opens on *'Unity C#, a spec, a doc'*, `ci-gate` is a build gate, the loop's step 3 is *'build only what the graph specifies'*, and his own example — how database migrations are performed — is the one part of his note that IS software. **The nouns are neutral and the worked examples, defaults and skills are not.** ⭐ SO THE HONEST STATEMENT OF THE GAP: reflow2 can MODEL a shop today, and nothing in what a shop owner would actually read shows them how. That is a delivery problem, and it is the same shape as two findings already on the record — `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue`, and the installer wording Alex himself caught, where the information existed somewhere the person was not. ✅ TWO MEASURED FACTS THE OPTIONS HAVE TO LIVE WITH: · `Project.domain` IS WRITTEN AND NEVER READ (`req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted`). The field that would carry 'this is a shop, not a service' already exists and drives nothing. · The Environment / EnvironmentRule compliance layer was DESIGNED IN FULL AND NEVER BUILT, and `dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built` says in as many words that it *'is what makes 'design a house' concrete'*. The non-software story has a designed, unbuilt half already sitting in the graph. OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) NOTHING TO DO — the requirement is accepted and the vocabulary is neutral; a competent agent adapts. Counter: the second user, holding the tool, concluded the opposite from what he actually saw. (b) ONE WORKED NON-SOFTWARE EXAMPLE end to end — his shop is the obvious candidate and he is volunteering to be the test case. Cheapest thing that would have prevented his impression, and it produces evidence rather than assertion. (c) MAKE `Project.domain` READ — let it select examples and defaults. **This is the option the design's own rules already point at:** `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` says a distinction no computation reads should be removed or made real, and `domain` is currently the former. (d) BUILD THE ENVIRONMENT COMPLIANCE LAYER, on the grounds that regulation and physical context are what non-software design mostly IS. Largest, and it has its own open decision already. (e) SAY IT PLAINLY IN THE DOCS — reflow2 is software-first today, other domains work but are untravelled. Costs nothing, makes no promise it cannot keep, and is the only option that stays honest whichever of the others is chosen. 📌 WORTH KNOWING WHO IS ASKING: this is the third distinct thread where Alex's use diverges from Anthony's, and his projects are the only non-reflow2, non-flo2 evidence the design has. `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` — which ALEX HIMSELF ASKED FOR — is the mechanism that would stop each of these arriving as a relayed email.		Captured under the brainstorm skill. Recorded as an open question rather than as a requirement precisely BECAUSE the requirement already exists and is accepted: the useful question is not 'should reflow2 design anything' (settled, yes) but 'what is still software-shaped after that was settled', and framing it the first way would have produced a duplicate of `req:design-anything` and lost Alex's actual point.proposednothing
OPEN — should a blast radius rank by relevance TO THE CHANGE rather than by global importance?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from a review of what dynograph-foundation offers that reflow2 does not yet use (2026-08-01, at Anthony's request). Nothing here is settled. THE OBSERVATION: propagate.rs:389 ranks impacted nodes by GLOBAL betweenness centrality — `design_network()?.betweenness()`. That answers 'is this node generally important in the design?', which is not the same question as 'is this node relevant to the change I just made?'. IP-9's stated intent is the second one. THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::personalized_pagerank (already a dependency, unused) is random-walk-with-restart — the teleport mass returns to a SEED SET instead of spreading uniformly, so scores measure relevance to those seeds. Seeding it on the change's own seed nodes gives exactly the missing question. CHEAP: the crate is already pinned, the function is exact on graphs this size, and propagate already builds the network. Small. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is a real one: betweenness is not wrong, it is answering a different and also-useful question. The existing doc comment defends it — 'a change landing on a high-betweenness node has a wider SECONDARY blast radius' — which is about onward propagation, not relevance. So this may be an ADDITION rather than a replacement, and two ranking columns may be worse for a reader than one. Whether a reader wants both, or one, or a blend, is undecided and is the actual open question. Filed as a backlog row on Anthony's word (2026-08-01) — the work is tracked; this Decision records that the SHAPE is still open.		Surfaced by comparing reflow2's actual imports against dynograph-graph's exports: 8 of 17 are used. This was the strongest of the unused ones because it lands on the most-read output in the system and the mismatch between the question asked and the question answered is documented in reflow2's own doc comment.proposednothing
OPEN — how should 'what is left to build?' be answered, given the artifact layer is modelled at COMPONENT granularity and therefore cannot answer it at all?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From item 1 of the Grok 4.6 agent feedback (2026-08-13), verified on reflow2's own export at `c18a4a1` on 2026-08-14. ⚠️ **SUBORDINATE TO `dec:idea-silence-is-reported-not-inferred`.** Anthony asked for this node AND for a step back, on the ground that patching one blind spot with one detector is how a tool overfits. **The narrow options below are only safe to take if they do not become the third instance of that pattern** — which is why (a), the obvious fix, is measured and argued against here. THE MEASURED STATE (`fact:the-build-list-is-suppressed-by-realized-via-component`): `what_next` returns Decisions only — 12 of 12. `arrival_delta` needs a Release/Epoch `target_id`. 43 live planned capabilities and 9 accepted-undelivered requirements appear in no tool's answer. `unrealized_capability` fires 3 times against them, 34 of 39 silenced by `realized_via_component`. ═══ ⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT DECIDES THE SHAPE: THE ARTIFACT LAYER CANNOT ANSWER THIS ═══ **81 of 161 capabilities have no artifact of their own.** That is not neglect — reflow2 models artifacts at COMPONENT granularity, so a capability is realized *via* the component that carries the code. `realized_via_component` is not a hack; **it encodes the modelling convention the design actually uses.** ⇒ **THEREFORE 'WHICH CAPABILITY LACKS AN ARTIFACT' IS NOT A MEANINGFUL QUESTION IN THIS DESIGN, AND NO REPAIR OF THE DETECTOR MAKES IT ONE.** The build list has to be computed from `Capability.status` and the golden thread — the things that DO carry per-capability truth — not from artifact presence. That is the load-bearing conclusion, and it removes the most tempting option rather than adding one. ═══ THE OPTIONS, WITH MEASURED COSTS ═══ (a) **FIX THE GUARD** so `realized_via_component` no longer inherits the component's artifacts. 🛑 **MEASURED COST: `unrealized_capability` goes from ~3 to ~81 gaps** — a 27× increase, every one of them firing on correct modelling. This is precisely BL-42's original failure returning at scale (*'13 of 51 gaps, every one produced by following the adopt skill's own instruction'*), and BL-5's recorded lesson says a loud detector needs a different QUESTION, not a tuned number. **Argued against on this node's own evidence.** (b) ⭐ **A REMAINING-WORK VIEW over data already held** — accepted/scheduled Requirements and Capabilities that are not computed-delivered, excluding `dropped`/`deferred`/discontinued and acknowledged-gap targets. The Grok report's own proposal, and a *sibling of `what_next`, not a replacement*. Cost: a new surface to maintain. Benefit: **adds no new judgement to the instrument** — it reads `status` and the golden thread, both of which already exist — so it cannot overfit a detector, and it answers the audience half (`dec:idea-silence-is-reported-not-inferred`: the loop and the delivery plan should not share a dashboard). ⚠️ It inherits the drift the Grok report names separately: `status` is ASSERTED while delivery is COMPUTED, and the two disagree. A view that reads `status` will be as stale as the statuses are. (c) **REPORT THE SUPPRESSION** — *'34 capabilities not asked about: their component already has an artifact.'* Generalises beyond this case; it is option (a) of the parent node. Cost: a convention every detector must honour. Benefit: the only option that makes the NEXT blind spot visible instead of the current one. (d) **SCHEDULE THE WORK, SO `arrival_delta` ANSWERS IT.** The machinery exists and is already the designed home for this. 🛑 **MEASURED: 23 `SCHEDULED_FOR` edges across 122 epochs and 31 releases.** The scheduling layer is built and effectively unused, so today this option answers almost nothing — and the Grok report hit exactly that, with its remaining-work list living as prose on an accepted Decision. Their item 9 proposes a detector for that shape (*an accepted Decision whose statement is a running delivery list with no `SCHEDULED_FOR` edges*). **Not free: it asks users to schedule before they can be told what is unbuilt.** (e) **NOTHING.** Counter: three agents in three weeks have now gone outside the graph to answer this. 📌 (b), (c) and (d) COMPOSE and are not rivals: (d) makes the plan structural, (b) reads it back for the person who asked, (c) says what neither could see. **(a) is the only one that has to be chosen against.**		Captured under the brainstorm skill, with each option's cost measured on reflow2's own export rather than estimated, because Anthony's stated worry was that a narrow fix creates the next problem and that worry cannot be settled by argument alone. The measurement changed the answer: the obvious repair — making the unrealized-capability detector honest at capability granularity — would raise gaps 27-fold against a modelling convention that is correct, so the artifact layer is the wrong source for this question entirely. Recorded as subordinate to `dec:idea-silence-is-reported-not-inferred` rather than as a standalone fix so that a future session cannot take the narrow option without meeting the general question first.proposednothing
OPEN — should a retrospective review ASK its questions or COMPUTE them, and is it ever allowed to grade?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised 2026-08-04 alongside dec:idea-retrospective-review-skill, of which this is the shape question rather than the whether question. THE FORK. OPTION A — A QUESTION LIST. The skill carries Anthony's sixteen questions as prose and the agent answers them by reading the design and the code. Cheap to build, works on day one, works on any project regardless of what the graph holds, and is what a human reviewer actually does. The objection is precise and comes from reflow2's own record: BL-179 settled that reflow2 does not encode a good practice as a detector, because Anthony objected that 'avoid monoliths' is 'kind of a subjective ask' — and the resolution was that reflow2 reports where two records the design ALREADY HOLDS disagree and rules on neither side. Sixteen prose questions answered by an agent is subjective grading with a checklist in front of it, and the answers would vary by model, by session, and by how much of the codebase happened to fit in context. OPTION B — EVERY QUESTION BACKED BY A COMPUTATION. Each question maps to a reading that already exists or is buildable over records the graph holds, and any question with no such reading reports NOT INFORMED with the reason instead of inviting an opinion. This is exactly ility_report's discipline (BL-184) turned into a skill, and the mapping is largely already there: 'too joined together' is modularity, misplaced capabilities and god-components; 'did the build separate what the design distinguishes' is granularity_report; 'what did we leave until last' is maturity_report's frontier; 'what happens if a key part breaks' is articulation points and single points of failure; 'can others read and change this' is partly coverage_report and the unregistered regions. The cost is that Anthony's speed-and-efficiency group and most of his security group have NO computation behind them today and would honestly report NOT INFORMED — which looks like a weaker skill and is a more honest one. OPTION C — THE CENSUS SHAPE, which is what actually produced BL-198..BL-203 and is neither A nor B. It asks nothing and grades nothing: it diffs artifacts the project maintains SEPARATELY and expects to agree — the schema against the graph against the tool surface, and the practice the skills PRESCRIBE against the practice the graph FOLLOWS. It surfaces disagreements and leaves every verdict to the human, which is precisely the BL-179 resolution generalised beyond detectors. Its limit is equally precise: it can only find a disagreement between two records that BOTH EXIST, so it is blind to anything nobody wrote down, and it says nothing about Anthony's speed, security or bad-input groups at all. AN HONEST OBSERVATION ABOUT THE THREE: they are not exclusive, and the census is the only one of them with evidence behind it today — six rows in one sitting, one of which (BL-199) explained a hard blocker that eleven releases of green instruments had missed. A plausible synthesis is C as the engine, B as the reporting discipline, and A kept only as the part a human is asked, never the part an agent answers. Nobody has chosen. NOT ASKED HERE, AND IT MAY MATTER MORE THAN THE FORK: whether a retrospective is worth anything when run by the same agent that built the thing. The census was, and its blind spot was real — BL-199 was found by a mechanical three-way diff, not by the agent noticing it had done something wrong.		Kept separate from dec:idea-retrospective-review-skill because one node holding two unrelated questions can never be answered, only half-answered. That node asks whether the skill should exist; this one asks what it would have to be to survive reflow2's own rule against subjective grading. Not registered as formal alternatives: registering them would make this a fork with a design behind each branch and start the loop asking Anthony to choose, which is exactly what a brainstorm should not do.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 serve a retrospective design-review skill?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-04, after the 'did we build this right?' census (docs/built-right-review.md, sourcing BL-198..BL-203): 'this exercise of retrospective design choices I think should be a skill within reflow2. This exercise of the agent being able to see the design in the current state and say, 'you know what, we could have done this better' is a good thing... I'm not sure, but being retrospective in analyzing what you've done is probably a good thing.' THE IDEA: a served skill that reads a design in its CURRENT state and reports where it would have been built differently — the counterpart to check-health (which asks how the design is SHAPED) and detect-and-ask (which asks what the design MEANS). HIS CANDIDATE QUESTION LIST, in his own words, four groups: STRUCTURE AND SETUP — did I use the right layout or pattern; is the setup easy to understand; can other people read and change this easily; did I keep things too joined together, or are they separate. SPEED AND EFFICIENCY — does this use too much time, space or power; where is the main slowdown or bottleneck; can I do tasks at the same time to speed things up; did I save data or results I do not need to keep. WEAK POINTS AND RISKS — what happens if a key part breaks right now; did I handle bad inputs or errors safely; where is the system likely to slow down or crash under heavy use; is private data or system access safe from outside threats. FUTURE CHANGES — how hard is it to add new features later; will this break if the size or user count grows ten times bigger; did I leave clear notes or guides for the next person. WHAT ARGUES FOR IT: the census that prompted this produced six backlog rows in one sitting, including BL-199, which explained why BL-176 had been invisible to self-host for eleven releases — so the exercise demonstrably finds things no existing instrument found. Several of his groups already have computations that exist and are not gathered anywhere: modularity and misplaced capabilities and god-components answer 'too joined together'; granularity_report answers 'did the build separate what the design distinguishes'; maturity_report's frontier answers 'what did we leave until last'; ility_report already maps findings onto quality axes and reports NOT INFORMED where nothing computes. WHAT ARGUES AGAINST IT, recorded beside the idea rather than used to kill it: reflow2 has one hard-won rule against exactly this shape — BL-179, where Anthony himself objected that 'avoid monoliths' is 'kind of a subjective ask', and the resolution was that reflow2 does not detect monoliths, it detects that two records the design ALREADY HOLDS disagree, and RULES ON NEITHER SIDE. A skill that asks sixteen questions in prose and lets an agent answer them would reintroduce precisely the subjective grading that ruling removed. The strongest form of the idea is therefore the one where every question is backed by a computation over records the design already holds, and any question with no such computation says NOT INFORMED rather than inviting an opinion — which is ility_report's discipline applied to a skill. That is a separate open question and is recorded as dec:idea-retrospective-asks-or-computes. ALSO OPEN, NOT ASKED HERE: whether the reviewer should be the same agent that built the thing (the census was, and its blind spot was real — it took a mechanical three-way diff, not judgement, to find BL-199).		Recorded so the idea is not lost while it is still an idea. Nothing here is intent: no Requirement, no Capability, and no claim that reflow2 will build this. The counter-argument is recorded beside the idea rather than used against it, per the brainstorm skill — an idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning.proposednothing
OPEN — should adopt be run on reflow2 itself, on a copy, as the one available GROUND-TRUTH test of what adopt recovers?
UNDECIDED — RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's hypothetical, 2026-08-16: 'this is a hypothetical question, not a go do this (yet).' DISTINCT FROM THE TWO THE GUARD NAMED, both read. `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` is ACCEPTED and settles WHAT reflow2's decomposition is; this is the OPEN question of whether to run the experiment that decision PLANNED. `dec:idea-should-reflow2s-own-design-be-re-derived-through-a-principled-se-process` asks whether to DECLARE the missing contracts by hand; this asks whether to RECOVER them mechanically and, more importantly, what running adopt would MEASURE about adopt. Three different acts. ⚠️ THE EXPERIMENT WAS ALREADY PLANNED AND NEVER RUN, and how it was recorded is itself the finding. `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` names two follow-ons IN ITS RATIONALE — **BL-83b** ('the retired crate view is recovered by adopt-on-a-copy') and **BL-83c** ('the divergence measured by `compare_designs`'). Neither appears anywhere else; there is no second design on disk. A plan reflow2 made for itself in July 2026 is reachable only by reading the reasoning of a decision about something else. THAT IS HOW I MISSED THE FUNCTIONAL DECOMPOSITION TWICE THE SAME DAY. This node exists partly so BL-83b stops being unfindable. WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY PREDICTS, verbatim: 'A functional carving comes from the product's purpose (a genesis input), not the code, and cuts across crate boundaries, SO ADOPT ON THE CODE CAN ONLY RE-DERIVE THE MODULE VIEW.' An adopt pass would reconstruct something close to the `reflow2-core` / `reflow2-mcp` / kit grouping — precisely the view retired in July. ⛔ IN PLACE IT WOULD BE DESTRUCTIVE, which makes 'on a copy' non-negotiable rather than tidy. Adopt instructs 'build one export document and `import_graph` it once'. Importing into a live 2,404-node graph MERGES: `cmp:*` ids collide, recovered module parents overwrite the functional ones, and a property once written cannot be removed. One-way door. ADOPT'S PREMISE ALSO DOES NOT HOLD: it is for a system 'with little or no requirements documentation', and reflow2 has 175 Requirements and 389 Decisions. Its central discipline — 'never infer a Requirement from the implementation that satisfies it' — means every requirement it recovered would be satisfied by construction, strictly WORSE than the authored ones present. ⭐ BUT ADOPT IS GOOD AT EXACTLY WHAT REFLOW2 LACKS. Phase 1 insists on 'both sides of every contract — this is where the structural findings come from'. That is the 73 coupled pairs with ZERO declared interfaces. Recovering contracts from imports and calls is what adopt's scan is FOR. ⭐⭐ THE ARGUMENT THAT MAKES IT WORTH DOING, and it is not self-hosting theatre: IT WOULD BE A GROUND-TRUTH TEST OF ADOPT ITSELF. Every adopt trial so far ran against a system whose true design nobody knew. reflow2 is the ONE system where the answer is known and recorded. `compare_designs` exists; `dec:design-diff-vocabulary` makes the comparison directional and banded. No other trial can ask 'how far is the recovered model from a design we know is right?' A FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION, recorded so the experiment can disconfirm it rather than be narrated afterwards: HIGH structural agreement (modules and couplings are visible in the code), NEAR-ZERO functional agreement (the eight boxes are not in the file tree), and a RECOVERED CONTRACT SET reflow2's own graph does not have. The third is the prize; the second would be a real finding about adopt's limits on functionally-carved systems. THE OPTIONS: (a) do not run it — the outcome is largely predicted and the cost is real; (b) run on a copy purely to harvest recovered contracts, discarding the rest; (c) run on a copy and MEASURE divergence with `compare_designs` — BL-83b plus BL-83c as planned; (d) run it and publish the comparison as the demonstration. ⚠️ PRECONDITION FOR (b)–(d): the copy must carry a DISTINCT `graph_id`, or the sync machinery treats two designs as one — a trap already recorded from the flo2 work. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether recovered contracts would be USABLE as-is or would need the same human judgement declaring them by hand needs. If the latter, (b)'s value collapses and only (c)'s measurement survives.		Recorded as brainstorming on Anthony's hypothetical, 2026-08-16, at his instruction to capture it. His question; the measurements, the prediction and the destructiveness analysis are mine. Kept at `proposed` rather than promoted, because he framed it explicitly as a hypothetical and not as intent. Its sibling is `dec:idea-genesis-reflow3-from-the-requirements-alone`.proposednothing
IDEA — scoped detection is BUILT and a real session still could not ask 'is this one Capability still in a gap?'. Should scope filter by relevance rather than by reachability, and should loop_status get a session mode?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Two of Alex's Opportunities, 2026-08-14 (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md), kept together because they are one question asked of two tools — and separable if the answer differs. HIS WORDS. On detect_gaps: 'Scoped `detect_gaps`: filter to gaps whose `affected_ids` include the seed (or its SATISFIES/REALIZES neighbors), and do not raise `unverified_capability` for `planned` + zero artifacts.' On loop_status: '`loop_status` session mode: 'building this Capability' hides unsurfaced project-wide gaps unless they touch the seed.' ⭐ THE SHARPENING, AND IT CHANGES THE QUESTION: SCOPING IS NOT MISSING. `cap:scoped-analysis` is built and shipped — 'A team asks the detectors about its own part, and is told what it did not see' (`chg:scoped-analysis-built`), and `loop_status` already takes a `contributor_id`. So this is not a request for a feature that does not exist. It is a report that THE FEATURE THAT EXISTS DID NOT HELP: he called `detect_gaps(scope: Capability)` at depth 1, 2 and 3, got `in_scope` of roughly 47–51 every time, 'almost every hit `unverified_capability` on unrelated planned work', and still could not answer 'is THIS Capability still in an `unrealized_capability` gap?' without grepping `affected_ids` by hand. THAT REFRAMES IT: the scope is computed by GRAPH REACHABILITY, and on a connected design a few hops reaches most of it. The question is whether scope should mean 'what the seed can reach' or 'what is actually about the seed'. THE OPTIONS: (a) FILTER BY `affected_ids` — exactly his proposal: a gap is in scope when the seed (or its SATISFIES/REALIZES neighbours) is in the gap's own affected set. CHEAP, and it answers the question he actually had. COUNTER: it narrows to gaps that already name the seed, so a gap about a neighbour that WILL matter to him drops out — and `cap:scoped-analysis`'s whole promise is that it 'names what it did not see', which this makes both more necessary and more voluminous. (b) SUPPRESS `unverified_capability` FOR `planned` + ZERO ARTIFACTS — his second clause, and independently useful. CHEAP. COUNTER: it is a phase judgement baked into a detector, and this project's standing preference is to report the fact and let the reader judge (`dec:report-dont-judge`). It may also be the same finding as `dec:should-a-design-be-able-to-say-it-describes-something-that-already-exists`, one layer along — a design that has not started building does not want build gaps at all. (c) A SESSION MODE ON `loop_status` — 'I am building this Capability'. Answers the noise complaint where he actually felt it: `next(0)` was detect-and-ask all session while the work was implement → user-correct → implement. COUNTER, and it is serious: `loop_status`'s contract is that a scoped answer must never read as 'the design is clean' — it already keeps unattributable debt under `scope.not_attributable` for exactly this reason. A mode that HIDES project-wide gaps is the one thing that contract forbids, so this option must be built as 'rank differently', not 'hide'. (d) DO NOTHING TO THE TOOLS; THE COMPLAINT IS ABOUT PHASE — he was mid-bugfix with a user watching a broken app, and reflow2 has no notion of that. His items 3 and 9 are the same complaint from the other side. COUNTER: 'wait for a phase model' has been the answer to several of these, and nothing is scheduled. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether depth was the wrong control or scope was the wrong concept; and whether 47–51 in_scope on his design is large relative to the design's size, which nobody measured.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Two ideas held in one node because they are one question asked of two surfaces; noted inside that they can be answered apart if the answer differs. The reframing — that scoping exists and did not narrow — is a finding, not a decision, and is stated as such.proposednothing
OPEN — how does 'search the graph before you add' become AUTOMATIC, when it is already written into five skills and still depends on somebody loading one?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, per Anthony's own standing rule that a genuinely new thing becomes a proposal one day accepted rather than a requirement written on his behalf. Nothing here is intent. HIS WORDS, 2026-08-11: 'we need to make the search the graph first a requirement that is automatic. something like anytime a user has an idea, requirement, feedback, etc - first go search the graph to see what's already there (this should prevent near duplicate nodes in the graph appearing).' ⭐⭐ THE RULE ALREADY EXISTS, IN FIVE SERVED SKILLS. Measured 2026-08-11: `capture-intent`, `revise-design`, `brainstorm`, `kpp-proposal` and `retire-from-design` all instruct it, and capture-intent's wording is almost exactly his: 'Search before you add. For each candidate, `search_design` with its key words first — the design may already say this. A hit that covers the same need means you update or link the existing node, NOT create a near-duplicate that HEAL will later flag and someone must merge. No hits is also information.' So the ask is not for the rule. IT IS FOR THE TRIGGER. And the trigger is the thing this project has now confirmed three times is missing: `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` (ACCEPTED) says skill use 'must be triggered by the SITUATION, not remembered — and THE USER MUST NEVER BE THE TRIGGER', measured on this repo 2026-07-31, and confirmed from the field on 2026-08-11 by the second user, who named exactly the two skills he types and neither of the two that would have fired on situations he was already in. ⭐⭐ AND THE MECHANISM IS ALREADY A REQUIREMENT, PROPOSED AND UNBUILT: `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` — 'a discipline that applies mid-task is delivered at the TOOL that triggers it, not from a catalogue read once at handshake.' That is precisely what he is asking for, one layer more general. This idea may not need a requirement of its own at all; it may be the first concrete instance of one that already exists and has never been accepted. 📌 THIS NODE IS ITSELF THE NINTH COLLISION recorded in fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input, and it was found BY DOING THE THING HE ASKED FOR: searching before adding. Had the search not run, this would have become a near-duplicate of a proposed requirement and a fifth restatement of an instruction already in five skills — which is the exact failure he is trying to prevent, reproduced in the act of trying to prevent it. WHAT EXISTS ON THE DETECTION SIDE, so this is not built twice. `possible_duplicate` fires on shared allocation sets with Jaccard ≥ 0.8 and asks rather than merges (`dec:ask-not-repair`); HEAL merges only on a human-asserted DUPLICATES edge. Both are AFTER-THE-FACT and STRUCTURAL — they catch two nodes that ended up allocated the same way. Neither can see 'the same idea in different words, newly written, allocated to nothing yet', which is the case he is describing. Prevention and detection are different problems here. IDEAS, unranked: (a) Put it on the TOOL, not the skill: `add_requirement` / `add_capability` / `add_decision` return near-matches alongside the write, or refuse-and-name when a match is close enough. Reaches every session including ones that load no skill. Cost — a write tool that sometimes refuses is a new failure mode on the hottest path, and BM25 near-matches are not reliable enough to refuse on (`dec:` on BM25 scores not being comparable across queries). (b) SEARCH ON THE WAY IN, NEVER REFUSE: the write succeeds and the response carries '3 existing nodes look close: ...'. No new failure mode, no judgement, and it puts the finding where the agent is already looking. Smallest honest version. (c) A pre-write hook or a served instruction at handshake. Cheapest to state and it is what already exists — five skills say it — so this is the option that has already been tried and is the reason he is asking. (d) Nothing new: ACCEPT `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` and build it, since this is an instance of it rather than a separate need. ⚠️ THE TRAP: a near-match list that is usually wrong trains the agent to ignore it, which is worse than silence — the same failure `unexpected_coupling` was retired for, and the one `v0.2.0-what-we-dont-know.md` names as the sharpest thing to watch ('a gap list you skim is worse than no gap list'). Whatever surfaces matches must be precise enough to be read every time, and BM25 alone has already been shown here to score the same topic 4.48 and 35.75 across two queries. ⚠️ SECOND TRAP, AND IT CUTS AGAINST THE WHOLE IDEA: a near-duplicate is sometimes CORRECT. `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` exists precisely because a body of intent that contradicts itself is still a design. Suppressing a second statement of the same idea can erase that the user said it twice, in different words, at different times — which is signal about what they keep coming back to, and is what `dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important` asks about from the other direction. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ SHARPENED 2026-08-12 — THE WRITE HALF SHIPPED; THE READ HALF IS WHERE IT EARNED ITS KEEP ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ ⭐ THIS SECTION WAS ADDED BY THE GUARD ITSELF. An agent tried to create a NEW node about exactly this and `add_decision` REFUSED it, naming this node and both routes on. The write half works, in the field, against its own author. That is the strongest evidence this node will ever get, and it arrived by accident. ANTHONY NAMED THE BEHAVIOUR AS SOMETHING HE VALUES, 2026-08-12: 'every time I ask a question or propose an idea, you do a search/research what has already happened. then we either sharpen the previous or add new content or all sorts of things that continually improves the design - i think this is awesome!' ⭐ MEASURED IN ONE SESSION — six saves, each with what it prevented: - 'a requirement that anything developed has something that uses it' -> already captured 2026-08-09 IN HIS OWN WORDS. A duplicate node. - 'accept the 26 delivered requirements' -> ELEVEN were satisfied only by `planned`/`in_progress` capabilities. Asserting delivery that had not happened, eleven times. - 'should we have a purge skill' -> `dec:proposed-requirements-pruned` had already settled DROPPED-NOT-DELETED. Re-deciding a settled question destructively. - 'a tool that does the import step' -> `import_graph` already took a `path`. Building a tool that existed. - 'treat the union of 2+ graphs as one graph' -> `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs`, his own federation model from six days earlier. Re-deriving his own thinking. - 'treat one side as immutable' -> `mirror_surface`, BUILT and stamping `mirror_of` / `mirror_content_hash` / `mirrored_at`. Specifying something already shipped. Plus a doc review that caught a section marked OUTSTANDING three days after the thing shipped. 🛑 AND THE ASYMMETRY THAT MATTERS: **ALL SIX HAPPENED ON THE READ PATH, WHERE NOTHING ENFORCES ANYTHING.** The refusal fires on add_requirement / add_capability / add_component / add_decision / add_constraint. It cannot fire when a user asks a question and an agent answers in prose. Those six happened because the agent chose to look. That is `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`'s failure with the trigger moved one step — not the user reminding the agent, but the agent remembering — and it degrades silently in a long session precisely when the graph is large enough to make searching most valuable. ⭐⭐ THE OBSERVATION THAT CHANGES THE VALUE CALCULATION: the write guard catches a near-duplicate NODE. It cannot catch a near-duplicate DECISION TO BUILD. **Four of the six saves prevented WORK, not nodes** — and work is the more expensive thing. So the unguarded half is plausibly worth more than the guarded half, which inverts the obvious reading that the write path is where the value is. ⚠️ SURVIVORSHIP BIAS, NAMED SO SIX IS NOT READ AS A RATE. Only the times it worked are visible; NOTHING RECORDS A SEARCH THAT DID NOT HAPPEN. `dec:loop-status-cannot-say-it-never-looked` is the same shape already on the record — 'clean' and 'never scanned' are one answer. OPTIONS FOR THE READ HALF, none taken: A — A READ-SIDE HINT on orientation reads. Rides the existing `loop_hint` carrier. EXPENSIVE: it needs to know what the user asked, which the tool layer never sees — so the agent must volunteer the query, which is the same trigger problem one layer down. B — MAKE THE ABSENCE COMPUTABLE. Do not fire at the right moment; record whether a search preceded a capture and report captures with none — `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` applied here. EXPENSIVE, and the asymmetry is already recorded above: a node created without a prior search is not distinguishable from one created after a search that found nothing. C — INSTRUMENT ONLY, so the habit's decay is visible. Cheapest; answers nothing. D — DO NOTHING; the write path guards where duplicates actually enter. Weakened by the four-of-six finding above.		The rule Anthony asked for is already written into five served skills, and the delivery mechanism he described is already a proposed requirement. What is missing is not the instruction but the trigger — the same gap confirmed three times this week. Recording it as an instance rather than a new need, and noting that the search which found this is the very discipline in question. SHARPENED 2026-08-12, and by the guard itself: an agent tried to open a new node on this and add_decision refused it, naming this one. Six measured saves in a single session, all on the READ path where nothing enforces the discipline — and four of them prevented WORK rather than nodes, which is the more expensive thing and inverts the assumption that the write path is where the value lies.proposedA capture tool tells you what the design already says, and makes you choose — sharpen or start new
OPEN — should severability be computed as a minimum EDGE CUT, not just as articulation points?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled. THE OBSERVATION: cut_structure (used today) reports articulation POINTS — single nodes whose removal splits the network. That answers 'what is a single point of failure'. It does not answer 'how separable are these two subsystems', which is a different and equally architectural question. THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::max_flow_min_cut (Edmonds-Karp, exact, unused) returns the minimum-capacity set of EDGES whose removal disconnects a source from a target. Read on a design graph: 'which contracts would you have to sever to split A from B, and how many?' Edge weights are already coupling weights, so the capacity has a meaning here rather than being invented. WHERE IT LANDS: dec:mosa-conformance is OPEN and its own text says reflow2 'already computes most of the criteria' for modular open systems conformance. Severability is one of the ones it does not. req:modularity-computed is the standing requirement that severability be computed rather than asserted. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS: min-cut needs a SOURCE and a TARGET, and nothing in the design says which two subsystems a user wants separated — so either the user picks the pair (a new question to ask) or reflow2 runs it over community pairs from leiden (defensible, but O(pairs) and the communities are themselves computed rather than declared). Also, low cut capacity is not automatically good: two subsystems SHOULD be coupled where the design says they should be, and a detector that rewards separation everywhere would push toward a design nobody wants — the same over-selectivity trap is_single_point_of_failure already had to be tuned out of.		Chosen from the unused set because it maps onto an OPEN decision rather than onto a hypothetical: dec:mosa-conformance already claims most criteria are computable, and this names one that is not.proposednothing
OPEN — should a Requirement with no recorded ORIGIN be a gap? The golden thread checks forward and nothing checks backward
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — 2026-08-11, from Anthony's observation that the governance work came from a real demand signal ('it was all taken from feedback from the storyflow project... I told reflow2 to consider it and do it'). Nothing here is intent. WHAT WAS MEASURED, and it is the reason the question exists. reflow2's own governance requirements DID come from a demand signal: `/home/ajs7/project/dev_storyflow/reflow2_feedback.md`, the GOVERNANCE-AS-DESIGN entry by api-boss, 2026-08-08. Six Requirements carry AUTHORED_BY to `who:storyflow-api-boss`, so the authorship survived. But: · searched every node in the design for the string `reflow2_feedback` → 12 hits, NONE of them any of the six governance requirements · the document is not registered as an Artifact · so the origin of this work exists only in Anthony's head, and he had to tell an agent where to look ⭐ THE SELF-INDICTMENT: `req:no-idea-goes-quiet` is ACCEPTED and reads 'an idea in the graph stays connected to whether it was built and to where it was written — THE USER NEVER HUNTS FOR THE SOURCE DOCUMENT AGAIN.' reflow2's own governance capture violates an accepted reflow2 requirement, and no detector could see it. ⭐ AND IT COST SOMETHING MEASURABLE, twice. The feedback entry ranked THREE asks. Only #1 reached the graph: #1 model VERIFIES onto DesignRule so enforced+no-check is detectable → BUILT (unverified_enforced_rule) #2 a Role/Seat node distinct from Contributor — duties attach to the SEAT, not the human → ABSENT, no such node type #3 an `obligation` category on DesignRule: 'MUST do X AT MOMENT Y' → ABSENT; categories in use are convention/methodology/None #3 carried the sharpest sentence in the entry — 'our doc map recorded WHO reads a file and WHAT it holds, and never WHEN — the missing axis was TIME, and no rule was being broken because no rule named a moment.' That finding is nowhere in this design. The entry did say #1 was 'the whole idea's leverage and the rest is optional', so building #1 first was RIGHT — but #2 and #3 were not DEFERRED, they evaporated, which is a different thing and the one nobody can see. IDEAS, unranked: (a) A gap for a Requirement with no incoming DOCUMENTS/Fragment/origin edge — 'what asked for this?' (b) No new detector; instead make the capture skills register the source document as an Artifact by default, so the edge exists by construction rather than by discipline. (c) Do nothing structural, and treat the origin as prose in the requirement's own statement. COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO (a), and it is the same trap that made `rule:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path` advisory: at genesis NOBODY has a source document — intent arrives by someone talking. A detector demanding an origin edge would fire against the entire design on day one and the only way to green it would be to fabricate origins. That argues (b) is the honest shape and (a) is only safe if it fires on requirements whose provenance says they came from a DOCUMENT. NOTE ON WHY THE DAU FRAME FITS: of the nine DAU requirement characteristics Anthony cited, TRACEABLE is defined as connecting 'directly back to top-level strategic guidance and forward to system design specs.' reflow2 checks FORWARD (the golden thread; unmotivated_capability fired on exactly this) and has no check at all for BACKWARD. COMPLETE failed too — 2 of 3 ranked asks are absent in any form.		The demand signal existed and became requirements — the process was run. What broke was traceability backward to the source and completeness across the source's three asks. Both are invisible to every detector reflow2 has, and an accepted requirement already says they should not be.proposedCapture FROM a document registers that document and links what came out of it, so the backward half of the thread exists by construction
OPEN — should a status that claims LESS than the structure shows be a gap, the way an overstated one already is?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — found 2026-08-11 while answering Anthony's question about work built without a requirement. Nothing here is intent. THE ASYMMETRY, read from the code rather than assumed. `detect_status_contradictions` (detect.rs:2146) fires in exactly two places, and both are OVERSTATEMENTS: · a Capability at `verified` with no passing check → 0.70 · a Requirement at `met` with nothing satisfying it → 0.70 Nothing anywhere looks at the opposite direction. THE INSTANCE THAT SURFACED IT: `cap:governance-proposal` sits at `planned` while `art:governance-proposal-skill` REALIZES it, it is allocated to `cmp:skills`, and that component's check passes. The skill is being SERVED to sessions right now. The status claims less than the structure shows, and no detector has an opinion. ⭐ THIS IS A NAMED-AND-UNBUILT CASE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT I INVENTED. The test at detect.rs:1401-1407 records the same limit from the Release side and assigns it: 'a status that claims less than the structure shows is `status_contradiction`'s territory, not this one's.' It was allocated to that detector and never written there. IDEAS, unranked: (a) Add the mirror rule to status_contradiction: a Capability at `planned`/`unrealized` with an incoming REALIZES, or with a passing check, is understating. (b) Lower severity than 0.70. Overstating is a claim with nothing behind it; understating is a record that has fallen behind reality — arguably drift, not a contradiction, and drift already has its own machinery. (c) Do nothing, on the grounds that understating harms nobody. COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO (c), which is why this is worth asking at all: understating is what makes `graph_report`'s delivery count too LOW, and a design that under-reports its own completion is the one nobody trusts the numbers on. It is also the direction that silently accumulates, because nothing complains. ⚠️ SIZING CAVEAT before anyone treats (a) as small: `Release.status` and `Capability.status` both DEFAULT to `planned` (detect.rs:1401-1403 states this for Release). So 'planned + realized' would fire on every capability whose status nobody ever set, which on a young design may be most of them. Whether that is signal or a flood is unmeasured, and measuring it is the first step, not the fix.		status_contradiction is one-directional and its own test file assigns the other direction to it. The instance that exposed it is shipped, served code recorded as `planned`. The open part is whether the mirror rule floods, because `planned` is a schema default nobody chose.proposednothing
PARKED, NOT ACCEPTED — should consistency/availability/partition-tolerance be vocabulary reflow2 offers? The federation seam is the road if any is ever taken. Anthony, 2026-08-12: revisit later, more important things first.
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12, second half of his CAP question. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen. DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-is-reflow2-itself-a-cp-store-behind-an-ap-record`, deliberately kept apart: that one asks whether CAP describes reflow2's OWN architecture. This one asks whether CAP is vocabulary reflow2 should HAND ITS USERS. One node holding both could only ever be half-answered. SIBLING, NOT DUPLICATE, OF `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph` (proposed, 2026-08-08). That node asks about the DIRECTION of inference — should the quality attribute drive allocation rather than be read off it. This asks whether a SPECIFIC well-known trade-off frame belongs in the vocabulary at all. Related, and the answers could differ: the ility→graph direction could be built without CAP ever appearing, and CAP could be added without changing allocation. ⭐ THE CONCRETE GAP, checked rather than asserted. `schema/dimensions.yaml` already carries NINE axes attachable to any node: reliability, performance, maintainability, security, scalability, observability, testability, coupling, maturity. **Consistency is not among them. Availability is not among them. Partition tolerance is not among them.** For a tool whose owner's stated operating context includes federated, independently-evolving systems, that is a real absence rather than a stylistic one. AND ONE PIECE ALREADY EXISTS UNDER A DIFFERENT NAME: `cap:seam-incompatibility` — 'say when two linked designs disagree at a boundary' — is, structurally, a consistency check across a partition between two independently-evolving replicas. The federation work (`cap:mirror-surface`, `cap:composed-analysis`, `cap:complementary-pairing`) is a distributed-design problem that has never been described in distributed-systems terms. ═══ THE OPTIONS ═══ A — NOTHING. CAP is domain knowledge the AGENT brings to a conversation, not vocabulary the graph must hold. An agent can already reason about it and record the resulting decision as an ordinary Decision node, today, with no change whatsoever. CHEAPEST, and the null hypothesis this has to beat. B — ADD `consistency` AND `availability` TO THE DIMENSION ENUM. Cheap, additive, existing graphs unaffected. `ility_report` already reports NOT INFORMED with a reason for axes it cannot compute — so honest silence is the built-in default and nothing pretends. NOTE: a new enum value moves NO stamp count, which would be the fifth recorded instance of the stamp being blind to a real compatibility event. C — ASK IT UPFRONT, at genesis or adopt: 'is this system CP or AP under partition, and L or C in normal operation?' This is exactly the shape `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph` argues for in Anthony's own words — 'if you don't ask upfront, these cost a lot in having to rework services after they've been already developed.' A CAP posture chosen late is a rewrite; chosen early it is a constraint everything else obeys. D — A CONTRADICTION DETECTOR, and the only option where anything COMPUTES. A design asserting strict consistency AND high availability across a declared partition boundary is claiming something the theorem forbids. reflow2 already has the machinery: `CONTRADICTS`, `cap:kpp` for inviolable intent, `constrains`, and `cap:key-interfaces` for computing whether a change crosses a published boundary. This is a KPP breach with a known proof. ═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══ ⚠️ 1. THE STRONGEST ONE — reflow2 IS DOMAIN-NEUTRAL AND CAP IS NOT. Its stated operating breadth is greenfield and brownfield and continual, across several organisations; the owner's own context is Space Force systems engineering and a Brookhaven beamline stack. CAP is meaningless for a beamline's mechanical design or a spacecraft thermal budget. Building a distributed-systems theorem into the core vocabulary privileges software architecture over every other domain the tool claims to serve. ⚠️ 2. 'PICK TWO OF THREE' IS ITSELF A MISLEADING FRAME, and shipping it would propagate the misreading. CAP forces a choice ONLY DURING a partition; in normal operation a system need not sacrifice either. That is precisely why PACELC exists. A tool that offers CAP as a first-class axis would be handing users the version practitioners most often get wrong. ⚠️ 3. VOCABULARY NOBODY USES IS THE SHAPE THIS PROJECT SPENT A MONTH REMOVING. Requirement's five-state lifecycle runs 3-of-5 unused; BL-198 was the removal work. Nine dimensions already exist and the ility report cannot inform four of them. Two more unused axes make the enum longer and the design no truer. ⚠️ 4. A PLANNED CAPABILITY COSTS THREE GAPS FOREVER (`dec:exploratory-staging`, measured: 34 of 73 open gaps came from routing wishes to Capability). Option D as a planned capability is a standing tax until someone builds it. 📌 WHERE THE IDEA IS STRONGEST, narrower than 'add CAP': not as a general axis, but where reflow2 ALREADY has the substrate — the federation seam. `cap:seam-incompatibility` computes disagreement between two independently-evolving designs, which is a consistency question with a real detector behind it. If any of this earns its place, that is the door, and it needs no enum change at all.		PARKED ON ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-12: 'we can add cap:seam-incompatibility as proposed, but leave it as not accepted. one day we can come back to this — it doesn't sound like it has huge applicability, so I think there are more important things to deal with in the interim.' WHAT THAT SETTLES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It settles the ROAD: if consistency vocabulary is ever taken up, it enters through `cap:seam-incompatibility` — the federation seam, where reflow2 already computes when two independently-evolving designs disagree at a boundary — and NOT as new `dimension` enum values (option B) or a general axis. It does NOT accept the idea, schedule it, or claim it will happen. Status stays `proposed`. 🛑 DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED AS A PLANNED CAPABILITY, and this is the one judgement made on his behalf rather than by his word. He said 'add cap:seam-incompatibility as proposed' — but `cap:seam-incompatibility` ALREADY EXISTS and is `realized` (it is the built detector this idea would extend), and Capability has no `proposed` status: its lifecycle is planned / in_progress / realized / verified. Creating a NEW planned Capability to hold the idea would cost THREE GAPS FOREVER — unmotivated, unrealized, unverified — which is `dec:exploratory-staging`'s measured finding (34 of 73 open gaps came from exactly that routing). Parking something explicitly because there are MORE IMPORTANT THINGS TO DEAL WITH, and paying a standing three-gap nag for it, would defeat his own stated reason. A proposed Decision is SILENT by construction — `detect_gaps` fires `undecided_decision_point` only on two or more REGISTERED alternatives — so the idea is kept, findable by search, and costs nothing until someone registers real alternatives under it. IF HE WANTS IT TRACKED AS WORK rather than kept as a thought, that is one `add_capability` call away and the three gaps are the honest price of scheduling it. The choice is his; the default taken here is the quiet one, matching what he asked for.proposednothing
IDEA — the blast radius reports one kind of reach. Should the summary band 'crossed a published Interface' apart from 'sits on the same Component', and name the siblings that are not actually impacted?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's idea, 2026-08-14 (Opportunities), in his words: '`propagate_change` summary: separate 'same Component dump' from 'crossed an Interface.' Default `full` off is right; the summary still needs a 'sibling Capabilities on the same Component, not actually impacted' band.' DISTINCT FROM `fact:defect-propagate-change-distance-two-is-not-an-edit-list`, which measures what happened (~65 named, 113 truncated, the Interface signal buried). This holds the unmade choice about the fix. THE OPTIONS: (a) BAND THE SUMMARY BY EDGE KIND — group the impacted set by HOW it was reached: through a shared Component, across a PROVIDES/CONSUMES Interface, along the Requirement/Decision thread. CHEAP, changes no traversal, and it makes the useful signal findable rather than smaller. COUNTER: it renames the problem if the bands are not ranked — a hundred nodes in three labelled groups is still a hundred nodes. (b) A NAMED 'NOT ACTUALLY IMPACTED' BAND, his exact phrasing — siblings on the same Component, reported as reached-but-probably-irrelevant. HONEST, and it keeps the count visible rather than filtering it away, which matters because this project's standing preference is to report rather than judge. COUNTER: 'not actually impacted' is a JUDGEMENT, and the tool would be making it. A sibling Capability on a shared Component sometimes IS impacted, and a band that says otherwise will eventually be believed on the day it is wrong. (c) WEIGHT THE TRAVERSAL rather than band the output — DEPENDS_ON already carries `weight` and `weight_basis`, and CONSUMES carries `weight` too. A radius that decayed through weak couplings would shrink honestly. COUNTER: almost nothing in a real design sets those weights, so the decay would be uniform and the answer unchanged — this is a fix that requires a habit nobody has. (d) DO NOTHING TO THE TOOL; FIX THE INSTRUCTION. The served loop says 'update ONLY what the blast radius names', which is what makes a wide answer a defect rather than information. Softening the instruction costs nothing. COUNTER: it concedes that the radius cannot be acted on, which is most of what the tool is for. ⚠️ AND A COUNTERWEIGHT FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION, measured on reflow2's own graph this session: `propagate_change` seeded from a TemporalFact returned ZERO impacted, because ABOUT_ENTITY is not traversed. ANY CHANGE HERE MUST NOT ASSUME THE TOOL'S PROBLEM IS ONLY THAT IT IS TOO WIDE. It is too wide from one seed type and silent from another, and a narrowing fix applied blind would make the silent case worse. NOT ESTABLISHED: the ratio — he did not report his design's total node count, so whether 178 is most of it or a tenth of it is unknown, and that number decides whether this is a threshold problem or a shape problem.		⭐ SHARPENED 2026-08-16 with a measurement and a doctrine tension, both of which narrow the question. MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN: a real change event (`chg:artifact-intent-stops-being-injected`) returned 19 nodes at distance 1 and 1,068 impacted in total, and the FOUR `boundary_crossings` were the only part worth reading. So the ask is real at this scale, not hypothetical. ⇒ AND HALF OF IT IS ALREADY BUILT, which is worth stating plainly so nobody builds it twice: the summary already returns `boundary_crossings`, naming the crossed interfaces by id, alongside `risk_crossings`. 'Crossed an Interface' is ANSWERED today. What remains unbuilt is only the other side of the pairing — naming the siblings that are NOT impacted. ⚠️ AND THAT REMAINING HALF IS A NEGATIVE CLAIM, which is the actual open question rather than an implementation detail.
