A band labelled 'not actually impacted' asserts that sibling capabilities on one Component are unaffected — and sometimes they ARE, through exactly the shared state that put them on the same Component. Propagation found them because a path exists; calling that path uninteresting is a judgement about coupling the graph does not hold. This runs straight into `dec:report-dont-judge`, and into propagate_change's own refusal to say what to EDIT (`fact:defect-propagate-change-distance-two-is-not-an-edit-list`, which the guard surfaced beside this). THREE HONEST FORMS IF THE VERDICT FORM IS REFUSED, none of which asserts anything the traversal did not establish: GROUP the ring by Component, so twenty siblings read as one component's worth; COUNT them — '17 of the 19 at distance 1 are capabilities on the same Component as the seed' is a fact, not a verdict, and is the sentence a reader actually needs; or SORT, putting crossings first and siblings last, changing only the reading order. NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the measurement that would decide between a verdict and a grouping: how often a same-Component sibling turns out to BE impacted. Nobody has looked.proposednothing
IDEA — the record-before-you-edit discipline can silently snapshot the NEW state. Should `record_change` refuse when the target has already moved, or be folded into the typed merge itself?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's idea, 2026-08-14 (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md, Opportunities), in his words: '`record_change` should refuse (or warn) if the target's current hash already differs from what the caller thinks they are snapshotting — or be a required first step inside the typed merge when `status` is `accepted`.' DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM `fact:defect-record-change-overwrites-the-name-of-the-event-it-is-filed-under`, which the near-duplicate guard surfaced: BOTH ARE FAILURES OF THE SAME CALL AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME FAILURE. That fact is about `record_change` clobbering the ChangeEvent's `name`, found serially; this is about the SNAPSHOT capturing state that had already moved, found under parallel writes. Whether they get one fix is part of what is open here — which is an argument for keeping them separate until somebody decides, not for merging them now. WHAT HE HIT (his item 2): in one batch he `record_change`d a Decision AFTER a sibling `add_decision` on the same id had already merged. The Snapshot stored the NEW statement. Nothing warned. In his words: 'the timeline for that revision is a lie; easy for any agent that parallelizes writes.' THE OPTIONS: (a) REFUSE ON A HASH MISMATCH — the caller states what it believes it is snapshotting; a difference is refused. CHEAP, and it matches doctrine already applied elsewhere: `set_artifact_checksum` is a two-sided accept for this reason, and `export_graph` refuses a divergent write rather than silently discarding. COUNTER: the caller has no hash in hand today, so this needs a new argument, and an agent that cannot produce one gets a tool it cannot call. (b) WARN RATHER THAN REFUSE. CHEAP, breaks nothing. COUNTER: the loss is silent precisely because the call reports success, and a warning nobody reads is this project's own recurring failure. (c) FOLD IT INTO THE TYPED MERGE when `status` is `accepted` — his stronger form: you cannot edit an accepted Decision without the snapshot happening first, because the tool does it. STRONGEST; removes the ordering hazard rather than reporting it. COUNTER: it makes one write path do two things, and `dec:ask-not-repair` is the standing preference for naming a problem over acting on it. (d) DO NOTHING; THE DISCIPLINE IS THE ANSWER. COUNTER, and it is measured rather than argued: the sibling fact was found on 2026-08-15 doing exactly this, STRICTLY SERIALLY and in the order `revise-design` prescribes, and data was lost anyway. Ordering discipline is demonstrably not sufficient for this call — which is evidence against (d) rather than for any particular replacement. NOT ESTABLISHED: how often the parallel-write case actually occurs — one report, one session.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Kept distinct from the name-overwrite fact after the guard named it: two failures of one call, found by two different routes, and whether one fix covers both is itself part of the open question. ⭐ UPDATED 2026-08-16 — A FIFTH OPTION ARRIVED BY SHIPPING SOMETHING ELSE, and it weakens (a), (b) and (c) without settling them. v0.32.0 gave every typed constructor a `revision` block: landing on an existing node now returns the properties the call OVERWROTE, with their prior values IN FULL, plus a `changed` flag and a `prior_content_hash`. Its own note names this exact ordering — snapshot BEFORE the merge, because afterwards it files the replacement as the prior state. ⇒ (e) THE INFORMATION IS NOW IN THE REPLY, SO PERHAPS NOTHING MORE IS OWED. A caller who merges first and snapshots second is now TOLD, in the merge's own response, what the prior value was — which is the fact the lying Snapshot destroyed, handed back at the moment of destruction. COUNTER, and it is why this does not close the question: the block reports to whoever reads the reply, and the failure mode here is an agent parallelising writes and reading nothing. A value returned to a caller who does not look is not the same as a refusal. ⇒ The open question narrows usefully: it is no longer 'how do we preserve the prior value' but 'does a returned value suffice, or must the ordering be enforced'. 📌 AND THE PRIOR-HASH OBJECTION TO (a) IS NOW WEAKER TOO: the counter said a caller has no hash in hand, so refusing on a mismatch needs a new argument. `prior_content_hash` is now returned by the constructors, so a caller who has touched the node HAS one.proposednothing
OPEN — reflow2's own rules are tracked by hand while reflow2 has a governance layer built to track them. Should they be wired into it?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. ⚠️ REFRAMED 2026-08-11 AFTER GETTING IT WRONG. The first version of this node asked whether reflow2 should automate git. That was not the question. Anthony: 'I'm not saying that reflow2 does the actual git operations itself; I'm arguing that reflow2's own rules shouldn't be tracked by hand, but by some governance rules (and this may be different for every project, which is kind of how we designed the governance entities for reflow2 anyways).' His original words were 'as part of governance', and the word was doing the work. ⭐⭐ THE FINDING, MEASURED 2026-08-11: REFLOW2 HAS A GOVERNANCE LAYER AND DOES NOT USE IT ON ITS OWN GOVERNANCE RULES. DesignRules in this design 10 carrying a VERIFIES edge 1 (per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global) `dec:export-once-per-pr` node type Decision — so `unverified_enforced_rule`, which scans DesignRules, CANNOT SEE IT Verification node for the lineage gate none `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly` advisory, unverified AND THE GATE IS REAL. `tools/reflow2_check.py` fails the build on a broken lineage chain — it did so twice on 2026-08-11 — and its own source at line 515 says: 'THE RULE THIS ENFORCES is `dec:export-once-per-pr`, accepted'. THE PYTHON NAMES THE RULE IT ENFORCES AND THE GRAPH DOES NOT KNOW THE CHECK EXISTS. Delete that check tomorrow and nothing in the design notices: no gap, no defect, no unverified rule. The rule keeps reading as governing while nothing governs. ⭐ SO 'CARRIED BY HAND' IS PRECISE AND IT IS NOT ABOUT GIT. The ENFORCEMENT is automated. The TRACKING of the enforcement is what is manual — a rule in one place, a check in another, and nothing joining them. That is the same shape this project keeps finding: the search-first rule living in five skills and firing only when one is loaded; the deferral discipline living in a table nothing computes on; mutation-checking practised in eight verifications and written down nowhere. ⭐⭐ AND THE GENERALISATION IS THE PRODUCT POINT, in his words: 'this may be different for every project, which is kind of how we designed the governance entities for reflow2 anyways.' The governance entities exist so ANY project can state its own policy and get gap detection on it — `DesignRule` with a three-state `enforced`, `unverified_enforced_rule` at 0.6, `cap:governance-proposal` to ask the consequence rather than inherit it. reflow2's own git and export policy is exactly the kind of project-specific rule that layer was built for, and it sits outside it. A consumer copying reflow2's example would copy the gap. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CHANGE, unranked: (a) MAKE THE EXISTING RULES FIRST-CLASS. `dec:export-once-per-pr` becomes (or gains) a DesignRule so the governance detector can see it; the lineage gate becomes a Verification with a VERIFIES edge to it; `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly` gets the same treatment or an honest statement that it cannot be checked. Pure wiring, no new mechanism, and it makes deleting a check visible. (b) ANSWER THE CHECKABILITY QUESTION PROPERLY. `req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all` is ACCEPTED and unbuilt: it splits 'no detector' into DEBT and ACCEPTED LIMIT. Nine of ten rules here are unverified and nothing distinguishes 'nobody has written the check' from 'no check is possible' — which is the difference between rule:bl-41 (LLM behaviour, arguably uncheckable) and the export rule (checked already, just not wired). (c) BOTH, since (b) is what stops (a) turning nine rules into nine permanent 0.6 gaps. (d) Nothing: the gate works, and wiring it into the graph changes no behaviour today. ⚠️ THE COUNTER TO (a) AND IT IS REAL: making rules first-class means `unverified_enforced_rule` starts firing on rules nobody intends to check, and this project has retired a detector before (`unexpected_coupling`) precisely for firing on correct work. That is why (b) is not optional — the enforced flag without the checkability answer converts honest advisory rules into permanent debt. ⚠️ THE NON-GITHUB CLAUSE STILL STANDS AND IS NOWHERE IN THE GRAPH. `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly` is stated entirely in GitHub's vocabulary — branch, open a PR, gates green, merge — and its four recorded traps are all forge mechanics. ON A BARE GIT REMOTE THERE IS NO PULL REQUEST. So the rule presumes a forge while reflow2 only requires git, and nothing says which parts survive. That is a live instance of `req:a-rule-states-its-scope-and-a-conflict-is-surfaced` (proposed): the rule does not state its scope, and on a plain remote it is partly UNFOLLOWABLE rather than merely unenforced. Any wiring must express the discipline in pure git — one commit per branch touches the export — with the PR being only where CI happens to notice. 📌 EVIDENCE OF THE COST, one day of this project's own work, four PRs all merged: two CI failures caused by the export discipline alone; roughly ten hand-driven restore-then-export-once cycles; a rebase needing a re-export because the three-way merge driver merges CONTENT correctly and cannot repair LINEAGE; the local and CI gates disagreeing in BOTH directions because one compares against HEAD and the other against main; and one PR left in draft after going green. A fleet of seven sessions reports the same and mitigates it with a social convention — 'only the boss exports' — which is the shape this project treats as a finding everywhere else. ⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN regardless: reflow2 must not push, merge or open a PR. `dec:repo-file-embedded` weighs local-first deliberately, and a design tool that writes to a remote is categorically worse than the friction it removes. Nothing in (a)–(c) requires it.		Reframed after misreading the question as git automation. The measurement is the argument: 10 DesignRules, 1 verified; the export rule is a Decision so the governance detector cannot see it; and the lineage gate that enforces it exists only as Python whose own source names the rule it enforces. The enforcement is automated and the tracking of it is not — so deleting the check would be invisible to the design. That is a product gap rather than a repo-hygiene one, because the governance entities exist precisely so any project can wire its own rules in.proposednothing
Define reflow2's black boxes and the contracts between them — DEFERRED behind bug work, on Anthony's word
SETTLED ON ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-16: DO IT, BUT NOT YET. His ruling: 'I'd like to actually define 'black boxes' and define contracts between them - this is not immediate (priority is resolving bugs)'. ⇒ OPTIONS (b) AND (c) ARE CHOSEN — declare the internal seams, and declare the foundation layer that the cohesion verdict currently rests on. Option (a) do-nothing is REJECTED; (d) subsystem-level allocation bookkeeping and (e) do-it-in-public were not taken up. ⇒ SEQUENCING IS PART OF THE RULING, not a note beside it: BUG WORK FIRST. `epoch:instruments-stop-overstating` and its five requirements come before this. ⭐ HIS STATED REASON FOR ACCEPTING THE DELAY, and it is the answer to the question that opened this whole thread: 'this conversation has led me to believe reflow2, when used on other projects, will actually lead you through a principled SE process (therefore the delay in properly modularizing reflow2 itself).' ⇒ THE SELF-HOST GAP IS NO LONGER READ AS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE PRODUCT. That is what makes the deferral defensible rather than merely convenient: the reason to hurry would have been that reflow2's own state implied something about what it does for its users, and the guided paths were found to sequence function before structure independently of the self-host. `genesis` seeds P0/P1 and STOPS before Components; `adopt` forbids inferring a Requirement from the implementation that satisfies it. WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND UNCHANGED BY THE DEFERRAL, so nobody later mistakes 'deferred' for 'resolved': • 73 coupled module pairs, ZERO sharing a declared Interface, 51 crossing a subsystem boundary. All 15 Interfaces sit at the SYSTEM edge; none describes an internal boundary. • The swap test: `cmp:detect` — 13 functions, 2 dependents, ZERO declared interfaces. Same for every module measured. There is nothing to swap against. • reflow2's own graph still does not do what its own `adopt` skill tells every user to do: 'both sides of every contract'. • The eight subsystems ARE a deliberate functional carving (`dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition`, accepted 2026-07-23, derived with the user) and they ARE cohesive — six couplings cross peer subsystems against 17 inside. The boxes are real; only the contracts are missing. ⚠️ And that cohesion verdict rests on treating Store and Vocabulary as FOUNDATION, which is an ASSUMPTION A READER SUPPLIES rather than something the design declares — which is why option (c), declaring the layer, is part of what was chosen rather than an afterthought. NOT ESTABLISHED, and it sets the cost when this is picked up: how many distinct CONTRACTS the 51 crossing pairs collapse into. The figure counts PAIRS and the real number is likely far smaller. Measuring that first would size the work before committing to it.		Anthony's ruling, 2026-08-16, given at the close of the systems-engineering thread he opened the same day. The measurements are mine; the choice, the priority ordering, and the reason for accepting the delay are his. Recorded as ACCEPTED with the work deferred rather than left `proposed`, because a deferral IS a decision — leaving it open would misreport an answered question as an unanswered one, and `arrival_delta` would keep asking. The sibling `dec:idea-does-reflow2-enforce-an-se-process-or-only-supply-the-vocabulary` stays `proposed`: he stated a BELIEF about it, not a ruling, and the distinction is his to close.acceptedA user can see that reflow2 guided them through a principled process, rather than having to take it on trust
IDEA — the two-sided accept has no answer for 'the code was wrong and now matches intent that never changed'. Should `as_built_aligned` be a third disposition?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's idea, 2026-08-14 (Opportunities), in his words: 'Checksum accept: allow `as_built_aligned` when a Requirement did not change and the file now matches it.' DISTINCT FROM THE THREE NODES THE GUARD NAMED, and the distinction is the interesting part. `dec:idea-does-change-type-need-more-values-or-a-second-axis` and its fact concern `ChangeEvent.change_type` — WHY A CHANGE HAPPENED. This concerns `set_artifact_checksum.disposition` — WHAT A CHANGE MEANS FOR THE DESIGN. Two different enums on two different tools, answerable differently. ⭐ THAT THE SAME MISSING MEANING IS ABSENT FROM BOTH IS EVIDENCE, NOT DUPLICATION: one absence is a wording gap; two independent absences of the same category is a category the vocabulary does not have. The third node measures the case; this holds the unmade choice. THE OPTIONS: (a) ADD `as_built_aligned` AS A THIRD DISPOSITION — exactly his proposal. It says the true thing: the design was right, the code was wrong, the code moved to meet it, intent never changed. CHEAP — enum values are not counted by the version stamp — with a precedent in `baseline_established`, added for the same reason one category along: forcing a record-only event through a code category 'writes a fiction into the ledger that exists to prevent fiction'. COUNTER: three dispositions is a decision an agent must get right under pressure, and his item 8 complaint was that choosing between TWO already costs a turn mid-bugfix. (b) LET `design_holds` CARRY IT, DOCUMENTED — say plainly that a fix restoring intended behaviour IS 'no design meaning', because the design did not move. CHEAPEST, no schema change, defensible on the plain reading. COUNTER: it collapses 'this change was meaningless' with 'this change repaired a violation of accepted intent', and the confirmation ledger then cannot count the second — exactly the number somebody would want when asking how often code drifted from design. (c) DERIVE IT INSTEAD OF ASKING — if the artifact REALIZES a capability satisfying a Requirement unchanged since the last baseline, the disposition is inferable and the agent should not be asked. ELEGANT, and it removes the mid-bugfix turn he complained about. COUNTER: `dec:two-sided-accept` exists because a SILENT accept 'is how a design erodes into fiction over N fix cycles while reporting zero gaps'. An inferred disposition is a silent accept wearing a computation, and the fix-cycle case is precisely what that decision guards. (d) DO NOTHING — two dispositions plus a prose note is enough. COUNTER: see the two-surfaces argument above. WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE INVARIANT: any new disposition must stay a DATED, ATTRIBUTABLE CLAIM counted apart in the confirmation ledger, as `baseline_established` is. The ledger's value is that it says HOW a design was confirmed, not merely that it was. NOT ESTABLISHED: frequency. One report. The ledger could answer it by counting `design_holds` accepts whose events carry `test_failure_fix` — a cheap sweep nobody has run.		Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Started as a new node rather than merged after the guard named the change_type pair: two enums on two tools answering two different questions, and the fact that the same meaning is missing from both is the evidence for acting rather than a reason to fold them together. Option (c) is included though it conflicts with an accepted decision, because it best answers his actual complaint and the conflict is worth seeing.proposednothing
OPEN — the general question behind five separate findings: should reflow2 make 'I could not see this' a reportable state, instead of adding a detector each time a blind spot is discovered?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, deliberately stepping back from a specific fix. HIS WORDS: *'sometimes I like to take a step back and ask what is the big picture and what do we want reflow2 to do. as the saying of 'missing the wood for the trees' says, I don't want to be hyper focused on solving this by creating another requirement which then causes another issue later on. I don't want this to become like a decision tree where it is so specialized to some training data that it is no longer generalizable.'* ⭐⭐⭐ **THE OVERFITTING CONCERN IS EXACTLY RIGHT, AND THE PROJECT HAS ALREADY WRITTEN IT DOWN AND ALREADY FAILED IT TWICE.** `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` (ACCEPTED 2026-08-07) says in its own text: · *'a detector that reaches zero findings by only asking questions the graph can already answer HAS BEEN TUNED TO THE INSTRUMENT. Satisfying this requirement by adding checks that happen to pass is the failure mode, not the fix.'* · *'One detector was added for that one case. **THE GENERAL PRINCIPLE WAS NEVER MADE A REQUIREMENT, so the next instance had to be found by hand again**, which is what happened today.'* THREE INSTANCES OF THE SAME PATTERN, EACH FOUND BY A HUMAN OR AN AGENT WORKING BY HAND: 1. `chg:orphan-decision-degree-zero` (2026-08-01) — *'GETTING A CLEAN BILL FROM EVERY DETECTOR — detect_defects 0, hierarchy_issues 0, dimension_drifts 0, propose_heal 0 — and then counting zero-degree nodes by hand'*. One detector was added for that one case. 2. `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` itself (2026-08-07) — six blind spots, every one found by a human querying by hand. 3. **2026-08-14, today** — 43 live planned capabilities invisible to every tool; the Grok agent *'had to leave the graph and grep the tree'* (`fact:the-build-list-is-suppressed-by-realized-via-component`). ⇒ **Fixing #3 with a detector would be the third time the special case is patched and the general principle is not.** That is the decision-tree overfit he is describing, arrived at empirically rather than as a worry. ═══ ⭐⭐ THE WOOD: ONE SHAPE UNDER MANY FINDINGS ═══ **REFLOW2 REPEATEDLY CANNOT DISTINGUISH 'NOTHING IS WRONG' FROM 'I COULD NOT SEE IT.'** Every instance below was found separately, and they are the same defect: · `unrealized_capability` suppressed by `realized_via_component` reads identically to a capability that is fine — 34 of 39 silenced (today). · The loop nudge state `absent` means BOTH *'not installed'* and *'this harness cannot have one'* — only one is actionable (today, `req:an-unavailable-loop-trigger-is-named-as-unavailable`). · `loop_status`'s sync reported the record `in_step` while `compare_designs` reported `identical: false` on the same file (today). · `dec:loop-status-cannot-say-it-never-looked` — ALREADY RECORDED: *'clean' and 'never scanned' are one answer.* · `coverage_report` exists **solely** to fix this for ARTIFACTS: *'a design covering 30% of a system reports the same 0 open gaps as one covering all of it.'* It is a point solution to the general problem. · AGENTS.md already states the rule and leaves it to the agent's virtue: *'`0 gaps` means NOTHING WAS DETECTED — never nothing is wrong.'* ⇒ **THE GENERALISABLE MOVE IS NOT ANOTHER DETECTOR. IT IS MAKING NON-OBSERVATION A FIRST-CLASS RESULT** — every reported clean state carrying what it did not look at, what it suppressed and why. `coverage_report` proves the shape works; nothing generalises it. ═══ 🛑 AND THE SECOND HALF OF THE BIG PICTURE: WHO IS ASKING ═══ The other thread running through today is that **reflow2's reports have no notion of AUDIENCE OR PURPOSE**, so unrelated concerns share one surface: · `loop_status.next` leads with 78 never-asked gaps when the user's question was *'what do we build next?'* — the Grok report's item 8: *'the loop and the delivery plan share a dashboard and they should not.'* · Gap ranking mixes design hygiene with unbuilt accepted scope (their item 3). · All ten rendered views slice by ASPECT and none by ALTITUDE (`dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect`). ⇒ Coherence maintenance and delivery planning are two jobs sharing one dashboard. **A remaining-work answer may therefore be a VIEW over what the graph already computes rather than a new detector** — which is also the anti-overfit route, since a view adds no new judgement to the instrument. ═══ SO WHAT IS REFLOW2 FOR? THE ANSWER THE GRAPH ALREADY GIVES ═══ Assembled from accepted nodes rather than invented here: reflow2 is the **persistent coherent design memory** that outlives a context window — it CAPTURES intent, COMPUTES what follows from it (`req:completion-computed`: delivery is computed from the golden thread, never asserted), REPORTS rather than judges (`dec:report-dont-judge`), ASKS rather than repairs (`dec:ask-not-repair`), and leaves the deciding to the human (`dec:three-party-checks`). **Nothing in that charter says reflow2 must enumerate every possible defect kind.** It says its answers must be honest about their own reach — which is the requirement above, and which no amount of detector-adding satisfies. OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) **REPORT SUPPRESSION AS DATA** — wherever a detector deliberately declines to fire, count it and say so (*'34 capabilities not asked about: their component already has an artifact'*). Generalises across every detector, adds no new judgement, and directly serves `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots`. Counter: needs a convention every detector honours, and an unhonoured convention is worse than none. (b) **A DELIVERY VIEW SEPARATE FROM THE LOOP SURFACE** — remaining work as a projection over data already held, leaving detectors untouched. Answers the narrow question and the audience half. Counter: does not stop the next blind spot being found by hand. (c) **A REQUIREMENT THAT EVERY REPORTED CLEAN STATE CARRIES ITS OWN REACH.** The strongest general form and the hardest: it constrains every existing report at once, and `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` would demand something compute it. (d) **ADD A DETECTOR FOR THE BUILD LIST.** The narrow fix. **Named as the option this node exists to question**, and the one that has already been taken twice with the recorded result that the next instance was found by hand. (e) **NOTHING — accept that agents must read `0 gaps` sceptically.** Counter: AGENTS.md already asks exactly that, in bold, and three agents in three weeks still had to find blind spots by hand. **An instruction that has failed three times is evidence about instructions, not about the agents.** ⚠️ THE HONEST RISK IN (a) AND (c): a report that lists everything it did not look at can drown the thing it did find. `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` already warns about the mirror failure — reaching zero findings by asking only easy questions — so both directions have a way to look good while being useless, and whichever is taken needs a measurement rather than a feeling.		Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's explicit request to step back before fixing. Recorded as its own question rather than folded into the remaining-work decision because the two are separately answerable and answering only the narrow one is the failure this node names. The load-bearing evidence is that the project already accepted the general principle in `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` and has now failed it three times — so the overfitting concern is measured history rather than a hypothetical, and the third instance was in hand before he raised it. The 'what is reflow2 for' summary is deliberately assembled from already-accepted nodes rather than composed fresh, since a charter invented in one session to justify one fix would be the same overfit at a higher level.proposedOPEN — should reflow2 measure a design's BREADTH against its DEPTH and prompt a step back? It is measurable, reflow2's own design is nearly all breadth, and an 'ideal ratio' would be the overfit the idea exists to prevent, OPEN — how should 'what is left to build?' be answered, given the artifact layer is modelled at COMPONENT granularity and therefore cannot answer it at all?
OPEN — should reflow2 build SME augmentation, the LLM-as-subject-matter-expert pass? Designed in full 2026-07-17, never built, never in the graph
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced 2026-08-11 by reading reflow2's own founding docs against the build, on Anthony's rule: an already-satisfied doc requirement is dropped, a genuinely new one becomes a proposal. Nothing here is intent. WHAT EXISTS: `docs/sme-augmentation.md`, a full design dated 2026-07-17. WHAT IS IN THE GRAPH: nothing. No Capability, no Requirement, no detector. Verified — zero occurrences of `sme_consideration` anywhere in the codebase, and `docs/requirements-coverage.md` carries it as ⬜ twice (GS-10 'SME gaps', EX-SME 'SME augmentation post-pass'). THE IDEA, in the doc's own framing: after faithful extraction, a gated pass in which the LLM adopts expert lenses for the project's domain and operating Environment and surfaces the considerations the user never stated — 'You want to build a house on Mars… launch windows, payload mass budget, teleoperated robots vs suited crew, in-situ resource use, radiation and dust mitigation.' Each proposal labelled on a grounding spectrum (`verified` / `extrapolated` / `speculative` / `contradicts_known`) with domain, evidence and confidence, landing as a supplementary Fragment at `provenance: inferred` via SUPPLEMENTS, surfaced as `sme_consideration` gaps to accept, edit or dismiss. ⭐ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS ⬜ SUGGESTS. The doc calls it 'the capability that most directly serves the vision's premise' — `req:no-se-knowledge` (accepted): the user never needs systems engineering. Every other mechanism reflow2 has REPORTS what the user already said or failed to say. This is the only designed mechanism that would supply expertise the user does not have. Without it, 'the user never needs to know systems engineering' is carried entirely by the ambient agent's ad-hoc judgement, unrecorded and ungraded. ⚠️ THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT AGAINST, and it may be decisive: the agent-native decision (2026-07-18, `dec:` surface-plan) made the ambient coding agent the LLM. An agent reading a brief ALREADY volunteers considerations — that is what agents do. So the question may not be 'should reflow2 build an SME pass' but 'does reflow2 need to MODEL what the agent already does anyway?' The doc's answer is implicitly yes — the value is the GROUNDING SPECTRUM and the `inferred` provenance, so the user can always tell what they said from what was proposed at them. That is a graph-shaped need, not an LLM-shaped one, and it survives the agent-native decision intact. IDEAS, unranked: (a) Build it as designed — a gated pass emitting `sme_consideration` gaps with the grounding spectrum. (b) Build only the RECORDING half: a way to mark a node as agent-proposed-not-user-stated with its grounding, and let the skills do the proposing. Much smaller; keeps the honest-provenance value and drops the pass machinery. (c) Declare it superseded by agent-native capture and retire the doc's requirement rather than leaving it ⬜ forever. (d) Nothing — it has been ⬜ for over three weeks and no user has asked for it. NOTE ON RELEVANCE, which is Anthony's actual question: `provenance: inferred` and the SUPPLEMENTS edge both already exist in the schema, so (b) is closer than (a) looks. Whether anyone WANTS this is unanswered — it has never been put to a user, and no friction report has asked for it.		The only designed mechanism that would supply expertise the user lacks, rather than reporting what they already said. Fully specified, never built, never in the graph. The agent-native decision weakens the case for the pass but not for the grounded-provenance half, which is the part only the graph can hold.proposednothing
OPEN — what evidence says a thread must not break: that it never changed, that it is heavily USED, or asking the person who depends on it?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-13. HIS WORDS: 'how does a requirement (actually the whole chain from idea --> fully implemented/fielded) become immutable? I suppose a user could declare at some point - this lifecycle is immutable, but for could we do something like the less times a full life cycle is adjusted/updated, the more stable it is - eventually becoming immutable - again, some parallels on Q-table from RL. like for instance, in reflow2, there are probably a few lifecycles that that have emerged as statistically stable and rarely changing' ⭐ WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE NODE FROM `dec:idea-a-satisfied-requirement-earns-a-stricter-mutability-class`. That node's triggers are all STATE-based — satisfied, verified, operational, shipped in a deployed release. This one is EVIDENCE-based: protection is inferred from observed behaviour rather than from a lifecycle position. They compose; they are not the same mechanism. 📌 AND SEPARATE FROM `dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important`, which shares the RL framing and asks the opposite question about the opposite signal: that one would raise a node's IMPORTANCE from repeated READS, this one would raise a thread's IMMUTABILITY. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ SHARPENED SAME DAY — THE GOAL IS NOT IMMUTABILITY, IT IS KNOWING WHAT A SECOND USER DEPENDS ON, AND BOTH PROPOSALS ARE PROXIES FOR IT ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Anthony, 2026-08-13, naming where the whole thread came from: 'this all started out of a comment from my brother that was 'As long as it doesn't mess with the core functionality.' however, I don't know exactly how he uses reflow2. so trying to figure out something that is either use based (something that is used a lot is probably liked and stable) or has not changed (what we just discussed).' ⭐⭐ **THAT REFRAMES BOTH PROPOSALS AS PROXIES FOR ONE UNOBSERVABLE: what Alex depends on.** 'Core functionality' is HIS phrase about HIS usage, and the reason a mechanism is being designed at all is that the fact is not available. Every option below should be judged on how well it stands in for asking him — not on how elegant the metric is. 🛑 **AND THE BASELINE ANY PROXY MUST BEAT IS: ASK HIM.** He is one message away, `dec:three-party-checks` says the human decides, and a point-blank question returns the fact itself rather than a correlate of it. The honest case for a proxy is NOT that it beats asking Alex — it is that it generalises to the users who cannot be asked, which is the actual product case. Recorded so the cheap answer is not skipped on the way to the interesting one. ═══ ⭐⭐⭐ THE GRAPH ALREADY PARTLY ANSWERS 'I DON'T KNOW HOW HE USES IT' ═══ `fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11` records Alex's own working path VERBATIM, and it is more specific than either proxy would produce: step 1 'record those at a high level' -> capture-intent NOT NAMED BY HIM step 2 'now let's order them' -> plan-increments NOT NAMED BY HIM step 3 'tackle them one at a time' -> his own framing step 4 'and brainstorm' -> brainstorm NAMED, he types it entry 'basically been using /where-am-i' -> where-am-i NAMED, he types it 🛑🛑 **AND THIS IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT DAMAGES THE USE-BASED PROXY, taken from the one real second user we have.** A usage counter would have found `where-am-i` and `brainstorm` — the two he TYPES — and would have scored `capture-intent` and `plan-increments` at ZERO, even though he performs their function every session in his own words. **USE TELEMETRY MEASURES WHAT GETS INVOKED, NOT WHAT GETS DEPENDED ON**, and for this project the gap between those is not incidental: it is `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`, ACCEPTED, whose whole content is that the trigger mechanism does not reach the user. ⇒ Worse for the proxy: the thing Alex most obviously depends on is the thing NOTHING would count. His four-step path silently assumes the design is still there and still coherent between sessions. No skill invocation represents 'the graph still says what I told it last week.' ═══ THE USE-BASED BRANCH IS NOT A NEW IDEA — IT IS A DESIGNED, UNBUILT THREAD ═══ `req:reflow2-can-say-which-of-its-own-skills-a-session-reached-for` ACCEPTED, and it is one of the top open gaps: NOTHING SATISFIES IT. 'recorded automatically, reported without judgement.' `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` OPEN — where the log lives. `what_next` ranks it SECOND of the unmarked decisions (1 governed, 1 scheduled into an increment). `dec:idea-measure-the-surface` OPEN — should real telemetry shape the surface, how far. `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` ACCEPTED — the verb, never the object. `dec:the-telemetry-kpp-question-waits-for-flo2` DEFERRED, with its trigger named. 🛑 **THE FATAL CONSTRAINT ON THE USE-BASED BRANCH, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL: THE SIGNAL IS ON ALEX'S MACHINE.** Every design graph is local (`dec:multi-writer-architecture`); his usage never touches this store. So 'used a lot' is unmeasurable HERE by construction, and no amount of instrumenting reflow2's own repo produces it — it would measure Anthony's usage and call it Alex's. ⭐⭐ **WHICH MAKES THE PREREQUISITE A DECISION THAT SCORES ZERO — AND ALEX ASKED FOR IT HIMSELF.** `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` ('should reflow2 ask, once, whether a project wants to send feedback back, and record that consent in the graph?') is the gate on ever seeing another user's usage. `what_next` surfaced it as the **`unexplored` draw — score 0, nothing in the graph points at it.** And `fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11` records Alex requesting exactly it: *'You should put in an update that asks me if I want to collect feedback and store my decision in the graph or something. That way you get what you want.'* ⇒ **THE SECOND USER ASKED FOR THE MECHANISM THAT WOULD ANSWER HIS OWN CONCERN, AND THE GRAPH SCORES IT AT ZERO BECAUSE NOTHING POINTS AT IT.** This is precisely the failure `what_next`'s exploration band exists for, arriving on a real question rather than as a worry about ranking. 📌 AND `bl-155` APPLIES TO THE USE PROXY UNCHANGED: reflow2 cannot tell 'unused' from 'unreachable'. `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` already drew the consequence — counts may justify OPTIMISING and never, alone, justify CUTTING. A mutability class derived from use would be using counts to decide what is protected, which is the mirror of the move that rule forbids, and it inherits the same blindness: the four skills Alex never invokes are unreached, not unwanted. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ THE Q-TABLE FRAMING IS ALREADY SETTLED DOCTRINE HERE, AND IT ARRIVES IN THIS DOMAIN WITH ONE TERM ANSWERED DIFFERENTLY ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ `dec:attention-is-measured-behaviourally-not-lexically` is **ACCEPTED** on Anthony's own word (2026-08-10). Its three consequences apply verbatim and should not be re-derived: (1) **A Q-VALUE DECAYS AND A COUNTER DOES NOT.** Here it bites harder: 'has not changed in three months' IS a recency statement. (2) **VISIT COUNT IS NOT VALUE — and there, the analogy BROKE:** *'THERE IS NO REWARD SIGNAL… The RL framing supplies STRUCTURE (decay, exploration) and does NOT supply the thing that makes Q-learning converge.'* ⭐⭐ **THIS IS WHERE THE DOMAINS PART.** A design thread HAS a reward signal already in the graph — 40 DriftEvents, verification runs with `last_run_at`, `OBSOLETES`, releases reaching an Environment. Contact with reality, observed rather than proxied. **Note this beats BOTH of Anthony's candidates on their own terms**: it is neither 'was not edited' nor 'was invoked often', but 'was exercised and did not break.' (3) **THE EXPLORATION TRAP.** For stability it is a feedback loop with the sign wrong: the harder something is to change, the less it is revisited, the more stable it scores. ═══ HIS EMPIRICAL CLAIM, TESTED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN 2026-08-13 ═══ ChangeEvents per ACCEPTED requirement (110): 0→67 1→21 2→21 5→1 ChangeEvents per Capability (152): 0→58 1→52 2→22 3→10 4→6 5→2 6→1 7→2 whole-thread (req + caps + artifacts) zero-change: 6 of 110 CHANGED edges land: art 555 · cap 180 · req 87 · dec 62 · cmp 43 · other 59 🛑🛑 **AT NODE LEVEL THE METRIC INVERTS.** `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` carries an 8,842-character statement; the sibling node records +4,770 characters appended in a single session. Its history: **0 ChangeEvents, 0 Snapshots.** ⇒ **THE MOST HEAVILY REWRITTEN REQUIREMENT IN THE DESIGN SCORES MAXIMALLY STABLE.** It measures RECORDING DISCIPLINE. 🛑 **AT THREAD LEVEL IT FAILS THE OPPOSITE WAY**, and the thread is the unit he chose: only 6 of 110 are quiet, because artifact churn dominates. Intent-only scoping (req 87 + dec 62 = 149 against art 555) may rescue it. ═══ THE OPTIONS, none taken ═══ A — COUNT RECORDED REVISIONS, threshold into a mutability class. **The measurements say do not build it**: it ranks the worst offenders safest. B — FIX THE RECORD FIRST, then count. Require a revision to a satisfied requirement to leave a Snapshot + ChangeEvent. Already named on the sibling node as 'the cheapest honest option', and a prerequisite either way. C — SCORE ON EVIDENCE OF EXERCISE, NOT ON SILENCE OR ON INVOCATION. Checks that have RUN and passed across releases, no DriftEvent, no OBSOLETES. The only option with a real reward term, immune to the recording hole, and **local — it needs nothing from Alex's machine**. Expensive: 37 of 139 verifications have never run. D — SCOPE THE COUNTER TO INTENT ONLY (Requirement + Decision). Restores thread-level signal; concedes the code cannot be frozen. E — WITHHOLD UNTIL THE HABIT EXISTS. `consumption.rs`'s `MIN_MODELLED_RATIO` shape: **absence is only informative when presence is the habit.** F — USE-BASED, and it is a DEPENDENT rather than an alternative. Blocked on `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` (consent), `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` (where the log lives) and `req:reflow2-can-say-which-of-its-own-skills-a-session-reached-for` (unsatisfied). Bounded by `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content`. **And measured against the one real second user it would have missed half his workflow.** G — ASK ALEX. Returns the fact rather than a correlate, costs one message, does not generalise. **The baseline the others must beat.** ⇒ **C IS THE STRONGEST ON THE EVIDENCE** — it is the only candidate that is local, has a genuine reward term, and cannot be fooled by silence — with **B** as its prerequisite for anything history-shaped and **E** as the guard. **F is worth having for its own sake** (it answers 'what do users reach for', which is an accepted unmet requirement) but is a poor instrument for THIS question. **G should happen regardless.** ═══ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea ═══ TIME-WITHOUT-CHANGE AND CORRECTNESS ARE NOT THE SAME THING, and neither are USE AND CORRECTNESS. A requirement nobody revisited may be settled, forgotten, or wrong in a way nobody looked hard enough to notice; a heavily-used path may be heavily used because it is unavoidable rather than because it is liked. Both proxies would make reflow2 most confident where it has looked least — and `bl-155`'s unused-versus-unreachable finding, now restated four times in this design, says the graph cannot tell the difference from inside. NOT DECIDED. The narrow question worth answering first is unchanged and now trebly supported — by both mutability proposals and by the use branch, which cannot detect a silent rewrite either: **should a revision to a satisfied requirement be required to leave a trace?**		Captured from Anthony's own framing, then SHARPENED the same day when he named where the thread came from: Alex's 'as long as it doesn't mess with the core functionality', plus 'I don't know exactly how he uses reflow2.' That reframes both candidates as PROXIES for one unobservable — what a second user depends on — and the right test for each becomes how well it stands in for asking him. THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING OF THE SHARPENING: the graph already partly answers the question. fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11 records Alex's working path verbatim, and it shows the use-based proxy would have found the two skills he TYPES (where-am-i, brainstorm) and scored at zero the two whose function he performs every session without naming (capture-intent, plan-increments). Use telemetry measures what is invoked, not what is depended on — which is req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session, accepted, firing again. AND THE STRUCTURAL BLOCK: every design graph is local, so Alex's usage never reaches this store. The prerequisite is dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded — which what_next surfaced as its zero-scoring `unexplored` draw, and which Alex himself asked for. The second user requested the mechanism that would answer his own concern, and the graph scores it at zero because nothing points at it. Recorded separately from the state-based sibling because the trigger differs in kind, and separately from the search-attention nodes because those raise IMPORTANCE from reads while this raises IMMUTABILITY.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 adopt OpenMBEE's rule that every interface speaks an open, published protocol?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a first-pass review of openmbee.org — website, repository listing and one truncated architecture page. THE OBSERVATION: Flexo's stated guiding principle is 'to adopt open, web-compatible standards for data exchange at every interface, including for both data format and exchange protocols', realised as a layered stack of micro-services where each layer is independently developed, tested and replaced, and where the seams speak SPARQL, GraphQL, OSLC and SysML v2. WHY THIS ONE IS UNCOMFORTABLE RATHER THAN MERELY INTERESTING: reflow2 measured its own seam band at 0.0% on 2026-08-03 — 73 component-to-component couplings, none of them running through a declared contract that one side provides and another consumes. BL-179 establishes that this is a NORMAL POSITION for a design that correctly did function first, and that finding stands. But OpenMBEE is a design of comparable ambition that made seam declaration a FOUNDING principle rather than a later phase, and holding the two side by side is the fairest available test of whether function-first is a trajectory or an excuse. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is not weak: standards at every interface is a rule with a price — it is why Flexo is a multi-service deployment where reflow2 is a single binary and a file in a repository, and `dec:install-once-per-machine` plus `req:thin-install` are commitments in the opposite direction. An internal seam between two modules of one binary does not need SPARQL; it needs to exist and be named. THE NARROWER VERSION WORTH TAKING SERIOUSLY: not 'every interface speaks a web standard' but 'every seam is DECLARED', which is reflow2's own `req:key-interfaces` already, unmet at 0%. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether declaring reflow2's internal seams changes any computation — `dec:edge-orthogonality` says a distinction earns its keep only when something reads it, and today the seams band reads it, which is one reader more than there was a week ago.		Recorded through the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request. The claim of strength here is about the PRINCIPLE as stated, not about its execution: the architecture page was truncated on fetch, no source was read, and whether Flexo's interfaces actually hold that line is unknown and is exactly what the deep review should test. Recorded beside the counter-argument per the skill's rule that an idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning while an idea recorded with its objection keeps both — and the objection here is real, since reflow2's single-binary posture is a deliberate decision rather than an oversight.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 speak SysML v2 at its boundary, given that is where the standards gravity has moved?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a first-pass review of openmbee.org — website and repository listing only, deep review pending. THE OBSERVATION: OpenMBEE's active development is not its stable product. MMS 4 stores models in SQL; the successor, Flexo / MMS 5, moves to an RDF quadstore and is described as 'GitHub for graphs', exposing SPARQL, GraphQL, OSLC and a SysML v2 API. A separate experimental SysML v2 execution environment (`Systemica`, Go) is also under way. Commits across those repositories were days old when reviewed (July–August 2026), so this is a live bet, not an aspiration. WHERE reflow2 STANDS: it has its own vocabulary — 29 node types, 60 edge types — and no standard interchange of any kind. It publishes three interfaces (`ifc:core-api`, `ifc:graph-export`, `ifc:mcp-tools`), and `export_surface` already emits a subset of a design deliberately. THE QUESTION IS NOT WHETHER TO ADOPT SysML v2 INTERNALLY — the vocabulary is load-bearing and `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` and `req:functional-vocabulary-computes` both depend on it — but whether reflow2 should be able to SPEAK it at the edge, in and out. THE ARGUMENT FOR: Anthony works in a defence/aerospace systems-engineering context and will be asked, professionally, why a design tool does not interoperate with the standard his field is converging on. An export that a SysML v2 service can ingest is a different claim from an export only reflow2 reads. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: SysML v2 is large, its tooling is young, and a partial mapping that silently drops what it cannot express would be worse than none — reflow2's whole posture is that a lossy translation must be reported, not quietly performed. Mapping 29 types onto SysML v2 would need the same no-silent-drop discipline `changelog_view` holds with `unmapped`. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether a faithful SUBSET mapping exists that reports what it could not carry.		Recorded through the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request to capture, as proposed ideas, the areas where OpenMBEE is stronger than reflow2 — before a deep review he intends to run against a clone of their repository. The strength claimed here is narrow and should be read narrowly: OpenMBEE has committed to a standard interchange and reflow2 has none. Whether their SysML v2 implementation is any good is exactly what the deep review is for, and nothing in this node asserts that it is.proposednothing
OPEN — should the Environment / EnvironmentRule compliance layer be built? The schema declares it, nothing writes or reads it, and it is what makes 'design a house' concrete
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced 2026-08-11 reading reflow2's founding docs against the build. Nothing here is intent. MEASURED, not assumed: EnvironmentRule instances in this design 0 QualityGate instances 0 occurrences of `unchecked_compliance` in the code 0 occurrences of `open_violation` in the code 0 typed constructor for EnvironmentRule none `docs/requirements-coverage.md` carries it as ⬜ three times (GS-9 compliance gaps, WS-4 the write side, WS-5 QualityGate) and its own 'Dormant schema scaffolding' section lists Environment compliance as deferred-not-dead. THE IDEA, from `docs/operating-environment.md` (2026-07-17): a design never exists in a vacuum. A house in Kennewick WA must meet city ordinances, county rules, state requirements, building and fire codes, seismic provisions and occupancy limits; the same house on Mars faces 0.38 g, no atmosphere, radiation shielding, pressure vessels and life support. Change the environment, change the entire constraint space. `Project OPERATES_IN Environment`; `Environment IMPOSES EnvironmentRule()`; compliance emits `COMPLIES_WITH` or `VIOLATES_RULE`; two detectors (`unchecked_compliance`, `open_violation`) ask the human; swapping the environment is a first-class ChangeEvent that re-evaluates every compliance edge. ⭐ THE DISTINCTION IT CARRIES IS ALREADY IN THE SCHEMA AND IS GOOD: three kinds of rule, kept apart. `Constraint` is SELF-IMPOSED ('budget under $500k'). `DesignRule` is a CHOSEN convention ('branch before pushing'). `EnvironmentRule` is EXTERNALLY IMPOSED — the design cannot negotiate it, only comply, seek a variance, or fail. Only the third is dictated by the world. reflow2 uses the middle one heavily (9 DesignRules, and this session settled the enforcement question on one); it has never used the third at all. ⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER, and it is strong: reflow2's own domain is SOFTWARE, where the operating environment rarely imposes an authoritative external ruleset, so dogfooding will never exercise this. Every instance would come from a consumer designing a house, a spacecraft or a regulated system — and no such consumer exists yet. Building it would mean building on the doc's argument alone, with no field evidence, which is the opposite of how everything else here has been decided. `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` cuts BOTH ways on this: the third party is exactly who would need it, and no third party has asked. ⭐ AND IT IS ANTHONY'S ACTUAL DOMAIN. Space Force systems engineering and NSLS-II beamline work both sit in heavily-regulated operating environments with externally imposed rulesets. The one person using reflow2 is in the domain the feature was designed for and has not reached for it — which is either evidence it is not needed, or evidence that nothing surfaces it. Those are opposite readings of the same silence and nothing distinguishes them today. IDEAS, unranked: (a) Build the whole layer — constructors, the two detectors, the swap-the-environment ChangeEvent. (b) Build only the WRITE side (constructors for EnvironmentRule + OPERATES_IN/IMPOSES/COMPLIES_WITH) and no detector, so somebody can record a regulation and see whether the vocabulary fits before a detector is written for it. Contradicts the project's own standing rule that a write side should land WITH its read side (requirements-coverage's WS-4/WS-5 note says exactly this and defers both on purpose). (c) Retire the scaffolding — `QualityGate` and `EnvironmentRule` are two of the five node types with zero instances, and the project's own test is 'unused AND redundant → retire; unused AND not-redundant → defer'. (d) Ask a consumer first. Nothing here is urgent, and the deciding evidence is a real design in a regulated environment.		Three doc requirements, a schema layer, and a worked Kennewick-vs-Mars argument, all dating to 2026-07-17 with zero instances and zero code. The vocabulary distinction it carries — self-imposed vs chosen vs externally imposed — is sound and already in the schema. What is missing is any evidence a user wants it, including from the one user whose own domain is regulated.proposednothing
DECIDED — a graph reports when the shared record has moved ahead of it, gated on a computed content hash, and never acts on it
DECIDED 2026-08-11, Anthony's word: 'yes, I like option A - let's implement.' OPTION A CHOSEN — speak on read, gated on the hash. B, C and D are recorded below as considered and not taken. HIS FRAMING, and it was the right diagnosis: 'It sounds like we have the tool, just not used well or surfaced.' ⚠️ THE TOOL WAS ALREADY BUILT. `import_graph` takes a `path`, so an agent catches a graph up with the committed record in ONE TOOL CALL and no terminal at all. The CLI flag `--import` is a second route for people without an agent, not the only one. So nothing new was needed on the doing side — only on the noticing side. ⭐⭐ THE MEASURED FINDING THAT SHAPED THE BUILD: `provenance::last_synced` — the content hash this seat believes is at a given path — was WRITTEN BY TWO PATHS AND READ BY ONE. `record_sync` is called by `export_graph` (exchange.rs:207) and by `import_graph` (exchange.rs:382); `last_synced()` was read at exchange.rs:171, inside `export_graph`, and nowhere else. **The design knew at the first moment of a session and spoke at the last** — when you tried to export, hours later, and the stale-seat refusal finally fired. Same family as `dec:one-retire-edge`'s 'a marker nothing reads is a comment', except here something did read it, at the wrong moment. 🛑 AND THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT THIS NODE FIRST CARRIED WAS FALSE, which is why the option was buildable at all. It said 'I have unexported work' and 'someone else's work has arrived' look similar from inside. They do not: `crates/reflow2-core/src/sync.rs` already distinguishes them exactly. File hash == `last_synced` ⇒ the file has not moved ⇒ every difference is the caller's OWN unexported work ⇒ silent. File hash != `last_synced` ⇒ somebody else has been there ⇒ actionable. One comparison, and no false-positive mode on solo work. WHAT WAS BUILT: `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/sync_debt.rs`, served as the `sync_status` tool and carried on `loop_status` as `record_moved` when there is something to say. One finding per file this seat has synced with — `in_step` / `behind` (the actionable one) / `moved_but_current` / `missing` / `unreadable`. The judgement is BORROWED from `sync::assess_overwrite` rather than reimplemented; this module supplies the enumeration, the gate and the wording. WHY IT LIVES AT THE MCP LAYER: `reflow2-core` does no file I/O, deliberately and repeatedly (`reconcile_artifacts` makes the caller supply hashes; `granularity` and `consumption` both say so). So the check could NOT go into `loop_status` in core, and belongs in the crate that already does this comparison for `export_graph`. 📌 A COST DECISION, PINNED BY A TEST: the export needed to compare against is the expensive half and the hash check is the cheap half, so `mine` is passed as a CLOSURE and is never built on the in-step path — the one every ordinary session takes. `the_expensive_export_is_not_built_on_the_ordinary_path` makes that a guarantee rather than a style choice. 📌 THE DESCRIPTION BUDGET FORCED THE SHAPE OF THE SURFACE: `loop_status`'s tool description was already at 1493 of 1500 characters, so the contract could not be documented there. Hence a dedicated `sync_status` tool carrying the full contract, with `loop_status` carrying only the finding — which is a self-explaining English sentence and needs no schema to interpret. WHAT WAS NOT CHOSEN, kept because the roads not taken are part of the design's memory: - B — AUTO-IMPORT. Closest to what was first asked for. Rejected: `import_graph` is an UPSERT, so an unasked one silently overwrites live session work, and doing it unasked makes it invisible. `dec:ask-not-repair`. - C — REFUSE ON FIRST READ. Rejected: a refusal on READ is heavy-handed, and a session deliberately working from an older design would meet it every time. - D — DOCUMENTATION ONLY. Rejected: the answer this project has already found wanting twice; a discipline written down and not triggered is one that does not happen. ⭐ THE DEPENDENCY STILL HOLDS: if `dec:central-host` goes the hosted way for the flo2 case, this question DISSOLVES for those users — there is no local store to catch up, because there is one graph everyone reads live. It stays live for anyone working from a checkout.		Anthony chose option A on 2026-08-11 after being shown that the tool already existed and only the trigger was missing. `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (accepted 2026-07-25) had already committed this project to building 'merge-on-pull ergonomics' and that clause had never been cashed, so this settles an unbuilt commitment rather than adding new scope. The node keeps its own refuted counter-argument on the record: the claim that unexported work and somebody else's arrival look alike from inside was disproved by reading sync.rs the same day, and it was that refutation which made option A buildable.acceptedA seat reports which shared records have moved ahead of it, and names what arrived
DECIDED — the agent never asks the user to pick a node type: a served interview step carries WHEN and WHAT to ask, a served routing table carries HOW their words map
DECIDED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY: **BOTH (a) AND (b).** A served interview step carries *when and what to ask* — in domain language only — and a served routing table carries *how the user's words map to node types*, plus which artifacts to expect for that kind of thing. His reasoning: **neither half is useful alone.** A skill without a table leaves the mapping improvised, which is the failure Alex hit; a table without a skill is never consulted. Option (c), leaving it to agent judgement, is closed — it has now been observed failing on the second user's first real project. Option (d), detecting it, stays rejected-for-a-reason: the evidence never enters the graph. ⇒ SATISFIES `req:the-kind-of-system-is-established-before-its-parts-are-captured` (captured the same day on Anthony's word, from Alex's report). This decision settles HOW that requirement is delivered; the requirement states WHAT is owed. ⭐⭐ THE PRIOR ART SETTLES THE SHAPE, AND ONLY HALF OF IT SURVIVES — `reflow/workflows/00b-framework_selection.json`, read 2026-08-14 at Anthony's pointer: · **THE TERMINOLOGY REGISTRY** (`definitions/framework_registry.json`: node → `service`/`gene`/`agent`/`species`) was CORRECTLY REJECTED by `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` (now `dropped`) — cosmetic renaming, plus a load-bearing claim that *'framework choice determines which NetworkX analyses are available'*, which gates capability on a self-declared label. **The routing table decided here is NOT that**: it maps the user's phrasing to reflow2's own unchanged vocabulary, and gates nothing. · **THE SEMANTIC-MATCHING INTERVIEW** is what survives, and it is not cosmetic. S-01A: *'Framework selection is an ARCHITECTURAL DECISION, not a configuration choice. Wrong framework = wrong insights.'* LESSON-04: *'Framework abstractions must match system semantics. Workflows are state machines (not services), even though both could be 'engineered systems'.'* **Its first action is 'Ask user to describe the system' — domain language, not node types.** 🛑 **AND THE DROPPED REQUIREMENT HAD ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN THE SURVIVOR.** `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` closes: *'domain as a hint to EXTRACTION and phrasing — what vocabulary the agent uses when talking to the user and reading their documents — without ever gating which computations run. That keeps the honest part of reflow's insight (a biologist should not be told about 'services').'* It was dropped as a registry, its surviving half was named in its own text, **nobody built it, and the second user then walked into exactly that gap.** A road correctly not taken left a fork nobody came back for. ═══════════════════════════════════════════════ RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14. HIS WORDS: *'It was a little unsure of how to store the data models for my project in the graph. It asked me what node types it should store them as. I didn't really know for sure so I told it to figure it out. It worked, but that might be confusing for someone who isn't technical… it should probably ask probing questions to figure this out without exposing internal components of the graph structure to the user.'* ⭐ THE INVERSION IS THE FINDING. Mapping a person's words onto node types IS the agent's job and is written down as such — `capture-intent` exists to turn what the user said into Requirements / Capabilities / Components / Interfaces, and `describe_schema` exists so the AGENT can discover the vocabulary rather than guess. **The agent had both and handed the question back to the user anyway.** The schema is not under-documented here; the labour was returned to the one person in the room with no reason to know the answer. 🛑 AND REFLOW2 CANNOT SEE THIS HAPPEN. Every detector reasons over nodes already in the graph, and a leaked question leaves no node — the user's confusion lives in the conversation, never in the record. `loop_status` would have read perfectly clean through the whole exchange. **Same shape as `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`: a discipline that exists only as an instruction, with nothing able to observe whether it held.** That is the standing argument for why the table matters as much as the skill line: a table can be wrong in public, an improvisation cannot. 📌 IT ALSO WORKED, WHICH IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART. He said *'I told it to figure it out'* and the result was fine. So the cost is not a wrong graph — it is that a non-technical user meeting the same prompt has no such escape, and answering it wrongly would put their design in the wrong shape without either party noticing. THE OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD. (a) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — an interview step in the skills: never ask for a node type; ask about the thing itself and do the mapping yourself. (b) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — a served routing table, phrasing → node type, plus expected artifacts per kind of thing. Precedent: `capture-session` ships one and its first dogfood found a hole in it. (c) LEAVE IT TO AGENT JUDGEMENT — **CLOSED**, observed failing. (d) DETECT IT — rejected for a reason: the evidence never enters the graph, so any check would have to live in the harness and read the conversation. ⚠️ ONE HONEST TENSION, UNCHANGED BY THE DECISION: some vocabulary reaching the user is CORRECT. `where-am-i` reports the design back in their words and gap questions are deliberately plain, so the rule is *never make the user choose the internal category* — not *never say a word from the schema*. Drawn loosely it would produce a skill that fights `describe_schema`'s legitimate use.		Raised under the brainstorm skill from Alex's report and settled the same day on Anthony's word, after reading the reflow prior art he pointed at. The reading changed the shape of the answer: reflow's S-01A turns out to contain two separable things, and reflow2 had dropped both together when only the terminology registry deserved it. Recording that split matters because the surviving half — the semantic-matching interview — was already named in the dropped requirement's own closing paragraph, and a future session finding `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` at `dropped` would otherwise reasonably conclude the whole idea was rejected.acceptedThe agent establishes what KIND of thing is being designed, in the user's own domain language, before it captures the parts — and never by asking the user to pick node types
OPEN — does the quality attribute a system is FOR decide how functions are allocated, and does each attribute need its own graph?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-08. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen. THE IDEA, his words: allocation of functions to systems/services could be driven by what the system is for — 'maybe you allocate functions based on it being fault tolerant or very highly reliable or easily maintainable or based on maximal performance' — and the agent would deduce the likely answer and then ASK ('is this design about performance or reliability or maintainability or highly secure'), because 'answering that question really determines how you allocate functions to which services' and 'if you don't ask upfront, these cost a lot in having to rework services after they've been already developed'. It follows an earlier thought of his in the same conversation: that allocation could be decided by graph theory alone — Leiden communities for clustering, or PageRank to avoid bottlenecks and god nodes — with domain-oriented and function-oriented decomposition 'thrown out the window'. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, checked rather than assumed: the `dimension` enum in schema/dimensions.yaml already carries reliability, performance, maintainability, security, scalability, observability, testability, coupling and maturity, attachable to ANY node; `propose_allocation` already clusters the weighted capability graph with Leiden and never auto-applies; `evaluate_allocation` already computes modularity, misplaced capabilities and god-components as selective articulation points; and `ility_report` (BL-184, from Anthony's own correction on 2026-08-03) already maps those computations onto the axis each one informs, emitting named findings and never a score. SO THE DIRECTION IS THE NEW PART: everything above runs GRAPH → ILITY, reading structure and saying what it implies. This idea runs ILITY → GRAPH, stating the attribute and letting it drive the allocation. Same vocabulary, opposite direction of inference, and that direction does not exist. AN OBSERVATION WORTH KEEPING WHATEVER IS DECIDED: the attribute may change not just the OBJECTIVE FUNCTION but WHICH GRAPH IS BUILT. Performance wants the call-frequency / data-volume graph and minimal cross-boundary chatter, which is what Leiden on DEPENDS_ON.weight already does. Reliability wants no articulation points and may deliberately DUPLICATE a function across services so one failure domain cannot take everything — which directly OPPOSES maximal modularity, since a modularity-optimal partition is often reliability-hostile. Maintainability wants things that change together to live together, which is a CO-CHANGE graph, a different edge set entirely. Security wants boundaries following trust and data classification with some nodes separated regardless of coupling — constrained partitioning, not clustering at all. Four attributes, four different graphs over the same functions; any single 'run Leiden and allocate' answer silently picks performance. THE ONE THAT IS RUNNABLE TODAY, and it is a cheap falsifiable experiment: maintainability. reflow2 already holds 316 ChangeEvents with CHANGED edges, which IS a co-change graph, already populated, needing no instrumentation — cluster it and diff against evaluate_allocation's current map to see whether things that change together are allocated together. Performance is NOT runnable: evaluate_allocation reports total_internal 1, total_external 0, unweighted_dependencies 1 — one capability-to-capability dependency edge in the whole design, unweighted, which is why modularity reads a meaningless 1.00. Reliability and security have no substrate at all yet. COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea rather than used to argue it down: (1) a service boundary carries obligations no coupling graph encodes — deployment unit, failure domain, team ownership, release cadence, data residency, regulatory scope — so two functions Leiden puts together may belong apart because one is audited and one is not, and no resolution parameter can see that; (2) this project has already paid twice for metric-driven verdicts, retiring `unexpected_coupling` because it fired on correct architecture ('that coupling IS the product') and accepting SPOFs deliberately in dec:sanitize-spof-accepted and dec:service-spof-accepted, so a purely metric-driven allocator would flag all three and be wrong each time; (3) clustering on ESTIMATED weights is an opinion with extra steps and a modularity score on top, which is worse than the opinion because it looks objective — the schema's own weight_basis (estimated / evidence / measured) exists to keep that distinction visible. WHERE THE IDEA IS STRONGEST, narrower than 'replace the old methods': it makes allocation ARGUABLE. Today domain-versus-function is unfalsifiable and the louder voice wins; computing modularity, bottleneck centrality and cross-boundary weight for candidate allocations turns it into evidence — which is the shape register_alternative / analyze_alternatives already have, with dec:parallel-alternatives putting AoA alternatives in design-space via CONTRADICTS.		Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent. Three things make it worth keeping even if none of it is built: the ility-to-graph direction is genuinely absent while its whole vocabulary is present; the four-graphs observation would change what any future allocation feature computes rather than merely how it weights; and the co-change experiment is runnable today on data already in the graph, which makes at least one branch falsifiable now instead of after instrumentation. The counter-arguments are recorded beside rather than against — an idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning, an idea recorded with its objection keeps both.proposednothing
OPEN — should the kit ship a command that tells a project how it is out of date, instead of every agent re-deriving the migration?
UNSETTLED. Six things are mechanically decidable and none is currently reported: (1) is anything under `.reflow2/` tracked by git; (2) are the MCP configs tracked, carrying absolute paths meaningless on another machine; (3) does `.reflow2/kit-version.json` match the installed kit; (4) do local skill copies exist and differ from the served ones, given a local copy silently SHADOWS the served one; (5) is `--graph-path` absolute rather than relative-and-cwd-dependent; (6) is a committed export present, and current against the live graph. SHAPES, not a recommendation: (a) extend `reflow2_init.py --check`, which already reports what a run would change and already owns the stamp and the skill mirrors — smallest, and it means one command answers 'what would change' and 'what is wrong'; (b) a separate `reflow2_doctor.py` beside `reflow2_check.py`, on the argument that 'would this install change files' and 'is this project's reflow2 setup sane' are different questions with different audiences; (c) fold the checks into `check_kit_manifest.py`, which already compares the stamp and is closest in spirit; (d) decline, and put the six checks in a served skill instead, on the ground that an agent can run git itself and instructions are cheaper than code. WHATEVER THE SHAPE, IT REPORTS AND DOES NOT REPAIR: `git rm --cached` is a judgement about someone's history, and rewriting an MCP config is not something to do silently. Name the finding, name the remedy, let the human run it — the same split `dec:ask-not-repair` draws for merges. AND IT CANNOT BE AN MCP TOOL: `dec:agent-navigates-content` keeps reflow2 out of file IO, and every check above reads the filesystem or shells to git. The kit is the home; the machinery is half-built there already.		Raised because the evidence arrived in an unusually clean form. `req:thin-install` is ACCEPTED and quotes Alex asking for exactly this on 2026-07-25; `cap:skills-served` delivered the forward half; and on 2026-08-08 Alex — the requirement's own author — spent eight manual steps escaping a 0.11.0 kit under a 0.24.0 binary, because nothing exists for a project installed BEFORE served skills. TWO AGENTS DERIVED THAT MIGRATION INDEPENDENTLY THE SAME DAY AND DISAGREED: his eight steps against my seven, overlapping on six. His included a regression (rewriting `--graph-path` to a relative path, the configuration `dec:no-design-here-never-looked` records as minting an accidental third graph in Anthony's own repo); mine got the stamp filename wrong on first pass. Neither was careless — the knowledge is scattered across the installer source, three accepted decisions and two verifications, and is re-derived per session. That is the failure reflow2's own instructions name as its reason to exist, pointed at the migration rather than the design. Evidence: fact:defect-a-pre-served-skills-install-is-stranded and fact:defect-installer-cannot-warn-that-the-graph-dir-is-already-tracked.proposednothing
DECIDED — a harness that cannot take the loop nudge is TOLD so, and the announcement distinguishes 'not installed' from 'cannot be installed here'
DECIDED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY: **ANNOUNCE THE ABSENCE (option c)** — install what the named harness can take, and say plainly when it gets no loop trigger. Option (b), registering a real per-harness equivalent, was NOT rejected: it is compatible with this and remains available wherever an event model turns out to exist. Option (a), leaving it Claude-only and silent, is closed. ⭐⭐ AND READING `cap:nudge-path-proven` BEFORE CAPTURING CHANGED WHAT THIS REQUIRES. **The absence is ALREADY announced.** That capability is VERIFIED and its backstop reports `installed | absent | broken | unknown`, carried both on the handshake instructions — *'the one channel every session reads unasked'* — and as a machine-readable field on `loop_status`. A naive reading of 'announce the absence' would have rebuilt something that exists. 🛑 **THE ACTUAL GAP IS NARROWER AND SHARPER: THE ANNOUNCEMENT CANNOT SAY WHY.** The backstop looks for a registered Stop hook. On an OpenCode or Grok project it finds none and reports `absent` — which is TRUE and reads as *'you forgot to install this'*. **It tells the user to fix something they cannot fix.** That is a different state from a Claude project where the hook was genuinely skipped, and reporting them identically sends one of the two users on an impossible errand. ⇒ SO THE REQUIREMENT IS A DISTINCTION, NOT A NEW ANNOUNCEMENT: *not installed here* (fixable — install it) versus *cannot be installed here* (permanent — the harness has no hook, so the loop is yours to run by hand). `absent` currently means both. 📌 WHY THIS FOLLOWS FROM THE PREVIOUS DECISION RATHER THAN MERELY SITTING BESIDE IT. `dec:idea-init-asks-which-harness-and-installs-only-that` (ACCEPTED, same day) makes init ASK which harness. Once the user has NAMED OpenCode, handing them silence about a missing safety net is exactly the silent-wrong-install failure that decision was taken to avoid. **Asking makes staying quiet indefensible: the moment the user tells you their harness, you owe them an honest answer about what it can and cannot have.** 🛑 A STALE CLAIM FOUND WHILE READING, AND IT IS A REAL DEFECT: `cap:nudge-path-proven`'s description ends *'This matters because reflow2_init installs no hooks at all: every consumer project has no session-end nudge, and until now nothing said so.'* **That is no longer true.** `ensure_hooks` registers four events (SessionStart, two PostToolUse matchers, Stop) into `.claude/settings.local.json`, measured by running init on 2026-08-14. A VERIFIED capability is carrying a claim about a peer that changed underneath it — the description was right when written and nothing re-read it. Worth correcting on its own, and worth noting as another instance of a fact that no computation reads and therefore nothing rechecks. ═══ THE ANALYSIS THIS WAS DECIDED FROM ═══ RAISED AS BRAINSTORMING by Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14 — the parenthetical half of his settings note, NOT covered by the upsert fix that closed the rest of it. HIS WORDS: *'`reflow2 init .` should upsert `settings.local.json` **(or whatever settings file is relevant for the agent harness)** instead of replacing it.'* ✅ MEASURED ON HEAD (`cbb1a19`): `ensure_hooks` writes to exactly ONE path — `project/.claude/settings.local.json`. `MCP_CONFIGS` generates three harnesses' server configs; `HOOK_EVENTS` is registered for one. **A project opened in OpenCode, Grok CLI or Copilot gets the MCP server and no loop nudge at all.** 🛑 WHY THAT IS MORE THAN AN INSTALLER ASYMMETRY: the served instructions argue for the hook in the strongest terms available — *'a discipline that depends on being remembered loses to urgency every time; fire it on a trigger, not on virtue'* — and say so because real use showed an agent under load keeps ADDING NODES while the capture→detect→ask→decide loop silently stops. Those harnesses run reflow2 with exactly the mechanism removed that exists because virtue was measured to fail. ⭐ IT COMPOUNDS WITH A SIBLING FINDING: `dec:idea-the-graph-vocabulary-never-reaches-the-user` records that reflow2 cannot observe an agent misbehaving in conversation. Here it cannot observe an agent that was never nudged either. Both are disciplines with no observer — and on a non-Claude harness there is not even a trigger. 📌 A SMALLER TELL IN THE SAME FILE: in `IGNORE_LINES`, `.mcp.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json` each carry an explanatory comment while `opencode.json` and `.vscode/mcp.json` get an empty one.
