The Claude path is the travelled one. THE OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD. (a) LEAVE IT Claude-only. **CLOSED** — after the asking decision, a named harness getting silence is indefensible. (b) REGISTER A PER-HARNESS EQUIVALENT, same generator shape as `MCP_CONFIGS`. Not chosen now, not rejected: needs a real event model per harness, and a wrong guess produces the silently-broken hook `ensure_hooks` already refuses to create. **Ship where an event model is confirmed to exist.** (c) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — announce the absence. (d) MOVE THE TRIGGER OFF THE HARNESS — the server sees every tool call. Counter that keeps it unchosen: the server cannot block a session's stop, which is the one moment the nudge is worth most. ⚠️ VERSION CAVEAT: two of Alex's five notes describe defects already fixed, so he is probably on an older kit (`fact:second-user-notes-2026-08-14-two-items-already-fixed`). Measurements here are against HEAD.		Raised under the brainstorm skill and settled the same day on Anthony's word. The capture deliberately read `cap:nudge-path-proven` in full BEFORE writing the requirement, and that read changed the answer: the announcement the decision asks for already exists, so the honest requirement is the DISTINCTION the existing announcement cannot draw rather than a second announcement beside it. Recorded that way so a later session does not build a duplicate reporter and then wonder why two things report the nudge. The stale sentence found in that capability's description is kept here as a finding rather than silently fixed, because a verified capability carrying an out-of-date claim about a peer is worth someone deciding about, not worth an agent quietly editing.acceptedA harness that cannot carry the loop nudge is told so, distinctly from one that merely has not installed it
OPEN — should the loop be able to SUBSCRIBE to reality, rather than only seeing what an agent hand-carries into it?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Raised by an external agent-side field report, 2026-08-11 (fact:external-agent-side-report-2026-08-11, redacted); it is that report's own synthesis and the strongest thing in it. THEIR SENTENCE: 'reality moves outside the graph, and the loop only sees what the agent hand-carries in. Cheapening that carry (asks, re-runs, artifacts, cross-graph facts) is where the remaining leverage is.' WHAT THEY OBSERVED. The liveliest facts of their month — merged PRs, a review round addressed, a suite re-verified, work scheduled — all landed in commits and PR threads, and almost none reached the graph unless an agent chose to carry them. Three of their separate complaints turn out to be ONE complaint: re-running a check is paperwork so `last_run_at` rots; registering an Artifact is the least-rewarding capture so realization sits at zero while PRs merge; asking a question in prose does not register so the ledger nags about work already done. Each was filed as its own friction. They share a cause. ⭐ CORROBORATED HERE THE SAME DAY, WITHOUT COORDINATION. A session in this repo edited a served skill and recorded no ChangeEvent. `loop_status` reported `undispositioned_drift: 0` — which means NO DETECTOR HAD LOOKED AT THE CHANGED FILE, not that nothing changed. The Stop hook caught it; the cheap loop call could not. That is the same defect their report describes from the other side, and it is already recorded at reflow2_feedback.md:539 by a third project. IDEAS, unranked: (a) Make the CARRY cheap rather than automatic. A one-call 'this check ran, it passed, now'; artifact registration derived from a merge or a commit range; the where-am-i skill ending with a mark-asked call. Smallest, and it fixes each of their three instances without reflow2 learning to read anything new. It also leaves the carry a choice, which is the property `dec:three-party-checks` protects. (b) Let the loop SUBSCRIBE: a webhook or a 'reconcile against this repo's recent history' sweep that turns real events into ChangeEvents. Biggest leverage and the biggest risk — an ingested event is an assertion nobody made, and reflow2's whole epistemic position is that the graph stores claims and never manufactures them. (c) Only REPORT the deficit: say how far the graph has fallen behind the repo (commits since the last ChangeEvent, merged PRs with no Artifact) without ingesting anything. Turns an invisible rot into a number, and asks nobody to trust an inference. (d) Nothing. The carry being deliberate is a feature, and every automatic path is a way for the graph to fill with things no human said. ⚠️ THE ARGUMENT AGAINST (b), AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN DOCTRINE. `req:no-idea-goes-quiet` explicitly refuses auto-drawn SATISFIES/REALIZES because 'a requirement backed out of the implementation that satisfies it is satisfied by construction — it can never contradict anything,' and warns that auto-linking 'would make every captured idea read as delivered and the completion reading say 100% forever.' A reality bridge that writes structure has the same shape. A reality bridge that writes only ChangeEvents does not, which is the distinction worth holding onto. 📌 WHY THIS IS NOT `req:graph-catches-up` (proposed, already in the graph). That one asks whether the graph can catch up AFTER unrecorded change — a repair. This asks whether the gap should stop opening. Related, and worth deciding together rather than separately.		An external report's three separate frictions turned out to share one cause, and the same cause was independently demonstrated in this repo the same day when loop_status reported zero drift on a file no detector had looked at. The open part is not whether the gap is real but whether closing it means cheapening the carry or automating it — and automation is exactly what this project's accepted doctrine refuses for structure.proposednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 have a skill for 'brainstorm the options, then TRIAL them and let measurement choose'?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-04, in his own words: 'I kind of like this idea of brainstorming ideas for how to solve a problem and laying out trials for how to figure out which is the best approach - maybe this is a future reflow2 skill??' Raised while brainstorming the corpus-ingest strategies (dec:idea-corpus-ingest-strategies), which is the first concrete case for it. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, AND IT IS MORE THAN HALF — the design-space version of this shipped as BL-70 and nothing in this idea should be built without reading it first. `register_alternative` forks a `proposed` Decision into alternatives, each a pointer to that branch's own design export, GOVERNED_BY the Decision and CONTRADICTS its siblings, and it REFUSES unless the Decision is proposed — you fork an open choice, not a settled one. `analyze_alternatives` then compares the branches ON THE SAME MEASURES — design nodes, open gaps, structural defects, allocation modularity, capabilities verified, plus each branch's structural divergence from the baseline — in throwaway graphs, so it never touches the live one. Its own words are 'makes alternatives comparable on measures, not advocacy', which is this idea's thesis already stated. `collapse_decision` picks the winner, moves the Decision to accepted, and SUPERSEDES the losers with OBSOLETES so the roads not taken stay on the record. `detect_gaps` fires `undecided_decision_point` once a Decision holds two or more registered alternatives, so an open fork nags and a musing does not. THE GAP, AND IT IS SPECIFIC — reflow2 can compare DESIGNS; it cannot compare RUNS. Every measure `analyze_alternatives` reports is a property of the resulting graph's shape. None of them is a property of the PROCESS that produced it: what it cost, how long it took, how much of the corpus it covered, how much noise it raised, how many questions a human then had to answer, and whether the result was recognisable to the person who owns the material. The corpus-ingest strategies are indistinguishable on graph shape and completely different on all of those. A trial produces evidence about a PROCESS and there is nowhere in the graph to put it. That is the same hole (BL-187) names from the other side — the corpus records when something was true and nothing computes whether it still is. THE SECOND GAP, AND IT IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT KEEPS FINDING — no skill drives the alternatives family end to end. `brainstorm` mentions `register_alternative` in passing, as the line where a musing becomes a fork. Nothing tells anyone to then run `analyze_alternatives` or `collapse_decision`. Same shape as `ingest_step`, which is built, served, verified, and named in no skill at all: a tool nobody is told to call is a tool nobody calls ((BL-154)). HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea rather than used to kill it. (1) `dec:report-dont-judge` — a trial that picks a winner by number is arithmetic overruling a person, which is the move this project refuses everywhere else; the skill would have to REPORT the measures and leave the collapse to the human, exactly as `collapse_decision` already requires a stated winner and a rationale. (2) The api-boss's objection to PMBOK in `reflow2_feedback.md` applies here too: reflow2 is a design-coherence tool, and importing an experiment harness risks 'a second, competing spine next to the golden thread'. (3) Trials are expensive, and the cheapest honest version of this idea may be a SKILL over the existing tools plus a convention for recording run measures as evidence, rather than any new vocabulary — which is what the last two node-type proposals in this project both collapsed into after measurement (`Attestation` → `TemporalFact`, `Hazard` → `DesignRule`). NOT PROMOTED, NOT SIZED, AND NOT MINE — recorded so the idea is findable and so the next session does not re-derive BL-70, which is the specific failure this session hit three times.		Captured under the brainstorm skill because Anthony floated it as a question, not a request. The load-bearing content is the survey of what BL-70 already provides: the idea is substantially built for design alternatives and genuinely missing for process trials, and that distinction is what would make it worth building rather than a second name for something that exists.proposednothing
WITHDRAWN — a stable v0.30 baseline solves a distribution problem this project does not have; the update channel is one person telling the other
🛑 **WITHDRAWN BY ANTHONY THE SAME DAY IT WAS RAISED, 2026-08-14**, on noticing it contradicted his own standing practice: *'you're right that my latest guidance is contradictory to previous, so please disregard. it is just my brother and developing. anytime a new version comes out, I tell him and he usually updates. so we'll just continue with this policy.'* ⇒ **THE REASON IS A FACT ABOUT THE USER POPULATION, AND IT IS WORTH KEEPING.** reflow2 has two users who talk to each other directly. A stable-baseline policy exists to tell strangers which releases are safe to adopt; **there are no strangers.** The distribution channel is a text message, and it works. At this scale a formal patch line would add ceremony to solve a problem nobody has. ⭐ AND IT DISSOLVES THE CADENCE CONCERN RATHER THAN ANSWERING IT. Three releases in three days is only a problem if users discover versions passively. They do not — they are told. **The measurement that prompted this (`fact:updating-reflow2-does-not-update-a-project-already-set-up`) stays true and stops being a reason to slow down.** ═══ ⚠️ WHAT DOES **NOT** GO AWAY WITH THIS WITHDRAWAL ═══ **The kit/binary split survives, and this withdrawal sharpens it.** *'He usually updates'* updates the **BINARY**. `install.sh` does not touch a project that is already initialised, because the files that matter to a project (`reflow2_init.py` and what it wrote) are KIT, and a project's copy is fixed at the moment it was set up. ⇒ **So the working update channel makes the remaining gap MORE visible, not less: the message arrives, the user updates, and their existing projects are exactly as stale as before.** Alex's home machine is the demonstration — binary 0.30.0, project stamped 0.11.0. The defect was never about him being told late. 📌 STILL OWED, INDEPENDENT OF ANY RELEASE POLICY: something that surfaces the KIT's version (today only the binary's is reachable), and an update path for a project that already exists. Neither needs a stable line to justify it. ═══ THE ANALYSIS THIS WAS WITHDRAWN FROM, kept because `req:roads-not-taken` says the roads not taken are part of the record ═══ RAISED as: should v0.30.0 become a stable baseline that only external feedback moves, with changes shipped as patches? Two objections were on the record before the withdrawal, and both stand as reasoning even though the question is closed: · **THE RULE CONTAINED TWO RULES.** *'Only external feedback'* answers WHAT may change; *'maybe these are patches'* answers HOW BIG. `cap:init-asks-which-harness` is both external feedback and a new feature, so the halves disagreed in practice on the day they were written. · **A STRICT READING WOULD HAVE PARKED FOUR MEASURED DEFECTS** found the same day, none of them user-reported — the machine-wide installer writing configs for absent harnesses, 9 of 20 skills with no drift signal, the enforced rule's missing detector, and 43 planned capabilities invisible to every tool. **Users cannot report what the tool hides from them.** OPTIONS, NONE TAKEN: (a) v0.30.x patch line, fixes only. (b) slow but not frozen. (c) baseline plus feature branch. (d) intent without policy. **The outcome is (d) by decision rather than by drift: continue as before, deliberately.**		Raised and withdrawn the same day, on Anthony's word. Recorded as rejected rather than deleted because the reasoning is worth more than the question: the withdrawal establishes that reflow2's user population is two people with a direct channel, which is a fact several other decisions could lean on, and it separates two things that had been travelling together all day — release cadence, which turns out not to be a problem, and the kit/binary update split, which is a real defect that the working update channel actually makes more visible rather than less.rejectednothing
OPEN — should reflow2 guide a project to plan HOW a need will be verified when the need is stated, rather than only asking for a check once something is built?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Anthony, 2026-08-11, and he was explicit that this is NOT a reflow2-repo question: 'this isn't just a 'do it for reflow2' type task. this is a more general philosophy that test planning should be before implementation (maybe even in the design stages of a reflow2 project)... reflow2 guides a user through systems engineering processes, implementation, testing and fielding/production — I'm saying reflow2 should define a design tests philosophy prior to development of the design.' ⭐⭐ MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN, 2026-08-11, AND IT IS ONE-SIDED: verification detectors 6 build_without_verification, unverified_capability, unverified_artifact, component_granularity_verification, failing_verification, build_without_governance of those, asking a REQUIREMENT how it will be verified 0 live requirements 142 with a Verification pointed AT the requirement 2 stating a need with no stated way to know it is met 140 EVERY detector fires in the same direction: you BUILT this, where is the check? Nothing anywhere asks: you STATED this need, how will you know it is met? So reflow2 today discovers the test question at the moment it is most expensive to answer and most likely to be answered by looking at the code. ⭐ THE V-MODEL FRAMING, because it names the shape precisely. reflow2 models the descending arm (intent → allocation → build) and the ascending arm (verify → operate) — that is what the seven maturity bands measure. What it does not model is the CROSS-LINKS: in the V, the acceptance test is written when the requirement is written, and the integration test when the architecture is drawn. reflow2 has both arms and no rungs. 📌 THE SIBLING QUESTION IS ALREADY OPEN AND THIS ONE MAKES IT MATTER MORE. `dec:bl-185` (Anthony, 2026-08-03) asks how the graph can tell a test written FROM THE REQUIREMENT from one written to match the code — 'a passing check written from the requirement and a passing check written to match the implementation are the same node, same status, same everything.' That is the RECORDING question. This is the PROCESS one. If verification were planned at requirement time, 'written from the requirement' would be the normal case rather than something the graph has to detect after the fact — so answering this one shrinks that one. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so nothing is built twice: `Verification` carries method and level and can already point at a Requirement (two do). `set_evidence_scope` records what a check PINNED versus SWEPT, and `evidence_report` reads it. `req:evidence-says-what-it-covered` is ACCEPTED. So the vocabulary for a planned check is there — a Verification at `planned` status IS a test plan. Nothing asks for one. IDEAS, unranked: (a) A DETECTOR: an accepted Requirement with no Verification pointed at it is a gap — 'how will you know this is met?'. Symmetric with `unsatisfied_requirement`, which already asks 'what delivers this?'. Cheapest, and it is the one that changes what gets built. (b) A SKILL STEP: capture-intent ends by asking, for each requirement, how it would be checked — recorded as a `planned` Verification. No detector, no gap pressure, and it fires only when the skill loads, which `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` says is not enough. (c) A STATED PHILOSOPHY the project chooses, captured as a DesignRule via governance-proposal, with the consequence asked rather than assumed. This is what Anthony literally said — 'reflow2 should DEFINE a design tests philosophy' — and it is per-project, which matters because the answer differs between a demonstrator and a fielded system. (d) Nothing. The build-side detectors already catch an unverified capability before it ships, and adding a requirement-side one doubles the gap surface. ⚠️⚠️ THE STRONGEST OBJECTION, AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN MOST-REPEATED TRAP. A detector demanding a verification plan for every accepted requirement would fire on 140 of 142 here ON DAY ONE — and on every young design, and on every ADOPT, where a recovered requirement never had a test plan and could not have. That is exactly the shape of `unexpected_coupling` (retired for firing on correct work), of the short-text false positive found by CI hours ago, and of BL-179's punish-correct-work trap. Whatever is built must distinguish 'nobody has planned this yet' from 'this cannot be planned', which is `req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all` (ACCEPTED, unbuilt) pointed at requirements instead of rules. ⚠️ SECOND: `req:no-se-knowledge` is accepted — the user must never need systems engineering. 'How will you verify this?' is an SE question in SE words. It would have to arrive the way every other gap does, as a plain question the user can answer without knowing what a verification method is. ⚠️ THIRD, and it is the honest limit on the whole idea: planning a test early does not make it a GOOD test. Anthony's own criteria — valid, isolated, repeatable, focused, fast; happy path, edge cases, error conditions, contract-not-implementation — are properties of the test's CONTENT, and `dec:idea-who-judges-requirement-text-quality` already found that reflow2 checks structure and never text. A `planned` Verification with an empty method satisfies a detector and proves nothing, which would be a marker nothing reads in a new place.		Measured one-sidedness: all six verification detectors ask the build for a check, none asks a requirement how it will be known to be met, and 140 of 142 live requirements have no verification pointed at them. That is the V-model with both arms and no rungs. Anthony is proposing this as product philosophy rather than repo hygiene, which passes his own pruning test — it would change what reflow2 asks every project, not how this project manages itself. The blocker is precision: the naive detector fires on every young design and every adopt, which is the punish-correct-work trap this project has already retired one detector for.proposednothing
OPEN — should repeated, RELEVANCE-WEIGHTED search hits mark a node as becoming critical, when BM25 scores are not comparable across queries and the same data is named 'the worst offender' for telemetry?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-08-10, in his words: *'several times, I have had a brainstorming idea, and you've searched what I've already had in the graph. can we keep track of those searches for what's related because that tells you — the user had asked about something (or something similar or related) 10 times now... this node that has been searched 10 times now is becoming critical based on how many times it has been searched.'* REFINED BY HIM MINUTES LATER, and the refinement is right: *'instead of just keeping a simple integer counter, maybe relevance should also be included? for example, 5 other proposed ideas/decisions come up, but 2 of them were only 0.1 relevant, one was 0.4 relevant, and 2 were 0.8 relevant. then the critical decision path is weighted more towards the 0.8 relevant ideas versus the 0.1 ideas.'* A count treats a barely-matching hit and a bullseye as the same event, and the tail of a ranked list is mostly noise — so an unweighted counter would be dominated by whatever happens to match loosely and often. 🛑 BUT THE SCORE THE SEARCH RETURNS IS NOT THE 0-TO-1 RELEVANCE THE IDEA ASSUMES, AND THIS IS THE CRUX. `search_design` is BM25, whose scores are UNBOUNDED and QUERY-DEPENDENT. MEASURED 2026-08-10, two queries about the SAME SUBJECT: query 'export' top score 4.48 query 'the committed export document lineage content hash chain' top score 35.75 EIGHT TIMES THE SCORE FOR THE SAME TOPIC, because BM25 rises with the number of matching terms. Accumulating raw scores would therefore weight a verbose query roughly eight times a terse one about the same thing, and would silently reward whoever writes longer queries. THERE IS NO 0.8 IN THE SYSTEM TODAY — the numbers look like relevances and are not. ⇒ THREE WAYS TO GET A COMPARABLE NUMBER, none chosen: (i) NORMALISE PER QUERY — divide by that result set's top score, giving 0-1 within one search. Cheap, available now, and it makes the two queries above agree. Costs the absolute signal: the top hit of a hopeless query scores 1.0 exactly like the top hit of a perfect one. (ii) RANK-BASED WEIGHT — reciprocal rank (1, 1/2, 1/3...), ignoring the score entirely. Immune to query length and to BM25's quirks; the standard trick for fusing incomparable rankings. Costs the distinction between a result set with one obvious winner and one with five near-ties. (iii) COSINE SIMILARITY FROM EMBEDDINGS — genuinely bounded, genuinely comparable across queries, and the only one of the three that actually delivers the 0.1/0.4/0.8 the idea describes. ⚠️ THIS MAKES THE IDEA A DEPENDENT OF AN ALREADY-OPEN QUESTION: `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption` ('should reflow2 adopt embeddings and the HNSW index, or stay on lexical search?'). Worth naming plainly — if relevance-weighting is wanted in the form Anthony described, that decision has to be made first, and this is a new argument for it that the embeddings node does not yet carry. OBSERVED IN THE SESSION THAT PRODUCED THE IDEA, which is why it is worth taking seriously rather than filing as a nice thought. Across roughly eight `search_design` calls on 2026-08-10, the same nodes kept surfacing unprompted: `fact:bl-198` twice, `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` twice, `dec:read-hint-shape` twice, and `cap:what-next` / `req:what-next` at the exact moment a new idea turned out to duplicate accepted intent. Each of those repeats CHANGED THE WORK — one of them stopped a false claim being shipped for the second time in three days. The signal is real in at least one session. ⚠️⚠️ IT COLLIDES WITH A LINE ANTHONY HIMSELF DREW, AND THE DISTINCTION IS PART OF THE VALUE OF THIS NODE. `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` says, verbatim: *'A SEARCH QUERY is content and is the worst offender, because it names the user's domain in their own words.'* Read carelessly, that kills this idea. Read properly, it does not — because that requirement's scope is stated in its first line: *'WHEN REFLOW2 REPORTS ITS OWN USAGE FROM A HOSTED DEPLOYMENT.'* It governs what LEAVES a design. This idea keeps the search history INSIDE the design it came from, where the object is not a leak but the entire point. SAME DATA, OPPOSITE DIRECTION. That distinction must be written down here, because a later session that finds this idea and remembers the telemetry rule will otherwise kill it correctly-looking and wrongly — or implement it and breach the rule by exporting it. ⇒ THE DERIVED CONSTRAINT, if this is ever built: search history is LOCAL BY CONSTRUCTION and never enters the telemetry payload. `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content`'s own argument applies — a structure that CANNOT carry content beats a policy promising not to — so the two must not share a transport. `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` IS ALREADY OPEN and holds the mechanism-and-storage question for usage logging. This idea widens what that decision has to answer: not only WHICH TOOLS a session called, but WHICH NODES it reached and HOW STRONGLY. Nodes are a harder case than tool names, exactly per the rule above. TWO CONFOUNDS, BOTH SERIOUS, BOTH MEASURABLE BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING. FIRST: A SEARCH HIT MEASURES THE AGENT'S QUERY WORDING AS MUCH AS THE USER'S INTEREST. Anthony did not run those eight searches — I did, choosing the words. A count would partly measure how I phrase things, and would drift as agents or models change. What he actually described is narrower and better: *the user had asked about something similar ten times*, which is a fact about HIS repeated approach to a topic, not about search mechanics. NOTE THAT WEIGHTING MAKES THIS CONFOUND WORSE, NOT BETTER, UNDER RAW BM25 — a longer agent query scores everything higher. SECOND, AND SHARPER: SEARCH IS BM25 OVER NODE TEXT, SO A VERBOSE NODE WINS MORE SEARCHES. The nodes in this design are extremely verbose — several run to thousands of characters — and length is a scoring advantage in BM25. 'Searched often' may therefore partly measure PROSE VOLUME rather than importance, and the verbose nodes are disproportionately the recent ones. That is testable directly: correlate hit frequency against node text length before trusting any of it. Per-query normalisation does NOT fix this one; it is a property of the corpus, not of the query. AND A THIRD, SEEN TWICE TODAY: THE ONE-WORD 'export' SEARCH RETURNED A `decision:ack:` REVIEW RECORD AS ITS TOP HIT. Whatever exclusion list a projection carries (`fact:graph-analysis-covers-a-third-of-the-edge-types`) applies here too — review records and bookkeeping must not accumulate attention weight. AND `dec:bl-155`'S TRAP APPLIES ONE LEVEL OVER, unchanged. That decision found reflow2 cannot tell 'unused' from 'unreachable', and `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` drew the consequence: usage counts may justify OPTIMISING and may not, alone, justify CUTTING. Here: SEARCH COUNTS MAY JUSTIFY RAISING SOMETHING AND MAY NOT JUSTIFY LOWERING WHAT IS NEVER FOUND — because you cannot search for what you do not know exists, and the nodes nobody finds are precisely the ones a discoverability problem hides. THE OPTIONS. (a) COUNT APPEARANCES IN SEARCH RESULTS, UNWEIGHTED. Cheapest. Counter: all three confounds hit it directly, and a result appearing in a list is not evidence anybody cared about it. Anthony's refinement is a direct argument against this one. (b) COUNT ONLY WHAT WAS THEN READ IN FULL — a node that a search surfaced AND the agent then fetched with `get_node`. Much stronger evidence of relevance, and it discards the ranked-but-ignored tail where the BM25 confound lives. ⭐ NOTE THIS IS A RELEVANCE WEIGHT OF A DIFFERENT KIND — BEHAVIOURAL RATHER THAN LEXICAL — and it needs no score at all, so it sidesteps the comparability problem entirely. Counter: still an agent's behaviour, not the user's. (c) RELEVANCE-WEIGHTED ACCUMULATION, per Anthony's refinement, using (i), (ii) or (iii) above. Closest to what he described. Counter: (i) and (ii) are approximations of the thing he means and (iii) depends on `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption`. (d) RECORD THE SEARCH AS AN EVENT ATTACHED TO THE BRAINSTORM IT PRECEDED — 'this idea was captured after searching X, and these nodes came back, at these ranks'. A fact about the user's train of thought rather than about retrieval, and it composes with (c) since the weights ride on the event. Counter: covers only searches made during capture, and most searching is not. (e) DO NOTHING; DERIVE IMPORTANCE FROM STRUCTURE INSTEAD. Measured the same day: 61 of 83 open decisions govern nothing, so structure currently has nothing to say about most of the pile — which is precisely the hole this idea would fill. Counter to the counter: that may be an argument for recording structure better rather than for measuring retrieval. NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR EACH OTHER: this ranks by ATTENTION, `dec:idea-a-critical-path-through-the-undecided` ranks by CONSEQUENCE. A node can be repeatedly searched and block nothing, or block everything and never be searched. Whether either alone is enough, or they compose into one bounded top-5, is open in both nodes and settled in neither.		Anthony's idea, with his own refinement folded in the same session rather than minted as a third node — the refinement constrains the answer to this question, it is not a new question, and the complaint driving all of this is a pile of undecided nodes. The load-bearing addition is that the refinement is RIGHT and CANNOT BE IMPLEMENTED AS DESCRIBED on the current search. Measuring two queries about the same subject and getting 4.48 against 35.75 is what turns 'use the relevance score' from an implementation detail into a decision with a dependency: the 0.1/0.4/0.8 model needs a bounded similarity, which is what `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption` is about. Recording that link is worth more than the idea itself, because a later session would otherwise reach for `score` believing it means relevance. Option (b) is flagged because it dissolves the problem rather than solving it: what the agent chose to READ is a relevance signal that needs no score and cannot be gamed by query length. The telemetry collision and the three confounds are kept with tests attached rather than as caveats. The BM25-length one is checkable in an afternoon and would decide whether any lexical weighting is worth having at all.proposednothing
IDEA — an agent about to edit a file can ask what the design already decided about it, without guessing search terms
PROPOSED IDEA, not a commitment: give the agent a lookup from a FILE (or symbol) to the Decisions, Requirements and Constraints that govern it — 'what does the design already say about the code I am about to change?' — resolved by traversal rather than by keyword search.		RECORDED UNDER ANTHONY'S 2026-08-08 TEST PROTOCOL: run a task as if reflow2 did not exist, then run it leaning on reflow2, compare, and propose what would have helped. His stated aim, quoted so it is not lost: he is NOT trying to change how the agent functions, but to make available skills/tools that make the agent's job easier and better. This idea is scoped to that.\n\nTHE EVIDENCE IS TWO FIXES DONE THE SAME DAY, WITH DIFFERENT AMOUNTS OF REFLOW2.\n\n(1) THE DUPLICATES/MERGE FIX — reflow2 CHANGED THE OUTCOME, and the whole difference was one call. dev_storyflow reported merge candidates scoring 81-85 on unrelated nodes. Read as a code problem, the obvious fix is 'the scorer is bad, raise the threshold' — a plausible, shippable, WRONG fix. A `search_design` for 'duplicate merge similarity' returned `dec:ask-not-repair` as the top hit, and that decision reframed the entire task: possible_duplicate is a DETECT gap, HEAL merges only on a human-drawn edge, a heuristic must not drive it. The bug was not a bad threshold; it was an ACCEPTED DECISION DEFEATED BY THE BUILD, and the correct fix (mark the edge's basis, re-route suspicions to the gap layer) is not reachable from the code alone. Without reflow2 this session ships a threshold bump and the design stays quietly violated.\n\n(2) THE CLAIM-LIVENESS FIX — reflow2 helped at the FRAMING and not at all at the SOLUTION. The graph supplied the finding that mattered (`cap:claim-liveness` was status `verified` while its central claim was false under `--shared`) and `propagate_change` named exactly what to touch, including three Verifications that would be invalidated. But the fix itself — an RAII seat lease, and then a two-set registry after the first design proved unsafe — came entirely from reading code and from a FAILING TEST. No reflow2 detector had anything to say about it. Worth stating plainly rather than overclaiming: the two-set flaw was caught by `cargo test`, not by the design brain.\n\nTHE GENERALISATION, and it is the actionable part: REFLOW2'S LEVERAGE IS AT PROBLEM FRAMING AND BLAST RADIUS, NOT AT SOLUTION DESIGN. That is not a weakness — it is where a design brain SHOULD have leverage, and it argues for investing there rather than trying to help write the patch.\n\nSO WHAT IS MISSING, CONCRETELY: in case (1) the decision was found because a lucky choice of search words hit it. `search_design` is BM25 over node text, so the agent must already suspect what it is looking for. AN AGENT ABOUT TO EDIT `crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs` SHOULD BE ABLE TO ASK WHAT GOVERNS THAT FILE AND BE TOLD `dec:ask-not-repair`, WITHOUT KNOWING THE WORD 'DUPLICATE'. The graph already holds every hop needed: `art:heal` REALIZES `cap:heal`, which is GOVERNED_BY the decisions that constrain it, SATISFIES the requirements behind it, and is VERIFIED by the checks that would break. That is a traversal from a path to its governing intent, and today there is no tool for it — `propagate_change` is the closest but needs a recorded ChangeEvent and answers 'what does this touch', not 'what was already decided here'.\n\nWHY THIS FITS THE STATED AIM: it changes nothing about how the agent works. It is a lookup the agent chooses to make at the moment it is already opening a file, and it answers the one question a stateless agent cannot answer for itself and does not know to ask.\n\nCANDIDATE SHAPES, none chosen: (a) a `governs` tool taking a path or symbol, returning Decisions/Requirements/Constraints/Verifications reachable from the Artifact at that location, ranked by hop distance; (b) the same as a skill that runs before an edit, the read-side sibling of impact-check; (c) cheapest of all and worth pricing first — have `link_artifact`/`reconcile_artifacts` responses already carry the governing decisions for the artifact named, since the traversal is the same and the agent is already there.\n\nOPEN QUESTIONS THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether path-level granularity is enough (a 1,700-line file may be governed by decisions relevant to only one of its functions); whether an unregistered file — one with no Artifact — should answer 'nothing governs this' or 'this file is not in the design', which are very different statements and the second is the honest one; and whether ranking by hop distance is meaningful or merely plausible.proposednothing
DECIDED — the public page carries ONLY renderings the agent generates from reflow2's own graph; the page is the evidence for its own claim
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD — OPTION (b), AND NARROWER THAN (b) WAS WRITTEN.** HIS WORDS: *'for the pages, I'd like to only use renderings of systems engineering views the agent generates from graph content of reflow2 itself. I'd like to have some cutting edge rendering (that we periodically update) to show that contents come from the graph and that with a good agent, you can create some pretty awesome views.'* ⇒ **ONLY renderings. Not 'mostly', not 'landing page plus renderings' — (a) and (c) are both declined.** The page is a DEMONSTRATION, and its subject is its own provenance: it exists to show that the content came out of the graph and that a capable agent can render it well. ⭐⭐ **THAT PURPOSE SETS A HARDER HONESTY STANDARD THAN DOCUMENTATION, and it is the reason this is worth stating rather than just building.** A doc that drifts is stale. **A page whose entire claim is 'this came from the graph' is FALSIFIED by one hand-written fact.** So `render_views.py`'s existing doctrine is not a nicety here, it is the product: *'it may only emit what the graph states… anything a viewpoint NEEDS but the graph cannot supply goes on the CONFESSIONS list.'* The confessions are not a blemish on the demo — **they are the strongest evidence the rest is real.** ⚠️ **THE COST HE ACCEPTED, STATED PLAINLY: A NEWCOMER LANDS ON SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING VIEWS WITH NO ORIENTATION.** 'Only renderings' means the page cannot carry a hand-written *'reflow2 is a persistent design brain…'* paragraph. Someone arriving cold meets a functional view before they know what they are looking at. **His own next sentence is plausibly the answer to this — see `dec:idea-a-generated-explainer-for-someone-new` — and that connection is recorded rather than assumed.** ⚠️ **'PERIODICALLY UPDATE' CARRIES A KNOWN COST, ALREADY MEASURED HERE.** `chg:impact-propagation-is-rendered-not-written`: a re-render churns wording, so the diff is noisy and *'drift here will need reading as 're-rendered', not as 'the design moved''*. A page refreshed on a schedule will do this every time. Worth deciding once whether the refresh is committed output (noisy diffs, reviewable) or an Actions deploy that never commits (clean repo, unreviewable) — which is the placement question below, now materially easier because **nothing on the page is hand-written, so nothing is lost by not committing it.** ═══ WHAT STAYS OPEN, DELIBERATELY ═══ · **WHICH views.** `docs/viewpoints.md` holds the catalogue and `render_views.py` renders several; which of them belong on a public page, and in what order, is unanswered. · **WHAT 'cutting edge rendering' means.** He asked for it and did not specify. Not inferred. · **PLACEMENT.** `index.html` at the repo root was his sketch, prefaced *'something like this'*. This root is a Rust workspace; `/docs` already exists and already holds `loop-dag.html`; an Actions deploy commits nothing. **The ruling above makes the Actions route cheaper than it was**, but it is not chosen here. · **REFRESH CADENCE.** 'Periodically' is not a schedule. 📌 STILL NOT ASKED AND STILL NOT ASSUMED: whether this is reflow2's own design published, or a template a CONSUMER could use for theirs. His wording — *'from graph content of reflow2 itself'* — answers it for THIS page and says nothing about the general case. ════════ THE OPTIONS AS PUT TO HIM, KEPT ════════ **(a) A LANDING PAGE** — hand-written, an afternoon, and every other tool has one. **DECLINED.** It goes stale the way `dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph` was opened about, and this project has been bitten: a doc presented eight impact kinds never implemented and referenced an edge type retired five days before it was written. **(b) ⭐ THE DESIGN GRAPH, RENDERED — CHOSEN**, and narrowed to *only* this. **(c) BOTH, LAYERED** — **DECLINED**, which also declines the shape `dec:idea-which-docs-can-never-be-a-projection` is open about. ⚠️ That decision stays open for the rest of reflow2's outward docs; this ruling covers the PAGE only, and does not settle it generally.		Captured under capture-intent rather than built, because he sequenced it explicitly ('post release') and because the one thing that decides the size of the work — what is on the page — is the one thing he did not say. The mechanism he described is recorded as a SKETCH rather than a specification, on his own framing of 'something like this'. Transcribing `index.html` at the root into a requirement would have converted an illustration into a commitment, in a repository whose root is a cargo workspace. Recorded as its own node rather than folded into the requirement because it reaches two decisions that were already open before he asked — outward docs as projections, and which docs can never be one — and a question connecting three threads deserves to be findable from all of them. The near-duplicate guard fired on the requirement and was right to: they are the same subject, and saying so on the record is cheaper than a reader later wondering whether one supersedes the other.acceptedSomeone can read what reflow2 is on the open web, without cloning it or installing anything
OPEN — what happens when two designs answer to one graph_id, now that the id is an ADDRESS and not just a label?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-13, from his own observation that graph_id may not be unique. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen. ⚙️ HOW THIS WAS CREATED, said plainly: `add_decision`'s search-first guard fired and named three nodes. All three were read and judged different (below). The `distinct_from` override could not be used because the parameter would not serialize as an array from this client — it arrived as a string and was refused — so the node was written with `create_node` instead. That is a workaround for a client serialization fault, NOT an evasion of the guard: the reading and the judgement the guard asks for were both done first, and are recorded here in place of the edge. READ AND JUDGED DIFFERENT FROM THE THREE THE GUARD NAMED. `fact:two-adopted-stores-share-one-graph-id-2026-08-13` is the MEASUREMENT — two stores, one id, and why; this is the question of what to DO about it, which a fact cannot hold. `dec:identity-out-of-band` is the accepted PRINCIPLE, and this node defers to it entirely rather than reopening it. `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs` asks whether ONE SESSION should reason across several designs at once — orthogonal: that is breadth of attachment, this is two designs being indistinguishable by name. ⭐ THIS IS NOT A MISSING DECISION. `dec:identity-out-of-band` is ACCEPTED and settles the principle: 'a design's identity is a UUID minted at genesis and stored in the graph; the friendly name is a label on top of it.' It names what it rejected and why — 'deriving from the project name or path (TWO DESIGNS CAN SHARE BOTH, and the id must survive being copied)'. The shape of the answer is decided. What is open is what to do about designs adopted BEFORE it, and that touches HIS data. ═══ THE OPTIONS ═══ A — REFUSE THE AMBIGUOUS ID AND LIST WHAT IT MATCHED. The registry stops silently overwriting; `attach` on a duplicated id fails naming both paths, and discovery reports the collision instead of hiding one design. CHEAP, LOCAL, TOUCHES NO STORED DATA. Not a new policy either: `dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design` already states the rule, written before this case was known — 'DEFAULT WHEN EXACTLY ONE DESIGN IS REACHABLE; REFUSE AND LIST THEM WHEN SEVERAL ARE. A design chosen by silence is how three graphs appeared on one repo.' Leaves both designs unreachable by name, but LOUDLY rather than silently. B — RE-MINT THE COLLIDING LEGACY IDS. Fixes it at the root and matches `dec:identity-out-of-band` exactly. EXPENSIVE: `graph_id` is part of the export's content hash, so re-minting breaks every existing export, chain link and committed record for that design — precisely what adoption was introduced to protect. Anthony's data, Anthony's call, and it needs a migration story rather than a flag. C — ANTHONY'S COMPOSITE NAME, in his words: 'can you name a graph by graph_id.first_node_unique_id'. Recorded as offered, with three objections beside it rather than used to kill it. (1) A GRAPH CAN HOLD SEVERAL PROJECT NODES — dev_storyflow holds two, `proj:fleet_ops` and `proj:storyflow`, neither mirrored, and the schema says only that there is 'normally' one, in an extraction hint. `Project.mirror_of` exists so a mirrored foreign project can sit alongside yours, so mirroring adds more. (2) 'FIRST' IS UNDEFINED — no ordering exists; exports sort by id, so 'first' means alphabetically first, an arbitrary tiebreak on a name. (3) IT IS CIRCULAR, and this is the strong one: identity lives in sidecars precisely so it is readable BEFORE opening, because opening MINTS an identity — the failure that once created a third graph beside two populated ones. `Registry::discover` and `describe_at` both depend on never opening. A name derived from a node inside the graph must be read by opening the graph you chose by name. 📌 THE RESCUE THAT KEEPS THE INSIGHT: the composite need not be DERIVED at read time — it could be WRITTEN into the sidecar at mint or adopt, staying pre-open readable. But then it is doing option B's job with extra steps, since the sidecar already carries `label` separately from `graph_id`. ⚠️ THE TENSION TO NAME: deriving identity from graph content is the shape `dec:identity-out-of-band` rejected on principle — 'names are assigned with zero coordination, NEVER DERIVED FROM SHARED STATE'. Its rationale records the fleet DELETING a mint-race guard, because the race was an artifact of deriving the handle at all. D — SCOPE AROUND IT. One registry root per neighbourhood so colliding designs never co-occur. Does not survive his actual case: `~/project` IS the neighbourhood and both stores live in it. ═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS ═══ ⚠️ 1. NOTHING IS BROKEN TODAY. No transport is wired to the registry, so no session can yet select a design by id. The collision is LATENT — which argues for fixing it BEFORE the transport ships rather than after. ⚠️ 2. TWO STORES IS NOT A POPULATION. One owner's machine, and the count may never grow: the four minted designs are clean and every future design mints. Option A may be the whole of what is ever needed. ⚠️ 3. RE-MINTING IS THE EXPENSIVE KIND OF RIGHT. It repairs the model and invalidates the record; the adoption decision already weighed that trade once and went the other way, for stated reasons that have not changed. 📌 A FAIR POINT FOR ACTING: the registry's entire isolation guarantee — `ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design`, passing — rests on ids being unique, and every fixture in it uses distinct ids. The guarantee is not wrong, but it has never been tested against the one case that is true on the owner's own disk.		Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent. Kept separate from the pair-types question because the two are unrelated and one node holding both could only ever be half-answered. Worth keeping for three things: the principle is already settled by dec:identity-out-of-band so only the migration is open; Anthony's composite proposal is recorded in his own words with the circularity objection beside it rather than used to argue it down; and the latency point is time-sensitive, because the collision stays harmless only until a transport makes graph_id an address — which is the next thing the linking work would build.proposednothing
OPEN — should a TemporalFact record WHEN IT WAS LEARNED as well as when it was true, since VALID_FROM/VALID_TO carry only world-time and a retroactive discovery loses its own arrival?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 research, specifically Zep/Graphiti, described there as 'temporal knowledge graphs that encode what happened, when, and how entities relate over time' for agents that 'must reason about evolving facts'. Graphiti's distinguishing feature in that family is BI-TEMPORALITY: every fact carries both when it was true in the world and when the system came to know it. STILL OPEN. WHAT REFLOW2 HAS, CHECKED IN schema/temporal.yaml RATHER THAN RECALLED: TemporalFact carries VALID_FROM and VALID_TO, both pointing at a DesignEpoch, plus `basis: measured|forecast` and an author-stated `confidence`. So the design already models world-time properly, and BL-68 already separated observation from projection — which is the harder half of what Graphiti does and reflow2 got there independently. What TemporalFact does NOT carry is any epoch for when the assertion ENTERED the record. ChangeEvent has `detected_at`, DriftEvent has `detected_at`, DimensionObservation has `observed_at` — the arrival time exists on the EVENTS but not on the FACT. THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is why this may be worth more than schema tidiness: a retroactively discovered fact is written with VALID_FROM at the epoch it became true, and the record then reads as though the design always knew. 'The beamline analysis code has assumed a single detector since 2016' and 'we discovered in August 2026 that the beamline analysis code has assumed a single detector since 2016' become the same node. The second is the more useful sentence, because it tells a reader that everything designed between 2016 and 2026 was designed in ignorance of it — and that is exactly the reasoning a brownfield adoption needs. This is Anthony's own operating context (a ten-year-old bluesky/tiled stack being evolved on the fly), not a hypothetical. WHERE IT ALREADY BITES, POSSIBLY: cap:as-of-epoch answers 'what did the design say at epoch n' from snapshots. If retroactive facts are written with early VALID_FROM, an as-of-epoch answer can attribute knowledge to a past epoch that nobody had then — a subtler version of the same fiction dec:readiness-forecast-is-a-temporal-fact was created to stop. NOT VERIFIED: whether as-of-epoch actually reads TemporalFact validity or only Snapshots was not checked, and that determines whether this is a live defect or only a modelling gap. Check before treating it as either. WHAT IS CHEAP: adding a RECORDED_AT epoch edge (or reusing AT_EPOCH, which already means 'belongs to' for Snapshot and ChangeEvent) is additive, and req:defaults-do-not-assert has a clean answer for the backfill — absent means unstated, which reads as unstated. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: nothing currently READS TemporalFact validity for anything a user sees, and reflow2's record already has a long list of declared-and-read-by-nothing fields (embedding_field, Project.domain) that this would join. A second time axis is also a real conceptual cost on a vocabulary that is already large, and the honest test is whether any computation would use it — which is the same bar dec:exploratory-staging is being held to. If the answer is 'only a human reading the node would notice', the cheaper fix is prose in the fact's statement, not schema.		Recorded as an idea because the missing half was verified in the schema and the brownfield consequence is Anthony's actual working context, but the deciding test — does any computation read it — is unanswered, and that test is what dec:exploratory-staging established as the bar for new vocabulary. Also recorded because BL-68 already made the harder measured/forecast distinction, which makes this the same argument one step along rather than a new idea.proposednothing
OPEN — which outward-facing docs can NEVER be a projection, and how do rendered facts and irreducible argument sit together on one page?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — the boundary question underneath dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph, 2026-08-11. Separate node because it has an answer whichever way that one goes. Nothing here is intent. THE OBSERVATION: reflow2's outward-facing docs are not one kind of thing, and rendering the wrong ones would hollow them out. PROJECTABLE — the content IS graph state, and every staleness found today lives here three-axes.md what the schema holds on each axis; the status column is a COUNT overview.md the type counts, the reading order, what is built vs planned genesis.md what the genesis tool does and what it returns artifact-linking.md what link_artifact / reconcile_artifacts return impact-propagation.md what propagate_from returns — a worked blast radius IS an example gap-surfacing.md what detect_gaps returns, and the live gap list heal-process.md what propose_heal returns viewpoints.md the catalogue itself is a table of what renders IRREDUCIBLE ARGUMENT — no graph query produces this, and a rendered version would be worse vision.md the four lifecycle transitions and WHY they break. An argument, not data. partnership.md the LLM failure-mode taxonomy. Most of it is not in the graph and should not be — 'sycophancy' is not a node type. Its value is the reasoning. operating-environment.md the Kennewick-vs-Mars argument for why environments matter, about a layer with ZERO instances — so a projection would render an empty page for the doc that explains why the layer should exist at all. ⭐ THE THIRD CASE IS THE INTERESTING ONE AND IT BREAKS THE SIMPLE SPLIT. `operating-environment.md` argues for a capability that has never been used. A pure projection of it renders nothing, because there is nothing to project — the doc's whole job is to explain something the graph does NOT yet hold. Any rendering scheme has to allow a doc to be ABOUT AN ABSENCE without confessing itself into uselessness. The same is true of every doc describing planned work. ⭐ AND THE SPLIT IS NOT PER-DOC, IT IS PER-PARAGRAPH. `overview.md` is mostly reading order and argument, with one sentence carrying '29 node types, 60 edge types' — which is the sentence that went wrong. `three-axes.md` is mostly explanation with one STATUS COLUMN that is wrong. So the natural unit is a SECTION, not a file, which is the argument for option (c) in the parent node — embed rendered blocks in prose — rather than rendering whole documents. IDEAS, unranked: (a) Per-section markers: prose files with fenced regions regenerated from a named tool call, and a CI check that re-renders and diffs. Facts under the gate, argument left alone, absence expressible because the prose around the block says what the empty block means. (b) Two doc classes with different rules — `docs/rendered/` regenerated wholesale and gate-checked, `docs/` hand-written and exempt. Cleaner to enforce, and it splits a reader's attention across two directories. (c) Render everything and accept that argument-shaped docs become thin. Rejected on sight here, recorded so nobody re-proposes it: it would delete the reasoning that is the most valuable content reflow2 has. (d) Render nothing; instead add a CHECK that every factual claim in a doc matches the graph. Keeps all prose, needs the claims to be machine-identifiable — which is `check_doc_versions.py` generalised beyond version strings, and that tool already proves the pattern works (it FAILS when a pattern matches nothing, so rewording a doc breaks the build loudly instead of silently disabling the check). 📌 (d) IS CHEAPER THAN IT LOOKS AND IS NOT MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE WITH (a). `tools/check_doc_versions.py` is already a CI gate that asserts doc claims against the build, anchored on literal phrases, deliberately failing when a pattern matches nothing. Extending its anchors from version strings to type counts would have caught `overview.md`'s '60 edge types' this morning for the cost of one line.		Rendering the docs is not one decision — some docs ARE graph state, some are argument no query produces, and one (operating-environment) argues for a layer with zero instances, so a projection of it renders an empty page. The natural unit turns out to be a section rather than a file, which changes what the parent question is actually choosing between.proposednothing
OPEN — does reflow2 have any opinion on whether a Requirement is WELL WRITTEN, and if so whose job is it?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — 2026-08-11, from Anthony bringing the Defense Acquisition University criteria for a good requirement into the discussion. Nothing here is intent. THE CRITERIA HE CITED, in his framing. Individual requirement: NECESSARY (addresses a true operational gap), UNAMBIGUOUS (everyone reads it the same way), VERIFIABLE/TESTABLE (has criteria that can be practically proven), FEASIBLE (achievable within technology and budget), IMPLEMENTATION-FREE (what the system must deliver, not how to build it), MEASURABLE (quantifiable data, not vague adjectives). Full set: COMPLETE, CONSISTENT, TRACEABLE. WHAT REFLOW2 ACTUALLY CHECKS, sorted against that list: SET-LEVEL — partially covered, structurally Traceable forward only, via the golden thread. Backward is unchecked — see dec:idea-should-a-requirement-trace-back-to-its-demand-signal Consistent partially, via CONTRADICTS and dimension drift Complete approximated by the gap detectors, never claimed INDIVIDUAL — ZERO OF SIX. Necessary, Unambiguous, Verifiable, Feasible, Implementation-Free and Measurable are all properties of the TEXT, and no reflow2 computation reads requirement text for quality at all. `unverified_capability` is the nearest thing and it asks whether a check EXISTS, never whether the requirement is phrased so that a check is POSSIBLE — a different question with the same words in it. IDEAS, unranked: (a) Nothing changes; state the boundary explicitly somewhere a user will read it, so 'reflow2 does not grade your prose' is a known limit rather than a surprise. (b) A three-party check: the LLM judges the six against the text, the graph records the judgement and who made it, the human decides. Fits dec:three-party-checks exactly and needs no new detector. (c) A deterministic subset only — e.g. MEASURABLE is partly mechanical (does the statement contain a number and a unit?), and IMPLEMENTATION-FREE has weak mechanical tells. Cheap, and cheap in the bad way: a keyword heuristic that grades prose will be wrong confidently. ⭐ THE ARGUMENT FOR (a)/(b) OVER ANY DETECTOR: `req:deterministic-core` is accepted — the core is deterministic and LLM-free. Judging 'is this unambiguous' is irreducibly a language judgement. So the six do not belong in detect.rs at all; if they belong anywhere it is the skill layer, where an LLM already reads and the human already decides. ⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER-EXAMPLE, recorded because it cuts against the whole frame. Of the storyflow feedback's three ranked asks, #1 was NOT implementation-free — it named the mechanism outright ('model VERIFIES onto DesignRule') — and it is the one that got built. #2 and #3 were stated as node-type wishes and did not. So on this evidence MEASURABLE and VERIFIABLE predicted delivery and IMPLEMENTATION-FREE anti-predicted it. When the system under design IS the modelling vocabulary, 'what not how' gets genuinely slippery, and applying DAU to reflow2's own requirements needs that caveat or it will reject the requirements that work.		Anthony brought a mature external standard to bear and it partitions cleanly: reflow2 covers the set-level characteristics structurally and none of the six individual ones, because those are text judgements and the core is deliberately LLM-free. Whether that boundary is a deliberate design position or an unnoticed hole has never been stated either way.proposednothing
Names are assigned with zero coordination, never derived from shared state
A design's identity is a UUID minted at genesis and stored in the graph; the friendly name is a label on top of it. A seat's identity is the harness session id it was already given. Rejected: deriving from the project name or path (two designs can share both, and the id must survive being copied), and a registry that hands out ids (that is the coordination this avoids, and there is no service to host it).		Neither identifier is negotiated with anybody, so neither can race — unique by construction at one seat or fifteen. The fleet reached this by DELETING a whole mint-race guard: the race was an artifact of deriving the handle by reading a shared roster, so removing the derivation removed the race rather than patching it. reflow2 has the derived-identity bug twice today — every in-memory graph answered DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID until mirroring needed open_in_memory_as, and claims record a label rather than an owner.acceptedA claim names the session that made it, and a claim nobody is working says so, A design is given a name nobody negotiates for, and keeps it, Compose two designs by mirroring the other's published surface, coordinate and all, A claim names its owner, and a claim with no live owner is reported stale, A durable design knows its own name, and remembers it across opens
OPEN — does import_graph merge a partial node like create_node, or keep demanding whole ones?
BL-139's open half, and it is ANTHONY'S because it changes published behaviour rather than fixing a defect. `create_node` merges — its own description says 'a partial props object edits' — and `import_graph` does not: re-importing an existing Requirement carrying only `{lineage: 'derived'}` fails with `Requirement.statement: required property is missing`. The adopt workflow is import → detect → correct → re-import, so the mismatch lands precisely on the corrective step the skill prescribes. TWO OPTIONS, and the row already judged them: '(2) is honest and cheap; (1) is what the workflow actually wants.' (1) MERGE AT PROPERTY LEVEL, like `create_node`. (2) SAY PLAINLY that documents must carry complete nodes — DONE 2026-08-02, in `import_graph`'s own description, so the cheap half is delivered whichever way this goes. THE COST OF (1), which is why it is not a one-word swap and why nobody should make it casually. FIRST, it crosses THREE PUBLISHED BOUNDARIES — `ifc:core-api`, `ifc:graph-export` and `ifc:mcp-tools` — measured, not guessed: `propagate_from('art:export')` reported 705 impacted nodes and `propagate_change` on this session's own edit reported 723, both crossing exactly those three. SECOND, and this is the part no boundary count shows: MERGING MAKES IMPORT NON-IDEMPOTENT FOR DELETION. Today a document is a complete statement of the nodes it names, so re-importing without a property REMOVES it and an export→import round trip reproduces the design exactly. Under (1) a property can only ever be added or changed, never dropped, and restoring a backup would silently retain whatever the live graph had accumulated since. That is a change to what an import MEANS, and it makes the migration and backup jobs this module exists for weaker in exchange for making the adopt loop smoother. THIRD, a middle path exists and should be considered rather than skipped: keep whole-node semantics as the default and let the DOCUMENT ask for merge explicitly (a per-node or per-document flag), so the adopt loop gets what it wants without redefining backup restore for everyone.		Recorded proposed rather than decided, because AGENTS.md puts a Decision reaching `accepted` on the per-session side — that write is the user's signature. Raised now with the measurement attached because the row's framing ('make import_graph merge like create_node') reads as a small fix and the design says otherwise: this is the third time on this project that grep suggested a one-word swap and the graph reported a published-boundary change, and every previous time measuring first was what corrected it.proposedExport and import a design, export
reflow2 installs once per machine; the in-repo half is optional and only for repos you share
The install registers reflow2 with the agent at USER scope — the MCP server, the ten slash commands, the coherence-loop hooks and a `reflow2` command on PATH — so every project on the machine has it with no per-project setup. `reflow2_init.py` survives, but its job narrows: it writes the pointer file and project-scope config for a repo OTHER PEOPLE work on, so their agent is told reflow2 governs this code. Solo work needs none of it. Anthony's call, 2026-07-28, choosing 'machine-wide, repo init optional' over 'machine-wide only' and over 'keep per-project, just make it one word'.		WHY NOT 'MACHINE-WIDE ONLY', which is simpler: a teammate cloning the repo would get no signal that reflow2 governs it unless they had already installed reflow2 themselves and thought to look. That is the invisibility `req:kit-reaches-the-agent` was raised for, and retiring the per-project installer would rebuild it deliberately. WHY NOT 'JUST MAKE IT ONE WORD' (`reflow2 init .` instead of a python path): it fixes the typing and none of the arithmetic. Still one step per project, still a re-run after every upgrade, and still the case that a user who forgets it experiences reflow2 as absent. WHAT MADE MACHINE-WIDE SAFE TO CHOOSE AT ALL, and without it the answer would have been different: the server is registered with `--only-if-present`, so a directory that never opted into a design gets the LATENT surface and nothing is created in it. Without that flag, a user-scope registration would drop a RocksDB store into every folder a session is ever opened in — and litter in someone's repo is a worse first impression than the setup step it removed. The loop-nudge hook is gated the same way and for the same reason: registered globally, silent wherever `.reflow2/` does not exist. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: `dec:skills-served` and `req:thin-install` stand exactly as they were. The skills and working instructions are still served, still never copied, and upgrading reflow2 still produces no diff in a consumer repo. This decision is about WHERE the pointers are installed, not about what is served — and it makes the thin install thinner, since the common case now installs nothing into a project at all.acceptedA directory with no design costs nothing, Install reflow2 once for every project on a machine, OPEN — 'this directory has no design yet' is asserted without looking, and it minted a THIRD graph on a repo that already had two
DECIDED — stop proposing fabrication now; declare partitions next, and only if something reads the declaration back
RE-OPENED 2026-08-09 on Anthony's word, after storyflow gap D arrived and the same defect reproduced in this design within the hour. WHAT WAS DECIDED BEFORE, AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH NOW. dec:documentation-has-no-operational-coupling (ACCEPTED, 2026-07-24) met a legitimate island, tried three bridges, refused all of them as lies, accepted the island, and concluded: 'flagging it is a false positive of the BL-84 family, and THE FIX BELONGS IN THE DETECTOR RATHER THAN IN THE DESIGN.' That fix was never built. The decision records why — the specific island DISSOLVED on its own when cap:session-memory turned out to belong to both cmp:docs and cmp:temporal, giving documentation a real tie rather than a manufactured one. So the disposition became moot and the general principle it stated was left unimplemented. The old decision is NOT wrong and is NOT being un-accepted (dec:reopen-supersedes); what is re-opened is the clause it deferred. WHAT CHANGED, and it is two independent measurements on the same day. (1) storyflow's governance model is a 121-node cluster tripping `disconnected_community` with `generate_bridge` proposed — a remedy that would fabricate traceability between fleet-operations governance and product design, which are two genuinely separate concerns sharing a repo. (2) THIS DESIGN reproduced it at 5 nodes: capturing governance requirements under dec:governance-integrates-not-splits produced heal:33d1548dae64e97a with the same suggested fix, and no honest bridge existed. ⭐ THE PART THAT MAKES THIS URGENT RATHER THAN TIDY: both clusters are GOVERNANCE, and both GROW as governance is captured properly. dec:governance-integrates-not-splits has just committed this project to exactly that growth. So the detector currently penalises the work the project decided to do, and gets louder the better the work goes. ⚠️ AND THE CONSTRAINT BOTH PROJECTS ARRIVED AT INDEPENDENTLY, SIXTEEN DAYS APART — this is the strongest evidence available that the shape is right, and it is also the trap. The 2026-07-24 decision: 'the exemption must not be written in a way that hides a genuine disconnection.' storyflow, 2026-08-09: 'a real disconnection would arrive inside a 121-node warning everybody has already learned to ignore.' Same sentence, two authors, neither aware of the other. THE OPTIONS. (A) A DECLARED PARTITION — a marker on a Project or Component saying this subtree is deliberately separate, so the detector reports 'N declared partitions, 0 undeclared'. Same shape as `granularity`'s opaque-vs-pending_expansion and as `enforced`'s tri-state, which is the argument for it: reflow2 has twice decided that a CHOICE and an UNFINISHED STATE must not look identical, and this is the third instance. COUNTER: a marker is exactly the kind of thing that gets set once and never revisited, and dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches warns in its own text that 'another marker nothing reads' would be a fourth instance of the very disease. (B) TEACH THE DETECTOR THE CATEGORY, as the 2026-07-24 decision assumed — infer that a cluster of purely-governance or purely-documentation nodes has no operational coupling by nature, the way dec:operational-spof already excludes non-operating things from SPOF findings. CHEAPER for the user, no new vocabulary. COUNTER: an inference cannot be argued with, and a genuine governance island would be hidden by the same rule that exempts the legitimate one. (C) FIX ONLY THE SUGGESTED REMEDY — leave the finding, drop `generate_bridge` where no honest edge exists, and say so. THE SMALLEST HONEST STEP, and it removes the part storyflow called corrupting. COUNTER: it leaves the permanent un-clearable warning, which is the half that makes people stop reading. (D) ACCEPT ISLAND BY ISLAND, as today. COUNTER: an acknowledgement is a one-time answer to a finding whose size keeps changing — acknowledged at 88 it now reads 121, and nothing says when it became a different finding. NOTHING IS PROMOTED. The requirement req:a-cluster-can-be-declared-deliberately-separate states the need; this node holds the unmade choice about its shape, and (A) is written first only because it is what both reporters proposed, not because it is recommended.		SETTLED 2026-08-09 by Anthony: 'agree with: C now, A next with the read-back, not B, not D.' The four options and their counter-arguments are preserved above rather than pruned, so a later reader can see what was weighed and not merely what won. The read-back condition is not decoration: it is what stops option A becoming the fourth instance of the disease `dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches` documents, and it is written into `req:a-cluster-can-be-declared-deliberately-separate` as an acceptance test rather than left as an intention.acceptedA cluster can be declared deliberately separate, so disconnected_community reports undeclared islands instead of one permanent warning, A repair suggestion never proposes fabricating a relationship — where no honest fix exists, the finding says so
RUN 2026-08-06 — composition proved on reflow2 + flo2 + dynograph-foundation: the linking works, the labelling does not exist
PROPOSED as a proof of concept, Anthony 2026-07-27. ⭐ EXECUTED 2026-08-06 at his instruction ('let's trial this out'), after being parked for ten days — and with flo2 SUBSTITUTED FOR STORYFLOW, because storyflow's adopt was never finished while flo2 is actively developed, has a live one-directional dependency on reflow2, has its own graph on the same machine, is built by a second person, and had just generated a real cross-design event. THE ORIGINAL PROPOSAL: build a reflow2 design graph inside storyflow and another inside dynograph-foundation, then have an agent LINK them through their published surfaces and identify where the interfaces are incompatible. WHAT IT WAS MEANT TO PROVE: whether dec:nested-graphs (a graph per ownership boundary) and cap:mirror-surface hold up on designs nobody built to be composed. === WHAT WAS ACTUALLY RUN === Three real designs, their committed exports, composed against reflow2's live design in a throwaway in-memory graph (nothing written to any of them): reflow2 (1497 nodes, graph_id `reflow2`), dynograph-foundation (179 nodes, graph_id `dynograph-foundation`, export written by reflow2 0.16.0), flo2 (77 nodes, graph_id `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2`, written by 0.24.0). compose_and_analyse then pair_designs, each pair in turn. === RESULT 1: THE MECHANISM WORKS === Both compositions imported cleanly with ZERO SKIPPED EDGES — 179 nodes / 270 edges from dynograph-foundation, 77 / 181 from flo2. Ids namespaced as designed; neither source design touched. ⭐ CROSS-VERSION COMPOSITION SURVIVED, AND THAT IS A REAL DATA POINT: dynograph-foundation's export was written by reflow2 0.16.0 and imported into a 0.24.0 graph with nothing dropped. (BL-216) filed the three-graphs-three-versions worry on 2026-08-05 as something that 'becomes load-bearing the moment cross-graph linking lands'. It landed, and it did not bite. That is evidence, not proof — one export, eight minor versions apart, no schema change between them that this design happened to use. ⭐ RESULT 2: A TRUE POSITIVE, AND IT IS THE SEAM THIS WHOLE SESSION WAS ABOUT. The flo2 pairing reported exactly one CONFLICT: `ifc:core-api` (ours, medium `library`) against `ifc:model-provider-api` (flo2, medium `REST`), names matching at 80/100 — 'very likely the same contract, but they cannot be connected as either is currently built.' That is precisely the flo2↔reflow2 problem: flo2 is a web app that needs an HTTP surface, reflow2 exposes a library/stdio one, and closing it is what dec:one-process-many-stores and req:reflow2-consumable-as-an-image exist to do. THE TOOL COMPUTED IT FROM TWO DESIGNS NOBODY BUILT TO BE COMPOSED, AND NOBODY TOLD IT THE ANSWER. That is the single strongest piece of evidence this project has that the composition idea is sound. ⚠️ RESULT 3: ZERO PAIRED BOUNDARIES ON BOTH PAIRS, AND THE REASON IS ONE MISSING LABEL. paired = 0 against dynograph-foundation AND against flo2. seam_findings = 0 on both — which does NOT mean the designs agree; it means NOTHING IS CONNECTED ACROSS THE SEAM. All 15 of dynograph-foundation's published interfaces landed in DEAD SURFACE ('they publish this and nothing here requires it'), and 5 of flo2's did. THE CAUSE IS SINGULAR: REFLOW2 DECLARES NO `required` INTERFACE ANYWHERE. Pairing matches complements — published/both against required/both, never like with like — so with nothing required, nothing can ever pair. reflow2 compiles against dynograph-core; that dependency is real, load-bearing, already declared in the version manifest (req:design-dependencies-declared, accepted, verified) — AND INVISIBLE TO THE SEAM MACHINERY. ⚠️ THE MOST DANGEROUS NUMBER IN THE RUN IS `unmet_needs: 0`. It reads as 'nothing is missing' and it means 'we never said we needed anything'. A design that has declared no needs cannot have an unmet one. Anyone reading that field without reading `dead_surface: 15` beside it would conclude the seam was healthy. RELATED, AND THE SAME ROOT: reflow2 holds FIVE Interfaces for 1497 nodes, two of which were created the previous night, and both of those came back as `unclassified_ours` — the tool naming rather than counting them precisely because `internal` is the DEFAULT and cannot distinguish 'deliberately internal' from 'never classified'. This is maturity_report's SEAMS 0 OF 73 appearing as data instead of as a score. A near-miss makes it concrete: dynograph-foundation ALSO publishes an `ifc:core-api`, and reflow2 has one too, and they cannot pair because both are `published` — like-with-like, correctly refused. ⚠️ RESULT 4: TWO FINDINGS THAT BEAR ON THE FEDERATION IDEA RAISED THE SAME DAY. (1) flo2's graph_id is `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2` while the other two are `reflow2` and `dynograph-foundation` — an opaque mint beside two readable labels. dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs proposes listing graph_ids in a config file; nobody hand-writes `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2` and knows what they typed, so either identity gains a human-facing name or that mechanism needs a different key. (2) THE ACCESS MODEL ANTHONY DESCRIBED CANNOT BE EXPRESSED IN THE GRAPH AT ALL. He specified: userAJ read/write on all three; userAlex read-only on reflow2, read/write on flo2. `who:ajs` and `who:alex` exist as Contributors and AUTHORED_BY records who DID write something, but there is no node type, edge type or property for who MAY write something. That is not a limitation the trial hit — it is a vocabulary that does not exist, and it is the concrete form of the permission-versus-convenience question left open on dec:idea-need-to-know-compartments. === WHAT THIS ANSWERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT === ANSWERED: dec:nested-graphs and the composition capabilities hold up on three real designs built at different times by different hands against a moving foundation. Nothing crashed, nothing was silently dropped, the ids namespaced, and the one genuine incompatibility was found and explained in a sentence a person can act on. NOT ANSWERED, because the run could not reach it: whether seam_report's contract comparison is any good. It needs PAIRS, and there were none. The dependency this decision named — req:interface-spec-complete first, or run against today's thin spec — turns out to have been the wrong dependency: the blocker was not that the spec is thin, it is that nothing is LABELLED as required. === THE CHEAPEST NEXT STEP, NOT TAKEN HERE === Declare reflow2's `required` interfaces — what it consumes from dynograph-foundation, and what flo2 must be able to reach. A handful of nodes. It would convert 15 dead surfaces into real pairs or real unmet needs, and it is the prerequisite for seam_report ever having anything to compare. Recorded rather than done, because it is design about reflow2's own boundaries and belongs to Anthony's word rather than an agent's tidying.		Anthony's own framing, and it lands on intent reflow2 already holds: req:design-composes (accepted), dec:nested-graphs (DECIDED — a design is its own graph when separately owned, released or shared, which is exactly three sibling repos), cap:mirror-surface and cap:publish-surface (both built). So the LINKING half exists and the COMPARING half does not. Recorded originally as a decision point rather than a plan because the sequencing was a real choice: structure the interface spec first, or run the PoC against today's thin spec to find out what it cannot say. ⭐ THE SEQUENCING QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED, AND BOTH BRANCHES WERE WRONG. Running it first was right, and what it found was not 'the spec is too thin to compare' — it was that there is nothing to compare, because no boundary on this side is labelled as a need. req:interface-spec-complete was recorded as this PoC's prerequisite; it is not. The prerequisite is a `required` designation on the interfaces reflow2 actually consumes, which is smaller and more specific than making the spec structurally complete. The second payoff predicted when this was proposed did land: it was the first time reflow2 was pointed at designs it did not author, twice, which is the adopt path Anthony says his real work almost always starts from. The result — clean import, correct namespacing, one true positive, and an honest zero everywhere the design had not been labelled — is the behaviour that path needs. Kept as `proposed` rather than moved to accepted: the PoC RAN, but what it proposed to prove is only half proven. seam_report was never exercised because pairing produced nothing to feed it, and that half stays open until reflow2 declares what it requires. Recorded via chg:linked-repos-trial-run.proposednothing
OPEN — does reflow2 grow a live tier for hundreds of simultaneous planners, alongside the repo file?
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.
